research.unit: F01 app-lifecycle (app module, CommandLine, Dock, process shim) — Electron v44.4.5 API model, Keld origin/main d150a14
research.summary: Census: 160 members (app 115 = 75 methods/30 events/10 properties; CommandLine 5; Dock 11; process 29). Keld today implements a 5-member slice live (app.whenReady/isReady/quit/on/off + ready and window-all-closed events, process.type/process.versions.electron shims) over keld_ipc LIFECYCLE_CHANNEL=3 {Ready, LastWindowClosed, Quit}; everything else in the family is TARGET, and keld-native lists deeplink/autostart/dock as names only. Corpus demand ranks: whenReady/ready, window-all-closed, quit, exit, getPath (Zettlr 40 call sites, draw.io 3), getVersion, requestSingleInstanceLock+second-instance (both apps), open-file (Zettlr 20 sites, draw.io 1), before-quit/will-quit, activate, relaunch (Zettlr), focus/show (Zettlr), isPackaged, setAppUserModelId, disableHardwareAcceleration, process.defaultApp/argv parsing (draw.io). Four design-changing facts: (1) [fact] host Ready is currently signalled on NavigationReady of a host-created window (crates/keld-core/src/app_session.rs:3900), while Electron's ready fires before any window exists — BrowserWindow compat needs Ready re-based. (2) [fact] Quit is a one-shot correlated Call with no veto; Electron before-quit/will-quit preventDefault and beforeunload cancellation (Zettlr depends on it) need a two-phase host protocol; app.exit(code) cannot be process.exit because the supervisor recovers nonzero Bun exits with a fresh generation and re-sends Ready (arch 06 §1) and treats status-zero post-ready exit as KELD-RUNTIME-012. (3) [fact] the strict Bun child receives only KELD_APP_LINK + log sinks, so single-instance lock, second-instance argv/cwd/additionalData, open-file/open-url, getPath roots and OS registrations (protocol client, login items, dock) must be host-owned and delivered as typed events/calls; research 186 row 2 already classifies the handoff tuple as untrusted input. (4) [fact] protocol-client and login-item registration are build-time declarations (Info.plist CFBundleURLTypes, .desktop, MSIX uap:Protocol) and v0 has no .app/plist/MSIX emitter (keld-auth rung 2), so the facade must return false with a diagnostic rather than a silent true. commandLine.* is on the never list (arbitrary Chromium flags) and becomes a facade-local no-op store with a one-time dev warning. Six atoms below; all labelled; unknowns kept explicit.

decisions.question: What does host `Ready` mean once BrowserWindow is app-created? Today Ready is emitted on AppWindowEvent::NavigationReady of a host-created window; Electron `ready` fires once after the main process's first event-loop tick, before any window exists, and apps create windows inside whenReady.
decisions.proposed_answer: Re-base LifecycleEvent::Ready to 'host initialized, window module available, zero app windows' and move the first-window creation to the facade's `new BrowserWindow` (window module Call). Keep the wire enum unchanged (Ready=0x00) so KEL-237 cells stay valid; change only the host emission point. The existing LifecycleSession.window_opened/window_closed counter remains the LastWindowClosed owner (host-side registry count, not a facade-local count), which also fixes `activate(hasVisibleWindows)`. Type: task gated by a grilling on cold-start budget (window creation now waits for Bun start + HELLO; arch 01 §5 ≤300 ms cold→first paint must be re-measured, not assumed).
evidence: [fact] crates/keld-core/src/app_session.rs:3900-3901 `AppWindowEvent::NavigationReady => router.signal_ready()`, `LastWindowClosed => router.signal_last_window_closed()`
[fact] crates/keld-wv/src/engine.rs:100-105 AppWindowEvent {NavigationReady: 'Initial renderer navigation completed on the live backend', LastWindowClosed}

[fact] Electron app.md 'ready': 'Emitted once, when Electron has finished initializing' and NOTE 'The ready event is only fired after the main process has finished running the first tick of the event loop'
[fact] electron-quick-start main.js:25-30 and draw.io electron.js:987 create windows inside app.whenReady().then(...)
[fact] KEL-142 spec AC3: 'No import-time ready promise, stdout readiness, renderer readiness' may stand in for host Ready
decisions.confidence: high that re-basing is required; medium on budget impact (unmeasured)
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Keep host-created first window and alias it to the first `new BrowserWindow` — rejected: hidden coupling (webPreferences/show:false/ready-to-show cannot be honored for a window that already navigated), ordering inversion, and a second `new BrowserWindow` would need a different path. (b) Emit `ready` from the facade at import — rejected by KEL-142 AC3 and by the lifecycle-corpus negative control (Promise.resolve() must fail the when-ready cell).
decisions.unknowns: Cold-start→first-paint cost of deferring window creation until Bun HELLO is unmeasured [unknown]; whether `will-finish-launching` on macOS should map to a distinct host event (applicationWillFinishLaunching) or alias ready as on Win/Linux [unknown — low demand: draw.io uses it only to register open-file].

decisions.question: How do before-quit / will-quit / quit (with preventDefault and beforeunload cancellation) and app.exit(exitCode) map onto a host that owns windows and a supervisor that recovers Bun crashes?
decisions.proposed_answer: Make Quit two-phase and host-owned: (1) a host→app `QuitRequested{source}` Event for Cmd+Q / dock Quit / OS logoff / facade app.quit(); the facade emits before-quit, then host closes windows (running renderer beforeunload via the window module), then will-quit; any preventDefault or a beforeunload veto sends `QuitCancelled` back and the host stays alive; otherwise the facade sends the existing correlated `Quit` Call and emits `quit(exitCode)` on Reply. (2) Add a distinct `Exit{code}` Call: host replies, skips before-quit/will-quit, tears down with KEL-96 ordering and exits with `code`; the supervisor must classify the following Bun exit as host-authorized (same rule already used for status-zero after accepted Quit). `window-all-closed` must NOT be emitted during a quit-initiated close (host suppresses LastWindowClosed while a Quit is in flight). Type: grilling → approved spec amendment to KEL-96/KEL-139 Quit ordering (architecture change: crash ownership of an app-requested exit).
evidence: [fact] Electron app.md: app.quit 'Try to close all windows. The before-quit event will be emitted first ... This method guarantees that all beforeunload and unload event handlers are correctly executed. It is possible that a window cancels the quitting'; app.exit 'Exits immediately with exitCode ... before-quit and will-quit events will not be emitted'; window-all-closed 'If the user pressed Cmd + Q, or the developer called app.quit() ... the window-all-closed event would not be emitted'
[fact] Zettlr source/main.ts:201-217 will-quit handler calls event.preventDefault(), awaits shutdownApplication(), sets canQuit=true, then app.quit() again
[fact] draw.io electron.js: app.exit(1) in export mode and uncaughtException (7 sites); Zettlr main.ts:41 app.exit(0) when lock not obtained; corpus scan app.exit count 7 (draw.io) / 14 (Zettlr)

[fact] docs/architecture/06-runtime-and-tooling.md §1: 'a recoverable nonzero Bun crash revokes its endpoint/token/stream before the persistent guardian's one Supervisor requests a fresh generation ... send Ready again'; 'Status-zero self-termination remains terminal; a status-zero exit after an accepted correlated Quit is host-authorized'; strict post-ready liveness surfaces KELD-RUNTIME-012 for unrequested status-zero
[fact] crates/keld-ipc/src/lifecycle.rs: LifecycleRequest has only Quit; no cancel/veto; lifecycle not guard-routed
[fact] grep of crates/keld-core/src/app_session.rs for applicationShouldTerminate / WM_QUERYENDSESSION / SIGTERM returns no handler: host-initiated OS termination sources are not implemented
decisions.confidence: high that process.exit cannot implement app.exit and that a veto phase is needed; medium on exact event/Call shape
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) app.exit → process.exit(code): rejected — nonzero exit is recovered with a fresh generation and Ready(g2) (opposite of Electron), zero exit becomes KELD-RUNTIME-012 diagnostics, and exitCode is lost. (b) before-quit as fire-and-forget emitted just before the existing Quit Call: rejected — Zettlr's preventDefault + async shutdown + second quit would race the host teardown and renderer beforeunload could not veto. (c) Facade-local suppression of window-all-closed by a 'quitting' flag: rejected as hidden coupling — the host owns window close order and must own the suppression.
decisions.unknowns: Whether `beforeunload` veto is reachable from the system webviews uniformly (WKWebView has no beforeunload dialog API; WebView2/WebKitGTK differ) [unknown — needs F03 window unit]; Windows session-end semantics (Electron emits none of before-quit/will-quit/quit on shutdown/logoff) have no Keld host handler yet [unknown].

decisions.question: Who owns single-instance lock, second-instance delivery, open-file and open-url, given the strict Bun child receives no argv/cwd and macOS Finder enforces single instance outside the app's control?
decisions.proposed_answer: One host-owned `deeplink` admission point (arch 05 §3 row 'protocol registration + single-instance handoff'), declared in keld.config.ts (`app.singleInstance: true`, declared schemes/file types), acquired by the host BEFORE Bun spawn so a losing second host never shows a window and exits 0. The host converts OS inputs into typed, bounded Events on a lifecycle-adjacent channel: `SecondInstance{argv, cwd, additionalData, source}`, `OpenFile{path}`, `OpenUrl{url}`, `Activate{hasVisibleWindows}`; the host queues them from process start and flushes them to the facade after HELLO and before `Ready` so a synchronously registered top-level listener observes them exactly as in Electron. `requestSingleInstanceLock()` in the facade becomes a synchronous read of a host-provided boot fact (the lock is already held by this host) plus registration of additionalData for *future* losers; `hasSingleInstanceLock`/`releaseSingleInstanceLock` are Calls. All delivered strings are untrusted data (research 186 row 2): no path becomes an fs grant; the app must open it through the dialog-like scoped-grant flow. Type: prototype (3-OS two-launch harness) then spec.
evidence: [fact] Electron app.md second-instance: 'emitted inside the primary instance ... when a second instance has been executed and calls app.requestSingleInstanceLock()'; 'argv will not be exactly the same list ... use additionalData'; 'If the second instance is started by a different user ... argv array will not include the arguments'; 'guaranteed to be emitted after the ready event'; requestSingleInstanceLock NOTE: mac/Linux single message limited to 32 MB, larger dropped (returns false, no event)

[fact] Electron app.md requestSingleInstanceLock: 'On macOS, the system enforces single instance automatically when users try to open a second instance ... in Finder, and the open-file and open-url events will be emitted ... when users start your app in command line, the system's single instance mechanism will be bypassed'

[fact] Electron app.md open-file: 'also emitted when a file is dropped onto the dock and the application is not yet running. Make sure to listen ... very early ... (even before the ready event)'; open-url: 'If you register the listener in response to a ready event, you'll miss URLs that trigger the launch'
[fact] docs/architecture/06-runtime-and-tooling.md: child gets 'KELD_APP_LINK ... and fixed-direction stdout/stderr log sinks ... no other inherited descriptor or OS handle'

[fact] docs/research/library/compatibility-competitors/186-electron-micro-surfaces.md row 2: 'Treat every handoff field as external input ... Keld needs one host-owned primary admission point, replay/duplicate policy, source/role identity, and typed deep-link parsing before routing' — marked NEW gap

[fact] draw.io electron.js:1718-1760 requestSingleInstanceLock → app.quit() on failure; second-instance handler createWindow() then `commandLine.pop()` as a potential file path (statSafe isFile check); electron.js:2142-2150 open-file registered inside will-finish-launching with event.preventDefault()
[fact] Zettlr main.ts:35-42 top-level requestSingleInstanceLock → app.exit(0); main.ts:139-181 second-instance and open-file with a `filesBeforeOpen` queue for pre-ready delivery
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Bun-side lock (lock file under userData, or a local socket): rejected — strict profile denies ambient fs/network (`connect`/`bind` always denied, KEL-78 §Network), and macOS Finder reopen is delivered to the host process regardless. (b) Resolve the lock after Bun starts: rejected — two hosts would each create a window and the loser's window would flash. (c) Deliver second-instance argv over the renderer bridge or ipcMain: rejected — wrong principal; delivery must be host→primary-role on a lifecycle channel.
decisions.unknowns: additionalData size cap: Electron allows up to 32 MB; kipc inline frames are small (VirtualPort MAX_PORT_MESSAGE_LEN=4096; lifecycle frames are unit enums today) — a documented smaller cap (▲) or chunked delivery is a decision for the kipc owner [unknown]. Whether `source` should distinguish CLI vs Finder vs URL-scheme for policy [lead]. Windows: Electron's ProcessSingleton lives under userData; Keld's equivalent identity (KEL-135 profile identity vs per-executable) is undecided [unknown].

decisions.question: Where do getPath(name), getAppPath, getVersion/getName/name, isPackaged, process.resourcesPath/defaultApp/argv values come from, and must `userData` match Electron's layout?
decisions.proposed_answer: Host-computed boot facts, delivered once after HELLO as a `BootDescriptor` Event (immutable for the generation; same transport as Ready) and cached synchronously in the facade so getPath/getVersion are synchronous like Electron. name/version/productName come from keld.config.ts (KEL-15) with package.json fallback; isPackaged = host-staged install root vs `keld dev` owner-private stage (KEL-96); process.argv is the host's OS argv re-shaped to packaged-Electron form `[exe, ...userArgs]` with process.defaultApp set only under `keld dev` (so draw.io's `argv.unshift(null)` and Zettlr's `extractFilesFromArgv` behave). `userData` must be a directory that is also a generated `app.fs.read`/`app.fs.write` grant root so electron-store/electron-log keep working under the strict profile; `sessionData` is Keld-owned (KEL-135 profile roots) and `setPath('sessionData')` is a documented ▲ no-op with diagnostic. `logs` defaults per Electron (~/Library/Logs/<name> on macOS; under userData on Win/Linux). Type: grilling (product decision on userData layout).
evidence: [fact] Electron app.md getPath: userData 'by default is the appData directory appended with your app's name'; sessionData 'By default this points to userData'; 'On failure, an Error is thrown'; setPath: 'If the path specifies a directory that does not exist, an Error is thrown'; 'override the sessionData path before the ready event'; setAppLogsPath default '~/Library/Logs/YourAppName on macOS, and inside the userData directory on Linux and Windows'

[fact] Electron process.md defaultApp: 'When the app is started by being passed as parameter to the default Electron executable, this property is true in the main process, otherwise it is undefined ... useful to determine how many arguments will need to be sliced off from process.argv'

[fact] draw.io electron.js:1056-1061 `if (process.defaultApp != true) argv.unshift(null)` then parseDrawioArgs(argv); electron.js:58 and :3796 getPath('userData') for Local Storage leveldb and userDataDir; Zettlr main.ts:59-72 setPath('userData', dataDir) + setAppLogsPath when --data-dir given; app.isPackaged 7 signals

[fact] docs/specs/kel135-persistent-profile-identity.md: Windows `FOLDERID_LocalAppData/Keld/profiles/v1/<identity>/webview2`; Linux `$XDG_DATA_HOME/Keld/profiles/v1/<identity>/webkit`; macOS identifier-addressed WKWebsiteDataStore ('Apple owns physical store layout'; 'no Apple physical-path claim')

[fact] docs/architecture/06-runtime-and-tooling.md: 'No environment identity, child payload ... can choose a role or authority'; crates/keld-guard/src/lib.rs evaluate() default-denies paths outside `app.fs.*` scope arrays (path_in_scope) and rejects `..`
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Compute paths in Bun from HOME/APPDATA/XDG env: rejected — duplicates KEL-135 policy (one rule one owner), env availability in the strict child is not a contract, and the value would not be tied to a grant. (b) Make getPath async: rejected — Electron contract is synchronous and corpus apps call it at module top-level (Zettlr 40 sites). (c) Point userData at the KEL-135 profile root: rejected for v1 unless decided — Electron's own guidance says app files should avoid Chromium subdirs; mixing engine stores with app data recreates the problem Electron documents.
decisions.unknowns: Whether migrated apps must find their *existing* Electron userData (e.g. ~/Library/Application Support/draw.io) — a product/migration decision, not derivable from docs [unknown]. Whether the strict profile exposes HOME/APPDATA at all to the child [unknown — KEL-78 spec lists inherited objects, not environment variables]. getPath('home'/'documents'/'downloads'/...) values are paths without authority; whether returning them without a matching grant misleads apps (▲ note) [lead].

decisions.question: How are setAsDefaultProtocolClient / isDefaultProtocolClient / removeAsDefaultProtocolClient and setLoginItemSettings / getLoginItemSettings implemented when the registrations are OS-level writes the strict child cannot perform and macOS/MSIX require build-time declarations?
decisions.proposed_answer: Build-time declarations in keld.config.ts (`app.protocols: ['drawio']`, `app.autostart: true|false`) materialized by keld-pack into Info.plist CFBundleURLTypes, Linux .desktop MimeType x-scheme-handler/<scheme>, MSIX uap:Protocol, and — for autostart — SMAppService (macOS, requires signed+notarized), HKCU Run + StartupApproved (Windows), XDG autostart .desktop (Linux, a Keld extra since Electron tags login items mac/win only). Runtime facade calls become guarded host Calls on `deeplink.register`/`autostart.set` whose grant shape is a literal allowlist: `app.deeplink.register: ['drawio']`, `app.autostart.set: ['self']`; `path`/`args`/`execPath`-style options that would register another executable are refused (never). When the host cannot materialize (no bundle in `keld dev`, unsigned, appx), the facade returns `false` and emits a KELD-NATIVE-* diagnostic — never `true`. Type: task, blocked_by KEL-19 (no .app/plist/MSIX emitter) and KEL-89 rung 2.
evidence: [fact] Electron app.md setAsDefaultProtocolClient: 'On macOS, you can only register protocols that have been added to your app's info.plist, which cannot be modified at runtime'; 'In a Windows Store environment (when packaged as an appx) this API will return true for all calls but the registry key it sets won't be accessible'; 'uses the Windows Registry and LSSetDefaultHandlerForURLScheme internally'; Returns boolean

[fact] Electron tutorial launch-app-from-url-in-another-app.md: 'On macOS and Linux, this feature will only work when your app is packaged'; dev mode on Windows requires `setAsDefaultProtocolClient(scheme, process.execPath, [path.resolve(process.argv[1])])`; Linux .desktop `mimeType x-scheme-handler/<scheme>`

[fact] Electron app.md setLoginItemSettings IMPORTANT: 'On macOS, your app should be code signed and notarized ... openAtLogin may silently fail'; options type mainAppService/agentService/daemonService/loginItemService, Windows path defaults to process.execPath, `enabled` toggles StartupApproved, `name` defaults to AppUserModelId; getLoginItemSettings status 'not-registered | enabled | requires-approval | not-found'

[fact] docs/specs/keld-auth.md host-broker chain rung 2: 'registration is unauthenticated last-writer on Windows — delivery ≠ ownership'; 'v0: effectively unavailable (no MSIX/uap:Protocol emitter exists; keld-pack is a name-only enum)'; macOS 'v0: no .app bundle/plist emitter exists → not reachable'

[fact] crates/keld-native/src/lib.rs MODULES includes 'deeplink', 'autostart' with no implementation; docs/architecture/05-webview-and-native.md §3 rows map them to app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient / app.setLoginItemSettings

[fact] corpus demand: neither draw.io nor Zettlr calls setAsDefaultProtocolClient or setLoginItemSettings (0 hits in usage scans); Zettlr declares a custom `safe-file://` protocol via protocol.handle (different unit)
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Runtime registry/LaunchServices writes from the Bun child: rejected — strict profile has zero ambient OS authority (KEL-78), Windows LPAC child cannot write HKCU Run, and runtime-only macOS registration is impossible per Electron's own doc. (b) Returning `true` optimistically to keep apps' happy paths: rejected — silent downgrade violates briefing invariant 3 and KEL-127 'no silent downgrade'. (c) Allowing `process.execPath` as the registered path: rejected — in Keld execPath is Bun, not the launchable app; the host/app bundle is the only valid target.
decisions.unknowns: Whether Keld should expose Linux autostart at all (Electron does not; adding it is a ✔+ extension that needs its own scoreboard note) [decision]. Exact SMAppService status mapping to Electron's four status strings is not verified against Apple docs here [unknown].

decisions.question: What happens to app.commandLine.*, enableSandbox, disableHardwareAcceleration/isHardwareAccelerationEnabled, disableDomainBlockingFor3DAPIs, getGPUInfo/getGPUFeatureStatus/gpu-info-update, getAppMetrics and process.noAsar on an engine that is not Chromium-with-flags?
decisions.proposed_answer: Facade-local, explicitly scored shims: `commandLine` keeps a private switch map so appendSwitch→hasSwitch/getSwitchValue/removeSwitch are self-consistent, never touches the engine, and emits one dev-only KELD-COMPAT warning per switch (never list: 'arbitrary Chromium/V8 flags'); `enableSandbox()` is a ✔ no-op (renderers are always sandboxed; calling after ready is still an error to match Electron); `disableHardwareAcceleration()` is ▲ and may map to an engine preference only through KEL-132's GPU/media guard, otherwise no-op with diagnostic; GPU info/metrics are host Calls returning Keld's process census (host + Bun roles + webview processes) with Electron field names where a 1:1 meaning exists and documented ▲ otherwise; `process.noAsar` is ✘ (no ASAR). Type: task (scoreboard entries + conformance cells), no boundary change.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: Emitted when all windows close; default (no listener) quits. If quit was initiated by app.quit() or Cmd+Q, Electron closes windows then emits will-quit and does NOT emit window-all-closed.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: Host emits LastWindowClosed whenever the count hits zero, including during Quit teardown → facade emits window-all-closed → quick-start/draw.io call app.quit() again (re-entrant Quit Call on a session already quiescing).
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Sequence test with two windows open: app.quit() → observed event list equals [before-quit, (window close events), will-quit, quit]; window-all-closed count = 0; exactly one Quit Call on the wire. Negative control: closing both windows manually yields [window-all-closed] and no will-quit.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: before-quit is emitted before windows start closing; preventDefault cancels termination; will-quit after all windows closed, also cancellable; app.quit guarantees beforeunload/unload run and a window returning false from beforeunload cancels quitting. After autoUpdater.quitAndInstall(), before-quit fires after window close events.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: LifecycleRequest::Quit is one-shot: host replies then ends the session (lifecycle.rs). No veto path. Zettlr's will-quit handler preventDefaults, runs async shutdown, then calls app.quit() again — with a one-shot Quit the host would already have torn down the link mid-shutdown.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: Returns true for the primary; false means another instance holds the lock and the caller should quit. second-instance fires in the primary after ready with (argv, workingDirectory, additionalData); argv may be reordered/extended; different user → no argv; mac/Linux message cap 32 MB (larger dropped silently, returns false, no event). macOS Finder second-open is handled by the OS as open-file/open-url, not second-instance.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: The strict Bun child cannot create OS locks or receive argv/cwd; if the lock is acquired after Bun start, two hosts show windows before resolution. Handoff tuple is untrusted external input (research 186) and must not be routed to privileged handlers. draw.io treats `commandLine.pop()` as a file path (statSafe isFile) — path becomes app-level fs access expectation.
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Two-launch harness per OS: launch A, wait Ready; launch B with argv [file.drawio] and cwd X → B exits 0 with no window ever created (window registry census), A's facade receives exactly one second-instance with argv containing file.drawio and workingDirectory X after ready. Replay control: launch B twice → two ordered events, never coalesced. Different-user control (Windows/Linux CI): argv empty. Oversize additionalData → documented cap error, no partial delivery.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: open-file is emitted when the OS asks the running app to open a file or when a file is dropped on the dock before launch; listeners must be registered very early (before ready) or launch-time events are missed; preventDefault to handle. open-url requires Info.plist CFBundleURLTypes + NSPrincipalClass AtomApplication. On Windows the path arrives in process.argv.

platform_notes.note: [fact] open-file/open-url/activate/did-become-active/did-resign-active/new-window-for-tab are NSApplicationDelegate-driven and arrive at the host; Finder-initiated second launches are coalesced by the OS into open-file/open-url, CLI launches bypass that (Electron app.md). [fact] Protocol handlers require Info.plist CFBundleURLTypes and NSPrincipalClass; not runtime-modifiable; v0 has no .app/plist emitter (keld-auth rung 2) so deep links are unreachable until KEL-19/keld-pack. prototype_candidates.question: Can one host-owned single-instance admission point deliver second-instance / open-file / open-url with Electron ordering (after ready, queued when pre-ready) on all three OS, with the loser never creating a window?
prototype_candidates.shape: Scratchpad-only two-launch harness around the existing no-flag host: host acquires an OS lock before Bun spawn (macOS: NSRunningApplication/bundle-id check + CLI path; Windows: named mutex under the KEL-135 identity; Linux: flock under $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR), forwards {argv, cwd, additionalData} over a new lifecycle-adjacent Event, facade queues until listeners/Ready. 3 cells + replay and different-user negative controls.
prototype_candidates.shows: Whether the admission tuple can be typed and bounded within kipc inline limits, how much pre-Ready queueing is needed, and the exact wire Event shape for the KEL-237 corpus extension.

prototype_candidates.question: Does a two-phase Quit (QuitRequested → veto window → Quit) plus a distinct Exit{code} Call preserve KEL-96 ordering (accept→reply→quiesce→revoke→reap→UI exit) and propagate exit codes without triggering supervisor recovery?
prototype_candidates.shape: Zettlr-shape fixture (will-quit preventDefault, async shutdown, second quit) and draw.io-shape fixture (app.exit(1) in headless export mode) against a patched LifecycleSession in a scratch branch; observe host exit code, generation count, descendant census, and KELD-RUNTIME-012 absence.
prototype_candidates.shows: Whether the supervisor's 'host-authorized exit' rule generalizes from status-zero-after-Quit to arbitrary codes-after-Exit, and whether window-all-closed suppression must live in the host (expected) or can live in the facade (expected to fail).

prototype_candidates.question: What is the cold-start → first-paint cost of re-basing Ready to 'zero windows' so the facade creates the first BrowserWindow after HELLO?
prototype_candidates.shape: Reuse the KEL-90/KEL-129 harness: measure fresh-process cold→PAINT-OPPORTUNITY for (a) current host-created window, (b) window created on facade Call after Ready; 30 samples each, bootstrap CI, per OS.
prototype_candidates.shows: Whether the ≤300 ms budget survives the Electron-faithful ordering or whether a `show:false` pre-created window + bind-on-first-BrowserWindow optimization must be specified explicitly (and scored as ▲ if semantics differ).

prototype_candidates.question: Can macOS cold-launch open-file/open-url be captured by the host and delivered to a top-level facade listener before `ready` without loss or duplication?
prototype_candidates.shape: `open -a <staged app> fixture.drawio` against a scratch host that records NSApplicationDelegate application:openURLs:/openFiles: into a bounded queue flushed after HELLO; facade fixture registers listeners synchronously and records order vs ready.
prototype_candidates.shows: Pre-Ready delivery feasibility and the need (or not) for a will-finish-launching distinct host event; also whether queue bounds need a documented cap.

never_list.surface: app.commandLine.appendSwitch / appendArgument with engine effect (any Chromium/V8 switch, incl. remote-debugging-port, no-sandbox, disable-web-security, js-flags)
never_list.rationale: Briefing never list and research 13: arbitrary Chromium/V8 flags undermine engine policy; Keld uses system webviews where the switch namespace does not exist (WKWebView/WebKitGTK) or would be engine-specific (WebView2). Facade keeps a no-op local map with a diagnostic.

never_list.surface: app.relaunch({ execPath }) to any executable other than the app's own launcher
never_list.rationale: Arbitrary exec from a strict role is on the never list (raw child_process/exec); relaunch must re-exec the host launcher only.

never_list.surface: setLoginItemSettings({ path, args }) / setUserTasks / setJumpList targeting a program other than the app's own launcher, and registering Bun's process.execPath
never_list.rationale: Autostarting or launching foreign executables is ambient OS authority; Bun's execPath is not the launchable app in Keld.

never_list.surface: setAsDefaultProtocolClient for a scheme not declared at build time in keld.config.ts / Info.plist / .desktop / uap:Protocol, or returning `true` when the OS registration did not happen
never_list.rationale: Runtime scheme minting is impossible on macOS and unauthenticated last-writer on Windows (keld-auth rung 2); a silent `true` is a silent downgrade forbidden by KEL-127.

never_list.surface: certificate-error → event.preventDefault() + callback(true) TLS trust override, select-client-certificate arbitrary selection, importCertificate into the platform store, from strict-profile roles
never_list.rationale: Network trust decisions are host/guard policy; app-level overrides reintroduce the Electron default-allow class (research 186). Legacy-profile only, visibly labeled.

never_list.surface: second-instance / open-file argv paths used directly as filesystem authority (implicit grant)
never_list.rationale: Research 186 row 2: handoff fields are untrusted external input; a delivered path is data until a scoped grant is minted through the dialog/deeplink grant flow.

never_list.surface: app.setPath('sessionData', …) relocating Keld-owned engine profile roots
never_list.rationale: KEL-135 owns persistent profile identity and roots; app-selected engine storage paths would duplicate policy and break identity-bound isolation. Documented ▲ no-op.

never_list.surface: process.noAsar / ASAR semantics
never_list.rationale: Keld has no ASAR archive layer; documented ✘ (not applicable), not emulated.

receipts.claim: ready: 'Emitted once, when Electron has finished initializing'; NOTE 'The ready event is only fired after the main process has finished running the first tick of the event loop. If an Electron API needs to be called before the ready event, ensure that it is called synchronously in the top-level context'

window-all-closed: 'If you do not subscribe to this event and all windows are closed, the default behavior is to quit the app ... If the user pressed Cmd + Q, or the developer called app.quit(), Electron will first try to close all the windows and then emit the will-quit event, and in this case the window-all-closed event would not be emitted.'

before-quit: 'Emitted before the application starts closing its windows. Calling event.preventDefault() will prevent the default behavior, which is terminating the application.' NOTE: after autoUpdater.quitAndInstall() before-quit is emitted after close on all windows; NOTE: not emitted on Windows shutdown/restart/logout. will-quit: 'Emitted when all windows have been closed and the application will quit' (cancellable). quit: (event, exitCode).

app.quit(): 'Try to close all windows. The before-quit event will be emitted first. If all windows are successfully closed, the will-quit event will be emitted and by default the application will terminate. This method guarantees that all beforeunload and unload event handlers are correctly executed. It is possible that a window cancels the quitting by returning false in the beforeunload event handler.'

app.exit([exitCode]): 'Exits immediately with exitCode. exitCode defaults to 0. All windows will be closed immediately without asking the user, and the before-quit and will-quit events will not be emitted.'

app.relaunch: 'Relaunches the app when the current instance exits. By default, the new instance will use the same working directory and command line arguments ... this method does not quit the app when executed ... When app.relaunch is called multiple times, multiple instances will be started'

second-instance: '(event, argv, workingDirectory, additionalData) ... emitted inside the primary instance ... when a second instance has been executed and calls app.requestSingleInstanceLock()'; 'argv will not be exactly the same list of arguments ... use additionalData'; 'If the second instance is started by a different user than the first, the argv array will not include the arguments'; 'guaranteed to be emitted after the ready event'

requestSingleInstanceLock: returns true for the primary, false means quit; 'On macOS, the system enforces single instance automatically when users try to open a second instance of your app in Finder, and the open-file and open-url events will be emitted ... when users start your app in command line, the system's single instance mechanism will be bypassed'; NOTE: on macOS and Linux the second instance's arguments and additionalData are one message limited to 32 MB; larger messages are dropped, method still returns false, primary does not emit second-instance.

open-file (macOS): 'also emitted when a file is dropped onto the dock and the application is not yet running. Make sure to listen for the open-file event very early in your application startup ... (even before the ready event is emitted). You should call event.preventDefault() if you want to handle this event. On Windows, you have to parse process.argv'. open-url: 'Info.plist file must define the URL scheme within the CFBundleURLTypes key, and set NSPrincipalClass to AtomApplication ... If you register the listener in response to a ready event, you'll miss URLs that trigger the launch'

activate (macOS): '(event, hasVisibleWindows) ... Various actions can trigger this event, such as launching the application for the first time, attempting to re-launch the application when it's already running, or clicking on the application's dock or taskbar icon.' will-finish-launching: 'On Windows and Linux ... the same as the ready event; on macOS ... applicationWillFinishLaunching'

setAsDefaultProtocolClient: 'Returns boolean - Whether the call succeeded'; 'On macOS, you can only register protocols that have been added to your app's info.plist, which cannot be modified at runtime'; 'In a Windows Store environment (when packaged as an appx) this API will return true for all calls but the registry key it sets won't be accessible by other applications'; 'uses the Windows Registry and LSSetDefaultHandlerForURLScheme internally'; isDefaultProtocolClient uses LSCopyDefaultHandlerForURLScheme

verdicts.reason: The core fact holds: Ready is emitted on NavigationReady of a host-created window and must be re-based for app-created BrowserWindow. The wire enum's own doc already carries the Electron-compatible meaning ("The host is ready for the app process to create windows / run"), so changing only the emission point keeps KEL-237 cells valid. But the reuse claim names the wrong owner, the budget unknown is mis-scoped, and the type is understated.

verdicts.reason: Two contrary facts. (1) Lock timing/ownership: Electron's lock is requested by app code at a point the app chooses, and the loser decides what to do with false. Both corpus apps run CLI exit paths BEFORE requesting the lock: draw.io handles export mode (app.exit(1) at electron.js:1699), -V/--version (app.quit at 1707) and -h/--help (1711) and only then calls requestSingleInstanceLock at 1718 — and it does so INSIDE whenReady, i.e. after ready; Zettlr calls handleExitArguments() at main.ts:30 before the lock at main.ts:35. A host that acquires the lock pre-spawn and makes 'a losing second host never show a window and exit 0' before Bun runs breaks `drawio -x file` and `drawio --version`/`zettlr --version` whenever a GUI instance is running, and breaks draw.io's post-ready lock request. The 'window flash' rationale for rejecting alternative (b) is also weak: Electron apps check the lock before creating any window, so the loser Bun creates nothing; the loser cost is Bun startup, strictly cheaper than Electron's loser (a full Chromium browser process). The doc also fixes the notify moment: second-instance is emitted 'when a second instance has been executed and calls app.requestSingleInstanceLock()' — argv/cwd/additionalData travel at call time, not at process start, and additionalData does not exist until the call. (2) Ordering: the proposal flushes SecondInstance, OpenFile, OpenUrl and Activate together 'after HELLO and before Ready'. app.md guarantees second-instance 'is guaranteed to be emitted after the ready event of app gets emitted', whereas open-file/open-url must be deliverable before ready. Delivering second-instance pre-ready is a divergence that Zettlr turns into data loss: main.ts:140-142 `if (!isAppServiceContainerReady()) return` drops the event. Everything else in A3 survives: strict child has only KELD_APP_LINK + log sinks (arch 06:188-189); KEL-78 denies connect/bind/socket (kel78 §Network line 228); research 186 row 2 classifies the handoff tuple as untrusted (186:58); macOS Finder single-instance/open-file text verified (app.md 1073-1096); 32 MB cap verified; MAX_PORT_MESSAGE_LEN=4096 verified (virtual_port.rs:15); draw.io commandLine.pop() isFile path at 1747-1756 verified; Zettlr filesBeforeOpen queue at main.ts:84-90,162-181 verified.

verdicts.correction: Keep host-owned lock *acquisition* (the host may pre-acquire pre-spawn so the primary identity exists before Bun), but preserve Electron's call-time semantics: the loser host still spawns Bun; requestSingleInstanceLock() is a synchronous read of the host-provided boot fact {lockHeld: bool} that must be valid before and after Ready, and the Call also carries additionalData to the host, which performs the notify-primary at that moment (second-instance payload = loser's OS argv/cwd + additionalData); the loser then does whatever the app does (app.quit/app.exit/continue). Split the host queues by Electron's ordering contract: OpenFile/OpenUrl (and launch Activate) flush after HELLO and before Ready; SecondInstance is held until after Ready. Offer the 'host exits loser before Bun' behavior only as an explicit keld.config.ts opt-in scored ▲, never the default. Rewrite the test oracle: launch B with `--version` while A runs -> B prints version and exits 0 via Bun; launch B during A's boot -> A receives second-instance strictly after ready.

epic.title: compat(app): Electron app lifecycle, single-instance, paths and process shim over host-owned lifecycle
epic.body:
## Scope
Electron `app` module (115 members: 75 methods, 30 events, 10 properties), `CommandLine` (5), `Dock` (11, macOS), `process` shim (29). Live today: `app.whenReady/isReady/quit/on/off/removeListener`, `ready` and `window-all-closed` events, `process.type='browser'`, `process.versions.electron='0.0.1'` (KEL-72). Everything else is TARGET.

## Corpus demand (resolved call sites, 2026-10-06)
whenReady/ready, window-all-closed, quit, exit, getPath (Zettlr ~40 sites, draw.io 3), getVersion, requestSingleInstanceLock + second-instance (both apps), open-file (Zettlr), before-quit/will-quit, activate, relaunch (Zettlr), isPackaged, setAppUserModelId, disableHardwareAcceleration, process.argv/defaultApp parsing (draw.io).

## Maturity ladder (exit criteria)
- L0: every `app` member exists with a typed `KELD-COMPAT` error for unsupported calls (never a silent no-op).
- L1: electron-quick-start and draw.io boot through `whenReady`, `activate`, `window-all-closed`, `quit` on macOS.
- L2: ordering sequences `before-quit → per-window close → will-quit → quit` (and the `quitAndInstall` inversion) pass conformance entries citing the pinned v44.4.5 `app.md` sentences, with negative controls; `second-instance` delivered exactly once with typed argv/cwd.
- L3: draw.io and Zettlr primary workflows exercise the family under `keld dev` (KEL-74 records, authority profile printed).

## Linear owners consumed
KEL-72 (lifecycle facade), KEL-142 (@keld/api lifecycle/channel), KEL-139/KEL-143 (Ready and generation recovery semantics), KEL-75 (role spawn facts), KEL-78 (strict child environment), KEL-19/KEL-15 (config/bundle emission), KEL-96 (keld dev exit codes).

## Design facts fixed by research (two refuters)
- Host `Ready` is emitted today on the first host-created window's navigation; Electron's `ready` fires before any window exists. Ready must be re-based to "host initialized, window module available" while keeping the wire enum unchanged (KEL-237 cells stay valid) and pairing the re-base with KEL-143 recovery semantics.
- Quit is one-shot and uncancelable today; Electron's cancelable `before-quit`/`will-quit` and renderer `beforeunload` need a two-phase, host-owned protocol. `app.exit(code)` cannot be `process.exit` (the supervisor would recover the role); it is a host Call.
- The strict Bun child receives only `KELD_APP_LINK` and log sinks, so single-instance, second-instance argv/cwd/additionalData, open-file/open-url, path roots and OS registrations are host-owned and delivered as typed events or boot facts.
- Protocol-client and login-item registration are build-time declarations materialised by packaging; the facade reports false with a diagnostic until an emitter exists.
- `app.commandLine.*` is a facade-local self-consistent store with a one-time dev warning (arbitrary Chromium flags are documented-never).

## Platform lanes
macOS first (Dock, open-file/open-url, activate, Handoff APIs are macOS-tagged: 44 members); Windows (jump lists, AppUserModelId, toast activator: 20 members); Linux (badge, desktop name: 4 members). `before-quit/will-quit/quit` are not emitted on Windows shutdown — documented ▲.

**Desired behavior:** The host owns the OS single-instance primitive (declared in `keld.config.ts`), pre-acquires it so the primary identity exists before Bun, and preserves Electron call-time semantics: `requestSingleInstanceLock()` returns the host verdict (the losing instance still runs its early CLI paths), `second-instance` delivers `(argv, workingDirectory, additionalData)` as opaque untrusted data exactly once after `ready`, and macOS `open-file`/`open-url` may precede `ready` and are queued per Electron rules. **Key interfaces:** Host deeplink admission point; lifecycle-adjacent typed events; `keld.config.ts` singleInstance/protocols declarations.

**Acceptance criteria:** the checklist above, each as a test with its negative control.

**Out of scope:** Build-time protocol/login-item registration emitters (F01-T6).

research.summary: F02 covers 32 entities / 606 raw members (BaseWindow 187, BrowserWindow 204 incl. the 126 inherited methods, View/WebContentsView/BrowserView/ImageView, 11 TouchBar classes, 2 option structs with 52+2 fields, WebPreferences 46 fields, JumpList/Task/Thumbar structs). [fact] Keld today has NO BrowserWindow facade: the host owns exactly one primary window per app session (keld-wv v0 WebviewSpec = title+size+initial; one window-filling webview per window), keld-core LifecycleSession only counts windows and emits Ready/LastWindowClosed, close is uncancelable (tao CloseRequested -> LastWindowClosed), no window id crosses kipc, no chrome options (titleBarStyle/vibrancy/frame/transparent) exist in any backend, and the destination keld-core window registry is TARGET per product-status/arch 01. Corpus demand ranks: (1) constructor + show:false/ready-to-show + backgroundColor (Zettlr 14 sites, drawio, progress-bar), (2) cancelable 'close' with async veto then explicit destroy()/close() (drawio + Zettlr both), 'closed' bookkeeping, isDestroyed, (3) getAllWindows/getFocusedWindow/fromWebContents, (4) maximize/minimize/fullscreen state + their events, (5) mac hiddenInset+vibrancy, win/linux frame:false+titleBarStyle hidden+titleBarOverlay (Zettlr), (6) parent/modal (Zettlr modals, drawio hidden export child), (7) setWindowOpenHandler with overrideBrowserWindowOptions (drawio). Six decision atoms: host-owned window identity mirrored in the facade; a two-phase host<->Bun close protocol (close veto, destroy, destroyed-object fence); ready-to-show from a hidden-window paint oracle (prototype-gated, highest risk); WebPreferences triage (policy vs engine-toggle vs never); BrowserWindow implemented once as BaseWindow+one WebContentsView with multi-view/BrowserView deferred to Tier 3; window chrome option tiering per engine. Key invariant consequences: missing setWindowOpenHandler must stay deny (Keld) and be an explicit divergence from Electron; nodeIntegration/contextIsolation:false/sandbox:false/webSecurity:false/offscreen/getNativeWindowHandle/hookWindowMessage are never or legacy-profile only; JumpList `program` must be pinned to the app's own executable.

decisions.question: Who mints window identity and where do getAllWindows/fromId/getFocusedWindow/fromWebContents/win.id resolve?
decisions.proposed_answer: [inference, evidence-backed] The host (keld-core registry, TARGET) mints an opaque (WindowId, WindowGeneration) per native window exactly as KEL-75 already requires for window-bound roles; the Bun-side @keld/api holds a facade-local mirror (Map<WindowId, handle>) updated by host events on the app-link before any user listener runs, so BrowserWindow.getAllWindows()/fromId()/getFocusedWindow() are synchronous local lookups (Electron's are synchronous, and quick-start's `getAllWindows().length === 0` in the `activate` handler must be answerable without an await). `win.id` is a facade-local monotonic positive integer (Electron: 'unique among all BaseWindow instances'), never the host WindowId, which stays opaque and is not reusable after destruction. Keld-core keeps generic names (window registry, no Electron-isms); Electron naming lives in @keld/electron.

decisions.question: How are close/closed/destroy/'Object has been destroyed' reproduced when the host owns the window and app code runs in a separate Bun process?
decisions.proposed_answer: [inference, evidence-backed] Two-phase close owned by the host: (1) native close request (button, Cmd+W, app.quit sweep, parent close) -> host emits CloseRequested{window, generation, seq} and does NOT close; (2) facade emits 'close' synchronously to listeners; if no listener called preventDefault, facade replies CloseAllow(seq); host then runs page unload, destroys the webview before the window (view_drop_order invariant), decrements the lifecycle window count, and emits Closed; (3) `win.destroy()` is a separate unconditional Destroy call that skips 'close' but guarantees 'closed' (Electron contract); (4) after Closed the facade fences the handle: every method/property except isDestroyed() throws Error('Object has been destroyed'). Deadline: if the Bun generation is dead or does not answer within the admission deadline, the host honors the user's close (window closes) — Electron's observable 'user can always close' wins over a dead veto; this is an explicit ▲ to record. 'close' must precede DOM beforeunload (Electron order), so the host must not start unload before CloseAllow.
evidence: browser-window.md 'close': 'Emitted when the window is going to be closed. It's emitted before the beforeunload and unload event of the DOM. Calling event.preventDefault() will cancel the close' (R2)

base-window.md destroy: 'Force closing the window, the unload and beforeunload event won't be emitted ... close event will also not be emitted ... but it guarantees the closed event will be emitted' (R3)
browser-window.md: 'Reading this property throws Object has been destroyed once the window has been destroyed'; isDestroyed note (R4)

drawio electron.js:947-975: 'close' handler calls event.preventDefault() unconditionally, sends 'isModified' to renderer, later calls mainWindow.destroy() guarded by !isDestroyed(); 'closed' splices windowsRegistry

Zettlr windows/index.ts:357-410: 'close' -> event.preventDefault() then async askUserToCloseWindow().then(window.close()); 'closed' deletes map entry; also app.quit() from inside 'close' on win/linux last window
crates/keld-wv/src/view_drop_order.rs: 'Platform bindings require the webview to release before the host window closes'
KEL-143 acceptance: 'Quit ordering is reply -> quiesce/drain -> revoke/close -> terminate/reap -> UI exit'; same native window survives Bun death
decisions.confidence: high on protocol shape; medium on dead-Bun deadline policy
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Host closes immediately and facade emits 'close' after the fact (breaks preventDefault, breaks drawio/Zettlr unsaved-changes flows). Facade-only 'virtual close' that hides the window instead of closing (window-all-closed/LastWindowClosed count would diverge; hidden windows still count as open in Electron). Implementing beforeunload veto in the host without the Bun round-trip (loses 'close' ordering).

decisions.question: Can `show:false` + `ready-to-show` + `backgroundColor` (the dominant corpus pattern) be honored on system webviews?
decisions.proposed_answer: [inference; prototype-gated] Electron fires ready-to-show when the renderer has rendered the page for the first time while the window is hidden, and documents that this depends on painting while hidden (paintWhenInitiallyHidden). Keld must (a) create the native window unmapped when show:false (NSWindow not ordered front / HWND without SW_SHOW / GtkWindow unrealized-but-created), (b) derive ready-to-show from a renderer-side first-frame oracle (the KEL-64 double-rAF beacon already used for first-paint, injected via the host pre-load script, not wry PageLoadEvent::Finished which learnings prove is navigation completion only), and (c) if an engine does not run rAF while unmapped, fall back to 'navigation finished + DOMContentLoaded' and record ▲ 'ready-to-show fires before first composited frame'. backgroundColor maps to native window background + engine default background (WebView2 put_DefaultBackgroundColor; WKWebView/WebKitGTK background color) and must be applied before first navigation to kill the white flash drawio guards against.
evidence: browser-window.md: 'the ready-to-show event will be emitted when the renderer process has rendered the page for the first time if the window has not been shown yet ... using this event implies that the renderer will be considered visible and paint even though show is false. This event will never fire if you use paintWhenInitiallyHidden: false' (R1)
browser-window-options.md paintWhenInitiallyHidden default true: 'Setting this to false will cause the ready-to-show event to not fire' (R7)

Zettlr: 14 ready-to-show sites, every create-*-window.ts uses show:false then window.once('ready-to-show', show); drawio progress-bar.js:44-59 same pattern; drawio createWindow sets backgroundColor to avoid white flash

crates/keld-wv backends emit AppWindowEvent::NavigationReady from load-finished only (wkwebview/mod.rs:723, webkitgtk/mod.rs:532, webview2/mod.rs:1985)

decisions.alternatives_rejected: Mapping ready-to-show to NavigationReady unconditionally (fires before paint; white flash; silently diverges). Showing the window regardless of show:false (breaks modals/hidden export windows: drawio export3 window and progress bar rely on hidden creation). Ignoring ready-to-show (Zettlr never calls show()).

decisions.question: How should BaseWindow/BrowserWindow inheritance, View/WebContentsView and the deprecated BrowserView be implemented without a parallel window model?
decisions.proposed_answer: [inference] Implement the 126 shared methods once on a BaseWindow facade over a single generated `window.*` kipc channel (KEL-98 echo-codegen owner, no new IDL); BrowserWindow = BaseWindow + exactly one host-created content WebContentsView whose `webContents` is the F03 handle, so `win.webContents`, loadURL/loadFile, ready-to-show, page-title-updated compose instead of duplicating. View tree methods (addChildView/removeChildView/setBounds/children) and multiple WebContentsViews per window are Tier 3 and stay ✘ until keld-wv ships multi-view composition (`set_bounds` + Anchor + HostHooks in the arch 05 sketch; v0 is explicitly one webview per window). BrowserView (deprecated upstream) is a thin adapter over WebContentsView, never a third model. Ownership divergence to encode: Electron destroys a BrowserWindow's webContents/renderer with the window but does NOT destroy a WebContentsView's webContents when a BaseWindow closes; Keld's host always owns both and should destroy view-before-window (view_drop_order) — expose that as ▲ for BaseWindow+WebContentsView users.
evidence: base-window.md intro: 'BaseWindow provides a flexible way to compose multiple web views in a single window. For windows with only a single, full-size web view, the BrowserWindow class may be a simpler option' (R5)

decisions.question: Which window chrome options (frame, titleBarStyle, titleBarOverlay, trafficLightPosition, vibrancy/visualEffectState, backgroundMaterial, transparent, roundedCorners, hasShadow) are Tier 1 and how do they tier per engine?
decisions.proposed_answer: [inference] Tier 1 (needed by Zettlr primary workflow): macOS titleBarStyle hidden/hiddenInset/customButtonsOnHover + trafficLightPosition (NSWindow fullSizeContentView + titlebarAppearsTransparent + titleVisibility hidden; entitlement-clean), Windows/Linux frame:false + titleBarStyle:'hidden' + titleBarOverlay{color,symbolColor,height} (host-drawn caption controls; Electron's Chromium WCO/`navigator.windowControlsOverlay`/CSS env vars have no WebView2/WebKitGTK equivalent -> ▲ documented emulation), `app-region: drag` support per engine (Windows: WebView2 non-client region support [lead]; macOS: host-side mouseDown passthrough; Linux: GTK drag via host), backgroundColor, hasShadow, minimum/maximum sizes. Tier 2 ▲: vibrancy/visualEffectState (NSVisualEffectView behind a non-opaque WKWebView — must avoid private drawsBackground API; arch 04 already marks vibrancy as a ▲ behavior note), backgroundMaterial mica/acrylic (DWM system backdrop, Win11 22H2+), roundedCorners. Tier 3/✘: transparent (Electron itself documents non-resizable, no click-through, DevTools disables it, no mac shadow, no Windows maximize; Linux NVIDIA/Wayland breakage per keld-wv AGENTS), setShape, thickFrame nuances, native macOS tabs.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: Emitted when the renderer has rendered the page the first time while the window is still hidden; implies the hidden renderer paints; never fires with paintWhenInitiallyHidden:false; apps call show() only inside the handler.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: System webviews may not composite while the window is unmapped; NavigationReady (load finished) is not paint; a wrong oracle either never shows the window (Zettlr 14 sites, drawio progress bar) or fires before paint (white flash).
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Fixture creates window with show:false, page draws a colored frame on first rAF and posts a beacon via window.keld; assert ready-to-show order: beacon -> ready-to-show -> show() -> OS-level window visible (screenshot/accessibility census); negative control: paintWhenInitiallyHidden:false must never emit ready-to-show within a bounded wait.

semantic_traps.member: 'close' event (cancelable) vs win.close() vs win.destroy() vs 'closed'
semantic_traps.electron_behavior: 'close' fires before DOM beforeunload/unload; event.preventDefault() cancels; destroy() skips close/beforeunload/unload but guarantees 'closed'; window.onbeforeunload returning anything but undefined cancels close.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: Host-owned window closes immediately today (tao CloseRequested -> LastWindowClosed, no veto); drawio's 'close' handler ALWAYS preventDefaults and later destroy()s after an async renderer round-trip; Zettlr preventDefaults then calls window.close() after a dialog; both would lose unsaved data or close twice.
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Sequence test over a real app-link: native close request -> facade 'close' with preventDefault -> window still enumerable/visible after deadline -> win.close() -> 'close' (no veto) -> 'closed' -> isDestroyed()==true -> LastWindowClosed. Negative control: destroy() path records no 'close' event and no beforeunload execution (page sets a flag in beforeunload).

semantic_traps.member: Destroyed-object fence ('Object has been destroyed'), isDestroyed()
semantic_traps.electron_behavior: After destruction, accessing most properties/methods throws 'Object has been destroyed'; isDestroyed() is the safe probe; 'closed' handler must drop references.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: A facade that silently returns undefined or sends stale ids to the host masks app bugs and can re-target a reused host id (identity reuse); drawio/Zettlr guard with isDestroyed() before destroy()/send.
semantic_traps.test_oracle: After 'closed': getBounds() throws Error whose message equals 'Object has been destroyed'; isDestroyed() returns true without throwing; fromId(oldId) returns null; host receives zero frames for the dead id (kipc transcript).

semantic_traps.member: app 'window-all-closed' vs hidden windows vs app.quit()
semantic_traps.electron_behavior: Emitted when all windows have been closed; default quits unless subscribed; NOT emitted when quit was initiated by app.quit()/Cmd+Q (windows close, then will-quit); hidden windows still count as open.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: LifecycleSession counts opened windows only; hidden-window creation (show:false) must still increment; the quit sweep must suppress LastWindowClosed->window-all-closed; drawio relies on window-all-closed with its own cmdQPressed check; Zettlr calls app.quit() from inside the last window's 'close'.
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Three cells: (a) hidden window alive -> closing the visible one emits no window-all-closed; (b) app.quit() with two windows -> two 'close' events, zero window-all-closed, one will-quit; (c) last user close -> window-all-closed -> (no listener) Quit call observed. Reuse keld-compat lifecycle-corpus denominator shape.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: Child always shows on top of parent; modal requires parent and disables parent; macOS modal = sheet attached to parent, children keep relative position when parent moves; Windows/Linux children do not move; Linux modal type changes to 'dialog' and many DEs cannot hide a modal; by default child windows close when their opener closes (outlivesOpener false).
semantic_traps.keld_risk: Three different native mechanisms (NSWindow sheet/addChildWindow, Win32 owner + EnableWindow(false), GTK transient_for+modal); close ordering must emit child 'closed' before parent 'closed' and decrement counts correctly; Zettlr paste-image/error modals and drawio hidden export child depend on it.
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Parent+modal fixture: parent.focus() while modal open does not steal focus (OS focus census), parent.close() -> child 'closed' precedes parent 'closed', window count reaches zero exactly once; per-OS assertion of sheet vs owned window recorded as platform note, not inferred cross-OS.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: Handler decides allow/deny per window.open/target=_blank; overrideBrowserWindowOptions customizes the child; outlivesOpener default false; createWindow bypasses new BrowserWindow and suppresses did-create-window; Electron v44 docs do not state the no-handler default; security checklist treats new webContents creation as an attack vector; drawio restates webPreferences because 'child windows inherit the opener's webPreferences'.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: Keld must default-deny popups without a handler (invariant 2; WebView2 backend already deny-all) and surface this as explicit ▲ vs Electron; an allowed child must be a host-minted window registered in the facade mirror (A1) with the opener's policy, never a raw engine popup.
semantic_traps.test_oracle: No handler: window.open('about:blank') in page -> no native window created (OS census), diagnostic emitted; handler allow with overrideBrowserWindowOptions -> did-create-window fires with a facade handle whose getParentWindow()==null and which closes with opener unless outlivesOpener:true (negative control).

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: The BaseWindow/BrowserWindow module cannot be used until the app 'ready' event is emitted (throws).
semantic_traps.keld_risk: Keld whenReady is a real host event (KEL-72); a facade that lazily queues window creation before Ready would silently reorder 'browser-window-created'/'ready'; must throw synchronously as Electron does.
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Constructing before the host Ready frame throws synchronously; constructing after resolves; the host receives no window.create frame in the first case (kipc transcript).

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: Destroying a BrowserWindow terminates its renderer; closing a BaseWindow does not destroy a WebContentsView's webContents (developer must close them); a WebContents can be presented in only one WebContentsView.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: Keld's host owns both and drops webview before window; faithfully leaking a detached webContents is impossible on system engines -> document ▲ (webContents destroyed with window) rather than emulate the leak.
semantic_traps.test_oracle: BaseWindow with WebContentsView: after window.close(), view.webContents.isDestroyed() is asserted true in Keld and the scoreboard row carries ▲ citing R5.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: Emitted when the web page becomes unresponsive / responsive again (Chromium renderer hang detector).
semantic_traps.keld_risk: WKWebView exposes content-process termination, not hang detection; WebView2 has ProcessFailed (unresponsive kind) [lead]; WebKitGTK web-process-terminated only; cannot promise identical timing -> ▲ or ✘ per engine.
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Per-engine: inject `while(true){}` in page; record whether/when the host observes an unresponsive signal; publish per-engine cell with measured latency or 'unsupported'; never synthesize the event from a timer in the facade.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: titleBarOverlay requires titleBarStyle != default; vibrancy must pair with visualEffectState on macOS; transparent windows are non-resizable, no click-through, no shadow on mac, DevTools disables transparency, cannot maximize on Windows.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: Zettlr sets backgroundColor only when vibrancy is off (its comment says backgroundColor nullifies vibrancy — corpus inference, not Electron doc); Keld must reproduce option validation errors identically and not silently ignore unsupported chrome on an engine.
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Option-matrix fixture: titleBarOverlay without titleBarStyle -> same error class as Electron (or ▲ recorded); vibrancy+backgroundColor -> screenshot luminance/alpha comparison on macOS vs documented expectation; unsupported combos produce a KELD-COMPAT diagnostic rather than a silent no-op.

semantic_traps.member: BrowserWindow top-level options silently ignored vs webPreferences
semantic_traps.electron_behavior: Fields like webviewTag/webSecurity belong in webPreferences; at top level they are ignored (drawio source comment; Electron docs do not list top-level validation) [inference].
semantic_traps.receipt: corpus drawio electron.js:727-728 comment; no Electron doc receipt
semantic_traps.keld_risk: A strict facade that rejects unknown top-level keys would break migrated apps; a permissive one hides misplacement — choose Electron behavior (ignore) plus a `keld migrate` warning.
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Construct with {webSecurity:false} at top level: window is created, engine web security remains on (probe cross-origin fetch fails), migrate report lists the misplaced key.

semantic_traps.member: getAllWindows() ordering / getFocusedWindow() when none focused
semantic_traps.electron_behavior: getAllWindows returns 'an array of all opened browser windows' (order unspecified); getFocusedWindow returns null when no window focused.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: Apps index [0] (drawio uses its own registry; Zettlr falls back to getAllWindows()[0]); Keld mirror should use creation order and must return null (not undefined) when the host reports no focus; focus state must be host-truth (KEL-64 learning: a key NSWindow is not proof the WKWebView has focus).
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Create A then B: getAllWindows() ids strictly increasing in creation order; OS-level focus change (AppleScript/SetForegroundWindow/xdotool) -> getFocusedWindow() updates before 'focus' listener runs; with app deactivated -> null.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: Disable the corresponding native control; 'not implemented on Linux' for movable/minimizable/maximizable/closable.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: drawio progress-bar uses closable:false + resizable:false then .close() programmatically; Keld must still honor programmatic close while disabling the button; Linux ▲ matches Electron's own gap.
semantic_traps.test_oracle: closable:false window: native close button disabled (accessibility census), win.close() still emits close/closed; Linux cell records ▲ identical to Electron.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: 'app-command' (Windows/Linux) delivers browser-backward/forward; 'swipe' (macOS) delivers left/right.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: Needs WM_APPCOMMAND hook and NSEvent swipe tracking in host backends; cheap but easy to forget; Zettlr primary workflow uses both for document history.
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Synthesize WM_APPCOMMAND / NSEvent swipe in a native fixture; assert exactly one facade event with the Electron string value.

receipts.claim: R1: ready-to-show 'will be emitted when the renderer process has rendered the page for the first time if the window has not been shown yet'; 'This event will never fire if you use paintWhenInitiallyHidden: false'; graceful-show alternatives (backgroundColor).

R2: 'close' is 'emitted before the beforeunload and unload event of the DOM. Calling event.preventDefault() will cancel the close'; 'closed': remove the reference; 'unresponsive'/'responsive' definitions; instance event order list (page-title-updated ... system-context-menu).
R3: destroy(): 'the unload and beforeunload event won't be emitted for the web page, and close event will also not be emitted for this window, but it guarantees the closed event will be emitted'.

R4: 'Reading this property throws Object has been destroyed once the window has been destroyed'; isDestroyed note 'Once a window is destroyed, accessing most of its other properties and methods throws Object has been destroyed'.

R5: BaseWindow intro (compose multiple web views); 'This module cannot be used until the ready event of the app module is emitted'; parent/child: child always on top; modal needs parent+modal; macOS modal = sheet, children keep relative position; Windows/Linux children do not move; Linux modal type -> dialog and DEs cannot hide modals; resource management: closing a BaseWindow does not destroy a WebContentsView's webContents; events list incl. persisted-state-restored; setParentWindow(null) makes top-level.

R6: static getAllWindows() 'An array of all opened browser windows'; getFocusedWindow() 'otherwise returns null'; fromId(id) 'BaseWindow | null'; fromWebContents 'null if the contents are not owned by a window'; win.id 'unique among all BaseWindow instances'; getNativeWindowHandle returns Buffer (HWND / NSView* / Window); setContentProtection NSWindowSharingNone / SetWindowDisplayAffinity; setIgnoreMouseEvents forward option macOS/Windows; setAlwaysOnTop levels.

R6b: BaseWindowConstructorOptions defaults: width 800/height 600, show true, frame true, parent null, modal false, title 'Electron', backgroundColor #FFF, titleBarStyle default (values default/hidden/hiddenInset/customButtonsOnHover), titleBarOverlay false, vibrancy values, backgroundMaterial auto/none/mica/acrylic/tabbed, roundedCorners Windows 11 22000+, movable/minimizable/maximizable/closable 'not implemented on Linux', alwaysOnTop 'Not supported on Wayland (Linux)', focusable:false implies skipTaskbar on Windows, transparent 'On Windows, does not work unless the window is frameless', name + windowStatePersistence (state persistence across restarts).
R7: BrowserWindowConstructorOptions extends BaseWindowConstructorOptions; paintWhenInitiallyHidden default true: 'Setting this to false will cause the ready-to-show event to not fire'.

R8: WebPreferences defaults: devTools true; nodeIntegration false; nodeIntegrationInWorker false; nodeIntegrationInSubFrames false (experimental); preload absolute path, 'will always have access to node APIs'; sandbox true since Electron 20, 'automatically disabled when nodeIntegration is set to true'; contextIsolation true; webviewTag false (its preload has node integration); webSecurity true (false also sets allowRunningInsecureContent); offscreen false; additionalArguments appended to renderer process.argv; partition 'persist:' prefix; 46 fields total.

R9: Security checklist 20 items; Node integration off default since 5.0.0; context isolation default since 12.0.0; process sandboxing default since 20.0.0; item 14 'the creation of new webContents is a common attack vector'; item 12 will-attach-webview; item 13 will-navigate.

R10: 'Each instance of the BrowserWindow class creates an application window that loads a web page in a separate renderer process'; 'When a BrowserWindow instance is destroyed, its corresponding renderer process gets terminated as well'; preload scripts run before web content with Node access; contextIsolation default + contextBridge.

R11: 'The BrowserView class is deprecated, and replaced by the new WebContentsView class'; main process only; cannot be used before app ready; setAutoResize/setBounds/getBounds/setBackgroundColor/webContents.

R12: WebContentsView extends View; options webPreferences | webContents (adopt existing); 'A WebContents may only be presented in one WebContentsView at a time'; cannot be used before ready. View: addChildView(view[,index]) reorders existing child to top; removeChildView no-op if not child; setBounds with animation options; getBounds relative to parent; setBorderRadius cutouts still capture clicks; bounds-changed event; children readonly.

R13: titleBarStyle hidden removes title bar keeping traffic lights (mac) / requires titleBarOverlay on Windows+Linux to restore controls; hiddenInset shifts traffic-light inset; customButtonsOnHover hides lights until hover; titleBarOverlay {color, symbolColor (Windows only), height}; 'titleBarOverlay requires the titleBarStyle param ... to have a value other than default'.

R14: frame:false removes all OS chrome; Linux/Wayland frameless has GTK shadow/resize bounds unless hasShadow:false; transparent windows: no click-through on transparent areas, not resizable (resizable:true may malfunction), CSS blur only affects web contents, transparency disabled when DevTools open, Windows cannot maximize via system menu/double-click, macOS no native shadow.

R15: app-region: drag / no-drag; draggable areas ignore all pointer events; text-selection conflict (user-select:none); right-click may open system menu on some platforms; setIgnoreMouseEvents(ignore[, {forward}]) forward on macOS/Windows.

Not emitted if the creation of the window is canceled from webContents.setWindowOpenHandler'; will-attach-webview preventDefault destroys guest; contents.close([opts]) waitForBeforeUnload; 'destroyed' event; isDestroyed; render-process-gone; the v44.4.5 doc does NOT state the no-handler default.

platform_notes.note: [fact] keld-wv already denies all NewWindowRequested before first navigation and requires that proof (KEL-168). [fact] Electron: transparent requires frameless; cannot maximize transparent windows; focusable:false implies skipTaskbar; backgroundMaterial needs Win11 22H2+; roundedCorners needs 22000+. [inference] titleBarOverlay must be host-drawn caption buttons (WebView2 has no Chromium WCO / navigator.windowControlsOverlay); app-region: drag needs WebView2 non-client-region support [lead: CoreWebView2Settings IsNonClientRegionSupportEnabled — version/behaviour unverified]. [fact] one CoreWebView2Controller per HWND region; multi-view needs multiple controllers [unknown cost]. session-end = WM_QUERYENDSESSION/WM_ENDSESSION. JumpList/Thumbar/overlay icon = ICustomDestinationList/ITaskbarList3 (windows-rs). [fact] KEL-135 requires two simultaneous windows and concurrent instances to follow the explicit WebView2 UDF ownership policy — multi-window acceptance is already a KEL-135 criterion.

platform_notes.platform: Linux (GTK3 + WebKitGTK 4.1 interim via wry; destination gtk4/webkitgtk-6.0; Wayland-first CI)
platform_notes.note: [fact Electron doc] movable/minimizable/maximizable/closable not implemented on Linux; alwaysOnTop unsupported on Wayland; modal windows become type 'dialog'; many DEs cannot hide a modal; frameless/Wayland has GTK shadow+resize border unless hasShadow:false. [inference] setPosition/getPosition/center are not honorable under Wayland (no client positioning) -> ▲; frame:false -> CSD via GtkHeaderBar or host-drawn controls; titleBarOverlay emulation host-drawn. [fact keld-wv AGENTS] NVIDIA proprietary + Wayland on WebKitGTK <=2.54 needs dmabuf safe-mode; transparency breaks (tauri#9394/#14924). [fact learnings] build_gtk must use tao default_vbox(), not gtk_window(). 'unresponsive' -> web-process-terminated only. Portal-first (ashpd) for dialogs/notifications; no JumpList/Thumbar/TouchBar equivalents (✘ by platform, same as Electron).

[fact] WKWebView lacks Service Worker on custom schemes (WebKit 206741) and WebView2 virtual-host SW limits (briefing) — affects window-level `partition`/resource expectations handled by KEL-79, not F02. [fact] No offscreen rendering on any system engine -> webPreferences.offscreen ✘; drawio PNG export (hidden transparent child + capturePage at deviceScaleFactor 2) is a primary_workflow risk needing an F03/F02 joint prototype.

never_list.surface: webPreferences.nodeIntegration / nodeIntegrationInWorker / nodeIntegrationInSubFrames = true
never_list.rationale: Briefing invariant 10 and research 13/214: renderer Node access is incompatible with host-enforced default-deny; Electron itself documents it disables the sandbox (R8).

never_list.surface: webPreferences.contextIsolation:false
never_list.rationale: Breaks the isolated-world bridge contract (KEL-142 AC: page cannot access the preload realm); Electron default true since 12 (R9).

never_list.surface: webPreferences.webSecurity:false, allowRunningInsecureContent:true
never_list.rationale: Disables same-origin policy inside a host-mediated resource model (KEL-79); security checklist items 6/8 (R9).

never_list.surface: webPreferences.experimentalFeatures, enableBlinkFeatures, disableBlinkFeatures, plugins, v8CacheOptions, enableWebSQL
never_list.rationale: Arbitrary Chromium/V8 feature flags; nonexistent on WebKit engines; briefing never-list 'arbitrary Chromium/V8 flags'.

never_list.surface: webPreferences.offscreen (OSR), setShape(initially)
never_list.rationale: No offscreen rendering on system webviews; a fake would be a silent downgrade (KEL-127 no silent downgrade). Tracked ✘, not quirk-flagged.

never_list.surface: getNativeWindowHandle, hookWindowMessage family, raw NSView/HWND/X11 Window exposure
never_list.rationale: Arch 01: handles never cross kipc; raw window message hooks give a Bun role in-process UI authority.

never_list.surface: JumpListItem/Task `program` naming any executable other than the app's own signed identity
never_list.rationale: Jump List tasks launch programs with args from the shell; only the ExpectedAppIdentity executable is permitted (raw process launch from strict roles is on the briefing never-list).

never_list.surface: A missing setWindowOpenHandler becoming 'allow'
never_list.rationale: Briefing invariant 2: a missing Electron permission handler must not become allow; Keld default-denies popups and records the divergence.

never_list.surface: webPreferences.session/partition pointing at app-chosen on-disk paths or another app's profile
never_list.rationale: KEL-135: engine creation requires host-validated profile identity; page/Bun input cannot choose another store.

never_list.surface: BrowserView as a third window model
never_list.rationale: Deprecated upstream (R11); Keld maps it onto WebContentsView to keep one view model (one rule, one owner).
