verdicts.lens: Keld invariants, ownership and reuse (four uniques; default-deny never defaulted to allow; no Electron-isms in keld-core/keld-ipc; no parallel owner; reuse of KEL-75/76/77/78/79/80/53/74/102/135/139-144; measured performance; spec+Linear gate; #312/#313/#319/#322/#323/#325 and KEL-127). Verified against origin/main d150a14, wry 0.56.1 and tao 0.37.0 registry sources.

verdicts.reason: Host minting of window identity is required by existing owners, not invented here: KEL-75 spec stores an opaque WindowGeneration per window incarnation with 'the app-session registry ... owns the monotonic generation counter' and 'Window affinity is not a reusable native window number'; arch 01 line 56 forbids reusable window handles; kel139 ownership table row 'Native window | KEL-96 / core + wv | Host remains sole owner'. A Bun-local mirror fed by app-link EVENT frames is consistent with the existing LifecycleLink demux and with arch 02 line 336-337 which tolerates blocking CALL only for sendSync, so the rejected per-call sync RPC is correctly rejected. Generic naming in keld-core keeps Electron-isms out of core.
verdicts.evidence: docs/specs/kel75-principalized-bun-child-roles.md:131-137; docs/architecture/01-overview.md:56,106,141; docs/specs/kel139-macos-product-spine.md:246; docs/architecture/02-ipc.md:336-337; crates/keld-core/src/lifecycle.rs:132-150 (count only, no id). Caveat: WindowGeneration exists only in the spec (grep of crates/ and packages/ returns nothing) and no window-registry spec exists under docs/specs/, so the whole atom is spec-gated, as the object already states.
verdicts.correction: Record explicitly that the host already creates the primary window after the authenticated HELLO and before any Bun code runs (arch 01 line 215: 'the window is created only after the authenticated HELLO'); the facade must either adopt that host window as the first new BrowserWindow() or the boot sequence must change. This is a KEL-96/KEL-139 boundary decision, not an 'unknown' footnote.

verdicts.reason: Today's uncancelable close is a Keld handling choice, not a platform limit: tao 0.37.0 `WindowEvent::CloseRequested` is only a notification ('The window has been requested to close') and the three backends choose to drop the View immediately (wkwebview/mod.rs:385-401, webkitgtk/mod.rs:467-474, webview2/mod.rs:2155-2173 close_requested_view). A host-held veto with a Bun round-trip is therefore implementable in the existing AppWindowEvent/AppWindowCommand seam without a parallel owner. The view-before-window drop order is a real crate invariant (view_drop_order.rs). The quit ordering the object attributes to KEL-143 appears in repo text as 'Quit reply then quiesce, revoke, link close, terminate/reap, event-loop exit'.
verdicts.evidence: ~/.cargo/registry/src/*/tao-0.37.0/src/event.rs:282-283; crates/keld-wv/src/wkwebview/mod.rs:385-401; crates/keld-wv/src/webkitgtk/mod.rs:467-474; crates/keld-wv/src/webview2/mod.rs:2155-2180; crates/keld-wv/src/view_drop_order.rs:1-10; docs/research/library/execution-governance/222-kel96-ready-frontier.md:147,375; crates/keld-core/src/app_session.rs:3893-3901.
verdicts.correction: The dead-Bun deadline rule collides with KEL-143's goal (same native window survives Bun generation loss): if the host honors a user close while no Bun generation is live, the window count can reach zero and LastWindowClosed has no listener generation. State the rule as its own atom: a close during generation loss either (a) is honored and the next generation receives a synthetic LastWindowClosed on admission, or (b) is parked until the admission deadline. Pick one in the registry spec; do not leave it as 'medium confidence'. Engine beforeunload support remains [unknown] on all three engines; no repo evidence exists.

verdicts.reason: The reuse claim is wrong on mechanism. The KEL-64 'double-rAF beacon' is an external benchmark instrument on a pre-spawn monotonic clock emitted by a fixture page to an external harness, not a host-injected script: keld-wv AGENTS.md calls it the 'KEL-64 external double-rAF image beacon', startup.rs:231 says 'KEL-64 first paint is external beacon, not this trace', and learnings 2026-08-17 scores it 'on untraced arms only'. There is no 'host pre-load script' seam shared across engines: the only shipped injection is the macOS-only KEL-142 WKContentWorld bridge (macos_bridge.rs:525-556), the WebView2 backend deliberately refuses AddScriptToExecuteOnDocumentCreated because wry's injection cost a measured 96-109 ms (webview2/mod.rs:11-16), and keld-wv has no WebKitGTK UserContentManager injection at all. Also no backend creates a hidden window today: all three use WindowBuilder::new().with_inner_size(...) with no with_visible(false) (wkwebview/mod.rs:460, webkitgtk/mod.rs:511, webview2/mod.rs:2734), so (a) is new work, not reuse.
verdicts.evidence: crates/keld-wv/AGENTS.md:32-37; crates/keld-wv/src/startup.rs:4,231; docs/agents/learnings.md:79; crates/keld-wv/src/wkwebview/macos_bridge.rs:525-556; crates/keld-wv/src/webview2/mod.rs:8-20; grep for WKUserScript/AddScriptToExecuteOnDocumentCreated/user_content_manager in crates/keld-wv/src returns only the macOS bridge and the WebView2 refusal comment; grep with_visible returns nothing.
verdicts.correction: Rewrite (b): the reusable asset is the double-rAF technique, not the KEL-64 instrument. The oracle needs a host-owned isolated-world script per engine: macOS extends the KEL-142 isolated bridge; Windows requires a measured decision because the backend already rejected document-created injection on startup-cost grounds (arch 01 §5 budget, >5% regression waiver rule); Linux requires a new WebKitGTK UserContentManager seam. Keep the prototype gate, but prototype P1 must also measure the injection cost against the 300 ms first-paint budget and define what 'first paint' means for a show:false window (the budget clock currently targets the host-created visible window).

verdicts.reason: The 'LEGACY-PROFILE ONLY: sandbox:false' classification contradicts the approved KEL-78 spec, which states 'Electron `sandbox` / `appSandbox` is not this key and MUST NOT be read as `legacy` or `strict`' and treats a leftover Electron sandbox option under a Strict request as UnexpectedGrant (do not start); research 213 carries the matching fail-closed test row 'legacy_declaration_comes_only_from_the_keld_profile_key_never_electron_sandbox_options'. The legacy profile is a Bun-role OS-containment state (keld-guard admit.rs ProfileState::{Unverified,Legacy,Strict}), not a renderer de-sandbox, and a system webview's renderer cannot be de-sandboxed by Keld at all. Separately, Electron preload 'will always have access to node APIs' (R8) while Keld's preload is a webview user script (arch 04 §3 layer 3), so filing preload under POLICY without a ▲ for Node access hides the largest semantic divergence in the field. The NEVER list, devTools→web.devtools, and the default-deny stance are consistent with arch 03 §3 and research 13.
verdicts.evidence: docs/specs/kel78-strict-profile-sandbox.md:560-570; docs/research/library/quality-evidence/213-test-ladder-every-surface.md:774; crates/keld-guard/src/admit.rs:87-92,553-558; docs/architecture/04-electron-compat.md:74-77; docs/architecture/03-security.md:242-245; docs/research/library/compatibility-competitors/13-electron-api-usage.md:42-49; docs/specs/kel135-persistent-profile-identity.md has no Electron session/partition mapping text (grep 'partition' empty).
verdicts.correction: Reclassify sandbox:false as ▲ ignored-with-diagnostic: the renderer stays engine-sandboxed, Keld emits a KELD-COMPAT diagnostic and a `keld migrate` report line, and it never selects or gates a Keld profile. Any preload `require`/Node usage is ✘ (or routed through the F03/F04 contextBridge/ipcRenderer facade), and the preload row must carry ▲ 'no Node access'. Mark session/partition→KEL-135 as a required KEL-135 spec extension (app-named store selection is currently outside its host-validated identity model), not as an existing mapping.

verdicts.reason: One BaseWindow implementation with BrowserWindow = BaseWindow + exactly one host-created content view matches the live substrate (engine.rs:77 'v0 is one window-filling webview per window'; no HostHooks/Anchor per engine.rs:16 and arch 05 lines 41-42), matches arch 04 §4 placing BrowserView mapping in Tier 3, and the corpus has zero BaseWindow/View/WebContentsView/BrowserView call sites, so DRY and demand agree. Keeping view composition ✘ until keld-wv ships set_bounds+Anchor avoids a parallel window model.
verdicts.evidence: crates/keld-wv/src/engine.rs:16,77-88,138-176; docs/architecture/05-webview-and-native.md:14,24-29,41-42,243; docs/architecture/04-electron-compat.md:135-142; crates/keld-wv/src/view_drop_order.rs.
verdicts.correction: The 'KEL-98 echo-codegen owner, no new IDL' clause is not supported by the KEL-98 spec as approved: its non-goals say it is 'a bootstrap for the existing echo vertical slice, not Keld's general contract authoring model', with 'no general Rust parser, derive/proc macro, IDL, or arbitrary schema generator', and the destination @keld/schema / keld gen is 'separately specified as TypeScript-native' (arch 01:128, arch 02 §4). Generating a window.* channel therefore needs a KEL-98 scope amendment or the @keld/schema spec, and the object must name that as a blocker. Also soften the trap claim that leaking a detached webContents is 'impossible' on system engines: WKWebView is an NSView that can be detached and re-added and WebView2 exposes put_ParentWindow; destroying view-with-window is a Keld ownership choice (▲), not an engine impossibility.

verdicts.reason: The macOS titleBarStyle/trafficLightPosition mapping to public NSWindow API, vibrancy as Tier 2 ▲ (arch 04 line 24 already lists 'BrowserWindow.vibrancy (macOS-only effect)'), the entitlement-clean transparency rule (research 06 line 35), and transparent as Tier 3 are consistent with repo sources. But the Tier 1 assertion for Windows/Linux frame:false + titleBarOverlay + `app-region: drag` has no receipt on any engine: `app-region` is a Chromium CSS property with no WebKit implementation, so WKWebView and WebKitGTK cannot report draggable regions to the host without a page-side hook that Electron apps do not ship; WebView2's non-client-region support is cited only as [lead]; and host-drawn caption controls over a child-HWND WebView2 or a GTK webview have no design or measurement in the repo. Zettlr's primary workflow depends on exactly this combination, so Tier 1 cannot be asserted until prototypes P3/P4 produce evidence.

verdicts.correction: Cheapest settling evidence: (1) fetch and pin the WebView2 ICoreWebView2Settings9.IsNonClientRegionSupportEnabled reference page (SDK/runtime minimums, frameless-HWND behavior, which CSS it honors) and record it as a receipt; (2) a WebKit source/bugzilla receipt that `app-region`/`-webkit-app-region` is unimplemented, which downgrades macOS/Linux drag to host-side emulation requiring an injected hit-test script (same seam problem as A3); (3) prototype P3 must include a Windows cell where host-drawn caption buttons coexist with a WebView2 child HWND and a Linux cell using gtk_window_begin_move_drag. Until then tier titleBarOverlay/app-region as PARTIAL with Zettlr's primary workflow flagged at risk, not Tier 1.

extra_findings.finding: Host-pre-created primary window vs new BrowserWindow(): the host creates the one primary window after the authenticated HELLO and before Bun user code runs (KEL-96/KEL-139 boot), while every corpus app calls new BrowserWindow() inside whenReady. Without an adoption rule the facade either creates a second window or must defer host window creation, which changes the KEL-64/arch 01 §5 first-paint clock (measured spawn→PAINT-OPPORTUNITY on that host window) and the KEL-139 'same native window identity' invariant. This is a boundary decision owned by KEL-96/KEL-139/KEL-143, not an A1 footnote.
extra_findings.evidence: docs/architecture/01-overview.md:215 ('the window is created only after the authenticated HELLO'); docs/specs/kel139-macos-product-spine.md:170,246; crates/keld-core/src/hello.rs:136-150 (config read for title/renderer/entry only).

extra_findings.finding: Identity conflation in reuse_points: keld-guard Principal::Webview.generation is 'Bumped on navigation so stale grants cannot carry over', whereas KEL-75's WindowGeneration is minted per window incarnation and the spec says 'Navigation generation and document nonce rotate independently inside that window and are not part of the role principal'. Treating Principal::Webview{id,generation} as 'the per-window principal' would tombstone window-bound roles on every navigation or let a navigation-stale grant survive a window swap. The registry spec must mint and carry two distinct generations.
extra_findings.evidence: crates/keld-guard/src/lib.rs:105-116; docs/specs/kel75-principalized-bun-child-roles.md:131-134.

extra_findings.finding: Popup default-deny on macOS/Linux is an engine/wry default, not a Keld-evaluated decision: keld-wv sets no wry new_window_req_handler, and wry 0.56.1's WKUIDelegate returns None (no popup) when the handler is absent while WebKitGTK's `create` signal is simply not connected. keld-wv AGENTS.md already warns for Linux that this fallback 'is not proof Keld evaluated the right principal/manifest'. The object's reuse point names only the WebView2 deny-all handler; setWindowOpenHandler routing needs host-owned handlers on all three engines or the macOS/Linux cells cannot claim default-deny provenance.

extra_findings.finding: Windows injection seam contradicts a measured decision: the WebView2 backend exists as direct COM precisely because wry's AddScriptToExecuteOnDocumentCreated bridge injection cost 96-109 ms during renderer boot. Any ready-to-show beacon, preload, or contextBridge user-script on Windows reintroduces that path and must be re-measured against the 300 ms first-paint budget with a waiver if >5% regression; 'same injection seam as KEL-142' is macOS-only today.
extra_findings.evidence: crates/keld-wv/src/webview2/mod.rs:11-16; docs/architecture/01-overview.md:185; AGENTS.md verification floor (>5% regression needs waiver).

extra_findings.finding: KEL-98 echo-codegen cannot own window.* generation under its approved scope ('not Keld's general contract authoring model'; 'no general Rust parser, derive/proc macro, IDL'); the destination @keld/schema / keld gen is TypeScript-native and separately specified. The object's A5 and reuse_points rely on KEL-127's 'existing echo-codegen owner' direction, which now conflicts with the KEL-98 spec text; one of them must be amended before a window channel can be generated.

extra_findings.finding: Guard gating of window commands: manifest `windows.<name>` grants are parsed-and-ignored today (guard lib.rs:565 'Unknown top-level keys ($schema, windows, audit) are ignored') and v0 evaluate denies every non-AppProcess principal (KELD-GUARD006). AppProcess-owned window ops can ship, but any window operation originating from a webview principal (window.open allow, child windows, webContents-initiated close) is hard-denied until KEL-102 window grants land; the security_mapping should state that dependency per row rather than only in A1/A4 blocked_by.

extra_findings.finding: Hidden-window creation changes what the first-paint budget measures: arch 01 §5 scores spawn→PAINT-OPPORTUNITY beacon on the host window; a show:false window that paints while unmapped produces a beacon with no visible paint, so corpus-app first-paint rows need a separate document class (visible-first-paint vs ready-to-show) or the budget scoreboard will pool incomparable samples.

verdicts.lens: Electron v44.4.5 semantics accuracy + corpus demand + sequencing/sizing (F02 windowing). Sources read: pinned docs saved under <scratchpad>/notes/f02-refute/ (browser-window, base-window, base-window-options, browser-window-options, web-preferences, web-contents, view, web-contents-view, browser-view, app, window-open-handler-response, custom-title-bar, custom-window-styles) plus Electron v44.4.5 source (lib/browser/api/web-contents.ts, browser-window.ts, base-window.ts, shell/common/gin_helper/trackable_object.h, shell/common/key_weak_map.h, shell/browser/api/electron_api_base_window.cc, shell/browser/native_window.cc, shell/browser/ui/cocoa/electron_ns_window_delegate.mm); corpus clones drawio-desktop/zettlr/electron-quick-start and *.usage.json; Keld repo at d150a14.

verdicts.reason: Host-minted opaque identity + synchronous facade-local mirror is consistent with every cited Electron contract and Keld invariant. Electron's getAllWindows/getFocusedWindow/fromId are synchronous (base-window.md:393-405; browser-window.ts:109-131 filters BaseWindow.getAllWindows()). Corpus sites verified: drawio electron.js:484 `getFocusedWindow() || getAllWindows()[0]`, Zettlr windows/index.ts:646-680 showAnyWindow/getFirstMainWindow, quick-start main.js activate handler. KEL-75 spec lines 131-134 ('Window affinity is not a reusable native window number'), arch 01 line 56, lifecycle.rs:132-150 counters all match. Blockers are real: product-status.tsv rows crate.keld-core/crate.keld-host say the destination registry is absent; no window-registry Linear id exists.
verdicts.evidence: trackable_object.h:39 `weak_map_id_ = ++next_id_` (ids are a single counter shared by ALL TrackableObject types, so Electron window ids are not dense per window — the facade's own monotonic counter is a legitimate implementation of 'unique among all BaseWindow instances'). key_weak_map.h:73 `std::unordered_map<K, Mapped> map_` + Values() iterates it: Electron's getAllWindows() order is UNSPECIFIED, not creation order. browser-window.ts:120-125: BrowserWindow.getFocusedWindow() also returns a window whose DevTools is focused (`webContents.isDevToolsFocused()`).
verdicts.correction: Two labelling fixes, not a redesign: (1) the semantic-trap oracle 'getAllWindows() ids strictly increasing in creation order' is a Keld-stronger guarantee than Electron (unordered_map order) — record it as ▲-stronger, never as parity; (2) getFocusedWindow must also return the window whose DevTools pane is focused, so the mirror needs devtools-focus truth from the host or a documented ▲. Also note fromWebContents is blocked by the F03 webContents handle (only A5 lists F03).

verdicts.reason: The two-phase protocol shape (host CloseRequested -> facade 'close' with preventDefault -> CloseAllow -> unload -> destroy webview before window -> Closed; destroy() skips close but guarantees closed; destroyed-object fence) is confirmed by docs and source. But the deadline clause is justified by a false Electron fact: 'Electron's observable user can always close wins over a dead veto'. In Electron the 'close' emit is synchronous on the browser-process UI thread (electron_ns_window_delegate.mm:411-414 `windowShouldClose` calls NotifyWindowCloseButtonClicked and returns NO; native_window.cc:548-555 observers_.Notify(WillCloseWindow,&prevent_default); electron_api_base_window.cc:165-169 `if (Emit("close")) *prevent_default = true`). A blocked or slow main process therefore keeps the window OPEN in Electron; the user cannot 'always close'. As written, a slow-but-alive Bun (drawio's close handler ALWAYS preventDefaults then awaits an async renderer round-trip, electron.js:947-966, with destroy() only after 'saveAndClose-result'/'draftRemoved', :893-945) would have the host close the window on deadline and lose unsaved work — the exact failure the protocol exists to prevent.
verdicts.evidence: browser-window.md:186-194 ('close' before beforeunload/unload; preventDefault cancels); base-window.md:578-588 (destroy skips close/unload, guarantees closed; close() same as clicking the button); base-window.md:602-607 isDestroyed note; drawio electron.js:947-975 and 893-945; Zettlr windows/index.ts:357-410 (preventDefault then askUserToCloseWindow().then(window.close()); app.quit() from inside 'close' on win/linux last window); keld-wv wkwebview/mod.rs:387-402 and webkitgtk/mod.rs:469-474 and webview2/mod.rs:2594-2605 (CloseRequested removes views, emits LastWindowClosed, no veto); view_drop_order.rs:3-5.
verdicts.correction: Keep the protocol; replace the deadline clause with: the host waits for CloseAllow/CloseVeto indefinitely while the owning Bun generation is alive (matches Electron's observable: a non-answering main keeps the window open), and releases the pending close ONLY on supervisor-confirmed generation death (KEL-143 seam), recorded as a Keld ▲ policy, not Electron parity. Add: a CloseRequested that arrives while a previous one is still unanswered for the same WindowGeneration must coalesce (Electron re-emits 'close' per attempt; drawio keys each attempt with a fresh uniqueIsModifiedId, so re-emission per native attempt is the parity behaviour — but CloseAllow must carry the seq it answers). Keep DOM-beforeunload engine support as the stated unknown.

verdicts.reason: The Electron side is accurately quoted (browser-window.md:35-55 and 267-273: ready-to-show when the renderer has rendered the page the first time while hidden; implies hidden paint; never fires with paintWhenInitiallyHidden:false; browser-window-options.md confirms default true and the visibilityState interaction). Corpus demand is confirmed: Zettlr 14 ready-to-show sites across 14 create-*/splash/onboarding files with 15 `show: false`; drawio progress-bar.js:44-59 same pattern; drawio electron.js:717 backgroundColor to avoid white flash. The Keld-side premise is also confirmed (NavigationReady is emitted from wry PageLoadEvent::Finished only: wkwebview/mod.rs:719-723, webkitgtk/mod.rs:528-532, webview2/mod.rs:1985; learnings.md:79 and keld-wv AGENTS.md:32-35). What is missing is the decisive fact: whether WKWebView, WebView2 and WebKitGTK run requestAnimationFrame / composite while their window is unmapped. No receipt exists either way, and the fallback ('navigation finished + DOMContentLoaded' with ▲) changes the observable contract for all 14 Zettlr sites.
verdicts.evidence: Missing evidence: (a) WKWebView not-in-window / ordered-out visibility semantics (WebKit treats a view with no window as not visible and suspends the display-refresh-driven rAF — this is a [lead], not a receipt); (b) WebView2 `ICoreWebView2Controller.IsVisible` docs state the WebView stops rendering when not visible — need the exact Microsoft Learn receipt and whether a hidden parent HWND with IsVisible=true still paints; (c) WebKitGTK unrealized GtkWindow behaviour. Also a labelling slip: the KEL-64 double-rAF beacon is an EXTERNAL bench image beacon on a pre-spawn clock (keld-wv AGENTS.md:32-35), not a host-injected pre-load script; the host-injection seam is KEL-142's WKContentWorld bridge (macOS only today).
verdicts.correction: Cheapest settling experiment (prototype P1, one afternoon per OS): in the existing keld-wv hello, create the native window without ordering it front (macOS: skip orderFront/makeKeyAndOrderFront; Windows: omit SW_SHOW; Linux: gtk_widget_realize without show), load a page whose first rAF callback calls window.keld.invoke('beacon'); record whether the beacon arrives within 2s, then show the window and screenshot for the white-flash negative control. Publish the three cells before committing to either oracle. Until then A3 stays prototype-gated and the ▲ fallback text must say 'fires at load-finished, before first composited frame'.

verdicts.reason: The triage is incomplete and one bucket contradicts the corpus it cites. (1) `disableBlinkFeatures` is placed in NEVER ('fail loudly, scoreboard ✘, no quirks flag'), yet drawio's PRIMARY main window sets `disableBlinkFeatures: 'Auxclick'` (electron.js:730, and again in the export window :3089). Fail-loud would make drawio's main window constructor throw — contradicting the decision's own claim that 'corpus apps need no never-listed field for primary workflow except drawio's offscreen export path'. (2) Only 44 of the 46 WebPreferences fields are triaged: `zoomMode` (web-preferences.md:42-44, new in 44) and `safeDialogsMessage` (:130) are missing. (3) `sandbox:false` as LEGACY-PROFILE ONLY ('refused in strict/release') would refuse Zettlr's startup splash screen (splash-screen.ts:65) and onboarding window (onboarding-window.ts:72) — both on the startup path — although on Keld the flag grants nothing (no Node exists in any renderer under any flag); the thing to refuse is a preload that imports Node, which `keld migrate` detects, not the flag. (4) `devTools` default is TRUE in Electron (web-preferences.md:3); Keld's 'off in release unless web.devtools' is a ▲ divergence the decision presents as policy without marking it.
verdicts.evidence: web-preferences.md field list (46 bullets: lines 3-166) vs the decision's 14 NEVER + 1 LEGACY + 8 POLICY + 21 ENGINE = 44. drawio electron.js:722-732 main-window webPreferences {spellcheck, contextIsolation:true, nodeIntegration:false, webviewTag:false, webSecurity:true, disableBlinkFeatures:'Auxclick', additionalArguments}; :3081-3098 export window {preload, backgroundThrottling:false, disableBlinkFeatures, offscreen:{deviceScaleFactor:2}, show:false, frame:false, enableLargerThanScreen, transparent (png+no bg), parent}. Zettlr splash-screen.ts:55-80 and onboarding-window.ts:72 sandbox:false with contextIsolation:true + preload. Electron defaults confirmed: nodeIntegration false, contextIsolation true, sandbox true since 20 and auto-disabled by nodeIntegration, webviewTag false (web-preferences.md:4-28,104-124).
verdicts.correction: Split NEVER into two buckets with different failure modes: (a) privilege-escalating -> fail loudly, no quirks flag: nodeIntegration:true, nodeIntegrationInWorker, nodeIntegrationInSubFrames, contextIsolation:false, webSecurity:false, allowRunningInsecureContent:true; (b) Chromium/V8-engine-only knobs -> accept, ignore, emit one KELD-COMPAT diagnostic, scoreboard ▲ (not ✘-fatal): enableBlinkFeatures, disableBlinkFeatures, experimentalFeatures, v8CacheOptions, enableWebSQL, enableDeprecatedPaste, plugins; `offscreen` -> ✘ with diagnostic (capturePage on a hidden non-OSR window is the stated unknown for drawio export). Reclassify sandbox:false as 'ignored + diagnostic' because the flag is a no-op on Keld; gate the legacy profile on detected Node use in the preload instead. Add zoomMode (engine toggle) and safeDialogsMessage (host dialog policy). Mark devTools default-true vs release-off as ▲.

verdicts.reason: Every Electron claim checks out and the corpus has zero demand for the deferred surfaces. base-window.md:1-14 and 67-71 (compose multiple web views; BrowserWindow simpler for one full-size view; closing a BaseWindow does not destroy a WebContentsView's webContents), web-contents-view.md:44 ('A WebContents may only be presented in one WebContentsView at a time'), browser-view.md:12/33 deprecated in favour of WebContentsView, view.md:7 and web-contents-view.md:7 cannot be used before ready. Corpus tally: no BaseWindow/View/WebContentsView/BrowserView call sites in drawio, Zettlr or quick-start (only drawio's 7 `<webview>` disable hits, F07). Keld side: engine.rs:77 'v0 is one window-filling webview per window'; arch 05 lines 22-45 name HostHooks/Anchor/destroy as destination API landing only with a live backend; arch 04 line 142 puts BrowserView mapping in Tier 3. DRY argument (126 shared methods once) is sound.
verdicts.evidence: Member counts verified from families/F02-windowing.json: BaseWindow 187, BrowserWindow 204, View 12, WebContentsView 2, BrowserView 6, total 606 across 32 entities. BrowserWindow-only additions confirmed in browser-window.md (webContents prop :510, loadURL :1264, loadFile :1321, capturePage :1253, focusOnWebView/blurWebView :1249-1251, showDefinitionForSelection :1533, six deprecated BrowserView methods :1762-1810, fromWebContents :476, fromBrowserView :483).
verdicts.correction: None required. Optional precision: state that the ownership ▲ ('webContents destroyed with window' for BaseWindow+WebContentsView) is only reachable once Tier 3 ships; until then the row is ✘, not ▲.

verdicts.reason: Tiering matches Zettlr's actual chrome code and the Electron docs, with two receipt errors and two omissions that change Tier 1 membership. Zettlr set-window-chrome.ts: macOS -> titleBarStyle 'hiddenInset' + vibrancy 'under-window' + visualEffectState 'followWindow' (backgroundColor only when vibrancy off — corpus comment, correctly labelled inference); win32 and Linux-non-native -> frame:false + titleBarStyle 'hidden' + titleBarOverlay {color '#00000000', symbolColor, height}. Electron constraints confirmed: custom-title-bar.md:148-149 titleBarOverlay requires titleBarStyle != default; custom-window-styles.md transparent limitations (no click-through, not resizable, DevTools disables, Windows no maximize, macOS no shadow); base-window-options.md: titleBarStyle default 'default', titleBarOverlay default false, vibrancy values, backgroundMaterial auto/none/mica/acrylic/tabbed, roundedCorners Win11 22000+. drawio's transparent use is confined to the hidden export window (electron.js:3096), so Tier 3 for transparent is defensible.
verdicts.evidence: Receipt error: R13/A6 say titleBarOverlay.symbolColor is 'Windows only'; v44.4.5 base-window-options.md:100-101 tags BOTH `color` and `symbolColor` as _Windows_ _Linux_, and custom-title-bar.md:153 says 'color (Windows Linux)'. Zettlr applies titleBarOverlay on Linux (non-native appearance) so Linux symbolColor is live demand. Omissions: Zettlr calls the runtime setter `setTitleBarOverlay` from its appearance provider on theme change (1 site), and the splash screen uses alwaysOnTop:true, fullscreenable:false, skipTaskbar:true, frame:false, titleBarStyle:'hidden' (splash-screen.ts:55-60) — none of which A6 lists in Tier 1 (they appear only in security_mapping). Prototype P3/P4 gating for app-region drag and vibrancy-over-non-opaque-WKWebView remains correct: no receipts exist.
verdicts.correction: Fix R13 to 'color/symbolColor: Windows and Linux'. Add to Tier 1: win.setTitleBarOverlay(options) runtime setter (Zettlr theme switch), alwaysOnTop, skipTaskbar, fullscreenable:false, closable/resizable/minimizable/maximizable:false (drawio progress-bar.js:40-45). Keep transparent/vibrancy/WCO parity as prototype-gated ▲.

extra_findings.finding: app.quit() / Cmd+Q sweep must run the same cancelable per-window 'close' protocol as a user close, and must tolerate app.quit() being called synchronously from inside a 'close' listener. KEL-143's quit ordering ('reply -> quiesce/drain -> revoke/close -> terminate/reap -> UI exit') treats window close as unconditional; the F02 object only says the sweep must suppress window-all-closed. drawio's 'close' handler preventDefaults unconditionally (so an unvetoable quit sweep would bypass its save prompt), and Zettlr calls app.quit() from inside the last window's 'close' handler while that close is still pending (reentrancy).
extra_findings.evidence: app.md:50-59 (quit closes windows first, then will-quit); base-window.md:584-588 (close() == button click, page may cancel); drawio electron.js:947-966; Zettlr source/app/service-providers/windows/index.ts:357-382; keld_state cites KEL-143 ordering as reply->quiesce->revoke/close.

extra_findings.finding: Sequencing: the object names six atoms but no tracer-bullet slice, and marks A2 blocked_by A1 (multi-window registry, no Linear id, destination registry absent). The two highest-demand behaviours (cancelable close + closed/isDestroyed fence; ready-to-show) are testable on today's single primary window by extending AppWindowEvent with CloseRequested{seq} and AppWindowCommand with CloseAllow/Destroy over the existing LIFECYCLE channel and app_session::coordinate_window_events. A fresh agent could finish that slice (one window, one backend, one conformance cell) without the registry; the registry then generalises it. Recommend naming this as slice 1 and demoting A1 from blocker to successor for A2.
extra_findings.evidence: crates/keld-wv/src/engine.rs:89-105 (AppWindowCommand {Quit,Fatal}; AppWindowEvent {NavigationReady,LastWindowClosed}); crates/keld-core/src/app_session.rs:3893-3905 coordinate_window_events; crates/keld-core/src/lifecycle.rs:132-150; product-status.tsv rows 3 and 12 (destination registry absent).

extra_findings.finding: Electron's no-handler popup default is ALLOW (confirmed from source, not docs): _callWindowOpenHandler returns a non-prevented defaultResponse and openGuestWindow runs. Keld's macOS/Linux backends today do not deny popups by policy — they simply have no wry new-window handler, so window.open is silently dropped by the engine default. That is an implicit, unlogged divergence, weaker than the WebView2 deny-all (webview2/mod.rs:1936-1946). The object's 'must stay deny + explicit ▲' is right, but the current-state claim should say 'implicitly dropped (no handler), not explicitly denied' for wkwebview/webkitgtk, and the slice must add an explicit deny + diagnostic there.
extra_findings.evidence: lib/browser/api/web-contents.ts:397-412 and 630-648 (v44.4.5); grep of crates/keld-wv/src for NewWindowRequested/new_window/create handlers hits only webview2/mod.rs and media.rs.

extra_findings.finding: WebView2 hidden-window painting is a concrete, receipt-less lead that decides A3 on Windows: ICoreWebView2Controller.IsVisible documents that an invisible controller stops rendering, and the interaction with a hidden parent HWND (SW_HIDE) is undocumented in the object. The A3 prototype must record IsVisible state explicitly; a Keld host that keeps IsVisible=true under a hidden HWND may be the only way to emulate paintWhenInitiallyHidden, and that must be measured, not assumed.
extra_findings.evidence: A3 unknowns list engine rAF behaviour generically; no Microsoft Learn receipt is cited for IsVisible; the only WebView2 facts in the object are NewWindowRequested and put_DefaultBackgroundColor.

extra_findings.finding: Reuse-point mislabel: the 'KEL-64 external double-rAF first-paint beacon' is a bench-side image beacon on a pre-spawn monotonic clock, not a host-injected pre-load script; only the KEL-142 WKContentWorld bridge (macOS) is a host injection seam, and it is renderer->host->Bun invoke, not an engine paint signal. A ready-to-show oracle built on it is a new renderer-side user script, not a reuse of KEL-64 code.
extra_findings.evidence: crates/keld-wv/AGENTS.md:32-35; docs/agents/learnings.md:79; briefing KEL-142 description (window.keld.invoke, WKContentWorld-isolated bridge).

extra_findings.finding: Corpus baseline mismatch worth stating in the scoreboard: Zettlr pins electron ^43.6.0 while the oracle is v44.4.5; the two new-in-44 BaseWindowConstructorOptions (`name`, `windowStatePersistence`) and `zoomMode` have zero corpus demand and should be explicitly deferred rather than counted toward the 606-member denominator as Tier 1.
extra_findings.evidence: corpus/zettlr/package.json:195; base-window-options.md:45-46; web-preferences.md:42-44; families/F02-windowing.json totals (606 across 32 entities confirmed).

extra_findings.finding: Trap list omission: `closable:false` + programmatic close is covered, but Electron's `enableLargerThanScreen` (drawio export window) and `fullscreenable:false` (drawio popup override, Zettlr splash) are used by both corpus apps and appear nowhere in the tiering.

epic.title: compat(window): BaseWindow/BrowserWindow over the host window registry — identity, cancelable close, ready-to-show, chrome options
epic.body:
## Scope
32 entities / 606 raw members: `BaseWindow` (187) and `BrowserWindow` (204, 126 inherited), constructor option structures (52 + 2 fields), `WebPreferences` (46 fields), `View`/`WebContentsView`/`BrowserView`/`ImageView`, 11 TouchBar classes (macOS), JumpList/Thumbar structures (Windows). Live today: the host owns exactly one primary window per session, created after the authenticated HELLO before Bun code runs; close is uncancelable; no window id crosses kipc; no chrome options exist; the destination window registry is TARGET.

## Corpus demand
Constructor + `show:false` + `ready-to-show` + `backgroundColor` (Zettlr 14 sites, draw.io), cancelable `close` with async veto then explicit `destroy()` (both apps), `closed` bookkeeping, `isDestroyed`, `getAllWindows/getFocusedWindow/fromWebContents`, maximize/minimize/fullscreen state + events, macOS `hiddenInset` + `trafficLightPosition`, Windows/Linux `frame:false` + `titleBarOverlay` (Zettlr), parent/modal (Zettlr), `setWindowOpenHandler` with `overrideBrowserWindowOptions` (draw.io).

## Maturity ladder
- L0: `BrowserWindow` class exists; unsupported options throw typed errors (privilege-escalating `webPreferences` fail loudly; engine-only flags are ignored with a diagnostic).
- L1: electron-quick-start runs unmodified on macOS (`new BrowserWindow`, `loadFile`, `getAllWindows`, close → closed).
- L2: two-phase close, tombstone-before-`closed`, `show:false`/`ready-to-show`, state events pass conformance entries citing the pinned `browser-window.md`/`base-window.md` sentences; the window-state mirror is proven coherent under a 10k-event stream.
- L3: draw.io and Zettlr window workflows pass under `keld dev` with KEL-74 records.

## Linear owners consumed
KEL-139/KEL-142 (host-created primary window, bridge), KEL-143 (window survives Bun generation loss), KEL-75 (WindowGeneration minting, window-bound roles), KEL-135 (profiles), KEL-132 (GPU/media), KEL-98 (contract codegen is NOT general — a window channel needs its own contract owner), KEL-64 (double-rAF technique for paint oracle).

## Design facts fixed by research (two refuters)
- The host mints opaque `(WindowId, WindowGeneration)`; the facade keeps a synchronous mirror updated by ordered host events before any user listener runs. `getAllWindows()` ordering is Keld-stronger than Electron (documented ▲-stronger).
- The host already creates the primary window before Bun runs; the first `new BrowserWindow()` adopts it (explicitly recorded) until Ready is re-based (F01-T2).
- Two-phase close owned by the host: `CloseRequested{window, generation, seq}` → facade emits `close` synchronously → `CloseAllow`/veto reply. The host waits indefinitely while the owning Bun generation is alive (Electron's delegate returns NO and waits); it closes on its own only when the generation is revoked. No host auto-close on timeout.
- Tombstone flips before `closed`; later member access throws the exact `Object has been destroyed` text; `destroy()` skips `close` and guarantees `closed`.
- `WebPreferences` triage: privilege-escalating fields (nodeIntegration, contextIsolation:false, webSecurity:false, allowRunningInsecureContent, enableBlinkFeatures, experimentalFeatures) fail loudly ✘; engine-flag fields such as `disableBlinkFeatures` (draw.io sets it on every window) are ignored with a diagnostic ▲; `sandbox:false` is ▲ ignored-with-diagnostic and never selects a Keld profile.
- One `BaseWindow` implementation; `BrowserWindow = BaseWindow + exactly one host-created content view`; View tree, BrowserView and multi-view are Tier 3.

## Platform lanes
macOS first (titleBarStyle/trafficLightPosition via public NSWindow API; vibrancy is Tier 2 ▲), Windows (frame:false + titleBarOverlay needs the WebView2 non-client receipt — open research F02-A6), Linux (GTK CSD).

research.unit: F03 webcontents-navigation (WebContents, webContents, WebFrameMain, webFrameMain, NavigationHistory, Debugger, webFrame, sharedTexture + 26 structures)
research.summary: [fact] The family is 34 entities / 381 members (WebContents alone 195). Corpus demand is narrow and consistent: both draw.io Desktop and Zettlr register `will-navigate` with an unconditional `event.preventDefault()` plus a `setWindowOpenHandler` (Zettlr deny-all; draw.io allows only `about:blank` with `overrideBrowserWindowOptions`), rely on `webContents.send` (49 / 9 call sites), `did-finish-load` (draw.io 7), `loadURL`/`loadFile`, `executeJavaScript` with awaited results (draw.io 5), zoom (`zoomFactor`/`zoomLevel`/`setVisualZoomLevelLimits`), `printToPDF`/`print`, `openDevTools`/`toggleDevTools`, `render-process-gone`, `destroyed`/`did-navigate`/`isDestroyed`, `console-message`, `unresponsive`; no corpus app uses NavigationHistory, Debugger, offscreen, sharedTexture, WebFrameMain frame-tree APIs, or `<webview>` (draw.io's 7 hits all DISABLE it). [fact] Keld today has no WebContents facade at all: keld-wv v0 `WebEngine` = create/navigate/eval(fire-and-forget)/set_bounds/devtools(Open|Close)/destroy; the only navigation observable is `AppWindowEvent::NavigationReady` from wry `PageLoadEvent::Finished`; the only policy hooks are Windows deny-all `NewWindowRequested` + guarded `PermissionRequested` (type-witnessed before first navigation); the KEL-142 macOS bridge supplies the reusable pieces (isolated `WKContentWorld` document-start user scripts, host-owned navigation generation counter, pending-call invalidation on navigation, `KELD-WV-011`). Window registry (H7) is TARGET in keld-core; KEL-79 (origin/resource/navigation/popup policy) is Backlog; KEL-132 is In Progress. Design answer: implement this family ONCE as (a) one engine-neutral per-webview navigation state machine in keld-wv keyed by (WebviewId, navigation generation) that synthesizes Electron's event vocabulary from raw engine signals, (b) guard-first navigation/popup policy (default-deny, app hooks can only further deny; host-initiated loads bypass `will-navigate` exactly as Electron documents but never bypass the guard), (c) `eval` extended with a structured result envelope, (d) preload = host-injected isolated-world document-start script with the Electron sandbox `require` subset, (e) a serialized host print/PDF broker, (f) devtools off in release unless `web.devtools`. Documented divergences (▲): default window.open = deny, devtools default off in release, zoom per-view not per-origin, `render-process-gone.exitCode`/`unresponsive` absent on WKWebView, NavigationHistory `pageState`/`restore` ✘. Never: sharedTexture/offscreen, Debugger CDP in production, device emulation, WebRTC policy knobs, `clone()`, Node-in-webview (`sandbox:false` honoring), trusting invalid certs via `certificate-error`.

decisions.question: Where is Electron's navigation event vocabulary (did-start-loading … did-finish-load/did-fail-load, did-navigate(-in-page), dom-ready, will-redirect, page-title-updated, destroyed) produced, and from what identity?
decisions.proposed_answer: One engine-neutral per-webview navigation state machine in keld-wv, keyed by (WebviewId, navigation generation) and reusing KEL-142's generation counter as the single document-identity source. Each backend feeds raw engine signals (WK: WKNavigationDelegate didStartProvisional/didCommit/didFinish/didFail/didFailProvisional + an injected isolated-world document-start reporter for DOMContentLoaded/hashchange/popstate/title; WebView2: NavigationStarting/SourceChanged/ContentLoading/DOMContentLoaded/HistoryChanged/DocumentTitleChanged/NavigationCompleted(IsSuccess, WebErrorStatus); WebKitGTK: load-changed/decide-policy/notify::title). The machine emits a pinned-oracle ordered sequence; `@keld/electron` only renames and fans out to listeners. `loadURL`/`loadFile` promises resolve on the generation's did-finish-load and reject with the generation's did-fail-load (errorCode/description) — a superseded navigation must reject the earlier promise. `webContents.id` = host WebviewId; `WebFrameMain` identity = (WebviewId, generation, frame token).
evidence: [fact] Electron docs define each event only by trigger ('onload dispatched', 'main frame navigation is done', 'document in top-level frame is loaded'); no total order is documented → order must be recorded from the pinned oracle (receipt R1–R4).
[fact] KEL-142 already owns generation rotation + pending-call invalidation (crates/keld-wv/src/wkwebview/macos_bridge.rs `navigation_started`, `settle(navigation, request)`; spec §5.2 steps 1–6).

[fact] Current observable is a single `NavigationReady` from wry `PageLoadEvent::Finished` (Started|Finished only) — insufficient for dom-ready/did-navigate/in-page/redirect (wkwebview/mod.rs:693-736; learnings 2026-08-17).

[fact] WebView2 documents its own partial order: SourceChanged before ContentLoading; ContentLoading after NavigationStarting/SourceChanged and before HistoryChanged/NavigationCompleted; DocumentTitleChanged may run before or after NavigationCompleted (receipt R20).
[fact] arch 02 §5: 'Webview navigation: principal generation rotates; pending replies to the old principal drop' — the same generation must drive both IPC and events (one rule, one owner).
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Per-backend ad-hoc emission in @keld/electron or in each backend (three parallel state machines, violates one-rule-one-owner and makes ordering untestable once); extending wry PageLoadEvent (interim scaffolding, only 2 states, being replaced by direct bindings); deriving document identity from URL strings (forgeable, breaks on same-URL reload).
decisions.confidence: medium-high on ownership/identity; medium on exact ordering until the oracle recording exists
blocked_by: Oracle recording of Electron 44.4.5 event order for file/http/failed/reload/hash/pushState cases (P1)
WebEngine trait design review (crate AGENTS.md) to add HostHooks/EvalCallback
decisions.unknowns: [unknown] Whether WKWebView exposes any delegate for same-document navigations (none seen in WKNavigationDelegate topic list; the injected reporter is the inferred fallback). [unknown] Electron ordering of page-title-updated relative to did-finish-load for file:// loads with synthesized titles (`explicitSet=false`).

decisions.question: Who decides whether a navigation proceeds, and what does `will-navigate` + `event.preventDefault()` mean under default-deny?
decisions.proposed_answer: Guard first, app second, deny-only hooks. The host evaluates every top-level/frame navigation against a generated allow-list (`web.navigate`-shaped origin/scheme scopes; app bundle resources and the app's own origin are implicit) BEFORE the engine commits (WK decidePolicyFor → .cancel/.allow; WebView2 NavigationStarting.Cancel; WebKitGTK decide-policy ignore/use). Only guard-allowed, non-host-initiated, non-same-document navigations are surfaced as `will-navigate`/`will-frame-navigate`, where the app may further deny; it can never widen. Host-initiated `loadURL`/`loadFile`/`reload`/`navigationHistory.go*` bypass `will-navigate` exactly as Electron documents but still pass the guard. Denied navigations produce a stable KELD code + diagnostic, not silence. Default allow-list scope is a user-owned choice (see unknowns).
evidence: [fact] Electron: 'This event will not emit when the navigation is started programmatically with APIs like webContents.loadURL and webContents.back. It is also not emitted for in-page navigations' (receipt R5).

[fact] Corpus: draw.io `contents.on('will-navigate', (event) => { event.preventDefault() })` unconditionally (electron.js:2192) and blocks `about:` in the isolated-world `navigation` listener because 'Navigations to about: URLs never reach will-navigate'; Zettlr denies all but dev `http://localhost:3000` and opens externally (attach-app-navigation-handlers.ts:67-83). A facade that surfaced host-initiated loads would blank both apps.

[fact] arch 03 §4.3 item 3: 'navigation policy hooks (allow-list)' are always-on webview hardening, 'not in this slice'; invariant 2 forbids a missing handler becoming allow; research 186 #4 shows Electron's handler-dependent allow-by-default is the anti-pattern.

[fact] Engines all provide a pre-commit veto: WKNavigationActionPolicy allow/cancel/download (R15), WebView2 NavigationStarting 'Navigations will be blocked until all NavigationStarting event handlers return' with Cancel (R20), WebKitGTK decide-policy default `webkit_policy_decision_use()` with deferral via ref+TRUE (R23).
[fact] KEL-79 acceptance owns 'navigation/popup/download/permission policy are explicit' and 'stale navigation principal' negatives (Linear, retrieved 2026-10-06).
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Emulating Electron's default-allow and trusting app `will-navigate` handlers (violates invariant 2; Electron's own security checklist #13 treats navigation limiting as app opt-in); surfacing host-initiated loads to `will-navigate` for 'completeness' (breaks both corpus apps); engine-level allow-everything with post-commit cancellation (bytes already loaded; arch 05 §2 requires failure before bytes).
decisions.confidence: high on ownership and the loadURL bypass; medium on default allow-list shape
blocked_by: KEL-79 (Backlog) or an approved spec slice naming the `web.navigate` grant shape
KEL-102 verified session snapshot for policy evaluation
decisions.unknowns: [unknown/user decision] Default allow-list: does an app that calls `loadURL('https://example.com')` need an explicit `web.navigate` grant (strict, recommended) or is any host-initiated top-level navigation implicitly allowed (Electron-like)? Recommendation: strict for remote origins, implicit for bundle resources; `keld migrate` emits the grant from observed loadURL literals. [unknown] Electron behaviour of `will-navigate` for `about:` URLs is only corpus-asserted (draw.io comment), not documented.

decisions.question: What does `setWindowOpenHandler` do in Keld when the host cannot yet mint windows, and what is the default when no handler is registered?
decisions.proposed_answer: Default = deny with a diagnostic (documented ▲ against Electron's default of creating a BrowserWindow). `{action:'deny'}` and malformed returns are exact matches (Electron also treats unrecognized returns as deny). `{action:'allow'}` requires the host to synchronously mint a child window + webview inside the engine's delegate on the UI thread, with the engine-supplied configuration (WK) / related-view (WebKitGTK) / NewWindow target (WebView2), and inherit the opener's isolated world + preload + guard install — this is gated on the keld-core window registry (H7) and is Tier 2 for `about:blank` children (draw.io) with `overrideBrowserWindowOptions` validated against the profile (nodeIntegration:true never). `did-create-window` fires only on a host-minted child; `outlivesOpener:false` is enforced by window-generation revocation (arch 02 §5 window close). `window.open()` in the page must return `null` on deny (native semantics).
evidence: [fact] Electron: unrecognized return 'will result in a console error and have the same effect as returning {action: "deny"}'; handler is 'Called before creating a window when a new window is requested by the renderer, e.g. by window.open(), a link with target="_blank", shift+clicking on a link, or submitting a form with <form target="_blank">' (R6); `did-create-window` 'Not emitted if the creation of the window is canceled' (R7); 'By default, child windows are closed when their opener is closed' (R8); window.open 'Returns Window | null' and 'When opening about:blank, the child window's WebPreferences will be copied' (R9).

[fact] Corpus: Zettlr returns `{action:'deny'}` always; draw.io allows `about:blank` with `overrideBrowserWindowOptions.webPreferences {contextIsolation:true, nodeIntegration:false, webviewTag:false, webSecurity:true}` and otherwise `openExternal(url)` or deny (electron.js:2197-2219).

[fact] Engine contracts: WKUIDelegate `webView(_:createWebViewWith:for:windowFeatures:)` 'The web view returned must be created with the specified configuration… A new web view or nil' (R16); WebView2 'If either Handled or NewWindow properties are not set, the target content will be opened on a popup window' (R20) — Keld already installs deny-all (webview2/mod.rs:1936-1946); WebKitGTK `create` 'The new WebKitWebView must be related to web_view… should not be displayed until ready-to-show' (R22).
[fact] Window registry is TARGET (arch 01 §3, product-status keld-core 'partial'); research 214 refuses a pre-H7 BrowserWindow shim.

decisions.question: How does `executeJavaScript` (and WebFrameMain/webFrame variants, insertCSS) return values and errors across three engines without a second IPC path?
decisions.proposed_answer: Extend `WebEngine::eval` (design review) with the destination `EvalCallback` carrying a structured-clone-compatible result or a typed error, implemented by ONE host-owned script envelope: the host wraps `code` as an async IIFE producing `{ok:true,value}` / `{ok:false,name,message,stack}` serialized with a single shared encoder (JSON-with-tags for Date/Map/Set/TypedArray refs → bulk lane per arch 02 §5 SCV codec), evaluated in the PAGE world (`executeJavaScript`) or in a named Keld app world that is never the bridge world (`executeJavaScriptInIsolatedWorld`; world ids are remapped, the KEL-142 world is unreachable). Queue the request until the current generation's did-stop-loading ('suspended until web page stop loading'); a generation rotation before completion rejects with a KELD code (reusing KEL-142 invalidation). `userGesture:true` is ▲ (no engine exposes a user-activation flag for evaluated script; WK/WebView2 may refuse `requestFullscreen`). `insertCSS` returns a host-minted key and is implemented by the same envelope inserting a `<style data-keld-key>`; `removeInsertedCSS` removes it.
evidence: [fact] Electron: 'Returns Promise<any> — resolves with the result of the executed code or is rejected if the result of the code is a rejected promise… Code execution will be suspended until web page stop loading' (R10); WebFrameMain variant 'rejected if execution throws or results in a rejected promise' (R11).
[fact] Corpus: draw.io awaits results at 3+ sites (`collectConfigPathsScript`, recents, settings; electron.js:491, 565, 609) — a `Promise<void>` facade fails draw.io's primary workflow.
[fact] Keld `eval` is fire-and-forget `Result<(), WvError>`; the callback form is explicitly deferred to the command-queue design (engine.rs module doc).

[fact] WebView2 `ExecuteScript`: result 'is a JSON encoded string. If the result is undefined, contains a reference cycle, or otherwise is not able to be encoded into JSON, then the result is considered to be null… If the script that was run throws an unhandled exception, then the result is also "null"' (R20) — undefined/throw/null are indistinguishable without an envelope.

[fact] WebKitGTK `webkit_web_view_evaluate_javascript` (since 2.40) runs in a named script world and returns a JSCValue via `_finish` (R25); WK `evaluateJavaScript(_:in:in:completionHandler:)` is the KEL-142 `evaluate_in_world` path (macos_bridge.rs:797).

[fact] KEL-142 AC2: page world cannot access the isolated native handler — app-visible isolated worlds must therefore be distinct from the bridge world; Electron reserves world 999 for contextIsolation (R13).
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Round-tripping results through the page-world `window.keld.invoke` bridge (page-controllable, forgeable, and the bridge admits one pending call per view); engine-native JSON only (loses undefined/throw/Date/Map and ordering of multiple evals); structured-clone over the engine message channel (WebView2 postMessage is string/JSON only — 06-webview-reality bridge table).
blocked_by: arch 02 §5 SCV codec owner (KEL-98 echo-codegen) for non-JSON values

[unknown] Whether WK evaluateJavaScript on a never-shown (hidden) view completes before first paint (affects Zettlr's hidden print window).

decisions.question: What is a 'preload script' in Keld, and what happens to `sandbox:false` / `nodeIntegration:true` apps?
decisions.proposed_answer: A preload is a host-registered, document-start user script in the Keld isolated world (the KEL-142 injection path), main-frame-only by default, bundled by `keld migrate`/`keld build` into the package and resolved by the host from the package root (an absolute path outside the package is a typed refusal, not a filesystem read). The isolated world provides the Electron sandbox `require` polyfill subset ONLY (`events`, `timers`, `url`, `electron` → contextBridge/ipcRenderer/webFrame/nativeImage/webUtils/crashReporter shims over `window.keld`). `sandbox:false` or `nodeIntegration:true` are never honored (no Node in a webview — it is not one of the four uniques, and the strict profile forbids ambient authority): the facade emits an explicit diagnostic and the cell scores ✘ unless `keld migrate`'s static scan proves the preload only uses the sandbox subset, in which case a `keld.compat.ts` quirk (`treatUnsandboxedPreloadAsSandboxed`) lets it run. `preload-error` (path + Error) is emitted when the injected script throws. On WebView2 the injection must use the async completion form (learning: sync form blocks UI 96–109 ms) and must be gated to the main frame (the API injects into all frames).
evidence: [fact] Electron: sandbox 'Default is true since Electron 20'; sandboxed preload `require` is a polyfill limited to events/timers/url + electron subset and 'you will not be able to use CommonJS modules to separate your preload script into multiple files'; 'Sandboxing is also disabled whenever Node.js integration is enabled' (R17, R18); contextIsolation 'enabled by default since Electron 12' (R19); preload 'will always have access to node APIs no matter whether node integration is turned on or off' (R12 — the part Keld cannot and must not clone).

[fact] Corpus: draw.io preload with contextIsolation:true/nodeIntegration:false/webviewTag:false/webSecurity:true (electron.js:721-729) and preload-side isolated-world `navigation` listener; Zettlr: 14 windows with preload, 12 `sandbox:true`, 2 `sandbox:false` (onboarding, splash) with contextIsolation:true.

[fact] KEL-142 §5.1/AC2: isolated `WKContentWorld` scripts at AtDocumentStart; 'page code observes window.keld.invoke before its first script runs'; page world cannot reach the native handler. WebView2 `AddScriptToExecuteOnDocumentCreated` 'runs on all top-level document and child frame page navigations' (R20); 06-webview-reality: pre-load user scripts ✅ on all three engines.

[fact] research 186 #5: 'Do not equate early script injection or an isolated world with a permission boundary… a compat escape hatch cannot silently turn a role/webview into an authority holder'; briefing never list: `nodeIntegration:true` in renderer.
[fact] Electron `webPreferences.nodeIntegrationInSubFrames` default false → preload main-frame-only by default (R12).
decisions.alternatives_rejected: A Node/Bun-backed preload runtime (fifth unique; violates invariant 1); honoring `sandbox:false` via a labeled legacy profile (legacy profile forfeits zero-authority for Bun roles per arch 03, it does not and cannot put Node inside a system webview); injecting preload into the page world (KEL-142 forbids page-world fallback).
blocked_by: F04/contextBridge-ipc family owns the shim surface; this unit owns registration/injection/ordering

decisions.question: How are print/printToPDF/devtools/Debugger mapped so that Tier 1 apps run while release policy stays closed?
decisions.proposed_answer: One host print broker (keld-native-style, serialized single-flight queue per host) implements `printToPDF` → bytes to the app role (WK `createPDF` macOS 11+; WebView2 `PrintToPdf` to a host-owned temp path then read back, Runtime ≥1.0.1020.30; WebKitGTK `WebKitPrintOperation` with GTK print-to-file settings — unverified) and `print()` → native dialog when `silent:false` (user-mediated, no grant) / explicit grant for `silent:true`; `failureReason` strings are matched to Electron's three documented values. DevTools: `openDevTools()/toggleDevTools()` are allowed under `keld dev` and when `web.devtools:true`; in release without the grant they are a no-op with a diagnostic and `isDevToolsOpened()===false` (▲ vs Electron `devTools` default true); WK requires `isInspectable=true` (macOS 13.3+, default false) and devtools-opened/closed events can only be synthesized from host-triggered opens (WK gives no inspector lifecycle callback → ▲). `Debugger` (CDP) is ✘ in production on all engines and at most dev-only on WebView2; `fromDevToolsTargetId`, `setDevToolsWebContents`, `inspectSharedWorker*`, `inspectServiceWorker`, `addWorkSpace`, device emulation are ✘.
evidence: [fact] Electron: printToPDF 'Returns Promise<Buffer> — Resolves with the generated PDF data'; options defaults Letter/portrait/printBackground false/scale 1 (R14); print `silent` 'Default is false'; failureReasons 'Invalid printer settings', 'Print job canceled', 'Print job failed'; invalid custom pageSize 'an error will be thrown' (R14); `webPreferences.devTools` 'Default is true' (R12).

[fact] Corpus: Zettlr pdf-exporter: hidden `BrowserWindow({show:false})` → `loadFile` → `printToPDF({printBackground:false, landscape:false, pageSize:'A4'})` → `close()` (pdf-exporter.ts:57-67); draw.io `contents.print(pdfOptions, cb)` with retry on 'Invalid printer settings' and `printToPDF(pdfOptions)` merge (electron.js:3303-3330); electron-quick-start calls `openDevTools()` unconditionally; draw.io `openDevTools` on an ipc message.

[fact] Engines: WK `createPDF(configuration:completionHandler:)` macOS 11+ returns Data (R27); `isInspectable` macOS 13.3+ 'Defaults to false' (R26); 06-webview-reality: 'App Store rules forbid enabling devtools features in release builds', devtools = Safari inspector, no CDP; WebView2 `PrintToPdf` writes to `ResultFilePath`, 'Only one Printing operation can be in progress at a time… completed handler is immediately invoked with isSuccessful set to FALSE' (R21); WebKitGTK `WebKitPrintOperation` run_dialog/print with GtkPrintSettings (R24, PDF path not in excerpt).

[fact] arch 03 §4.3: 'devtools off in release unless web.devtools: true'; Windows backend already `SetAreDevToolsEnabled(cfg!(debug_assertions))`; learning: wry devtools needs the `devtools` feature or release builds fail.
[fact] briefing never list: 'full CDP in production webviews'; research 13 never table.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Electron-faithful devtools-on-by-default in release (violates arch 03 and App Store constraint); per-call concurrent PrintToPdf on WebView2 (documented to fail the second call); implementing printToPDF in the app role via a headless Chromium (bundles an engine; invariant 1/5).

security_mapping.keld_mapping: Evaluated by keld-guard as the app's AppProcess request against generated `web.navigate`-shaped origin/scheme scopes before the engine commits; bundle resources implicit; `file://` is served through the KEL-79 resource adapter bound to (WebviewId, generation), never as a privileged file origin (research 186 `grant_file_protocol_extra_privileges`); downloadURL → download policy (KEL-79) + fs.write scope via dialog-selected path.
Only guard-allowed, page-initiated, cross-document navigations reach the handler; preventDefault denies; the handler cannot widen; no handler ⇒ guard decision stands (no implicit allow).
