platform_notes.platform: macOS (AppKit + WKWebView via objc2; tao+wry interim)
platform_notes.note: [fact] Navigation veto: WKNavigationDelegate decidePolicyFor(WKNavigationAction) with WKNavigationActionPolicy allow/cancel/download (macOS 10.10+); progress: didStartProvisional/didCommit/didFinish/didFail/didFailProvisional; crash: webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate (no reason/exitCode). [inference] No delegate for same-document navigation or DOMContentLoaded → needs the injected isolated-world reporter (KEL-142 user-script path). [fact] window.open: WKUIDelegate createWebViewWith must return a WKWebView built from the supplied configuration or nil (synchronous, UI thread). [fact] pageZoom macOS 11+ (CSS zoom, per view); createPDF(configuration:) macOS 11+ returns Data; isInspectable macOS 13.3+ default false (App Store forbids devtools features in release — 06-webview-reality); no CDP; evaluateJavaScript in WKContentWorld macOS 11+ (KEL-142 forbids page-world fallback). [fact] WKWebView lacks Service Worker on custom schemes (WebKit 206741) → KEL-79. [fact] Engine version is OS-locked (10–15% of users on multi-year-old WebKit) → feature-gate scanner. [fact] All engine mutations on the UI thread (crate AGENTS.md); `startup` module macOS-only. [unknown] printing/createPDF on a never-shown view; backForwardList mutation for removeEntryAtIndex.

[fact] NavigationStarting blocks until handlers return and supports Cancel (redirects re-enter with the same navigation id); NewWindowRequested opens a popup unless Handled/NewWindow set — Keld installs deny-all before first navigation (`GuardInstalled` witness, KEL-168); ProcessFailed kinds include BROWSER_PROCESS_EXITED, RENDER_PROCESS_EXITED, RENDER_PROCESS_UNRESPONSIVE, FRAME_RENDER_PROCESS_EXITED (richer than Electron). [fact] Documented partial order: NavigationStarting → SourceChanged → ContentLoading → (DOMContentLoaded) → HistoryChanged → NavigationCompleted(IsSuccess/WebErrorStatus); DocumentTitleChanged may run before or after NavigationCompleted; SourceChanged fires on fragment navigation but not pushState with the same URL; CapturePreview fails before first ContentLoading. [fact] ExecuteScript returns a JSON string and collapses undefined/exception to "null" → envelope required. [fact] AddScriptToExecuteOnDocumentCreated runs in all top-level and child frames; the synchronous wait form stalls the UI thread 96–109 ms (learning 2026-08-15) → async completion handler only. [fact] Controller ZoomFactor is per-site last-used and ZoomFactorChanged fires right after ContentLoading on navigation; programmatic put_ZoomFactor emits no event. [fact] PrintToPdf (ICoreWebView2_7, Runtime ≥1.0.1020.30) writes to an absolute file path, one print operation at a time, concurrent call completes with isSuccessful FALSE; PrintToPdfStream/Print/ShowPrintUI exist in later interfaces [lead]. [fact] CDP exists on WebView2 (Chromium) but is still never in production. [fact] Devtools currently `SetAreDevToolsEnabled(cfg!(debug_assertions))`; WebView2 user-data folder is selected before any window (KEL-135); virtual-host-name Service Worker limits → KEL-79. [fact] Enterprise DowngradeVersion policy means N-2 Chromium must be tolerated.

platform_notes.platform: Linux (GTK + WebKitGTK; wry interim = GTK3/WebKit2GTK 4.1, destination webkit6/gtk4)
platform_notes.note: [fact] decide-policy signal with navigation-action / new-window-action / response decisions; default handler calls webkit_policy_decision_use(); ref + return TRUE defers. [fact] create signal for window.open: returned view must be related (`related-view`) and shown only after ready-to-show. [fact] zoom-level property default 1.0 (per view); 2.54 adds a `magnification` property. [fact] evaluate_javascript (since 2.40) runs in a named script world and returns JSCValue; WebKitGTK versions are frozen per distro release (years-old engines on LTS). [fact] WebKitPrintOperation: run_dialog or print with GtkPrintSettings/GtkPageSetup, finished/failed signals; PDF-to-file path not in the documented excerpt [unknown]. [fact] Inspector requires the devtools build flag/feature; no CDP. [fact] GPU safe-mode (NVIDIA + Wayland, `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1`) applied by exact-self re-exec; `degraded-rendering` is a separate fact from render-process-gone. [fact] Custom-scheme body access requires 2.40+ (historically broken, wry#666); WebRTC backend unstable (GstWebRTC re-plumb). [fact] `build_gtk` must use tao `default_vbox()` (learning 2026-08-17).

prototype_candidates.question: Can one engine-neutral navigation state machine reproduce Electron 44.4.5's observed event ORDER for file/http/302/failed/reload/hash/pushState/beforeunload cases?
prototype_candidates.shape: P1: Instrumented electron-quick-start main logging all WebContents navigation events + loadURL promise settlement with hrtime to JSON (pinned Electron 44.4.5, immutable blob per research 214); same harness against keld-wv WK first (raw delegate + injected reporter) then WebView2/WebKitGTK; diff tool reports per-scenario sequence equality.
prototype_candidates.shows: The oracle recording that D1 depends on; which Electron events need the injected document-start reporter; whether dom-ready/did-finish-load/did-navigate can be emitted in order from (WebviewId, generation) alone.

prototype_candidates.question: Does WK createWebViewWith with the supplied WKWebViewConfiguration give the child the parent's isolated-world user scripts, message handler and guard install before its first script runs?
prototype_candidates.shape: P2: macOS objc2 spike under the KEL-142 bridge: page calls window.open('about:blank') and window.open(sameOrigin); delegate returns a host-minted view in a new NSWindow; assert KELD_KEL142_BIND fires for the child generation, page cannot reach the handler, and closing the opener closes the child.
prototype_candidates.shows: Feasibility of `{action:'allow'}` + did-create-window + outlivesOpener once H7 exists; about:blank WebPreferences-copy semantics (draw.io's path).

prototype_candidates.question: Can a single host-owned eval envelope distinguish undefined / thrown / rejected / Date / Map results on WebView2's JSON-only ExecuteScript and on WK/WebKitGTK, and what does async AddScriptToExecuteOnDocumentCreated injection cost?
prototype_candidates.shape: P3: Windows spike: envelope wrapper + tagged JSON encoder; 7 fixtures (1+1, undefined, throw, Promise.reject, Date, Map, 64 KiB string); measure injection wall time with the async completion form vs the known 96–109 ms sync stall; confirm per-frame gating.
prototype_candidates.shows: D4 contract and D5 injection path on the hardest engine; attributed cost for the arch 01 §5 first-paint budget.

prototype_candidates.question: Does printToPDF produce a valid PDF from a hidden window on all three engines, and how must concurrent calls be serialized?
prototype_candidates.shape: P4: three-engine matrix: hidden view → load A4 fixture → PDF via createPDF / PrintToPdf(temp path) / WebKitPrintOperation(print-to-file) → assert %PDF header, page count, printBackground effect; two concurrent calls; GTK dialog-less path discovery.
prototype_candidates.shows: D6 feasibility; the Zettlr pdf-exporter and draw.io print cells; which PrintToPDFOptions are ▲ per engine (headerTemplate, pageRanges, scale).

prototype_candidates.question: Can host-initiated loads be tagged so draw.io's and Zettlr's unconditional `will-navigate → preventDefault()` handlers do not block the app's own loadURL, while anchor/https/about: navigations are correctly denied?
prototype_candidates.shape: P5: keld-wv WK spike: generation-tagged navigate(); page fixtures with anchor click, location.assign, form submit, window.open('about:blank','_self'), hash change; app handler denies everything; assert loadURL/reload complete, page-initiated cross-document navigations are vetoed pre-commit (no bytes loaded), same-document navigations are not surfaced.
prototype_candidates.shows: D2's bypass/veto split and the guard-first ordering before any resource bytes (arch 05 §2).

never_list.surface: sharedTexture module (importSharedTexture, sendSharedTexture, setSharedTextureReceiver, subtle) + OffscreenSharedTexture/SharedTexture* structures + offscreen rendering (paint, startPainting/stopPainting/isPainting, setFrameRate/getFrameRate, invalidate, beginFrameSubscription/endFrameSubscription, webPreferences.offscreen)
never_list.rationale: Experimental in Electron; no engine path on WebView2 (offscreen ❌, open issue) and only hacks on WK/WebKitGTK (06-webview-reality); zero corpus demand; Tier 3 research at most, documented-never for v1.

never_list.surface: Debugger (CDP) in production webviews; fromDevToolsTargetId; getOrCreateDevToolsTargetId; setDevToolsWebContents; inspectSharedWorker/inspectSharedWorkerById/getAllSharedWorkers/inspectServiceWorker; addWorkSpace/removeWorkSpace; enableDeviceEmulation/disableDeviceEmulation
never_list.rationale: Briefing never list ('full CDP in production webviews'); WK and WebKitGTK have no CDP; App Store policy; device emulation is CDP-backed.

never_list.surface: Honoring webPreferences.sandbox:false, nodeIntegration:true, nodeIntegrationInWorker/InSubFrames, additionalArguments, enableBlinkFeatures/disableBlinkFeatures, experimentalFeatures, webSecurity:false, allowRunningInsecureContent, or any Chromium/V8 switch via this family
never_list.rationale: No Node in a system webview (four uniques only); default-deny is sacred; Electron's own security checklist items 2, 6, 8, 9, 10 say the same; explicit diagnostic + ✘, never a silent downgrade.

never_list.surface: certificate-error callback(true) / select-client-certificate app-chosen trust in release
never_list.rationale: TLS trust is a host decision; an app hook may only deny; honoring app trust of invalid certificates would let a compromised main role MITM its own webview.

never_list.surface: setWebRTCIPHandlingPolicy / getWebRTCIPHandlingPolicy / setWebRTCUDPPortRange / getWebRTCUDPPortRange
never_list.rationale: Chromium-only knobs; no WK/WebKitGTK API; documented ✘ rather than a silent no-op.

never_list.surface: clone()
never_list.rationale: Chromium SiteInstance/process-sharing semantics have no equivalent in system engines.

never_list.surface: forcefullyCrashRenderer in production builds
never_list.rationale: No public engine API to crash the content process; a test hook only; a production facade must not fake a crash event.

never_list.surface: executeJavaScriptInIsolatedWorld / setIsolatedWorldInfo targeting Keld's bridge world (Electron world 999 equivalent)
never_list.rationale: KEL-142 AC2: the isolated native handler must be unreachable from app-visible worlds; app world ids are remapped.

never_list.surface: A renderer-side `webFrame`/`WebFrameMain` that exposes routing ids, OS pids or frame tokens as authority
never_list.rationale: Identity is host-minted (WebviewId, generation, frame token); PIDs are diagnostic only (arch 04 §3.1).

receipts.claim: R1: loadURL/loadFile 'Returns Promise<void> - the promise will resolve when the page has finished loading (see did-finish-load), and rejects if the page fails to load (see did-fail-load). A noop rejection handler is already attached… If the existing page has a beforeUnload handler, did-fail-load will be called unless will-prevent-unload is handled.'

R2: did-finish-load 'Emitted when the navigation is done, i.e. the spinner of the tab has stopped spinning, and the onload event was dispatched.'; did-fail-load 'like did-finish-load but emitted when the load failed' with net error list; did-fail-provisional-load 'emitted when the load was cancelled (e.g. window.stop())'; dom-ready 'Emitted when the document in the top-level frame is loaded.'

R3: did-navigate 'Emitted when a main frame navigation is done. This event is not emitted for in-page navigations… Use did-navigate-in-page'; did-start-navigation details {url, isSameDocument, isMainFrame, frame, initiator}; render-process-gone 'Emitted when the renderer process unexpectedly disappears'; RenderProcessGoneDetails reasons clean-exit/abnormal-exit/killed/crashed/oom/launch-failed/integrity-failure/memory-eviction.

R4: page-title-updated 'Fired when page title is set during navigation. explicitSet is false when title is synthesized from file url.'; did-start-loading/did-stop-loading 'Corresponds to the points in time when the spinner of the tab started/stopped spinning'; will-redirect/did-redirect-navigation for server-side redirects.

R5: will-navigate 'Emitted when a user or the page wants to start navigation on the main frame… This event will not emit when the navigation is started programmatically with APIs like webContents.loadURL and webContents.back. It is also not emitted for in-page navigations… Calling event.preventDefault() will prevent the navigation.' isSameDocument 'always set to false for this event'.

R6: setWindowOpenHandler details {url (resolved), frameName, features, disposition, referrer, postBody}; 'Returning an unrecognized value such as a null, undefined, or an object without a recognized action value will result in a console error and have the same effect as returning {action: "deny"}'; 'Called before creating a window when a new window is requested by the renderer, e.g. by window.open(), a link with target="_blank", shift+clicking on a link, or submitting a form with <form target="_blank">'. send/sendToFrame: Structured Clone; 'Sending Functions, Promises, Symbols, WeakMaps, or WeakSets will throw an exception'.
R7: did-create-window 'Emitted after successful creation of a window via window.open in the renderer. Not emitted if the creation of the window is canceled from webContents.setWindowOpenHandler.'

R8: WindowOpenHandlerResponse {action allow|deny, overrideBrowserWindowOptions, outlivesOpener ('By default, child windows are closed when their opener is closed'), createWindow (did-create-window not emitted)}.

R9: window.open 'Returns Window | null'; 'webContents.setWindowOpenHandler has final say and full privilege'; 'When opening about:blank, the child window's WebPreferences will be copied'; outlivesOpener default false.

R10: executeJavaScript 'Returns Promise<any> - A promise that resolves with the result of the executed code or is rejected if the result of the code is a rejected promise… Code execution will be suspended until web page stop loading.'; setZoomLevel 'scale := 1.2 ^ level', limits 300%/50%; NOTE zoom policy 'same-origin by default… propagates across all instances of windows with the same domain. To use per-webContents zoom instead, set the zoom mode to isolated'; setVisualZoomLevelLimits 'Visual zoom is disabled by default'; close() → 'the WebContents will be destroyed and no longer usable. The destroyed event will be emitted'; getAllWebContents includes 'opened DevTools'; macOS focus/blur note.

R11: WebFrameMain.executeJavaScript 'rejected if execution throws or results in a rejected promise'; reload() 'Only results in false when the frame has no history'; `detached`: 'If a frame is accessed while the corresponding page is running any unload listeners, it may become detached as the newly navigated page replaced it in the frame tree'; fromId returns undefined, fromFrameToken returns null when absent.

R12: WebPreferences: devTools default true; nodeIntegration default false; preload 'will always have access to node APIs no matter whether node integration is turned on or off. The value should be the absolute file path'; sandbox 'Default is true since Electron 20'; contextIsolation 'Defaults to true'; webviewTag 'Defaults to false'; zoomFactor default 1.0; webSecurity default true; backgroundThrottling true; offscreen false/useSharedTexture false; spellcheck true.

R13: webFrame (renderer) zoom same formula; executeJavaScriptInIsolatedWorld worldId range 1..536870911, '999 is the world used by Electron's contextIsolation'; setIsolatedWorldInfo; Chrome extensions reserve [1<<20, 1<<29); setSpellCheckProvider shape; findFrameByRoutingId/routingId deprecated.

R14: print(): silent 'Default is false', color default true, landscape default false, duplexMode simplex|shortEdge|longEdge, callback(success, failureReason), failureReasons 'Invalid printer settings' / 'Print job canceled' / 'Print job failed', custom pageSize <353 microns 'an error will be thrown'; printToPDF 'Returns Promise<Buffer> - Resolves with the generated PDF data'; PrintToPDFOptions defaults landscape false, displayHeaderFooter false, printBackground false, scale 1, pageSize Letter, pageRanges ''; openDevTools modes left/right/bottom/undocked/detach, activate default true; capturePage stayHidden/stayAwake.

R15: WKNavigationActionPolicy cases cancel / allow / download (macOS 10.10+); WKNavigationDelegate 'Asks the delegate for permission to navigate to new content based on the specified action information'; didStartProvisionalNavigation / didCommit / didFinish / didFail / didFailProvisionalNavigation / webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate abstracts.

R16: WKUIDelegate webView(_:createWebViewWith:for:windowFeatures:) 'Creates a new web view… The web view returned must be created with the specified configuration. WebKit loads the request in the returned web view.' Returns 'A new web view or nil'.

R17: 'Starting from Electron 20, the sandbox is enabled for renderer processes without any further configuration'; sandboxed preload require polyfill limited to electron subset (contextBridge, crashReporter, ipcRenderer, nativeImage, webFrame, webUtils) + events/timers/url; 'you will not be able to use CommonJS modules to separate your preload script into multiple files'; 'Sandboxing is also disabled whenever Node.js integration is enabled'; app.enableSandbox() forces globally.

R18: Security checklist: 'By default, Electron will automatically approve all permission requests unless the developer has manually configured a custom handler'; items 12 (will-attach-webview), 13 (will-navigate 'prevent navigation to unexpected origins'), 14 (setWindowOpenHandler deny), 17 (validate IPC sender via frame.origin), 18 ('The file:// protocol gets more privileges in Electron than in a web browser').
R19: 'Context isolation has been enabled by default since Electron 12'; exposing ipcRenderer.send directly is warned against.

R20: WebView2 ICoreWebView2: NavigationStarting 'Navigations will be blocked until all NavigationStarting event handlers return' (Cancel); NewWindowRequested 'If either Handled or NewWindow properties are not set, the target content will be opened on a popup window'; ProcessFailed kinds incl. RENDER_PROCESS_UNRESPONSIVE and FRAME_RENDER_PROCESS_EXITED; ExecuteScript result 'is a JSON encoded string. If the result is undefined… the result is considered to be null… If the script… throws an unhandled exception, then the result is also "null"'; AddScriptToExecuteOnDocumentCreated 'runs on all top-level document and child frame page navigations'; SourceChanged before ContentLoading, ContentLoading precedes HistoryChanged and NavigationCompleted, DocumentTitleChanged 'may run before or after the NavigationCompleted event'; CapturePreview 'fails if called before the first ContentLoading event'.

R21: ICoreWebView2_7.PrintToPdf(ResultFilePath, printSettings, handler): absolute path, overwrite, E_INVALIDARG for invalid path; 'Only one Printing operation can be in progress at a time. If PrintToPdf is called while a PrintToPdf or PrintToPdfStream or Print or ShowPrintUI job is in progress, the completed handler is immediately invoked with isSuccessful set to FALSE'; introduced WebView2 Win32 1.0.1020.30. ICoreWebView2Controller.ZoomFactorChanged: 'When it is modified using the ZoomFactor property… no ZoomFactorChanged event is triggered. WebView associates the last used zoom factor for each site… When the zoom factor changes due to a navigation change, the ZoomFactorChanged event runs right after the ContentLoading event.'

R22: WebKitWebView::create 'Emitted when the creation of a new WebKitWebView is requested… The new WebKitWebView must be related to web_view, see WebKitWebView:related-view… should not be displayed to the user until the WebKitWebView::ready-to-show signal is emitted.'

R23: WebKitWebView::decide-policy types NAVIGATION_ACTION / NEW_WINDOW_ACTION / RESPONSE; 'The default signal handler will simply call webkit_policy_decision_use()'; deferral via g_object_ref + return TRUE.

R24: WebKitPrintOperation 'Controls a print operation… set the print settings with webkit_print_operation_set_print_settings() or display the print dialog with webkit_print_operation_run_dialog()'; finished/failed signals; zoom-level property default 1.000000.

R25: webkit_web_view_evaluate_javascript (Since 2.40): asynchronous, `world_name` 'The name of a WebKitScriptWorld or NULL to use the default', result via webkit_web_view_evaluate_javascript_finish returning JSCValue.
R26: WKWebView.isInspectable 'A Boolean value that indicates whether you can inspect the view with Safari Web Inspector'; macOS 13.3+; 'Defaults to false'.

R27: WKWebView.pageZoom 'The scale factor by which the web view scales content relative to its bounds', default 1.0, equivalent to CSS zoom, macOS 11.0+; createPDF(configuration:completionHandler:) 'Generates PDF data from the web view's contents asynchronously', macOS 11.0+, completion (pdfDocumentData, error).

R28: BrowserWindow.webContents 'Reading this property throws Object has been destroyed once the window has been destroyed'; ready-to-show 'Emitted when the web page has been rendered (while not being shown)… will never fire if you use paintWhenInitiallyHidden: false'; win.destroy() forces close without unload; close event precedes beforeunload/unload.

R29: Debugger 'An alternate transport for Chrome's remote debugging protocol'; sendCommand resolves {} when no result; 'detach' fires 'either when webContents is closed or DevTools is invoked for the attached webContents'.

R30: process-model: 'Preload scripts contain code that executes in a renderer process before its web content begins loading… granted more privileges by having access to Node.js APIs'; 'Each instance of the BrowserWindow class creates an application window that loads a web page in a separate renderer process. You can interact with this web content from the main process using the window's webContents object.'; preload-error 'Emitted when the preload script preloadPath throws an unhandled exception error'.

R31: NavigationHistory.removeEntryAtIndex 'Can't remove entry at the "current active index"' returns boolean; restore 'Will make a best effort to restore not just the navigation stack but also the state of the individual pages… recommended to call this API before any navigation entries are created'; NavigationEntry.pageState 'A base64 encoded data string containing Chromium page state'.

verdicts.reason: The identity atoms survive (webContents.id = host WebviewId; promise correlation per generation; raw engine signals per backend), but the ownership atom is wrong on two counts. (1) Placing a state machine in keld-wv that 'synthesizes Electron's event vocabulary' and emits 'a pinned-oracle ordered sequence' puts an Electron-ism (Electron's event names and total order) into the engine crate, whereas arch 04 §3 layer 4 assigns host-side emulation of 'webContents routing identity' to the keld-compat crate and keld-compat/AGENTS.md says compat pressure stays there; arch 05 §1 describes keld-wv's job as generic hooks ('principal identity per navigation, pre-load script atomicity, navigation interception, window.open handling, print, zoom, find'), not Electron ordering. (2) 'Reusing KEL-142's generation counter as the single document-identity source' names the wrong owner: KEL-102 §(GuardSnapshot) says the Webview principal generation is 'Created and rotated only by the host webview/navigation registry' and arch 03 §1 says webview identity 'is derived from the host's engine/navigation registry'; the bridge's BridgeState.navigation_generation (macos_bridge.rs:301,334) is a private per-bridge counter bumped from wry PageLoadEvent::Started (wkwebview/mod.rs page_load_trace_handler) while the guard principal generation is still 0 (arch 03 §4.3). Today there are two counters and no registry; the destination owner is the keld-core registry (arch 01 §3 table: keld-core owns 'window registry'), which engine.rs's module doc also names as the owner of the callback/command-queue plumbing. Minor: the quoted sentence 'principal generation rotates; pending replies to the old principal drop' is arch 02 §7 line 362, not §5.

epic.title: compat(webContents): navigation event vocabulary, navigation policy, window-open handler, executeJavaScript, preload registration, print/devtools
epic.body:
## Scope
34 entities / 381 members: `WebContents` (195), `WebFrameMain`, `NavigationHistory`, `Debugger`, `webFrame` (renderer), `webContents` module, input-event and print structures, `sharedTexture`/offscreen structures (never). Live today: no WebContents facade; keld-wv `WebEngine` = create/navigate/eval(fire-and-forget)/bounds/devtools/destroy; the only navigation observable is a page-load-finished event; Windows denies popups and guards permission requests; the KEL-142 macOS bridge supplies the isolated-world injection seam and a navigation generation counter.

## Corpus demand (resolved)
`will-navigate` + unconditional `preventDefault` and `setWindowOpenHandler` (both apps; Zettlr deny-all, draw.io allows only `about:blank` with `overrideBrowserWindowOptions` after an `openExternal` side effect); `webContents.send` (Zettlr 49 / draw.io 9); `did-finish-load`; `loadURL`/`loadFile`; awaited `executeJavaScript` (draw.io 5+); zoom; `printToPDF`/`print`; `openDevTools`; `render-process-gone`; `destroyed`; `before-input-event` + `pasteAndMatchStyle` (draw.io). Zero demand for NavigationHistory, Debugger, offscreen (except draw.io's export window), sharedTexture, WebFrameMain frame-tree APIs.

## Maturity ladder
- L0: `webContents` facade exists with typed errors; never-list rows published.
- L1: `loadURL/loadFile`, `did-finish-load`, `send`, `executeJavaScript` work for quick-start and draw.io on macOS.
- L2: ordered navigation vocabulary, will-navigate veto semantics (guard ∧ app), window-open handler default, destroyed semantics pass pinned conformance entries on each engine or carry an explicit per-engine ▲.
- L3: corpus apps' navigation workflows pass under `keld dev`.

## Linear owners consumed
KEL-79 (origin/resource/navigation/popup policy), KEL-132 (media/GPU), KEL-142 (isolated world, generation counter), KEL-135 (profile), KEL-80 (bounded host→renderer delivery), SCV codec owner (open — see F03-D4).

## Design facts fixed by research (two refuters)
- Split ownership: keld-wv delivers a small engine-neutral navigation signal set (provisional-start, commit, same-document change, dom-content-loaded, finish, fail{code}) per backend; Electron's event vocabulary is synthesised once above it (facade/keld-compat), keyed by `(WebviewId, navigation generation)`. One generation owner is required (two counters exist today: bridge vs guard) — decision F04-A4.
- Navigation policy is guard-first, app-hook deny-only: the app's `will-navigate`/`will-frame-navigate` hook is invoked for every page-initiated cross-document navigation, the guard decision is computed independently, outcome = guard ∧ app; programmatic `loadURL` bypasses the app hook but not the guard.
- `setWindowOpenHandler`: the handler is always invoked (draw.io's has side effects); unrecognised returns are deny; default without handler is deny-with-diagnostic (▲ or `windowOpenHandler` quirk, chosen in the PR); `allow` requires synchronous host window minting inside the engine delegate.
- `executeJavaScript` needs an `EvalCallback` result envelope on `WebEngine::eval` and a structured-clone-compatible codec; the SCV codec has no owner yet (F03-D4 open).
- Preload runs in a dedicated app content world (third world), not the trusted KEL-142 world — panel contested decision; F07 owns the preload runtime.
- Devtools are dev-only; a host print broker serves `printToPDF`/`print`; `Debugger` is ✘.

research.unit: F04 ipc-bridge (ipcMain/ipcRenderer, contextBridge, MessageChannelMain/MessagePortMain, utilityProcess/parentPort, IpcMainServiceWorker, webUtils)
research.summary: F04 is 15 entities / 77 members. Corpus demand ranks: (1) ipcRenderer.send/on/once + ipcMain.on + event.reply/event.senderFrame (draw.io's entire IPC is this one shape via a preload request/response multiplexer, no invoke); (2) ipcRenderer.invoke/ipcMain.handle (Zettlr: 186 invoke sites, 26 handle); (3) contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld (both apps; draw.io exposes 2 keys, Zettlr 5 incl. a raw send/sendSync/invoke/on passthrough plus process.env copy); (4) ipcRenderer.sendSync + event.returnValue (Zettlr: 6 sites on config/citeproc hot paths; draw.io 0); (5) event.sender as a WebContents handle (Zettlr: BrowserWindow.fromWebContents, sender.cut/copy/paste/startDrag/inspectElement); (6) webUtils.getPathForFile (Zettlr drop handling); (7) ipcRenderer EventEmitter surface beyond the API model (Zettlr calls ipcRenderer.setMaxListeners(100) at preload load). Zero corpus demand for MessageChannelMain/MessagePortMain/postMessage/utilityProcess/parentPort/IpcMainServiceWorker/exposeInIsolatedWorld/executeInMainWorld. Keld LIVE today: one macOS page-world facade window.keld.invoke (channel 1 only, 4096-byte payload, one pending invoke per WebView, host-minted correlation, WKContentWorld.defaultClientWorld isolated relay, KELD-WV-011 fail-closed) -> keld-core RendererBridgeEndpoint -> primary app-link CALL -> @keld/api channels.handle (echo descriptor only); @keld/electron ships app lifecycle only (no ipcMain, no preload injection, no renderer shim); keld-runtime VirtualPortRegistry (64-msg queue, 4 KiB inline, one-shot transfer, KELD-RUNTIME-004..011) is a Unix library/test surface with no renderer route; RoleRegistry has primary + app-bound only (window-bound is T4, not admitted); guard Principal::Webview{id,generation} exists but evaluate() denies every non-AppProcess principal before grant lookup and the manifest 'windows.*.channels' grant vocabulary (incl. the 'el:*' example in arch 03) is not live. TARGET per arch 02 §5: Electron string channels ride an 'el:*' compat namespace as EVENT/CALL frames with a postcard SCV codec; MessagePorts map to host-owned virtual ports; utilityProcess.fork is a request for a host-declared role with PID diagnostic-only; sendSync is a blocking CALL with deadline, rate-limited and dev-warned (KEL-127 binding). The six decision atoms below: (A1) string-channel carriage = one fixed kipc control channel pair per direction carrying the Electron channel string inside the SCV payload, guard-matched by host against 'el:' grant globs — never runtime-minted u16 ChannelIds; (A2) the current KEL-142 floor (single pending, 4 KiB, channel 1) cannot carry either corpus app and must be superseded by a specified renderer IPC floor v2 (multi-pending with host credit, send/on, bulk sized to draw.io export payloads) before any ipcRenderer facade is scored; (A3) contextBridge semantics (copied+frozen data, proxied functions, Error custom-prop loss, Symbol drop) are implemented ONCE in the isolated-world shim over the existing page/isolated relay; real isolation on WKWebView/WebKitGTK, documented ▲ emulation on WebView2 which has no isolated-world API; (A4) sender identity = host-minted (webview id, navigation generation) snapshotted at dispatch; senderFrame null on generation mismatch, event.reply silently dropped on stale generation (matches Electron sendToFrame -> false), subframe IPC ✘ because window.keld is main-frame only; (A5) sendSync needs a per-engine blocking primitive prototype before any contract claim — no primary source found for a synchronous page->host call on WKWebView/WebKitGTK; and the Electron returnValue-set-later behavior means the reply slot must stay open until set or deadline; (A6) utilityProcess/MessageChannelMain/IpcMainServiceWorker are deferred behind pinned-oracle conformance fixtures (KEL-75 AC7) with zero corpus demand; IpcMainServiceWorker and exposeInIsolatedWorld/executeInMainWorld/UtilityProcess.login go on the never/T3 list. Highest-risk semantic traps with independent oracles: on/handle are two namespaces for the same string (Zettlr registers both 'config-provider'); invoke error text is exactly "Error invoking remote method '<ch>': <error.toString()>" and no-handler is "...Error: No handler registered for '<ch>'"; duplicate handle throws synchronously; send throws synchronously on Function/Promise/Symbol/WeakMap/WeakSet while invoke rejects; dispatch order frame.ipc -> contents.ipc -> ipcMain and first-defined-wins for handle; MessagePortMain queues until start(); parentPort queues until first 'message' handler.

entities: ipcMain (Module, main): on, off, once, addListener, removeListener, removeAllListeners, handle, handleOnce, removeHandler

ipcRenderer (Module, renderer): on, off, once, addListener, removeListener, removeAllListeners, send, invoke, sendSync, postMessage, sendToHost (+ inherited EventEmitter surface not in the model, e.g. setMaxListeners used by Zettlr preload)
IpcMainServiceWorker (Class, main): on, once, removeListener, removeAllListeners, handle, handleOnce, removeHandler
MessagePortMain (Class, main, not exported): postMessage, start, close, event message, event close
parentPort (Module, utility; process.parentPort): postMessage, event message
utilityProcess (Module, main): fork(modulePath, args, options{env, execArgv, cwd, stdio, serviceName, allowLoadingUnsignedLibraries[macOS], respondToAuthRequestsFromMainProcess})
UtilityProcess (Class): postMessage, kill, events spawn/error[experimental]/exit/message/login, props pid/stdout/stderr
IpcMainEvent (Structure): type, processId, frameId, returnValue, sender, senderFrame[readonly, nullable], ports, reply
IpcMainInvokeEvent (Structure): type, processId, frameId, sender, senderFrame[readonly, nullable]
IpcMainServiceWorkerEvent (Structure): type, serviceWorker, versionId, session, returnValue, ports, reply

Cross-unit edge (owned by the webContents unit, semantically the main->renderer half of this family): webContents.send/postMessage/sendToFrame/ipc, webFrameMain.send/postMessage/ipc, events ipc-message/ipc-message-sync
deprecated_or_experimental: contextBridge.executeInMainWorld (stability_experimental)
UtilityProcess event 'error' (stability_experimental)
IpcMainServiceWorker* (documented as a 'subtle variation' of IpcMain for service workers; obtained via session.serviceWorkers — access path not stated in its own page; treat as T3/never for v1)
ipcRenderer.sendSync (documented 'last resort'; blocks the whole renderer)
File.path (removed; replaced by webUtils.getPathForFile)
electron_surface.platform_specific: utilityProcess.fork option allowLoadingUnsignedLibraries is macOS-only; UtilityProcess.kill uses SIGTERM on POSIX and GetExitCodeProcess/waitpid semantics for exit code; everything else in the family is engine-neutral in Electron because Chromium provides isolated worlds, structured clone and MessagePort transfer on all three OSes — Keld's engines do not (see platform_notes).

semantic_traps.member: ipcMain.on vs ipcMain.handle on the same channel string
semantic_traps.electron_behavior: [fact] Two independent namespaces: EventEmitter listeners (on/once) and a separate _invokeHandlers Map (handle). Zettlr registers BOTH ipcMain.on('config-provider') (for sendSync) and ipcMain.handle('config-provider') (for invoke). A sendSync/send reaches only listeners; an invoke reaches only the handler.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: A facade that keys both on one map (or on @keld/api channels.handle's single-handler-per-id rule) throws 'already has a handler' at Zettlr boot. The el: control plane must carry a kind discriminator (event | invoke | sync) and keep two registries.
semantic_traps.receipt: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electron/electron/v44.4.5/lib/browser/ipc-main-impl.ts (retrieved 2026-10-06): '_invokeHandlers: Map' separate from EventEmitter; corpus zettlr/source/app/service-providers/config/index.ts lines ~127-140
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Fixture registers on('x') and handle('x'); renderer sends send('x'), sendSync('x'), invoke('x'); assert listener fired exactly twice (send+sendSync), handler exactly once, no registration throw. Negative control: delete the handle registration -> invoke rejects with the no-handler text while send still delivers.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: [fact] handle throws synchronously `Attempted to register a second handler for '${method}'`; non-function throws TypeError; handleOnce wraps handle and calls removeHandler before invoking; removeHandler deletes if present (idempotent).
semantic_traps.keld_risk: @keld/api channels.handle currently throws KELD-API-001 'Echo channel already has a handler' — different text and a different exception site; draw.io uses ipcMain.once/removeListener heavily (dynamic per-export listeners), so removal semantics on string keys must be exact.
semantic_traps.receipt: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electron/electron/v44.4.5/lib/browser/ipc-main-impl.ts (retrieved 2026-10-06): 'throw new Error(`Attempted to register a second handler for \'${method}\'`)'
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Register handle('a') twice -> second throws with that exact message synchronously (not a rejected promise); handleOnce('b') then invoke twice -> first resolves, second rejects no-handler; removeHandler('zzz') does not throw.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: [fact] Main replies {error: error.toString()} after console.error; renderer throws `new Error(`Error invoking remote method '${channel}': ${error}`)`; with no handler the error is `No handler registered for '${channel}'`. Docs: 'only the message property from the original error is provided to the renderer'; 'The Error object in the renderer process will not be the same as the one thrown in the main process.' Handler lookup order: mainFrame.handle -> contents.handle -> ipcMain.handle, first defined wins.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: @keld/api's handleEchoCall collapses every failure to CallError KELD-API-001 'application channel call failed' and never carries the handler's error.toString(); apps that branch on err.message (Zettlr catches generically; draw.io not applicable) get a different string. Also leaking Keld codes/stack into the renderer would be a new disclosure path — Electron leaks only toString().
semantic_traps.receipt: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electron/electron/v44.4.5/lib/browser/ipc-dispatch.ts and lib/renderer/api/ipc-renderer.ts (retrieved 2026-10-06); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electron/electron/v44.4.5/docs/api/ipc-main.md 'Errors thrown through handle in the main process are not transparent'
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Handler throws Object.assign(new Error('boom'), {code: 'X'}); renderer assert err.message === "Error invoking remote method 'c': Error: boom" and err.code === undefined; invoke('nohandler') -> message ends with "Error: No handler registered for 'nohandler'". Negative control: a facade returning KELD-API-001 text fails both asserts.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: [fact] 'Sending Functions, Promises, Symbols, WeakMaps, or WeakSets will throw an exception'; DOM objects / Electron objects throw; 'prototype chains will not be included'. send/sendSync throw synchronously; invoke is `async invoke(...)` so the same failure surfaces as a rejected promise.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: A JSON passthrough silently drops Map/Set/Date/BigInt/typed arrays/undefined and never throws on functions (silent divergence); a facade that throws asynchronously for send changes the caller's control flow. SCV codec must reproduce the sync-throw vs reject split.
semantic_traps.receipt: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electron/electron/v44.4.5/docs/api/ipc-renderer.md lines 201-215 (sendSync text) and invoke section (retrieved 2026-10-06); lib/renderer/api/ipc-renderer.ts 'async invoke'
semantic_traps.test_oracle: send('c', () => {}) throws synchronously (try/catch, no await); invoke('c', () => {}) returns a promise that rejects; send('c', new Map([[1,2]])) delivers a Map (instanceof Map in main); send('c', new (class K { m(){} })()) delivers a plain object without m. Differential oracle: compare against globalThis.structuredClone in Bun and in the WebKit page.

semantic_traps.member: Dispatch ordering: ipc-message -> frame.ipc -> contents.ipc -> ipcMain
semantic_traps.electron_behavior: [fact] 'IPC messages sent with ipcRenderer.send, sendSync or postMessage will be delivered in the following order: 1. contents.on("ipc-message") 2. contents.mainFrame.on(channel) 3. contents.ipc.on(channel) 4. ipcMain.on(channel)'. Emitters are looked up by frameTreeNodeId so IPCs sent during unload still dispatch.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: A facade with only global ipcMain is fine for both corpus apps today but if contents.ipc/frame.ipc are added later with a different order, ordering-sensitive apps break silently; ordering is a tested contract (crates/keld-compat/AGENTS.md).
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Register listeners at all four levels appending to an array; one send -> array equals ['ipc-message','frame','contents','ipcMain']. Negative control: reverse registration order must not change delivery order.

semantic_traps.member: sendSync / event.returnValue timing and missing listener
semantic_traps.electron_behavior: [fact] returnValue is a setter that sends the reply the moment it is assigned (`set: (value) => event._replyChannel.sendReply(value)`), so a listener may set it asynchronously after returning and the renderer still unblocks; with zero listeners on every emitter Electron logs `WebContents #N called ipcRenderer.sendSync() with 'ch' channel without listeners.` [unknown] what the blocked renderer receives when returnValue is never set (docs silent; source suggests reply is bound to the event object's lifetime).

decisions.question: How do arbitrary Electron string channels (ipcMain.on('export-finalize') registered at runtime) ride kipc, whose channels are u16 handles resolved at handshake, without minting per-string channel ids or bypassing the guard?
decisions.proposed_answer: One fixed, generated kipc control channel per direction for the compat namespace (e.g. el.r2m for renderer->main CALL/EVENT/sync-CALL, el.m2r for host-routed EVENT to a webview generation, el.ports for virtual-port frames); the Electron channel string, kind discriminator (event | invoke | sync | ports) and SCV-encoded args are payload fields in a generated (KEL-98-style) Rust-owned struct. The host guard matches the string against the webview's windows.<name>.channels 'el:<glob>' grant before forwarding (default-deny), so the string is authorization input at the host and only a routing key in the Bun role. Owner: arch 02 §5 (spec amendment) + keld-guard channel-grant vocabulary (KEL-102) + @keld/api registry split (listeners vs invoke handlers). Observable contract: an ungranted string never reaches ipcMain; a granted one dispatches in Electron order. First falsifier: a renderer send on a string outside the glob that still invokes a Bun listener.
evidence: [fact] arch 02 §2: 'channels are u16 handles resolved at handshake from schema names (string names never travel per-call)'; channel-table exchange is not live; ChannelId doc in frame.rs says v0 hardcodes echo.

[fact] arch 02 §5: 'ipcRenderer.send/on ⇄ EVENT frames on a compat channel namespace (el:*)'; arch 03 §2 manifest example 'channels: ["notes.*", "el:*"]' and 'Channel grants are a separate, not-yet-live vocabulary'.

[fact] Electron dispatch keys purely on the string (lib/browser/ipc-dispatch.ts targets.find(_invokeHandlers.has(channel))); draw.io registers/removes string listeners dynamically per export (electron.js ~3132-3387).
[fact] keld-guard evaluate() currently denies every non-AppProcess principal before grant lookup (learning 2026-08-14), so webview channel grants require new guard code, not configuration.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Minting a u16 ChannelId per Electron string at runtime: unbounded allocation on a hot path, no live channel table, violates 'string names never travel per-call' only nominally while needing a per-string handshake; (b) Facade-side allowlist in @keld/electron: bypasses keld-guard (sacred default-deny); (c) JSON passthrough of args: loses SCV parity (see A4/A5 traps).
decisions.confidence: medium — the namespace and grant shape are already written in arch 02/03; the open part is the guard vocabulary implementation and whether the host needs to decode any SCV (it should not: match on string + byte length, forward opaque bytes).
decisions.unknowns: Which Linear id owns the windows.*.channels grant vocabulary (KEL-102 vs KEL-97 vs new); whether audit:'all' logging requires a Rust SCV decoder (would pull Electron-isms into keld-ipc — arch 04 §3 forbids); glob grammar for 'el:' (reuse the '**' vetted matcher or a channel-specific one).

decisions.question: Can the live KEL-142 renderer floor (window.keld.invoke only, channel 1, 4096 bytes, one pending call per WebView) carry the ipcRenderer facade for the first two corpus apps, or must a renderer IPC floor v2 be specified first?
decisions.proposed_answer: It cannot; a specified floor v2 is a prerequisite and should be the first ticket in this family's sequence. Required additions, each falsifiable: (1) N pending invokes per WebView with a host-enforced credit window (not a renderer queue) — Zettlr fires 186 invoke sites and draw.io multiplexes rendererReq with its own reqId; (2) window.keld.send (fire-and-forget EVENT) and window.keld.on (host->renderer EVENT fan-out) — draw.io's entire protocol is send/on/once; (3) a payload bound sized by measurement to draw.io export round-trips (XML/PNG data in event.reply('export-success', data)) with chunking or a bulk adapter, not 4 KiB; (4) declared channel = the el: control channel, not channel 1. Owner: KEL-80 (Backlog) bounded slice + arch 05 §2 destination shape; implementation seam = extend wv_link.rs envelope kinds and RendererBridgeEndpoint, never a second renderer protocol (KEL-142 Linear text). Observable contract: draw.io preload loads unmodified and one export round-trip completes. First falsifier: two concurrent invokes from one page both settle correctly on the v2 floor; on the v1 floor the second rejects KELD-WV-011 'another renderer invoke is already pending'.
evidence: [fact] macos_bridge.rs PAGE_FACADE_SCRIPT: 'if (channel !== 1) return fail(...)', 'payload.byteLength > 4096', 'if (pending !== null) return fail("another renderer invoke is already pending")'; KEL-142 spec §4.1 'Exactly one renderer-originated invoke may be pending per WebView'.
[fact] corpus: zettlr 186 ipcRenderer.invoke sites; drawio preload exposes request/registerMsgListener/sendMessage/listenOnce over send/on/once only; drawio main replies export data via event.reply.
[fact] arch 05 §2 destination window.keld {invoke, send, on, stream, meta}; arch 02 §2 GRANT frames exist in the schema with no live sender/receiver.

[fact] KEL-80 Linear acceptance (2026-09-20): WriteQueue has no aggregate pending-call/byte budget; '4 KiB is the present virtual-port inline ceiling; 1 MiB/16 MiB arms belong only to protocols that actually admit them'.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Serialize all Electron traffic through the single-pending floor with a renderer-side queue: violates KEL-142 §6 'slow consumer cannot grow a renderer queue' and would deadlock draw.io's listener-then-reply patterns; (b) Build the ipcRenderer facade against JSON postMessage directly to the host without the wv-link envelope: second renderer-routing protocol, forbidden by KEL-142/KEL-80 text.
decisions.confidence: high that v1 is insufficient (direct code facts); medium on the exact v2 numbers (need the A2 prototype measurements).
decisions.unknowns: Measured per-engine cost of WKScriptMessage/PostWebMessage copies at 64 KiB–4 MiB; whether draw.io export payloads exceed 16 MiB (app-link MAX_FRAME_LEN) in practice; exact credit numbers (must come from KEL-80's ownership ledger, not guessed).

decisions.question: Where and how is contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld implemented so that copied-and-frozen data, proxied functions, Error custom-property loss and Symbol dropping hold on three engines, given only WKWebView/WebKitGTK have isolated worlds?
decisions.proposed_answer: Implement the preload runtime once as the isolated-world shim (the realm the KEL-142 ISOLATED_BRIDGE_SCRIPT already owns): preload executes there with a shimmed require('electron') returning {contextBridge, ipcRenderer, webUtils, webFrame-subset} (the sandbox-preload module map Electron documents); exposeInMainWorld serializes the api graph into a frozen proxy tree installed into the page world via the existing host->page evaluate-in-world path (macOS evaluate_in_world; WebKitGTK equivalent), with function calls relayed over the existing page<->isolated postMessage channel and results copied (no shared object identity). On WebView2 there is no isolated world: the same shim runs in the page world before page scripts but keeps preload state in closures and installs the identical frozen proxy tree — a documented ▲ 'isolation-emulated' cell, never silent. Owner: @keld/electron renderer shim (new package surface) + keld-wv injection; conformance cell per contextBridge row of Electron's type table. Observable contract: Object.isFrozen(window.api) on all engines; page cannot reach preload closures on WKWebView/WebKitGTK; on WebView2 the scoreboard says ▲. First falsifier: page mutates window.api.o.a and the preload observes the change.
evidence: [fact] context-bridge.md: 'Function values are proxied to the other context and all other values are copied and frozen'; type table rows for Error/Promise/Function/Symbol/Element; 'contextBridge API can only be used when contextIsolation is enabled' (context-bridge.ts).
[fact] sandbox.md: sandboxed preload require is limited to electron {contextBridge, crashReporter, ipcRenderer, nativeImage, webFrame, webUtils}, events, timers, url.
[fact] ICoreWebView2 reference lists no isolated-world API; WKContentWorld doc (macOS 11+); WebKitGTK register_script_message_handler doc notes separate *_in_world variants.
[fact] arch 04 §3 item 3 already commits to 'mapped to real isolated-world exposure where the engine supports it, documented emulation otherwise'.
[fact] corpus: drawio preload relies on the isolated world to keep a navigation listener page scripts cannot remove; Zettlr preload exposes a raw per-method passthrough and process.env copy.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Run preload in the page world on every engine for uniformity: downgrades macOS/Linux isolation that already exists (KEL-139 requires trusted bridge logic outside page JS); (b) Deep-clone via JSON: drops Map/Set/Date/typed arrays and Promise/Function proxies that the Electron table supports; (c) Transpile apps' preloads at migrate time to remove contextBridge: code change, violates 'config-only changes' destination.
decisions.confidence: medium-high — engine facts are primary-sourced; the proxy design is standard but its WebView2 security posture must be labeled, not argued away.
decisions.unknowns: Whether WKContentWorld function proxies can be made synchronous for the page (Electron's proxied functions return promises when the target returns promises but are otherwise synchronous calls) — on Keld the page->isolated relay is postMessage (async), so synchronous return values of exposed functions (Zettlr's config.get returns sendSync result synchronously) depend on A5.

decisions.question: What are event.sender / event.senderFrame / event.reply / processId / frameId under Keld's host-minted (webview id, navigation generation) identity, and what happens on navigation races, stale replies and subframes?
decisions.proposed_answer: sender = a facade WebContents object keyed by the host webview id (stable across navigations, as Electron's WebContents is), with the methods the corpus calls (send, cut/copy/paste/selectAll, inspectElement, startDrag) delegated to host operations; senderFrame = a facade WebFrameMain carrying url/origin snapshotted from the host navigation registry at dispatch time and null when the dispatch-time generation differs from the live generation; event.reply = host-routed EVENT bound to (id, generation-at-dispatch); the host silently drops it when the generation rotated (Electron's sendToFrame returns false without throwing); event.sender.send targets the live main frame; processId/frameId = opaque host ids (not OS PIDs). Subframe-originated IPC is ✘ for now because window.keld is main-frame only (KEL-142 AC 'an iframe has no own window.keld'). Owner: keld-core window/webview registry (TARGET, KEL-139/KEL-142 lineage) for identity; keld-compat 'webContents routing identity' (arch 04 §3 item 4) for the facade; conformance cells cite ipc-main-event.md. Observable contract: draw.io validateSender(event.senderFrame) accepts same-origin app frames and rejects after navigation. First falsifier: a listener receives a senderFrame whose url is taken from the message payload (forged-url fixture passes).
evidence: [fact] ipc-main-event.md: senderFrame 'May be null if accessed after the frame has either navigated or been destroyed'; reply 'will send an IPC message to the renderer frame that sent the original message'.
[fact] web-contents.ts sendToFrame: returns false when getWebFrame finds no frame belonging to the contents; ipc-dispatch.ts addReplyToEvent uses sendToFrame([processId, frameId]).
[fact] keld-guard Principal::Webview{id, generation}: 'Bumped on navigation so stale grants cannot carry over'; arch 02 §7 'pending replies to the old principal drop'.

[fact] corpus: drawio validateSender returns false on null and prefix-matches frame.url; Zettlr BrowserWindow.fromWebContents(event.sender), event.sender.cut(), event.senderFrame ?? undefined passed to Menu.popup.
[fact] KEL-142 spec acceptance: 'an iframe has no own window.keld'.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Throw 'Object has been destroyed' from senderFrame access after navigation: Electron documents null, not throw; (b) Deliver reply to the new document after navigation: violates arch 02 §7 generation drop and Electron's frame-bound reply; (c) Expose OS PIDs as processId: PID is diagnostic-only per arch 04 §3.1.
decisions.unknowns: Electron's behavior of webContents.send on a destroyed WebContents (throw vs no-op) was not verified from docs in this pass; whether the host registry can snapshot frame url/origin for every dispatch without allocation on the hot path (arch 02 §6).

decisions.question: Can ipcRenderer.sendSync be a blocking CALL with deadline (KEL-127) on system webviews that only offer asynchronous page->host messaging, and what reply semantics must it keep?
decisions.proposed_answer: Unknown until prototyped; no primary source in this pass shows a synchronous page->host call on WKWebView or WebKitGTK. Proposed route: prototype three engine primitives — (mac/linux) synchronous XMLHttpRequest to a host-served custom-scheme endpoint bound to the document nonce; (windows) WebView2 host-object sync proxy — each measured for RTT, deadline enforcement and UI-thread behavior; then freeze sendSync as: blocking CALL on the el: sync kind, host deadline (reuse APP_LINK_IO_DEADLINE class, exact value from measurement), per-document rate limit with a dev-mode console warning, reply slot held open until returnValue is set or the deadline fires (Electron's setter sends on assignment, even after the listener returned), missing-listener -> dev warning plus deadline error. If no engine primitive proves viable, the cell is ▲ 'async-only; requires keld.compat.ts sendSync: "reject"' with an explicit diagnostic — never a silent async rewrite (KEL-127). Owner: arch 02 §5 sendSync bullet + keld-wv per-engine adapter + @keld/electron; corpus demand: Zettlr (config/citeproc hot paths), draw.io none. First falsifier: Zettlr's window.config.get() returns a Promise instead of a value.
evidence: [fact] ipc-renderer.md: 'Sending a synchronous message will block the whole renderer process until the reply is received, so use this method only as a last resort'; ipc-dispatch.ts returnValue setter sends on assignment; console.warn when no listener anywhere.
[fact] briefing KEL-127: 'sendSync async replacement changes caller contract (must stay blocking CALL with deadline, rate-limited, dev-warned)'; arch 02 §5 same.
[fact] corpus zettlr: 6 sendSync sites, all behind contextBridge-exposed synchronous functions (config.get/set, getCitationCallback) whose callers expect a synchronous return.
[fact] WKContentWorld/WKScriptMessageHandler, WebKitGTK script-message-handler and WebView2 WebMessageReceived are all asynchronous post/receive APIs per their docs fetched this pass.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Rewrite sendSync to return a Promise and patch callers at migrate time: forbidden by KEL-127 and not config-only; (b) Atomics.wait on a SharedArrayBuffer with a worker relay: requires cross-origin isolation headers on the app origin and a worker-side async channel — possible but unmeasured; park as a prototype variant; (c) Busy-wait polling: blocks the UI thread with no deadline guarantee.

decisions.question: When do utilityProcess/UtilityProcess/parentPort, MessageChannelMain/MessagePortMain and IpcMainServiceWorker get built, and against what oracle?
decisions.proposed_answer: Defer all three behind (1) zero measured corpus demand (draw.io 0, Zettlr 0, quick-start 0) and (2) KEL-75 AC7's requirement that facade behavior be proven against pinned-oracle conformance fixtures first. Sequence: publish ✘ cells with denominator honesty now; land a MessagePortMain conformance fixture (queue-until-start, FIFO, close event, postMessage-only transfer) mapped onto RoleRegistry virtual ports as the first Tier-2 slice because its generic owner already exists; utilityProcess.fork follows as a thin request for an app-bound role once KEL-75 T4 window-bound roles and the role grant subset are live (window-bound is not admitted in RoleOwner today); IpcMainServiceWorker stays documented-never for v1 (SW transport unproven on WKWebView custom schemes). Divergences to pre-declare: QueueFull (64) and 4 KiB inline as ▲; PID diagnostic-only; fork options that widen authority -> scored ✘. First falsifier: a fork({env}) child observing the env, or a transferred port reaching a stale generation.
evidence: [fact] corpus usage scans and greps: no MessageChannelMain/MessagePortMain/utilityProcess/parentPort/postMessage(transfer) hits in any of the three apps.
[fact] KEL-75 AC7: facade observable events/transfer validation/queue-start/disconnect must match a recorded pinned-oracle conformance entry; 'An operation without an oracle remains unknown'.
[fact] role.rs RoleOwner: Primary, AppBound only; 'window-bound is T4 and is not admitted here'; arch 02 §2 'T3 virtual ports remain a Unix library/test surface'.

[fact] research 186 row 7: utilityProcess forwards cwd/env/stdio/session and structured-clones arbitrary values with port disentangling; gap 6 requires strict-profile negative tests for inherited cwd/env, raw PID/kill, session/network authority, transferred ports across generations.
[fact] briefing: WKWebView lacks Service Worker on custom schemes (WebKit 206741); IpcMainServiceWorker page states it is a variation of IpcMain targeted at service workers.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Build utilityProcess.fork now as a child_process.fork facade for Bun: a parallel process model (invariant 4 / briefing never-list 'raw child_process from strict roles'); (b) Implement MessagePortMain over DOM MessageChannel inside one Bun role without host mediation: 'Browser and Bun endpoints never connect directly' (arch 02 §5); (c) Map IpcMainServiceWorker onto the app-link: no SW substrate exists to send from.
decisions.confidence: high for deferral and never-classification; medium on slice order.
decisions.unknowns: Whether the 20-app Tier-2 corpus (not yet declared) contains utilityProcess users that would reorder this; whether KEL-79's resource transport will ever admit Service Workers on any engine.

never_list.surface: IpcMainServiceWorker, IpcMainServiceWorkerEvent, IpcMainServiceWorkerInvokeEvent (v1)
never_list.rationale: Requires Service Workers on the app resource transport; WKWebView lacks SW on custom schemes (WebKit 206741) and WebView2 has virtual-host SW limits; zero corpus demand; revisit only if KEL-79 proves SW transport (T3).

never_list.surface: contextBridge.exposeInIsolatedWorld(worldId, ...) and contextBridge.executeInMainWorld
never_list.rationale: Chromium-numeric world ids (0/999/1000+) have no engine-neutral meaning; executeInMainWorld is experimental; zero corpus demand.

never_list.surface: UtilityProcess 'login' event / respondToAuthRequestsFromMainProcess
never_list.rationale: Network auth challenges are the KEL-89 auth broker's; a role answering HTTP auth is ambient network authority.

never_list.surface: utilityProcess.fork options as authority: env, cwd, execArgv, allowLoadingUnsignedLibraries, arbitrary modulePath outside the declared bundle
never_list.rationale: Research 186 row 7 / KEL-75 facade boundary: 'allowLoadingUnsignedLibraries can never silently weaken a strict profile'; strict roles have no inherited env/cwd; translated to reviewed policy or scored ✘.

never_list.surface: UtilityProcess.pid as identity, reap or routing input
never_list.rationale: arch 04 §3.1: 'A returned PID is diagnostic only, never a Keld identity or control handle.'

never_list.surface: Raw child_process/exec facade behind utilityProcess
never_list.rationale: Briefing never-list; parallel process model is a fifth unique.

never_list.surface: Exposing the whole ipcRenderer object over contextBridge, or ipcRenderer.send/on without a channel grant
never_list.rationale: Electron itself yields {} for the module; the tutorial calls raw exposure 'a powerful API without any kind of argument filtering'; Keld additionally requires the el: grant at the host.

never_list.surface: Renderer-side or facade-side channel allowlists in place of keld-guard
never_list.rationale: Default-deny is sacred; the guard is the sole owner of channel grants (arch 03 §1).

never_list.surface: Direct renderer-to-role transport for MessagePort transfer
never_list.rationale: arch 02 §5 / KEL-75: 'Browser and Bun endpoints never connect directly'; ports are host-owned.

never_list.surface: Silent async rewrite of sendSync
never_list.rationale: KEL-127: caller contract must remain a blocking CALL with deadline; any deviation is an explicit quirks flag or ▲ cell.

never_list.surface: process.env / process.argv copied into the main world by preload (Zettlr pattern) under the strict profile
never_list.rationale: Strict preload realms have no ambient env; allowed only as a visibly labeled legacy-profile cell.

never_list.surface: SCV decoding in keld-core/keld-ipc for routing
never_list.rationale: arch 04 §3 / crates/keld-compat AGENTS: no Electron-isms in keld-core/keld-ipc; the host matches channel string + length and forwards opaque bytes.

receipts.claim: ipcMain.handle: 'If listener returns a Promise, the eventual result of the promise will be returned as a reply'; 'Errors thrown through handle in the main process are not transparent as they are serialized and only the message property from the original error is provided to the renderer process'; 'To reply to a synchronous message, you need to set event.returnValue'; 'event.reply(...) will automatically handle messages coming from frames that aren't the main frame (e.g. iframes) whereas event.sender.send(...) will always send to the main frame'.

ipcRenderer.send/sendSync: 'Arguments will be serialized with the Structured Clone Algorithm, just like window.postMessage, so prototype chains will not be included. Sending Functions, Promises, Symbols, WeakMaps, or WeakSets will throw an exception.' 'Sending non-standard JavaScript types such as DOM objects or special Electron objects will throw an exception.' sendSync: 'Sending a synchronous message will block the whole renderer process until the reply is received, so use this method only as a last resort.' invoke: 'If the handler in the main process throws an error, the promise returned by invoke will reject'; 'The Error object in the renderer process will not be the same as the one thrown in the main process.' postMessage transfers MessagePort objects 'available in the main process as MessagePortMain objects'. on: 'Do not expose the event argument to the renderer for security reasons!'

IpcMainImpl: handle throws `Attempted to register a second handler for '${method}'`; non-function throws TypeError; handleOnce = handle + removeHandler before calling; constructor registers this.on('error', () => {}) so a channel named 'error' does not throw; _invokeHandlers is a Map separate from EventEmitter listeners.

Dispatch: event.reply = event.sender.sendToFrame([processId, frameId], ...); returnValue is a setter that calls event._replyChannel.sendReply(value) on assignment; invoke picks the first of [webFrameMain.ipc, sender.ipc, ipcMain] whose _invokeHandlers has the channel; errors reply {error: error.toString()} after console.error; no handler -> `No handler registered for '${channel}'`; sendSync with no listeners anywhere logs `WebContents #${id} called ipcRenderer.sendSync() with '${channel}' channel without listeners.`; '-ipc-ports' wraps transferred ports as MessagePortMain and emits on the frame/contents/ipcMain emitters.

IpcRenderer extends EventEmitter; invoke is `async invoke(...)` and throws `Error invoking remote method '${channel}': ${error}` when the reply carries error; send/sendSync call the native binding synchronously.

webContents.send/postMessage delegate to mainFrame; sendToFrame returns false (no throw) when the frame is not found or does not belong to the contents ('Frame ids are global; only address frames that belong to |contents|').

contextBridge: api must be Function/string/number/Array/boolean/object thereof; 'Function values are proxied to the other context and all other values are copied and frozen. Any data / primitives sent in the API become immutable'; Error: 'any custom properties on the Error object will be lost'; Function: 'Prototype modifications are dropped. Sending classes or constructors will not work'; Symbol: 'Symbols cannot be copied across contexts so they are dropped'; 'Attempting to send the entire ipcRenderer module as an object over the contextBridge will result in an empty object'; exposeInIsolatedWorld worldId: '0 is the default world, 999 is the world used by Electron's contextIsolation feature'; executeInMainWorld returns 'A copy of the resulting value'.

context-bridge.ts: every method calls checkContextIsolationEnabled which throws 'contextBridge API can only be used when contextIsolation is enabled'; exposeInMainWorld = binding.exposeAPIInWorld(0, key, api).

Context isolation 'has been enabled by default since Electron 12'; preload's window 'is actually a different object than the website would have access to'; exposing ipcRenderer directly 'would allow any website to send arbitrary IPC messages'.

Sandboxed preload require can import only electron {contextBridge, crashReporter, ipcRenderer, nativeImage, webFrame, webUtils}, events, timers, url; polyfills Buffer/process/setImmediate; 'you will not be able to use CommonJS modules to separate your preload script into multiple files'.

IPC tutorial: 'We don't directly expose the whole ipcRenderer.invoke API for security reasons'; sendSync 'will block the renderer process until a reply is received'; 'don't just pass the callback to ipcRenderer.on as this will leak ipcRenderer via event.sender'; renderer-to-renderer via main broker or MessagePort; 'Electron's IPC implementation uses the HTML standard Structured Clone Algorithm'.

IpcMainEvent: processId 'internal ID of the renderer process'; frameId; returnValue 'Set this to the value to be returned in a synchronous message'; senderFrame 'May be null if accessed after the frame has either navigated or been destroyed' (Readonly); ports; reply 'send an IPC message to the renderer frame that sent the original message'. IpcMainInvokeEvent: type, processId, frameId, sender, senderFrame (same nullability).

webFrameMain: delivery order 'contents.on(ipc-message) -> contents.mainFrame.on(channel) -> contents.ipc.on(channel) -> ipcMain.on(channel)'; invoke handler order 'contents.mainFrame.handle -> contents.handle -> ipcMain.handle, first one that is defined will be called'; frame.isDestroyed(); frame.detached; frame.url; frame.origin per RFC 6454; frame.send throws on Functions/Promises/Symbols/WeakMaps/WeakSets.

webContents.send: Structured Clone, 'Sending non-standard JavaScript types such as DOM objects or special Electron objects will throw an exception'; contents.ipc 'An IpcMain scoped to just IPC messages sent from this WebContents' with the same four-step order; events ipc-message / ipc-message-sync; contents.isDestroyed().

MessagePortMain 'is the main-process-side equivalent of the DOM MessagePort object' using Node EventEmitter; start: 'Messages will be queued until this method is called'; close: 'Disconnects the port'; event 'close': 'Emitted when the remote end of a MessagePortMain object becomes disconnected'. MessageChannelMain 'create a pair of connected MessagePortMain objects'. lib/browser/message-port-main.ts rewraps incoming ports as MessagePortMain and unwraps on postMessage.

message-ports tutorial: 'MessagePortMain queues messages until the .start() method has been called'; 'Electron adds one feature to MessagePort that isn't present on the web ... the close event'; 'the usual IPC methods like send and invoke cannot be used to transfer MessagePorts, only the postMessage methods can'.

utilityProcess.fork options: env 'Default is process.env'; execArgv; cwd; stdio 'Default is inherit', stdin other than ignore 'will result in an error'; serviceName; allowLoadingUnsignedLibraries (macOS); respondToAuthRequestsFromMainProcess; 'utilityProcess.fork can only be called after the ready event has been emitted on App'; kill 'uses SIGTERM but will ensure the process is reaped'; pid 'Until the child process has spawned successfully, the value is undefined. When the child process exits, then the value is undefined after the exit event'; 'No matter if you listen to the error event, the exit event will be emitted'; exit code from waitpid/GetExitCodeProcess.
parentPort 'is only available as a property of the process object'; 'Messages received on this port will be queued up until a handler is registered for this event'.

webUtils.getPathForFile: 'In the case where the object passed in is not a File object an exception is thrown. In the case where the File object passed in was constructed in JS and is not backed by a file on disk an empty string is returned.'

IpcMainServiceWorker: 'Communicate asynchronously from the main process to service workers'; 'This API is a subtle variation of IpcMain—targeted for communicating with service workers'; members on/once/removeListener/removeAllListeners/handle/handleOnce/removeHandler; access path not stated on this page.

Process model: preload scripts 'execute in a renderer process before its web content begins loading'; 'Context Isolation means that preload scripts are isolated from the renderer's main world'; the utility process 'runs in a Node.js environment' and 'can establish a communication channel with a renderer process using MessagePort'.

WKContentWorld: 'An object that defines a scope of execution for JavaScript code, and which you use to prevent conflicts between different scripts'; available macOS 11.0+; members page, defaultClient, world(name:).

ICoreWebView2 lists AddScriptToExecuteOnDocumentCreated ('run after the global object has been created, but before the HTML document has been parsed'), ExecuteScript, PostWebMessageAsJson/AsString, add_WebMessageReceived; no method mentioning an isolated world or content world.

webkit_user_content_manager_register_script_message_handler (since 2.8) exposes window.webkit.messageHandlers.<name>.postMessage(value) delivered via the script-message-received signal; registration fails if the name is already registered; separate *_in_world variants exist.

Keld arch 02 §5 compat mapping: el:* namespace for send/on; invoke/handle as CALL/REPLY with postcard SCV; MessagePorts as host-owned virtual-port pairs with one-shot receiver-bound transfer; utilityProcess.fork as a host-declared role request with PID diagnostic only; 'sync sendSync supported but rate-limited + dev-warned (it's a blocking CALL with a deadline)'. §2: channels are u16 handles, channel table not live, GRANT has no live sender/receiver. §7: navigation rotates the principal generation and pending replies to the old principal drop.

Keld arch 04 §3: preload & renderer shim 'mapped to real isolated-world exposure where the engine supports it, documented emulation otherwise'; §3.1 utilityProcess/MessageChannelMain stay facades over host-declared roles and host-owned ports; PID diagnostic only; 'These contracts are not live in v0'. ipcMain/contextBridge are 'later slices'; keld migrate not live.

Keld arch 03 §1-2: webview principal = host WebView id + navigation generation; manifest example 'windows.main.channels: ["notes.*", "el:*"]'; 'Channel grants are a separate, not-yet-live vocabulary'; the 'roles' key is ignored by the current parser. arch 05 §2: window.keld {invoke, send, on, stream, meta} is 'Destination; not implemented in the live hello backends'; @keld/electron's renderer shim implements ipcRenderer/contextBridge over it.

KEL-142 spec §4.1 renderer floor (channel nonzero u16, only channel 1, payload <= 4096 snapshotted, opts unsupported, exactly one pending invoke per WebView, host mints corr id, no replay, window.keld frozen/non-configurable, no send/on/stream/meta); §4.2 channels.handle contract; §5 WKContentWorld required, page-world fallback forbidden; §6 ordering rules; §7 KELD-WV-011 / KELD-API-001.

KEL-75 spec: host owns VirtualPort pairs; receiver 'must be an already authenticated role or a live webview/navigation generation'; FIFO per generation, one-shot transfer, host-visible close/disconnect, bounded queues; facade maps MessageChannelMain/MessagePortMain/webContents.postMessage/utilityProcess.postMessage onto it; AC7 pinned-oracle facade conformance; 'allowLoadingUnsignedLibraries can never silently weaken a strict profile'; PID diagnostic only.

Live code: macos_bridge.rs PAGE_FACADE_SCRIPT/ISOLATED_BRIDGE_SCRIPT (channel 1, 4096 bytes, single pending, pagehide rejection, defaultClientWorld + pageWorld, macOS 11 requirement); wv_link.rs MAX_RENDERER_PAYLOAD_LEN 4096, envelope Bind|Invoke; @keld/api channels.handle accepts only echoChannel and rejects LIFECYCLE_CHANNEL 3; echo-call.ts collapses handler failure to KELD-API-001; @keld/electron index exports app only; virtual_port.rs DEFAULT_PORT_QUEUE_CAPACITY 64, MAX_PORT_MESSAGE_LEN 4096, KELD-RUNTIME-004..011; role.rs RoleOwner Primary|AppBound ('window-bound is T4 and is not admitted here'); keld-guard evaluate denies non-AppProcess before grant lookup; PermissionsManifest reads only 'app'.

verdicts.reason: The carriage shape (fixed control channel(s), Electron string + kind + SCV bytes inside the payload, no runtime-minted u16 ids, host-side guard before forwarding) is consistent with arch 02 §2/§5 and the four-uniques floor and is not contradicted. Two load-bearing sub-claims are contradicted by the sources: (1) 'the namespace and grant shape are already written in arch 02/03' and 'Owner: ... keld-guard channel-grant vocabulary (KEL-102)'. docs/specs/kel102-host-guard-enforcement.md lines 33-36 list 'Adding roles, window grants, channel grants, manifest generation ...' as explicit NON-goals; KEL-102 Linear scope is manifest loading + privileged dispatch only; KEL-97 Linear owns role-link principal binding only. No Linear owner for windows.*.channels exists. (2) The documented channel-grant direction is not string-glob matching: docs/architecture/03-security.md line 172-173 says 'Channel grants connect to the schema layer: a channel's declared capability set (from .k.ts contracts) must be ⊆ the caller's grants', and line 121-123 says `**` is the only wildcard a scope has, 'a lone * matches literally', and channel grants are 'a separate, not-yet-live vocabulary'. The manifest example `"el:*"` (line 97) is therefore an illustrative string whose matching semantics are undefined by any live owner; under the existing path/URL matcher it would match the literal text `el:*`. Also keld-guard already has the deny variant for this (`DenyReason::ChannelForbidden { channel }` = KELD-GUARD003, lib.rs lines 293, 320, 361) which `evaluate()` never returns (lib.rs 699-706 denies every non-AppProcess as KELD-GUARD006 first; keld-cli permissions.rs line 64 'Unused in v0'); the object proposes new guard code without naming this existing owner.
