verdicts.reason: The live floor's three limits are code facts, and both corpus apps violate all three on their happy paths: Zettlr issues 186 `ipcRenderer.invoke` sites (any two overlapping settle the second as KELD-WV-011 busy); draw.io's preload uses only send/on/once (no invoke exists in the floor) and replies export data (`event.reply('export-success', data)` with base64 PNG/JPEG or XML) and whole-file contents (`readFile` → `mainResp`) that are not 4 KiB-bounded. arch 05 §2 already names `window.keld {invoke, send, on, stream, meta}` as the destination and `FrameKind::Grant` has no live sender, so a specified floor v2 is a genuine prerequisite, not optional polish.
verdicts.evidence: [fact] crates/keld-wv/src/wkwebview/macos_bridge.rs:69 `if (channel !== 1) return fail(...)`, :71 `payload.byteLength > 4096`, :72 `if (pending !== null) return fail("another renderer invoke is already pending")`; docs/specs/kel142-macos-renderer-bridge-api.md lines 114-126. [fact] corpus grep: zettlr/source `ipcRenderer.invoke` = 186, `ipcMain.handle` = 26, `webContents.send(` = 49; drawio-desktop `ipcRenderer.invoke` = 0, `ipcRenderer.send(` 2 / `.on(` 3 / `.once(` 1 in electron-preload.js. [fact] drawio electron.js:3259/3337/3353/3380 `event.reply('export-success', data)` where `data = img.toPNG()`/`toJPEG()` optionally `.toString('base64')`; :2403 `const LARGE_IMAGE_AREA = 30000000;` (draw.io explicitly handles ≥30-megapixel exports). [fact] docs/architecture/05 lines 133-146 window.keld destination shape; docs/architecture/02 line 254 'FrameKind::Grant exists in the wire schema but has no live sender/receiver'. [fact] packages/@keld/kipc/src/transport.ts:17 MAX_FRAME_LEN = 16 MiB.
verdicts.correction: Sizing/sequencing: as written the 'first ticket' bundles four changes (host credit window for N pending, send/on, bulk sizing by measurement, el control channel) — not a tracer bullet. Split it: v2a = N-pending with host credit + `send`/`on` over the existing wv-link envelope, 4 KiB kept, falsifier 'two concurrent invokes settle; draw.io preload loads unmodified and one small rendererReq/mainResp round-trip completes'; v2b = bulk lane sized by measuring real draw.io export/readFile payloads (30 MP PNG base64 can exceed 16 MiB, so this is a STREAM/bulk-ref lane question, not a bigger inline bound). Ownership caveat: the object cites 'KEL-80 Linear acceptance (2026-09-20 additive update)' and 'KEL-142 Linear: must not create a second renderer-routing protocol'; neither is verifiable here (Linear unavailable headless; the KEL-142 spec file contains only 'no second renderer CALL is admitted'), and docs/research/library/execution-governance/236-execution-readiness-graph.md line 228 records KEL-79/KEL-80 as 'Parked by explicit owner orders (2026-08-19/20); YAGNI gates'. Publishing floor v2 under KEL-80 therefore needs an explicit unpark decision recorded, or a new owner.

verdicts.reason: The placement (preload runtime once in the isolated world; WebView2 as labeled page-world emulation) and the value semantics are correctly sourced, but the proposed call mechanism — 'function calls relayed over the existing page<->isolated postMessage channel' — is asynchronous, while Electron's contextBridge function proxies are synchronous same-isolate calls whose return values (including function-valued returns) are copied back synchronously. Under an async relay every exposed function returns a Promise. Zettlr's preload breaks at first use independent of sendSync: `window.ipc.on(channel, listener)` must synchronously return an unsubscribe *function* (a function in return position, proxied back into the page world), `getCitationCallback(db)` returns a function, `config.get()` returns a value, `process.uptime()` returns a number, `getPathForFile(file)` returns a string. draw.io's `electron.request` is void so it would survive by accident. This is therefore not a semantic unknown deferred to A5; it is a separate decision-bearing atom (cross-world synchronous call) that the design as stated fails.
verdicts.evidence: [fact] https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electron/electron/v44.4.5/shell/renderer/api/electron_api_context_bridge.cc ProxyFunctionWrapper: `maybe_return_value = func->Call(func_owning_context, recv, proxied_args.size(), proxied_args.data())` inside a `v8::TryCatch` — synchronous; promises are proxied only when the returned value `IsPromise()` (lines 243-347). [fact] docs/api/context-bridge.md lines 82, 144, 151, 158 (copied+frozen, Error custom props lost, Symbol dropped, ipcRenderer→empty object); lib/renderer/api/context-bridge.ts `checkContextIsolationEnabled`. [fact] corpus zettlr/source/common/modules/preload/index.ts:38-50 `on: (channel, listener) => { ...ipcRenderer.on(channel, callback); return () => ipcRenderer.off(channel, callback) }`, :69-78 `getCitationCallback` returns a function, :56-66 `config.get/set` return sendSync results synchronously, :96 `uptime: () => process.uptime()`, :106-114 `getPathForFile`. [fact] crates/keld-wv/src/wkwebview/macos_bridge.rs:510-540 isolated script in `WKContentWorld::defaultClientWorld`, facade in `pageWorld`, both `forMainFrameOnly=true`; page↔isolated traffic today is `window.webkit.messageHandlers.__keld_wv_link_v1` (async). [fact] https://webkitgtk.org/reference/webkit2gtk/stable/method.UserContentManager.register_script_message_handler_in_world.html 'since: 2.22'. [fact] learn.microsoft.com ICoreWebView2 reference fetched 2026-10-06: no method mentions an isolated world.
verdicts.correction: Keep 'implement once in the isolated world' but replace the relay atom: (1) add a prototype atom 'synchronous cross-world call on WKWebView and WebKitGTK' — candidate [lead, unverified]: both worlds share the DOM, so a synchronous `dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(...))` on a hidden node runs the isolated-world listener synchronously and request/reply can ride shared DOM state (attribute/text strings), giving Electron-equivalent sync semantics without a host round trip; measure cost and confirm JS values do not leak across worlds; if it fails, the cell is ✘/▲ 'exposed functions return Promises' with a `keld.compat.ts` diagnostic, never silent; (2) on WebView2 the single world gives synchronous calls natively — its ▲ is isolation only, so split the WebView2 cell into 'synchrony ✔ / isolation ▲'; (3) add conformance vectors for function-valued return proxies in both directions (Zettlr `on()` unsubscribe, `getCitationCallback`) and for Promise-returning functions (Zettlr `invoke` passthrough); (4) only sendSync-backed exposed functions (`config.get/set`, `getCitationCallback`'s inner function) depend on A5.

verdicts.reason: Electron behavior is correctly stated: `senderFrame` is documented nullable after navigation/destruction; `event.reply` is `sender.sendToFrame([processId, frameId], ...)` and `sendToFrame` returns false (no throw) when `webFrameMain.fromId` resolves no RenderFrameHost; Principal::Webview{id, generation} and arch 02 §7 'pending replies to the old principal drop' exist; KEL-142 AC 'an iframe has no own window.keld' is in the spec. Corpus demand for sender/senderFrame is exactly as described (draw.io `validateSender` null-check + `frame.url` prefix test in 25 call sites; Zettlr `BrowserWindow.fromWebContents(event.sender)`, `sender.cut/copy/paste/selectAll/inspectElement/startDrag`, `event.senderFrame ?? undefined`).
verdicts.evidence: [fact] docs/api/structures/ipc-main-event.md 'May be null if accessed after the frame has either navigated or been destroyed'. [fact] lib/browser/ipc-dispatch.ts `event.reply = (channel, ...args) => event.sender.sendToFrame([processId, frameId], channel, ...args)`; lib/browser/api/web-contents.ts:133-138 `const frame = getWebFrame(this, frameId); if (!frame) return false;`; shell/browser/api/electron_api_web_frame_main.cc FromID → `content::RenderFrameHost::FromID(...)`, returns Null when absent. [fact] crates/keld-guard/src/lib.rs:105-111 `Principal::Webview { id: u32, generation }`; docs/architecture/02 line 362. [fact] docs/specs/kel142-macos-renderer-bridge-api.md:377 'an iframe has no own window.keld'. [fact] corpus drawio electron.js:694-700 validateSender; zettlr/source/app/service-providers/windows/index.ts:157-201 and menu/index.ts:239.
verdicts.correction: Two semantic corrections and one resolved unknown: (1) Electron's reply drop is keyed to RenderFrameHost identity, which survives same-document navigations (hash/pushState) — draw.io mutates `location.hash` for file state — so Keld's generation must rotate only on cross-document navigation (the KEL-142 document nonce boundary), never on same-document URL changes, or draw.io's rendererReq/mainResp replies would be dropped where Electron delivers them; state this as the contract and add a hashchange-during-pending fixture. (2) 'silently dropped' is not the only Electron outcome: when the WebFrameMain object exists but its render frame is disposed, `frame.send` throws 'Render frame was disposed before WebFrameMain could be accessed' (electron_api_web_frame_main.cc:262-268), and `WebFrameMain::Send` throws 'Failed to serialize arguments' on unserializable args — so the facade's `event.reply` must still throw for serialization failures and the drop-vs-throw boundary should be recorded as ▲. (3) The object's unknown 'webContents.send on a destroyed WebContents (throw vs no-op)': `WebContents.prototype.send` delegates to `this.mainFrame.send`, which throws the disposed-frame error above once the frame is gone; the destroyed-WebContents `mainFrame` getter path itself was not verified in this pass.

verdicts.reason: The contract half is correctly sourced (blocking renderer, returnValue setter sends on assignment so a listener may set it after returning, console.warn when no listener anywhere, sync throw on unserializable args) and the mechanism half is genuinely unproven for WebKit engines: WKScriptMessageHandler/WKScriptMessageHandlerWithReply and WebKitGTK script-message handlers (including `_with_reply`) are asynchronous, and no primary source for a synchronous page→host call on WKWebView/WebKitGTK was found in this pass either. Zettlr's six sendSync sites (3 in preload, 2 in pinia/config.ts via `window.ipc`, 1 passthrough) are real and sit behind synchronously-returning exposed functions, so a silent Promise rewrite would break `window.config.get()` consumers.
verdicts.evidence: [fact] docs/api/ipc-renderer.md lines 226-229 'block the whole renderer process until the reply is received ... last resort'. [fact] lib/browser/ipc-dispatch.ts `addReturnValueToEvent`: `set: (value) => event._replyChannel.sendReply(value)`; sync-path `console.warn("WebContents #${id} called ipcRenderer.sendSync() with '${channel}' channel without listeners.")`. [fact] shell/renderer/api/electron_api_ipc_renderer.cc SendSync: `SerializeV8Value` failure returns with exception set (sync throw), then `MessageSync(...)` + `DeserializeV8Value(result)`. [fact] corpus zettlr preload/index.ts:37,57,63,74 and pinia/config.ts:20 `const ipcRenderer = window.ipc`, :28,:49. [fact] scratchpad prototypes/f05-wk-scheme/main.swift is a working WKURLSchemeHandler + WKScriptMessageHandler harness; prototypes/sync-probe is an Atomics.wait probe in Bun only (not in a webview).
verdicts.correction: Three upgrades to the object: (1) the 'docs silent / unknown' observable for a never-set returnValue is derivable from source: `ReplyChannel` is a cppgc wrappable with `CPPGC_USING_PRE_FINALIZER(ReplyChannel, EnsureReplySent)`; when the IpcMainEvent is garbage-collected with the callback still pending, Electron posts `SendError(..., "reply was never sent")`, so the blocked renderer eventually receives the plain object `{ error: 'reply was never sent' }` as sendSync's return value (no throw) after a GC-dependent, nondeterministic delay (shell/common/gin_helper/reply_channel.{h,cc}). Record that as the oracle; Keld's typed deadline error is therefore a ▲ by construction, not something to 'record before scoring'. (2) The Windows [lead] is now a [fact]: the ICoreWebView2 AddHostObjectToScript reference states host objects are exposed as `window.chrome.webview.hostObjects.sync.{name}` whose 'function runtimes or property access synchronously block running script waiting to communicate cross process for the host code to run' (learn.microsoft.com, fetched 2026-10-06); only the WebKit engines lack a primary source. (3) Cheapest settling experiment: extend prototypes/f05-wk-scheme/main.swift so page.html runs a synchronous `XMLHttpRequest` (`open(..., false)`) against the registered scheme and the `WKURLSchemeHandler` answers after a host-side hop; observe whether `start(task)` fires while the page thread is blocked, the RTT, and main-thread behavior; repeat on WebKitGTK with `webkit_web_context_register_uri_scheme`. Also note a sync-XHR lane is a second renderer→host carriage unless its request body is the same wv-link envelope and it is nonce-bound like the script-message path (KEL-142 §5).

verdicts.reason: Zero corpus demand is confirmed by direct grep (no occurrence of MessageChannelMain, MessagePortMain, utilityProcess, parentPort, IpcMainServiceWorker, exposeInIsolatedWorld, executeInMainWorld, ipcRenderer.postMessage or webContents.postMessage in zettlr/source, drawio-desktop/src or electron-quick-start), KEL-75 AC7 does require pinned-oracle facade fixtures before facade code, and the Electron semantics cited for the deferred fixtures (queue until start(), 'close' on remote disconnect, transfer only via postMessage, parentPort queues until a 'message' handler, pid undefined before spawn and after exit, fork only after ready) are all in the pinned docs/sources. The decision text in the object is truncated after 'mapped', so the remaining sequence could not be checked.
verdicts.evidence: [fact] corpus grep -rln over zettlr/source, drawio-desktop/src, electron-quick-start: no matches. [fact] docs/specs/kel75-principalized-bun-child-roles.md lines 80-83 (AC7) and 362-370 (facade boundary). [fact] docs/api/message-port-main.md 'Messages will be queued until this method is called', 'Emitted when the remote end ... becomes disconnected'; docs/tutorial/message-ports.md lines 63-65. [fact] docs/api/parent-port.md 'queued up until a handler is registered'; lib/utility/init.ts:24-34 `parentPort.on('newListener', ...) start()` / `on('removeListener', ...) pause()`. [fact] shell/browser/api/electron_api_utility_process.cc:559-561 `ThrowTypeError("utilityProcess cannot be created before app is ready.")`; docs/api/utility-process.md lines 114-116 pid semantics, 106-107 SIGTERM/reap, 173 exit always emitted. [fact] docs/api/ipc-main-service-worker.md 'subtle variation of IpcMain ... for service workers'; ipc-dispatch.ts resolves it via `event.session.serviceWorkers`.
verdicts.correction: (1) Oracle pin mismatch: KEL-75 pins `competitors/electron@cbb5e25d1dca07f5001b9c2f9feec23cdd445cb6`, which GitHub resolves to a main-branch commit dated 2026-08-17 ('build: generate the Node startup snapshot on cross-arch builds too (#52874)'), not v44.4.5; a MessagePortMain/utilityProcess fixture cannot cite both — the family must name one pinned oracle per corpus manifest (research 214 canonical-bytes rule) and reconcile KEL-75 AC7 with the v44.4.5 baseline before any ✘ cell is published as 'deferred behind pinned-oracle fixtures'. (2) parentPort emulation must also *pause* delivery when the last 'message' listener is removed (lib/utility/init.ts removeListener → pause()), not only queue-until-first-handler. (3) Record the exact fork-before-ready throw: a TypeError with message 'utilityProcess cannot be created before app is ready.' (4) Electron source shows `postMessage`-carried IPC (`-ipc-ports`) does NOT emit `contents.on('ipc-message')` and does NOT attach `event.reply`, contrary to web-frame-main.md's 'send, sendSync or postMessage ... delivered in the following order' — a doc/source discrepancy the MessagePort fixture must encode from source, not docs.

extra_findings.finding: Function-valued return values must cross the bridge in both directions. Zettlr's `window.ipc.on()` returns an unsubscribe function and `getCitationCallback(db)` returns a function; Electron proxies a returned Function synchronously (ProxyFunctionWrapper → PassValueToOtherContext). Any shim that only proxies functions in the exposed api graph (not in return/argument positions) or that returns Promises breaks Zettlr at its first `on()` call (`off is not a function`). Add explicit conformance cells for 'function in return position' and 'function in argument position (callbacks)'.
extra_findings.evidence: corpus zettlr/source/common/modules/preload/index.ts:38-50, 69-78; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electron/electron/v44.4.5/shell/renderer/api/electron_api_context_bridge.cc ProxyFunctionWrapper (synchronous func->Call, return value passed back via PassValueToOtherContext)

extra_findings.finding: Error objects travel over IPC in the corpus: draw.io replies `event.reply('mainResp', {error: true, msg: e.message, e: e, reqId})` with a live Error instance, and `event.reply('export-error', e)`. The SCV codec must encode Error (name/message/stack, custom props dropped) rather than treating it as unserializable; a facade that throws on Error breaks every draw.io error path. arch 02 §5 lists Error in the SCV domain; make it a golden vector.
extra_findings.evidence: corpus drawio-desktop/src/main/electron.js:4541 and :3421; docs/api/context-bridge.md line 144 (Error copied, custom properties lost)

extra_findings.finding: Renderer-side drop semantics are now a [fact], not an inference: Electron's renderer wires `ipcNative.onMessage` to `sender.emit(channel, { sender, ports }, ...args)` on the ipcRenderer EventEmitter, so a main→renderer message with no listener is dropped, and `IpcRendererEvent.sender` is the ipcRenderer instance itself (not a WebContents). The shim must pass `{sender: ipcRenderer, ports}` as the first listener argument and must not queue host→renderer EVENTs for late listeners unless labeled ▲.
extra_findings.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electron/electron/v44.4.5/lib/renderer/ipc-native-setup.ts lines 9-14

extra_findings.finding: Payload sizing for A2 is not just 'above 4 KiB': draw.io explicitly handles exports with area ≥ LARGE_IMAGE_AREA = 30,000,000 px (base64 PNG) and returns whole file contents through `readFile` → `mainResp`. These can exceed the app-link MAX_FRAME_LEN (16 MiB), so the bulk path must be a STREAM/bulk-reference lane with chunking, not a larger inline frame bound; measure real draw.io export sizes before fixing any number.
extra_findings.evidence: corpus drawio-desktop/src/main/electron.js:2403, 3239-3259, 4234-4238; packages/@keld/kipc/src/transport.ts:17 MAX_FRAME_LEN = 16 MiB

extra_findings.finding: `ipcMain.handle` registration semantics the trap list gets right but the owner mapping does not: Electron throws synchronously `Attempted to register a second handler for '${method}'` and `TypeError: Expected handler to be a function, but found type '...'`; @keld/api's channels.handle throws `KELD-API-001: Echo channel already has a handler` and collapses handler failures to 'application channel call failed'. The Electron facade needs its own two-registry object (listeners + invoke handlers) layered over @keld/api, with Electron's exact strings as renderings; the current single-handler-per-id rule must not be reused as the ipcMain registry.
extra_findings.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electron/electron/v44.4.5/lib/browser/ipc-main-impl.ts lines 15-22; packages/@keld/api/src/channels.ts:29,73; packages/@keld/api/src/echo-call.test.ts:81

extra_findings.finding: Two pinned Electron oracles are in play: this map uses v44.4.5 docs while KEL-75 (owner of utilityProcess/MessagePortMain facade conformance, AC7) pins commit cbb5e25d1dca07f5001b9c2f9feec23cdd445cb6, a 2026-08-17 main-branch commit. Conformance cells must cite exactly one pinned oracle per corpus manifest; reconcile before any F04 cell is published.
extra_findings.evidence: docs/specs/kel75-principalized-bun-child-roles.md line 36; GitHub API commits/cbb5e25d... → 'build: generate the Node startup snapshot on cross-arch builds too (#52874)' 2026-08-17T01:05:15Z

extra_findings.finding: sendSync with no returnValue ever set: Electron does not hang forever nor throw — the cppgc pre-finalizer `ReplyChannel::EnsureReplySent` sends `{error: 'reply was never sent'}` when the event object is garbage-collected, and the renderer's sendSync returns that plain object. The oracle is nondeterministic in timing, so Keld's deadline is a documented ▲, and the fixture must assert on the eventual value shape rather than timing.

The contract must bind generation to the document (KEL-142 document nonce), not to URL changes, and a hashchange-during-pending fixture must be a negative control.

epic.title: compat(ipc): ipcMain/ipcRenderer/contextBridge over host-routed el:<channel> frames, enumerated guard grants and a lifted renderer floor
epic.body:
## Scope
15 entities / 77 members: `ipcMain` (9), `ipcRenderer` (11), `contextBridge` (3), `MessageChannelMain`/`MessagePortMain`, `utilityProcess`/`UtilityProcess`/`parentPort` (→ KEL-75 roles), `IpcMainServiceWorker` (never), `webUtils.getPathForFile`, event structures. Live today: one macOS page-world `window.keld.invoke` (channel 1 only, 4096-byte payload, one pending invoke per WebView, host-minted correlation, isolated-world relay) → `@keld/api` echo handler; no ipcMain, no preload injection, no renderer shim; the Unix VirtualPortRegistry (64-message queue, 4 KiB inline, one-shot transfer) has no renderer route.

## Corpus demand (resolved call sites)
draw.io: `ipcRenderer.send`/`on`/`once` + `ipcMain.on` + `event.reply` (15 replies) via one `rendererReq` channel multiplexed by `reqId`; `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld` (2 keys); `event.senderFrame.url` read by `validateSender`; `webContents.send` 9. Zettlr: `ipcRenderer.invoke` 186 / `ipcMain.handle` 25, `send` 35, `sendSync` 6 (config store construction), `webContents.send` 49, `event.sender` as a WebContents handle, `webUtils.getPathForFile`, `setMaxListeners(100)`. Zero demand for MessageChannelMain/MessagePortMain/utilityProcess/parentPort/IpcMainServiceWorker.

## Maturity ladder
- L0: all 15 entities exist; never/deferred rows published with denominator honesty.
- L1: draw.io's send/on/once/reply pattern and Zettlr's invoke/handle pattern run on macOS over the lifted floor.
- L2: ordering per channel, error envelope (message-only to the renderer, typed code on the wire), `senderFrame` null-after-navigation, stale-generation reply drop, bounded credit/backpressure pass pinned conformance entries.
- L3: corpus apps' IPC workflows pass under `keld dev` with facade-overhead measured (X05).

## Linear owners consumed
KEL-80 (bounded virtual channels: N-pending credit window, host→renderer events — the floor v2), KEL-142 (bridge seam), KEL-136 (transport), KEL-75 (virtual ports, roles), KEL-102 (guard dispatch), SCV codec owner (F03-D4, open), `windows.<w>.channels` grant vocabulary spec (open, no owner today).

## Design facts fixed by research (two refuters + panel)
- Carriage: one fixed, generated kipc control channel per direction for the compat namespace; the Electron channel string, a kind discriminator (event | invoke | sync | ports) and the SCV bytes are payload fields; the host matches the channel string against the per-window enumerated `el:<channel>` grant (`KELD-GUARD003` on miss) and forwards opaque bytes. No runtime-minted u16 ids.
- The renderer→main authorization boundary is the enumerated per-window channel grant, not the preload (both corpus preloads expose arbitrary-channel send/invoke to the page); `keld migrate` emits enumerated grants from static analysis and refuses `el:*`.
- The live KEL-142 floor cannot carry either corpus app; floor v2 (KEL-80 slice) = (a) N pending invokes per WebView under a host-enforced credit window, (b) `window.keld.send` + `window.keld.on` host→renderer events, (c) payload bound raised by measurement (draw.io ships base64 PNG exports through IPC).
- `event.sender` = facade WebContents keyed by host webview id; `event.senderFrame.url` host-minted and null after navigation; `event.reply` binds to the sender document generation (survives same-document hash changes, as Electron keys on the frame host); stale replies are dropped silently like Electron.
- `ipcMain.handle` errors reach the renderer as the message only; the typed `KELD-*` code stays on the wire and in diagnostics.
- `sendSync` must remain a blocking CALL with deadline, rate limit and dev warning (arch 02 §5, KEL-127); it is SCAFFOLDED (typed throw + fix-it to invoke) until the WKWebView synchronous-XHR experiment passes (Zettlr-gated, 0 draw.io sites).
- MessageChannelMain/MessagePortMain/utilityProcess/parentPort are deferred behind zero demand and KEL-75 AC7 (pinned-oracle fixture first); IpcMainServiceWorker/exposeInIsolatedWorld/executeInMainWorld are documented ✘.

research.summary: F05 covers 43 entities / 368 members (Session 88, protocol 18, net/ClientRequest/IncomingMessage/WebSocket 51, DownloadItem 28, WebRequest 8, Cookies 5, ServiceWorkers/ServiceWorkerMain 15, Extensions 7, netLog 3, 29 structures). Corpus demand is narrow and concrete: Zettlr's `protocol.handle('safe-file')` (unprivileged scheme, serves any readable absolute path, consumed by 23 renderer/main files), Zettlr's `ses.clearStorageData({storages:[cookies,localstorage,shadercache]})` in 12 window factories, draw.io's `session.defaultSession.webRequest.onHeadersReceived` (CSP for all contents) + `onBeforeRequest({urls:['file://*']})` (block file loads outside the app dir), draw.io's indirect `net.request` via electron-updater (`session.fromPartition('electron-updater',{cache:false})`), Zettlr's `net.online` gate; neither app installs a permission handler (so Electron's documented default-allow applies to them today); Extensions appear only in Zettlr's non-packaged dev path; quick-start uses nothing in F05. Keld today: no scheme registration (keld-wv `WebEngine` v0 omits `register_scheme`; no WKURLSchemeHandler/WebResourceRequested/register_uri_scheme code), no session/cookie/download/net facade (`@keld/electron` = app only; keld-native = fs.read/fs.write), keld-guard already evaluates `app.net.connect` URL scopes with the live authority rule but "no URL-valued capability is wired to it yet", `web.camera`/`web.microphone` default-deny with `Principal::Webview` is live, KEL-135 gives one host-owned persistent profile per signed app (+ ephemeral dev) with no partition concept, KEL-79 (origin/resource transport) is parked by owner orders and has no spec file. Six decision atoms: (1) scheme declaration is static host config, `protocol.handle` is a Bun producer behind the arch-05 host resource adapter; (2) missing permission handler = guard default-deny, present handler only narrows after guard Allow; (3) main-process `net` is Bun networking under `app.net.connect`, never engine session — where egress is enforced for strict roles is an open research/prototype question; (4) `webRequest` is not generically emulable on system engines — migrate the two corpus uses to static `web.csp` + resource scopes, API itself ▲; (5) one default session = KEL-135 profile; storage/cookie ops become host-brokered profile operations, partitions ▲ until KEL-135 grows; (6) a documented-never set (Extensions, netLog, TLS-trust overrides in strict, HID/USB/Serial/Bluetooth/WebAuthn choosers, ServiceWorkerMain, sharedDictionary, networkEmulation). Insufficient evidence is stated as unknown rather than filled in.

decisions.question: How are Electron custom schemes (`protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged` + `protocol.handle`) realized when the scheme must exist before any engine view is created and the handler runs in a supervised Bun role?
decisions.proposed_answer: Scheme declaration is static, host-owned configuration (`keld.config.ts` scheme table with explicit privilege bits: standard/secure/supportFetchAPI/corsEnabled/allowServiceWorkers/stream/bypassCSP), consumed by keld-wv at engine construction on all three platforms; `keld migrate` lifts the app's `registerSchemesAsPrivileged` array into that table. `protocol.handle(scheme, handler)` is a facade that registers the Bun role as the producer for that scheme behind the architecture-05 host resource adapter: engine request → adapter binds active WebView+navigation generation → keld-guard evaluates the scheme/origin/method against the declared scheme and the producer role → routed kipc request to the Bun handler (Electron `Request`-shaped: url, method, headers, body, initiatorOrigin) → bounded `Response` chunks back through the adapter (WKURLSchemeHandler / WebResourceRequested / WebKitURISchemeRequest). Any file bytes the handler reads go through the role's own `fs.read` grants — the scheme itself mints no filesystem authority. Runtime `registerSchemesAsPrivileged` after `ready`, or for a scheme not in the static table, returns a typed KELD-COMPAT error; `protocol.handle` on a built-in scheme (file/http/https) is ✘ (see platform notes). Built-in intercept* and register*Protocol deprecated methods are facaded onto `handle` or ✘. [inference] This is the only shape that satisfies 'one host-owned scheme declaration' (research 186 row 1), the arch-05 guard-before-bytes flow, and the engine construction-time constraints.
evidence: [fact] protocol.md v44.4.5: registerSchemesAsPrivileged 'must be called before the ready event of the app module gets emitted' and 'can be called only once'; CustomScheme privileges all default false; 'non-standard schemes can not recognize relative URLs'.

[fact] Apple WKWebViewConfiguration.setURLSchemeHandler: registered on the configuration (construction time); 'It is a programmer error to register a handler for a scheme WebKit already handles, such as https, and this method raises an invalidArgumentException'.

[fact] WebView2 ICoreWebView2CustomSchemeRegistration: registrations are environment-creation options, 'valid and immutable throughout the lifetime of the associated WebView2s' browser process and any WebView2 environments sharing the browser process must be created with identical custom scheme registrations, otherwise the environment creation will fail'; custom schemes 'participate in CORS and adheres to CSP'; HasAuthorityComponent false → opaque origin.
[fact] crates/keld-wv/src/engine.rs lines 8–11: register_scheme omitted because wry custom protocols are builder-time.
[fact] docs/architecture/05-webview-and-native.md §2 resource flow and docs/architecture/02-ipc.md §3 (`keld://c/{channel}` bulk lane).

[fact] Zettlr corpus: source/app/util/custom-protocols.ts registers 'safe-file' with protocol.handle after ready (lifecycle.ts line 66), never calls registerSchemesAsPrivileged (grep: none), and serves any readable absolute path via fs.access + fs.readFile with 500+message on error; 23 files depend on the literal 'safe-file://' prefix.

[fact] research 186 row 1: 'A Keld resource transport needs one host-owned scheme declaration, explicit privilege bits, URL/path parsing that rejects traversal/ambiguous encoding, and a scoped resource grant before file or network access.'
decisions.confidence: high that declaration must be static and host-owned; medium on the exact producer-routing lane (virtual ports vs bulk scheme lane)
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Dynamic runtime registration mirroring Electron: impossible on WKWebView after configuration and on WebView2 after environment creation without recreating every view/environment; (b) URL rewriting of app schemes onto `keld://` inside the compat preload: breaks `request.url`/`initiatorOrigin` observables and Zettlr's 23 string-prefix comparisons; (c) running the handler in the host (Rust) by re-implementing Zettlr's file logic: duplicates app policy and violates 'one rule one owner'; (d) granting the producer role `fs.read: ["/**"]` so Zettlr runs unmodified: forbidden widening — migrate must emit explicit roots and the scoreboard records ▲.
decisions.unknowns: Which lane carries handler responses (KEL-80 virtual ports are 4096-byte inline today; the arch-02 bulk scheme lane is destination-only) — needs the P1 prototype. Exact Electron error text when registerSchemesAsPrivileged is called after ready (not fetched). Whether WebView2 custom scheme + WebResourceRequested can stream large bodies without a full copy (unmeasured). How Zettlr's UNC→/Volumes mapping maps onto fs.read scopes (user-owned migrate decision).
blocked_by: KEL-135 (profile per engine already needed for view creation)

decisions.question: What does the `session.setPermissionRequestHandler` / `setPermissionCheckHandler` facade do when no handler is installed, and what authority does an installed handler have?
decisions.proposed_answer: No handler ⇒ keld-guard default-deny for the requesting `Principal::Webview` (today KELD-GUARD006/007 for media; the same path for every other permission string once named), recorded as a scoreboard ▲ against Electron's documented auto-approve. Handler installed ⇒ it is consulted only after the guard returns Allow for that webview principal and permission (guard-before-handler, KEL-102), so app code can narrow but never widen. `callback(true)` with no grant ⇒ deny plus a KELD-GUARD001 fix hint naming the `windows.<w>.web.*` grant to add; `details.requestingUrl`/`isMainFrame` are filled from host-minted navigation state, not from engine callbacks (which pass no origin on wry). Both request and check handlers share one evaluation so the two cannot disagree (research 186: Electron's are independent allow-by-default paths).
evidence: [fact] docs/tutorial/security.md v44.4.5: 'By default, Electron will automatically approve all permission requests unless the developer has manually configured a custom handler.'

[fact] docs/api/session.md v44.4.5: 'Please note that you must also implement setPermissionCheckHandler to get complete permission handling.'; request handler: 'Calling callback(true) will allow the permission and callback(false) will reject it. To clear the handler, call setPermissionRequestHandler(null).'

[fact] research 186 row 4 (source @96f3996): with no request handler RequestPermissionsWithDetails grants each requested permission except geolocation CLI denial; check returns true except deprecated sync clipboard read.

[fact] docs/architecture/03-security.md §3 item 3 and crates/keld-wv/src/media.rs: camera/microphone default-denied via keld_guard::evaluate as Principal::Webview; missing identity/AppProcess fail closed (KELD-GUARD007).
[fact] briefing invariant 2: 'A missing Electron permission handler must NOT become allow'.

[fact] corpus: neither draw.io nor Zettlr installs any permission handler (grep setPermission*: none), so Electron grants them everything today; Zettlr uses Notification and clipboard; draw.io uses clipboard.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Mirror Electron default-allow under the legacy profile: still bypasses keld-guard (invariant 2) — rejected outright; (b) treat app callback(true) as the grant: makes application code the authority source (research 28 'allow-by-default … per-feature application callbacks as the authority source' is the explicit refuse row); (c) separate request vs check evaluation: reproduces Electron's two-path inconsistency.
decisions.unknowns: The permission-string → capability-name table beyond web.camera/web.microphone (notifications, geolocation, clipboard-read, clipboard-sanitized-write, fullscreen, display-capture, idle-detection, pointerLock, openExternal, fileSystem, …) and its owner (KEL-102 policy injection vs KEL-15 schema). Whether saved engine permission preferences can bypass new-request callbacks on restart (arch 03 names this open for KEL-135).

decisions.question: What backs `net.request` / `net.fetch` / `net.WebSocket` / `ClientRequest` in the Bun main process, and where is `app.net.connect` enforced for a strict role that is supposed to have zero ambient OS authority?
decisions.proposed_answer: The facade wraps Bun's own HTTP/WebSocket stack (never the engine session): `net.fetch` ≈ Bun fetch with Electron's `Request`-first-argument contract; `ClientRequest` replays Electron's event ordering (response/login/finish/abort/error/close with close last, abort suppressed if already closed, error ⇒ close with no response); `useSessionCookies` stays false and `true` is a typed unsupported (▲); `session`/`partition` options are accepted and ignored for in-memory, typed-unsupported for persist: (▲); `bypassCustomProtocolHandlers` is moot because Bun fetch never reaches app schemes (custom-scheme and `file:` fetches from main are ✘ unless routed to the host resource adapter — not in v1). `net.isOnline/online` map to a host-reported connectivity fact (new tiny broker op, or ▲ constant true with doc note). Enforcement location of `app.net.connect` is NOT decidable from current evidence: the guard matcher is live, but no URL-valued capability is wired, and strict-role containment (Linux bwrap network namespace; Landlock network is port-level; macOS/Windows have no per-process egress primitive in the current profiles) cannot express a host allowlist. Proposed answer = run the P2 prototype comparing (i) host-owned local forward proxy inside the role's network namespace with CONNECT-level allowlist evaluated by keld-guard, versus (ii) host byte-brokering over kipc; adopt (i) unless measurement shows otherwise. Corpus pressure is low: draw.io's only main-process HTTP is electron-updater (replaced by the KEL-53 keld-update adapter, Tier 2), Zettlr uses `got` (Node stack ⇒ Bun fetch) and `net.online`.

[fact] docs/api/client-request.md v44.4.5: useSessionCookies 'Default is false'; redirect 'Defaults to follow'; 'The close event indicates that no more events will be emitted on either the request or response objects'; 'The abort event will not be fired if the request is already closed'; setHeader 'can be called only before first write. Calling this method after the first write will throw an error.'

decisions.question: Can `session.webRequest` (onBeforeRequest/onHeadersReceived/…) be emulated on system engines, and how do draw.io's two uses migrate?
decisions.proposed_answer: No generic emulation: WKWebView cannot intercept schemes it handles natively (http/https/file), WebKitGTK has no response-header rewrite hook for network loads, and only WebView2 (Chromium-derived) offers WebResourceRequested — a single-platform partial would be a silent per-OS divergence (forbidden). The `webRequest` object exists at L0 with typed KELD-COMPAT errors naming the replacement, scoreboard ▲. `keld migrate` rewrites the two corpus patterns to host-owned static policy: (1) draw.io's `onHeadersReceived` CSP string → `windows.<w>.web.csp` (host injects it as a response header on `keld://`/app-scheme responses via the resource adapter, and as meta for file-less loads), preserving 'strictest of multiple policies wins' because the header path is the one Electron uses; (2) draw.io's `onBeforeRequest({urls:['file://*']})` app-dir allowlist → the resource-transport root scope (navigation allow-list + resource roots), which already fails closed. The quirks flag records the mapping so a later dynamic handler cannot silently widen it. WebRequest single-listener semantics ('Only the last attached listener will be used') are preserved in the L0 stub so re-registration behaves identically.
evidence: [fact] drawio-desktop/src/main/electron.js lines 994–1021: onHeadersReceived sets `Content-Security-Policy` ('default-src self; script-src self wasm-unsafe-eval; connect-src self …') on every response; onBeforeRequest with `{urls:['file://*']}` cancels loads whose URL does not start with codeUrl.

[fact] docs/tutorial/security.md v44.4.5: CSP example uses webRequest.onHeadersReceived with `'Content-Security-Policy': ["default-src 'none'"]`.

Storage/cookie ops become host-brokered operations on that profile — a small `web-data` native module (clear(storages, origin), cookies get/set/remove/flush, cacheSize) implemented per engine (WKWebsiteDataStore / WebView2 Profile+CookieManager / WebKitWebsiteDataManager+CookieManager) and exposed as `app.system: ["web-data.clear", "web-data.cookies"]` grants in the existing `system` array (no new grant vocabulary). Electron storage-type names are mapped with a documented ▲ for types the engine lacks (e.g. `shadercache` on WebKit). The Bun role never sees profile paths (KEL-135 rule).

verdicts.reason: The load-bearing atoms hold against the Keld sources: scheme declaration must be static and host-owned (keld-wv v0 omits register_scheme because engine custom protocols are builder-time; WKWebViewConfiguration/WebView2 environment constraints are receipted), and protocol.handle as a Bun producer behind the arch-05 adapter reuses the destination resource flow (engine → Rust adapter bound to active WebView+generation → keld-guard → broker → routed kipc to a supervised role) and the arch-02 keld://c/{channel} bulk lane rather than inventing a transport. Rejected alternatives (c) and (d) are correctly refused on one-owner and no-widening grounds. Prior decisions #322–#325 narrowed KEL-79 to product-spine subsets, but the KEL-139/KEL-142 specs contain no scheme or resource-transport text, so the author's 'parked, no spec file' blocker is accurate. Three corrections are required before this is specs-ready (see correction).

verdicts.correction: (1) Privilege-bit placement and YAGNI: `bypassCSP` and `allowServiceWorkers` are hardening opt-outs, and architecture 03 §2 says CSP 'Opt-out is a named, linted grant' — they belong in the generated `keld.permissions.jsonc` (host-enforced), not in `keld.config.ts` (arch 04 §2 scopes that file to identity/windows/engine policy). Neither corpus app calls registerSchemesAsPrivileged, so a seven-bit privilege table has zero demand; v1 should carry scheme names only and record all privilege bits as ✘/▲ pending demand (root AGENTS.md YAGNI). (2) 'Any file bytes the handler reads go through the role's own fs.read grants' presumes the arch-05 §3 `fs+` 'strict-profile virtual Node-fs facade', which is not specced or live; under KEL-78 Zettlr's raw `fs.readFile` fails with an OS error, not KELD-GUARD001/002, so the stated test oracle is unreachable until that facade exists — add it to blocked_by. (3) The live fs broker caps one read at MAX_FS_CONTENT_BYTES = 8 MiB (crates/keld-native/src/fs.rs:42) with 64 KiB chunks; safe-file resources above 8 MiB would return the app's 500 where Electron returns 200 — either the resource broker path is a streaming/range path (arch 05 flow names 'range and bounded body') or this is a declared ▲.

verdicts.reason: The invariant atoms are confirmed by code and spec: keld-guard today denies every non-AppProcess principal before grant lookup (so a missing handler cannot become allow), the manifest parser ignores the `windows` top-level key (so `windows.<w>.web.*` grants are destination, consistent with the stated blocker), and KEL-102 §4 defines guard-before-handler and a webview policy-injection API whose destination row names 'Per-window grants, navigation rotation, origin context, channel grants and CSP'. 'Handler only narrows after guard Allow' is exactly the KEL-102 boundary. Two blockers are missing from the list (see correction).

verdicts.correction: Add two blockers: (a) `details.requestingUrl`/`isMainFrame` 'from host-minted navigation state' depends on origin/navigation ownership, which KEL-135:654 assigns to KEL-79 (parked) — without it the facade can only report the webview id, not an origin, and that must be a ▲. (b) The uniform rule 'guard default-deny for every permission string' is only enforceable for permission kinds the engine actually surfaces to the host; WKWebView exposes a media-capture decision handler but [inference, not verified here] no notifications or geolocation callback, WebView2 exposes a fixed PermissionKind enum, WebKitGTK exposes PermissionRequest subclasses. The permission-string table therefore needs a per-engine reachability column (✘ where the engine never asks), or Keld would be claiming a deny it cannot observe.

verdicts.reason: The enforcement location is NOT an open question: the approved KEL-78 strict-profile spec already decides it. KEL-78 denies direct `connect`/`bind`/`socket` for strict roles always, states that a keld-guard net grant MUST NOT widen the child's OS profile, and states 'Brokered net is host-side after keld-guard'. That refutes both halves of the proposed answer for the strict profile: (1) 'wraps Bun's own HTTP/WebSocket stack' cannot work because Bun fetch's connect() fails at the OS layer regardless of grants; (2) preferred option (i), a local forward proxy 'inside the role's network namespace', requires the child to connect() to the proxy, which the same rows forbid, and macOS/Windows strict profiles have no role network namespace at all. The author's rejected alternative (b), host-side brokering, is the only KEL-78-compatible location; preferring (i) 'unless measurement shows otherwise' inverts invariant 5 — the simpler correct path is the baseline and an unmeasured 'every byte copied' claim decides nothing. The Bun-stack answer is permissible only under the visibly-labelled legacy profile (KEL-127). The facade-semantics atoms (event ordering, useSessionCookies=false, session/partition ignored, Bun never reaches app schemes) survive as behavior of whatever facade fronts the broker.

extra_findings.finding: WKWebView does not implement Electron's non-standard-scheme restrictions. An unprivileged custom scheme on macOS resolves relative URLs, serves fetch(), exposes localStorage and has origin '<scheme>://'. Every CustomScheme privilege bit except what WebView2/WebKitGTK can express is a per-engine ▲, and Zettlr's safe-file becomes a storage-bearing origin on macOS. This also means the 'Keld must NOT make it standard for convenience' trap is moot on macOS: the engine already does.
extra_findings.evidence: Live probe scratchpad/prototypes/f05-wk-scheme/main.swift: 'REQ safe-file:///dir/sub/rel.png', 'REQ safe-file:///dir/sub/rel.txt', 'MSG fetch-ok:TXT', 'MSG ls-ok', 'MSG origin:safe-file://'; contrast f05docs/api_protocol.md:99-116.

extra_findings.finding: Sizing blocker missing from D1: the Bun producer's file bytes must pass the keld-native FsBroker, whose content ceiling is 8 MiB (MAX_FS_CONTENT_BYTES), and the only live inline lane is the 4096-byte virtual port. Zettlr's safe-file handler serves .pdf/.mp4/.webm (CONTENT_TYPE_MAP) via a whole-file fs.readFile; media over 8 MiB cannot reach the renderer until a streaming lane and a chunked fs read exist. The D1 'tracer bullet' is therefore not finishable for Zettlr media parity even after KEL-79 unparks.
extra_findings.evidence: crates/keld-native/src/fs.rs:42 'pub const MAX_FS_CONTENT_BYTES: usize = 8 * 1024 * 1024' and :252 'use at most 8 MiB'; crates/keld-runtime/src/lib.rs:755 (4096 inline ceiling); corpus/zettlr/source/app/util/custom-protocols.ts CONTENT_TYPE_MAP (.mp4/.webm/.pdf) and fs.readFile.

extra_findings.finding: Permission-hook coverage is engine-specific and must be a column in D2's permission table: WKUIDelegate hooks only geolocation, media capture and device-orientation; WebView2 exposes 14 kinds; WebKitGTK exposes 10 request types. For unhookable kinds (e.g. Notification on WKWebView) keld-guard is never consulted and the engine's own policy decides, so 'default-deny via guard' is unobservable there and must be recorded as engine-decided ▲.
extra_findings.evidence: Apple WKUIDelegate method list (requestGeolocationPermissionFor, requestMediaCapturePermissionFor, requestDeviceOrientationAndMotionPermissionFor); learn.microsoft.com webview2-idl COREWEBVIEW2_PERMISSION_KIND_* (14); webkitgtk.org *PermissionRequest (10); probe 'MSG Notification:function perm:default'.

extra_findings.finding: D3's enforcement-location framing omits that Windows already has a live all-or-nothing egress primitive (zero-capability LPAC is the stated authority boundary). The P2 prototype as written ('inside the role's network namespace') is Linux-only; a Windows leg (LPAC + host proxy via ACL'd named pipe) is required and macOS is the only platform with no identified primitive.
extra_findings.evidence: docs/architecture/03-security.md:226-234 (Windows: 'the live zero-capability LPAC + reviewed ACL/handle-list mechanism is the authority boundary'; macOS: 'App Sandbox helper remains unverified; deprecated sandbox_init ... rejected').

extra_findings.finding: Proxy-seam coverage gap for the one corpus net consumer: Bun's fetch honors `proxy` and HTTP(S)_PROXY/ALL_PROXY/NO_PROXY, but Zettlr's updates and link-preview use `got` (node:http). Whether Bun's node:http honors those variables is unverified; if not, a netns/LPAC-contained role denies got even with a valid app.net.connect grant unless migrate injects a proxy agent. Cheapest experiment: run got under Bun with HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:1 and observe connect target.
extra_findings.evidence: bun.sh/docs/api/fetch 'Proxying requests' (fetched text: 'Bun uses ALL_PROXY ... Node.js does not'); corpus/zettlr/source/app/service-providers/updates/index.ts:24; corpus/zettlr/source/common/util/fetch-link-preview.ts:17.

extra_findings.finding: D2's corpus-risk sentence overstates: draw.io and Zettlr use main-process `clipboard`/`Notification` modules, which Electron's session permission handlers never gate; the only renderer-side surface that Electron's default-allow check currently grants is Zettlr's 11 `navigator.clipboard.writeText` sites (clipboard-sanitized-write). On WKWebView the engine applies user-activation gating (NotAllowedError without a gesture) rather than any embedder decision.

epic.title: compat(session): custom schemes, permission handlers, net stack, webRequest, session/profile and downloads over host-owned transport and KEL-135 profiles
epic.body:
## Scope
43 entities / 368 members: `Session` (88), `protocol` (18), `net`/`ClientRequest`/`IncomingMessage`/`WebSocket` (51), `DownloadItem` (28), `WebRequest`, `Cookies`, `ServiceWorkers`/`ServiceWorkerMain`, `Extensions`, `netLog`, 29 structures. Live today: no scheme registration (engine custom protocols are builder-time), no session/cookie/download/net facade, keld-guard evaluates `app.net.connect` URL scopes but nothing is wired to it, `web.camera`/`web.microphone` default-deny with a webview principal is live, KEL-135 gives one host-owned persistent profile per signed app (ephemeral in dev), KEL-79 (origin/resource transport) is Backlog with no spec file.

## Corpus demand
Zettlr `protocol.handle('safe-file')` (unprivileged scheme serving readable absolute paths; 23 consumers), `ses.clearStorageData` in 12 window factories, `net.online`; draw.io `session.defaultSession.webRequest.onHeadersReceived` (CSP for all contents) and `onBeforeRequest({urls:['file://*']})`, indirect `net.request` via electron-updater (`session.fromPartition('electron-updater')`); neither app installs a permission handler (Electron default-allow applies to them today); Extensions only in Zettlr's dev path.

## Maturity ladder
- L0: every entity exists with typed errors; never list published.
- L1: one live `Session` (= KEL-135 profile), `clearStorageData` subset, `net.fetch` over the Bun stack (legacy) / host net broker (strict), webRequest listeners as recorded no-ops behind host containment.
- L2: scheme table + `protocol.handle` producer routing, permission inversion, DownloadItem lifecycle pass pinned entries per engine.
- L3: Zettlr `safe-file://` workflow passes under `keld dev`.

## Linear owners consumed
KEL-79 (resource transport, parked), KEL-135 (profile identity; needs a `clear(types)` operation amendment), KEL-78 (strict net containment — decided: strict roles never connect directly), KEL-102 (broker admission), KEL-74/KEL-237 (evidence), arch 05 §2 resource adapter.

## Design facts fixed by research (two refuters)
- Scheme declaration is static host configuration (`keld.config.ts` scheme table lifted by migrate from `registerSchemesAsPrivileged`), consumed by keld-wv at engine construction; `protocol.handle` registers a Bun producer behind the host resource adapter; bytes flow guard → broker; privilege bits are declared for migrate/scoreboard purposes but enforcement is per engine (WKWebView does not implement Electron's non-standard-scheme restrictions; custom schemes have no Service Workers on WKWebView).
- No permission handler ⇒ guard default-deny for the requesting webview principal (▲ against Electron auto-approve); an installed handler is consulted only after the guard allows and can only narrow; permission strings are engine-hook-dependent (a third column: guard-evaluable vs engine-decided).
- `net.*` wraps the Bun HTTP stack (never the engine session) under legacy; under strict it is a facade over a host net broker (new keld-native `net` row + spec; KEL-78 decides strict roles never connect directly). `useSessionCookies:true` is a typed ▲.
- `session.webRequest` is not emulated generically (only WebView2 could); listeners exist at L0 with typed errors, become recorded no-ops ▲ only after host file:// containment + always-on CSP injection land with a negative control (draw.io's two uses migrate via generated policy).
- v1 has exactly one `Session` = the KEL-135 profile; `fromPartition('persist:x')`, in-memory partitions, `fromPath` are typed ▲ until KEL-135 grows; `clearStorageData/clearCache` map to a KEL-135 host-side profile clear operation (not a new keld-native module).
- Never: Extensions/loadExtension, netLog, ServiceWorkerMain, network emulation, certificate verify overrides (legacy-profile question is owner-decided), proxy/connection control assigned explicitly.

research.unit: F06 native-desktop (Menu/MenuItem, Tray, dialog, Notification, clipboard/ClipboardItem, shell, screen/Display, globalShortcut, powerMonitor/powerSaveBlocker, nativeTheme, nativeImage/NativeImage, systemPreferences, safeStorage, pushNotifications/inAppPurchase, desktopCapturer, ShareMenu)
research.summary: [fact] F06 covers 38 entities / 350 members of the v44.4.5 model; every module is main-process only (nativeImage/shell/clipboard renderer use is deprecated or non-sandboxed only), so every call maps to Principal::AppProcess over kipc into a keld-native module that does not exist yet. [fact] Keld state: keld-native ships only the retained FsBroker (fs.read/fs.write, KEL-130, Done) and a MODULES name list (menu, tray, dialog, notify, clipboard, shortcut, screen, power, shell, secrets, deeplink, autostart, dock; 'capture' from arch 05 §3 is absent from MODULES — a code/spec gap); no F06 channel is reachable from the shipping host until KEL-102/T3 admission; @keld/electron exports only `app`. Corpus demand ranks dialog (drawio showMessageBox x7, open/save x4 each; Zettlr showMessageBox 24, dialog in 21 files) > shell (openExternal 3/7, openPath, showItemInFolder, trashItem) > Menu (both apps: buildFromTemplate + setApplicationMenu, 13 roles in drawio, 45 accelerators per Zettlr platform menu, popup with frame) > screen (workArea/getDisplayMatching) > clipboard (drawio uses the 44 W3C promise shape with ClipboardItem; Zettlr on ^43.6.0 uses sync readText and the removed writeImage) > nativeTheme (themeSource writes, 'updated') > nativeImage (createFromDataURL().toPNG(), createFromPath for icons) > Tray/Notification (Zettlr only) > systemPreferences (getAccentColor, subscribeNotification AppleInterfaceThemeChangedNotification). Zero corpus use of globalShortcut, powerMonitor, powerSaveBlocker, safeStorage, desktopCapturer, ShareMenu, pushNotifications, inAppPurchase — Tier 2/3 as arch 04 §4 already says. Six decision atoms change design or sequencing: (1) dialog-chosen paths must become host-minted, session-bound fs grants consumed by the existing FsBroker (drawio's blessPath/realpath/sibling-draft pattern is the oracle) — KEL-130 explicitly excluded dialog grants and binds scopes to an immutable manifest digest; (2) all F06 UI objects are host-main-thread handles with host-assigned ids and write-through property setters, click/event dispatch host→Bun; (3) guard grant shape for resource-less capabilities: the arch 03 `system: [...]` flat list is evaluable today as operation="system", path="<capability>" with zero guard changes; (4) shell.openExternal: the guard refuses scheme-wide grants by design while the median app's legitimate policy is 'any http(s)/mailto/tel URL the user clicked' — needs a host confirmation grant kind, not a wider glob; (5) binary payload/NativeImage model: Bun-side immutable value object + host decode at consumption, bounded by MAX_FRAME_LEN 16 MiB / 8 MiB content ceilings, with a `clipboardLegacySync` quirks flag reusing the KEL-127 blocking CALL primitive for 43-shape apps; (6) safeStorage is a host secrets broker (KEL-78 denies keychain to strict children), fail-closed where Electron Linux falls back to plaintext basic_text — blocked on the KEL-89 D5 secrets fast-follow spec. Notifications are gated by packaging identity (Windows AppUserModelID + Start Menu shortcut; macOS code signing) and so sequence behind KEL-19/KEL-103, not behind kipc work.

decisions.question: What is the object/identity model for host-owned UI handles (Menu, MenuItem, Tray, Notification, popup) across the Bun/host process boundary?

Lifetime: handles die with their Bun generation (tray icons, popups, notifications, power assertions are released) — a deliberate ▲ versus Electron's GC-driven Tray lifetime. epic.title: compat(native): dialog, shell, Menu/Tray, clipboard, screen, nativeTheme, nativeImage, Notification, safeStorage and power/shortcut brokers behind generated grants
epic.body:
## Scope
38 entities / 350 members, all main-process: Menu (13), MenuItem (21), Tray (36), dialog (8), Notification (30), clipboard/ClipboardItem (11), shell (7), screen/Display (31), globalShortcut (7), powerMonitor (16), powerSaveBlocker (3), nativeTheme (9), nativeImage/NativeImage (24), systemPreferences (28), safeStorage (8), pushNotifications/inAppPurchase (mac), desktopCapturer (Tier 3), ShareMenu. Live today: keld-native ships only the retained FsBroker (fs.read/fs.write) and a MODULES name list (`capture` is missing from it: code/spec gap); no F06 channel is reachable until KEL-102/T3 admission; `@keld/electron` exports only `app`.

## Corpus demand
dialog (draw.io showMessageBox ×7 incl. one `showMessageBoxSync` on the close path, open/save ×4 each; Zettlr showMessageBox 24, dialog in 21 files) > shell (openExternal, openPath, showItemInFolder, trashItem) > Menu (both: buildFromTemplate + setApplicationMenu; 13 roles in draw.io; 45 accelerators per Zettlr platform menu; popup) > screen > clipboard (draw.io uses the W3C promise shape with ClipboardItem; Zettlr sync readText) > nativeTheme (themeSource, `updated`) > nativeImage (createFromDataURL().toPNG(), createFromPath) > Tray/Notification (Zettlr) > systemPreferences (accent colour, theme-changed notification). Zero use of globalShortcut, powerMonitor, powerSaveBlocker, safeStorage, pushNotifications, inAppPurchase, ShareMenu, desktopCapturer.

## Maturity ladder
- L0: every module exists; unsupported members throw typed errors; `capture` added to MODULES or named as intentionally absent.
- L1: dialog/shell/Menu/screen/clipboard/nativeTheme/nativeImage work for draw.io and Zettlr on macOS through guarded brokers.
- L2: dialog-minted scopes, menu role execution host-side, accelerator semantics, theme `updated` event, clipboard shapes pass pinned entries on each OS.
- L3: corpus workflows pass under `keld dev` with KEL-74 records and `app.system` grants recorded.

## Linear owners consumed
KEL-130 (FsBroker retained scopes — dialog grants extend the same set), KEL-102 (broker admission; the guard's accepted operation set is hard-coded to fs.read/fs.write today), KEL-89 (secrets/auth), KEL-78 (strict: no keychain reach from the child), KEL-132, KEL-208/KEL-209 (URL-scope authority rule), KEL-19/KEL-103 (Windows AppUserModelId, bundle metadata).

## Design facts from research (NOT yet independently refuted — batch 2 refutes; decisions below stay open)
- Host-owned UI handles: every Menu/MenuItem/Tray/Notification/popup is a host main-thread resource with a host-assigned `(generation, id)`; facade proxies are write-through; clicks arrive as host→Bun messages; `role` items execute host-side without a round trip (Electron ignores `click` when `role` is set).
- Resource-less capabilities keep the arch 03 §2 literal shape `app.system: ["clipboard.read", …]` evaluated with the existing matcher (operation=system, path=literal) — no guard schema change.
- NativeImage is a Bun-side immutable value object (bytes + sniffed format + size + representations); decode/encode happens host-side only at consumption; clipboard baseline is the v44.4.5 W3C shape.
- safeStorage is a thin facade over a host `secrets` module; Linux `basic_text` plaintext degradation is reported, never emulated.
- Blocking dialogs (`showMessageBoxSync`, draw.io close path) depend on the panel's S0 link-drain gate; until then they are SCAFFOLDED (typed throw + fix-it) or served through the worker-owned transport once approved.

research.summary: [fact] Family = Electron `webviewTag` element: 113 members (65 methods, 35 events, 13 attributes), renderer-only, not exported, carrying Electron's own "we recommend not to use the webview tag" warning. [fact] Corpus demand for the tag itself is zero: draw.io's 7 "webview" hits are six `webviewTag: false` and one `will-attach-webview` → `event.preventDefault()`; Zettlr and electron-quick-start contain no `<webview>`. What the corpus actually needs from this unit is the renderer-side compat user-script: `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld` (draw.io 2, Zettlr 5), `ipcRenderer.send/on/once/removeListener/removeAllListeners` (draw.io), `ipcRenderer.invoke` (Zettlr 187 sites) and `sendSync` (Zettlr 6, synchronous `config.get` inside preload-exposed functions), `ipcRenderer.setMaxListeners(100)`, `process.type/versions/platform/env/argv` re-exposed to the page, `webPreferences.additionalArguments` read as `process.argv` in preload, `webUtils.getPathForFile`, and an isolated-world `window.navigation` listener that only works because page code cannot reach preload objects. [fact] Keld live state: macOS-only `window.keld.invoke` installed as a `WKContentWorld.defaultClientWorld` document-start user script plus a frozen pageWorld facade (channel 1 only, 4096 B, one pending invoke, host-minted document nonce, `KELD-WV-011`); WebView2 injects no bridge at all (wry's 96–109 ms blocking injection was deliberately removed); WebKitGTK is wry scaffold with no isolated world; no preload loading, no `@keld/web` package, no renderer `@keld/electron` shim, no custom scheme, no window registry beyond `LifecycleSession` window counting; devtools: WebView2 debug-on/release-off until guard owns `web.devtools`, wry open/close elsewhere. Recommended sequencing: (1) Tier-1 renderer user-script over `window.keld` (requires lifting the KEL-142 floor: multiple pending invokes, string channels, structured-clone codec, host→renderer events) with isolation claimed only on WebKit engines and a documented ▲ page-world emulation on WebView2; (2) `webviewTag:false`/`will-attach-webview` zero-webview semantics as a conformance cell now; (3) `<webview>` → host-owned child webview stays Tier 3 and is not on the draw.io/Zettlr path. Two design atoms need prototypes before any spec: `sendSync` feasibility on system engines (no synchronous native bridge exists on any of the three; only a synchronous XHR to a host scheme could block), and whether WebView2's page-world emulation of `contextBridge` leaks preload internals.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: [fact] 'Preload scripts contain code that executes in a renderer process before its web content begins loading' (process-model.md); webview preload 'will be loaded before other scripts run in the guest page'; must be file: (asar virtual dirs); when guest has no node integration 'this script will still have access to all Node APIs, but global objects injected by Node will be deleted after this script has finished executing'; with nodeintegrationinsubframes 'All your preloads will load for every iframe, you can use process.isMainFrame'.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: WKUserScript AtDocumentStart forMainFrameOnly=true matches the default (main-frame-only) but not nodeIntegrationInSubFrames. WebView2 AddScriptToExecuteOnDocumentCreated runs 'on all top-level document and child frame page navigations' — over-broad; must self-gate on frame identity or Electron's main-frame-only default is violated. The Node-globals-then-delete semantics cannot exist on Keld; a preload that uses Node APIs runs with sandbox:false expectations and must fail with a diagnostic, never silently.
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Fixture page records `performance.now()` and a marker set by preload; assert marker exists before the first inline <script> runs, in the main frame; assert a same-origin child iframe does NOT see the marker by default; negative control: remove injection → marker absent → test fails. Run per engine; classify divergence per KEL-79 table.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: [fact] source: `if (!process.contextIsolated) throw new Error('contextBridge API can only be used when contextIsolation is enabled')`; contextIsolation defaults true since Electron 12; with isolation on, `window.hello = 'wave'` in preload is undefined to the page.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: Keld isolation is non-optional. An app with `contextIsolation: false` that assigns window.* in preload expecting the page to see it will break; the migrate path must emit an explicit ✘/diagnostic for contextIsolation:false and nodeIntegration:true rather than running a 'compatible-looking' page-world preload.

Second cell: webPreferences.contextIsolation:false → Keld emits KELD-COMPAT diagnostic and scoreboard ✘; negative control: silently honoring it fails the cell.

semantic_traps.member: contextBridge value marshalling (proxies, immutability, dropped prototypes/Symbols/Error props)
semantic_traps.electron_behavior: [fact] 'Any data / primitives sent in the API become immutable and updates on either side of the bridge do not result in an update on the other side'; Function: 'Prototype modifications are dropped. Sending classes or constructors will not work'; Error: 'Custom properties on the Error object will be lost'; Symbol: 'dropped'; functions are 'proxied through Electron to ensure that contexts remain isolated'; exposing the whole ipcRenderer yields 'an empty object'.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: Zettlr's `ipc.on` returns an unsubscribe closure precisely because 'the function will be cloned across the context bridge, so not the same object'. A WebView2 page-world emulation would hand the page the same object identity (no clone) and break apps relying on cloning semantics or leak preload internals; a WebKit two-world implementation must reproduce the exact drop table.
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Table-driven cell per row of Electron's type-support table: expose {fn, promise, err:Object.assign(new Error('x'),{custom:1}), sym:Symbol(), cls:class{}}; page asserts fn !== exposed original, err.custom === undefined, sym absent, class call throws, mutation on one side invisible on the other. Negative control on WebView2 emulation: identity-equality passes → cell must be recorded ▲ not ✔.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: [fact] send/invoke use the Structured Clone Algorithm; 'Sending Functions, Promises, Symbols, WeakMaps, or WeakSets will throw an exception'; DOM objects (ImageBitmap, File, DOMMatrix) throw; invoke rejects with `Error invoking remote method '${channel}': ${error}` and 'only the message property from the original error is provided to the renderer'.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: arch 02 §5 plans a postcard SCV codec; it must throw synchronously (DataCloneError shape) for the same inputs and must map kipc ERR frames to the exact 'Error invoking remote method' string with message-only fidelity; a typed KELD-* error leaking through changes caller contract.
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Cells: send(()=>{}) throws synchronously; invoke to a handler that throws Object.assign(new Error('boom'),{code:7}) rejects with message === "Error invoking remote method 'ch': Error: boom" and no `code`; Date/Map/Set/TypedArray round-trip equal. Negative control: a handler rejection surfacing a KELD-IPC-* string fails the cell.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: [fact] 'Send a message to the main process via channel and expect a result synchronously'; 'Sending a synchronous message will block the whole renderer process until the reply is received'; main sets event.returnValue.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: No system engine offers a synchronous JS→native message with reply (WKScriptMessageHandler replies are async; WebView2 postMessage is one-way JSON; WebKitGTK handlers return async). KEL-127 requires sendSync to remain a blocking CALL with deadline, rate-limited and dev-warned — the only engine mechanism that blocks the main thread is a synchronous XHR to a host-owned scheme (arch 02 bulk lane), which is deprecated-but-functional in browsers and depends on KEL-79. Zettlr calls sendSync inside preload-exposed `config.get`/citation callbacks that the page consumes synchronously, so an async replacement silently breaks Zettlr.

decisions.question: Where does preload + compat user-script execute per engine, and what isolation claim can Keld honestly make?
decisions.proposed_answer: macOS: append preload and compat script to the existing MacRendererBridge WKUserContentController in WKContentWorld.defaultClientWorld (AtDocumentStart, main-frame-only) — real isolation, same as Electron's world 999 model; contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld = isolated→page proxy installed by the pageWorld facade pattern already used for window.keld (✔). Linux: WebKitGTK webkit_user_script_new_for_world + register_script_message_handler(name, world_name) (both UI-process APIs, 2.22/2.40+) — real isolation (✔) but requires replacing the wry scaffold's init-script path. Windows: WebView2 exposes no isolated-world API in its reference and WebView2Feedback has no tracked request; the only hook is AddScriptToExecuteOnDocumentCreated in the page realm, all frames, async. Therefore WebView2 contextBridge is a documented ▲ emulation (closure-scoped, frozen, non-configurable, runs before page scripts, self-gated to `window === window.top`), with the rule that preload must contain no secrets or authority — which Keld's host-minted document nonce already guarantees. The security claim 'page cannot access preload realm' (KEL-142 acceptance) is true on WebKit engines only and must be stated per engine on the scoreboard.

decisions.question: How is `require('electron')` (and Node globals) resolved inside a preload on Keld?
decisions.proposed_answer: Mirror Electron's own sandboxed-preload contract exactly: `keld build`/`keld migrate` bundles each preload (Electron already forbids CommonJS splitting under sandbox) and provides a polyfilled `require` whose loadable map is precisely {contextBridge, crashReporter(map), ipcRenderer, nativeImage(subset), webFrame(subset), webUtils, events, timers, url, node:events, node:timers, node:url} plus globals Buffer, process (synthesized subset), setImmediate/clearImmediate. Preload bytes are resolved by the host from the verified app bundle (ExpectedAppIdentity), never from an app-supplied absolute path; `file:`/`asar:` paths are rewritten at migrate time. Any preload importing outside that map (i.e. relying on sandbox:false / nodeIntegration) is a static-analysis ✘ with an exact diagnostic naming the module; no legacy-profile auto-downgrade.
evidence: sandbox.md: exact module list and 'you will not be able to use CommonJS modules to separate your preload script into multiple files'

decisions.alternatives_rejected: Running preload in a Bun role (preload must share the DOM/window with the page — a Bun process has no DOM; would invent a second renderer model). Allowing `require` of arbitrary app files from preload (needs filesystem authority inside the webview principal).
decisions.unknowns: crashReporter and nativeImage subsets available in preload are owned by other units; exact mapping here is only 'present in the loadable map'.

decisions.question: Can ipcRenderer.sendSync keep its blocking caller contract on system engines, and through which lane?
decisions.proposed_answer: [fact] None of WKScriptMessageHandler (async reply), WebView2 postMessage (one-way JSON), or WebKitGTK message handlers block the calling JS. The only engine-neutral primitive that blocks the main thread with a reply is a synchronous XMLHttpRequest to a host-owned scheme/origin (the arch 02 §3 bulk lane). Proposed: sendSync = synchronous XHR POST to `keld://c/el-sync/{channel}` carrying the host-minted document nonce header, host enforces deadline + rate limit, dev build logs a warning per call (KEL-127 wording); response body is the SCV-encoded returnValue. Promise-returning emulation is rejected (changes caller contract; Zettlr's exposed `config.get` must return synchronously). If the prototype shows sync XHR is blocked by CSP/COEP or by engine policy on custom schemes, sendSync becomes a documented ✘ with per-call diagnostics.
evidence: ipc-renderer.md: 'block the whole renderer process until the reply is received'
research 06 bridge table: no binary/sync path; custom scheme streaming on all three (GTK 2.40+)
arch 02 §3: bulk rides keld://c/{channel}; postMessage control-only
briefing KEL-127: sendSync replacement must stay blocking CALL with deadline, rate-limited, dev-warned
Zettlr preload: sendSync inside synchronous exposed functions (config.get/set, citation)
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Atomics.wait on SharedArrayBuffer (main thread cannot block on Atomics.wait in browsers; requires COOP/COEP and a worker relay). Busy-wait on a flag set by an async reply (freezes the event loop that must deliver the reply — deadlock). Async Promise shim with a quirks flag (violates KEL-127; breaks Zettlr synchronously).
decisions.unknowns: [unknown] Whether WKURLSchemeHandler serves synchronous XHR on the main thread without deadlock when the handler's reply is produced on the host UI thread (WKURLSchemeHandler callbacks arrive on the main thread; a round trip to Bun must not block that thread — KEL-142 §6 rule). [unknown] WebView2 WebResourceRequested deferral semantics under sync XHR. [unknown] Chromium/WebKit timelines for removing synchronous XHR entirely.

decisions.question: What must change in the KEL-142 window.keld floor before an Electron renderer shim can sit on it without a second protocol?
decisions.proposed_answer: Lift, in place, four frozen floor rules via a KEL-142 successor spec (candidate owner KEL-80): (1) pending set > 1 with host-enforced credit (Zettlr fires concurrent invokes from 65 files); (2) string channel names mapped through a host-declared compat namespace (`el:*`, arch 02 §5) onto u16 ids, with undeclared channels failing KELD-WV-011 — the manifest, not the page, declares channels; (3) payload > 4096 B via the bulk lane reference, not a larger inline bound; (4) host→renderer push (`window.keld.on`/EVENT) for ipcRenderer.on and webContents.send. All stay on the one wv-link decoder, one app-link, one document nonce. The Electron shim imports `@keld/web` (to be created) and never a native handler. Until these land, the shim's scoreboard cells are SCAFFOLDED, not PARTIAL.

decisions.question: When <webview> ships (Tier 3), is it a host-owned child webview or an iframe emulation, and which attributes map to which Keld owners?
decisions.proposed_answer: Host-owned child webview: a second WebviewId principal created by the host, parented to the embedder's window and positioned from an embedder-reported rect (ResizeObserver/IntersectionObserver → host set_bounds), with its own navigation generation, its own preload (same A2/A3 rules), partition→KEL-135 store identity (`persist:`=identity-bound, else memory-only), src/loadURL→host navigate under the KEL-79 navigation allow-list, allowpopups→deny unless granted (KEL-168 handler), useragent→per-view engine UA, nodeintegration/disablewebsecurity/plugins/enable|disableblinkfeatures→never (refused at attach with a code), embedder↔guest ipc (send/sendToHost/ipc-message)→KEL-75 T3 virtual-port pair bound to both generations, executeJavaScript/insertCSS/print/printToPDF/capturePage/openDevTools from the embedder→host-mediated calls evaluated as the embedder principal against explicit grants. getWebContentsId returns a host-minted opaque id. This preserves the 'separate process, asynchronous interaction' semantics Electron documents; an iframe emulation cannot.

security_mapping.keld_mapping: Each channel is a manifest-declared compat channel (`el:*` namespace) granted to Principal::Webview(WebviewId, generation); remote-content webviews default `channels: []` (arch 03 §4.3). Undeclared channel → KELD-WV-011 before app dispatch. postMessage ports → KEL-75 host-owned virtual-port pairs, one-shot transfer, receiver-bound.

Host-mediated virtual-port pair bound to (embedder WebviewId, gen) and (guest WebviewId, gen); stale generation drops; frameId never used as identity. No ambient grant: the pair is minted at attach.

Synthesized per window by the host: argv = declared additionalArguments only (never the real host argv); env = empty or declared allowlist (Zettlr copies process.env into the page — on Keld this must be the declared subset, ▲); versions.electron='0.0.1' shim; versions.chrome only on WebView2 (▲ elsewhere).

Host-mediated: engine drop/open events mint a per-drop retained scope (KEL-130 retained filesystem) and return the path only when `fs.read` for that scope is granted by dialog/drop selection; ✘ where the engine exposes no backing path.
