platform_notes.note: [fact] WKContentWorld (defaultClientWorld / named) available macOS 11+; Keld fails closed below 11 (product baseline 12+). Isolated world shares the DOM — DOM state is not protected, only JS variables. User scripts are AtDocumentStart/AtDocumentEnd, forMainFrameOnly selectable; evaluateJavaScript(_:in:in:) can target a world and frame. [fact] Service Workers do not work for pages served over a WKURLSchemeHandler custom scheme (WebKit 206741, still NEW; only http/https with App-Bound Domains) — any compat page relying on SW must load over authenticated HTTPS (KEL-79 adapter) or be ✘. [fact] Devtools = Safari Web Inspector, no CDP; opening programmatically relies on `developerExtrasEnabled` + private `_inspector` in wry — App Store rules forbid devtools features in release builds; `isDevToolsFocused`, `devtools-*` events have no public hook (▲/✘). [fact] WKScriptMessageHandler replies are async; no synchronous bridge (A4). [fact] Per-view UA via customUserAgent; print via WKWebView.printOperation (macOS 11+); capturePage via takeSnapshot; findInPage via WKFindConfiguration (macOS 10.15+). [inference] render-process-gone maps only to webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate (no reason). [unknown] File backing path for dropped files (webUtils.getPathForFile).

[fact] AddScriptToExecuteOnDocumentCreated is the only pre-page hook: page realm (no isolated/content world API in the ICoreWebView2 reference; zero WebView2Feedback requests found), runs in ALL frames (must self-gate for Electron's main-frame-only default), asynchronous with an open first-navigation race (#5716) — Keld must add an injection-complete witness to the guard→devtools→bounds→navigate typestate; wry's synchronous wait cost 96–109 ms and is rejected. [fact] postMessage accepts JSON-convertible values only; no binary lane (bulk via WebResourceRequested). [fact] Virtual host mapping supports Service Workers but mappings must be consistent across all WebViews in the browser instance — relevant to KEL-79's 'WebView2 virtual-host SW limitation' acceptance and to per-partition <webview> isolation. [fact] CDP is available (CallDevToolsProtocolMethod) but is on the never list for production; OpenDevToolsWindow exists, there is no close API (closeDevTools ▲). [fact] Popups escape the guard until a NewWindowRequested handler lands (KEL-168) — allowpopups must stay deny until then. [fact] Keld real-qualifies only Windows 11 x64 today. [fact] IME/focus: no MoveFocusRequested/NotifyParentWindowPositionChanged registration yet (research 199) — Tab/IME handoff for a child <webview> is unproven.

platform_notes.platform: Linux (GTK + WebKitGTK; wry scaffold, GTK3/WebKit2GTK 4.1 today)
platform_notes.note: [fact] Isolated worlds exist: webkit_user_script_new_for_world (2.22+) and register_script_message_handler(name, world_name) (2.40+) from the UI process; WebKitScriptWorld objects (web-process extension API) are not needed for user scripts + handlers but are for window-object-cleared hooks. [fact] Custom-scheme request body access requires 2.40+ (historically broken, wry#666); distros freeze WebKitGTK per release so the compat baseline must be version-gated at runtime with a doctor line. [fact] WebGL silently falls back to software and masks the renderer string; NVIDIA+Wayland DMA-BUF needs WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1 (KEL-132 re-exec, live); WebRTC backend is being re-plumbed onto GstWebRTC (treat unstable); drag-and-drop fixes still landing in 2.51.x; media strategy conservative (H.264-first). [fact] Devtools = WebKit inspector behind a build flag; open/close via wry today. [fact] Unhandled media requests deny by default on WebKitGTK 2.52.6/wry 0.56.1 but that is not evidence of guard evaluation (KEL-132 binds the real principal). [unknown] Fcitx/IBus candidate placement and Compose handling in Keld (research 199); portal-first file access affects webUtils.getPathForFile.

platform_notes.platform: Cross-engine browser quirks list (web baseline input for the polyfill pack / feature-gate scanner)
platform_notes.note: [fact] Service Workers: WKWebView ✘ on custom schemes; WebView2 ✔ with consistent virtual-host mappings; WebKitGTK ✔ on http(s), custom-scheme behavior untested (KEL-79). [fact] Custom schemes: streaming on all three (GTK 2.40+); privilege bits (standard/secure/fetch/SW) are a host declaration, not a string router (research 186 row 1). [fact] iframe origins: opaque origin on NavigateToString/with_html blocks fetch (learnings 2026-08-14) — compat pages must load from a real origin. [fact] Clipboard: Electron's synchronous clipboard-read permission is a documented exception in its default-allow handler (research 186 row 4); web clipboard API prompts differ per engine — Keld routes clipboard through the native broker, not navigator.clipboard permissions. [fact] Drag/drop: WebKitGTK fixes in 2.51.x; navigateOnDragDrop default false in Electron must be emulated (prevent default navigation on file drop). [fact] IME/focus/accessibility: UNPROVEN on all engines (research 199). [fact] WebGL/WebGPU: WebKitGTK software fallback masking; WebGPU availability per OS version — [unknown] exact matrix. [fact] Codecs/media: WebKit-family H.264-first; WebRTC unstable on Linux. [fact] Media capture: default-deny via guard on all three (live v0). [fact] Storage: WebSQL default true in Electron (enableWebSQL) but removed in modern WebKit/Chromium → ✘ documented-never. [fact] DevTools: CDP only on WebView2; inspector elsewhere. [unknown] showOpenFilePicker/File System Access on WebKit (listed as lagging in research 06).

prototype_candidates.question: Does a WebView2 page-world emulation of contextBridge leak preload internals or object identity, and does the async injection race actually bite?

never_list.surface: <webview nodeintegration> / webPreferences.nodeIntegration:true / nodeIntegrationInWorker / nodeintegrationinsubframes
never_list.rationale: Renderer Node integration is the briefing never-list item; Electron itself documents it disables the sandbox (sandbox.md) and escalates XSS to RCE (security.md item 2). Keld webviews have no ambient OS authority by construction.

never_list.surface: disablewebsecurity / webSecurity:false / allowRunningInsecureContent
never_list.rationale: Disables same-origin policy (security.md item 6, 8); Keld's webview principal/origin model (arch 03 §1) and CSP injection depend on SOP.

never_list.surface: enableblinkfeatures / disableblinkfeatures / experimentalFeatures / webpreferences feature strings beyond the allowlisted subset
never_list.rationale: Arbitrary Chromium/Blink flags are on the briefing never-list; they are meaningless on WebKit engines and would make behavior engine-divergent and unmeasurable.

never_list.surface: plugins attribute
never_list.rationale: Browser plugins (PPAPI) have no equivalent on any system engine and widen attack surface; documented-never.

never_list.surface: inspectServiceWorker / inspectSharedWorker / any CDP-backed webview method in production
never_list.rationale: Full Chrome DevTools Protocol in production webviews is on the never list (briefing; research 13); only WebView2 even has CDP.

never_list.surface: sendInputEvent from a renderer (embedder) into a guest
never_list.rationale: Synthetic OS-level input injection is authority a webview principal must not hold; at most legacy-profile with explicit grant, never default.

never_list.surface: Exposing raw ipcRenderer / ipcRenderer.on / Node globals via contextBridge in Keld-authored shims
never_list.rationale: Electron's own guidance (context-bridge.md 'security footgun'; security.md item 20); Keld's shim exposes only the typed facade, and corpus apps that do this get their own code's behavior, not a Keld-provided escape hatch.

never_list.surface: A second renderer-native handler (`window.ipc`, `window.electron` native object) beside window.keld
never_list.rationale: KEL-142 Independence and §12 forbid a second renderer-routing protocol; one wv-link decoder, one document nonce, one app-link.

never_list.surface: process.env passthrough of the real host environment to preload/page
never_list.rationale: Zettlr copies process.env into the page; on Keld the host environment is authority-bearing material (app-link tokens live in the host) — only a declared allowlist is exposed.

never_list.surface: enableWebSQL / WebSQL
never_list.rationale: Removed from modern WebKit and Chromium; cannot be polyfilled honestly; documented-✘.

A1 lists blocked_by: [] — that is wrong. verdicts.reason: Engine placement facts survive: macOS install() uses one per-view WKUserContentController with the isolated script/handler in defaultClientWorld and only the frozen facade in pageWorld, AtDocumentStart, forMainFrameOnly=true, fail-closed below macOS 11 — appending preload+compat script there is the right seam. WebKitGTK APIs are correctly cited and, better than the author states, the UI process can both receive replies (register_script_message_handler_with_reply(name, world_name), 2.40) and evaluate into the named world (webkit_web_view_evaluate_javascript(..., world_name, ...), 2.40), so the GTK [unknown] about needing a WebKitWebProcessExtension is resolved negative. Two load-bearing claims are false. (1) 'contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld = isolated→page proxy installed by the pageWorld facade pattern already used for window.keld': the existing pattern is an async window.postMessage relay whose shape KEL-142 §5.1 restricts to 'no broader shape than window.keld.invoke'; exposing arbitrary app function tables widens the relay grammar (§12: stop and revise), and an async relay cannot return values synchronously, which Zettlr's exposed config.get / citation callback require (they return sendSync results synchronously to the page). A cross-world synchronous call path (shared DOM per WKContentWorld doc, e.g. synchronous CustomEvent dispatch) is an unlisted design atom. (2) 'preload must contain no secrets or authority — which Keld's host-minted document nonce already guarantees' is wrong on WebView2: kel142 §5.2 step 4 has the isolated script retain the nonce outside the page world; with no isolated world on WebView2 the nonce would live in the page realm and be readable, so the identity model is not transferable. Identity there must come from host-side engine metadata: the ICoreWebView2 instance that raised WebMessageReceived (host-bound WebviewId) plus host-tracked navigation generation; WebMessageReceivedEventArgs.Source is only 'the URI of the document that sent this web message', not a frame identity. The 'self-gated to window === window.top' emulation is page-controlled and therefore not a boundary; whether ICoreWebView2.WebMessageReceived fires for child frames vs only ICoreWebView2Frame.WebMessageReceived was not verified by the author or by me.

extra_findings.finding: Synchronous cross-world calls are a missing design atom. Zettlr exposes functions whose page-visible return value is produced synchronously (config.get, getCitationCallback → sendSync). Even if sendSync itself is solved via a synchronous XHR to a host scheme, the isolated→page function proxy must also be synchronous. The existing KEL-142 relay is async window.postMessage. WKContentWorld documents a shared DOM across worlds, so a synchronous DOM event dispatch (CustomEvent with mutable detail) is the candidate mechanism; it has no owner, no test oracle and no mention in the object.

epic.title: compat(renderer): preload runtime, sandboxed-preload require shim, process polyfill, disabled-<webview> contract, browser-quirk ledger
epic.body:
## Scope
`<webview>` tag (113 members, Tier 3) plus the renderer-side compat user-script: `ipcRenderer`/`contextBridge`/`webFrame` subset, `process` polyfill (`type='renderer'`, versions, argv from `additionalArguments`, platform/arch/env policy), `webUtils.getPathForFile`, preload execution order. Live today: macOS KEL-142 isolated `WKContentWorld` script + frozen page-world facade (`window.keld.invoke` only), main-frame-only, document start; no app-preload injection; no `@keld/web`.

## Corpus demand (corrected: draw.io DISABLES `<webview>` everywhere — all 7 hits are `webviewTag:false` or a `will-attach-webview` preventDefault)
draw.io preload: `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld('electron', {request, registerMsgListener, sendMessage, listenOnce})` over `ipcRenderer.send/on/once`, `process.type/versions`, `--initial-adaptive-colors=` from `process.argv`, localStorage seeding, a Navigation-API guard. Zettlr preload: ipc {send, sendSync, invoke, on → off closure}, config get/set via sendSync, `process` {platform, version, versions, arch, uptime, getSystemVersion, env copy, argv}, `webUtils.getPathForFile`; `sandbox:false` on two windows that still only use the sandboxed allow-list.

## Maturity ladder
- L0: `webviewTag` accepted and defaulted false; `<webview>` is an unknown element; `will-attach-webview` registrable (never fires).
- L1: draw.io's preload runs byte-for-byte unmodified in a Keld content world and its page round trips work on macOS.
- L2: preload order (before page scripts), sandboxed `require` allow-list, process polyfill fields, isolation negative tests, Error/Symbol value-table semantics pass pinned entries per engine (✔ WK/WebKitGTK; ▲ WebView2 where no isolated world exists).
- L3: Zettlr preload (sync-returning wrappers) handled per the F04-A3/A5 decisions.

## Linear owners consumed
KEL-142 (world/injection seam; spec revision for a third world and the relay), KEL-79 (WebView2 worlds, origin), KEL-80 (floor v2), KEL-132.

## Design facts fixed by research (invariants refuter; semantics refuter pending batch 2)
- Ship the renderer user-script + disabled-webview contract first; `<webview>` element stays Tier 3 as a host-owned child webview mapping (never a DOM-embedded engine), with zero corpus pressure.
- The preload runs in a dedicated app content world (third world) registered at document start on the same per-view user-content controller as the KEL-142 scripts, with a relay no broader than `window.keld.*`; the KEL-142 isolation negative tests must pass with the preload present (panel contested decision PANEL-D21 decides same-world vs third-world on measured results).
- `require('electron')` resolves exactly the sandboxed-preload module map (contextBridge, crashReporter, ipcRenderer, nativeImage, webFrame, webUtils) plus events/timers/url and the globals Buffer/process/setImmediate/clearImmediate; preload bytes are host-loaded from the bundle-relative path inside the content-authenticated package (never an absolute path read).
- `process.env` re-exposure to the page (Zettlr) is an information-flow decision with no owner (open).
- Migrated apps change origin when `file://` or a custom scheme is replaced; web-storage continuity is a product decision (open F07-A6).

research.unit: F08 diagnostics-crash-tracing (crashReporter, contentTracing, app.getAppMetrics/ProcessMetric/CPUUsage/MemoryInfo, process.getProcessMemoryInfo/getHeapStatistics/getCPUUsage, GPUFeatureStatus) — Electron v44.4.5 pinned docs vs Keld origin/main d150a14, 2026-10-06
research.summary: [fact] Corpus demand for this family's module surfaces is zero: neither draw.io Desktop, Zettlr nor electron-quick-start calls crashReporter.*, contentTracing.*, app.getAppMetrics, app.getGPUFeatureStatus/getGPUInfo, process.getProcessMemoryInfo/getHeapStatistics/getCPUUsage (grep over the clones, 2026-10-06). What the corpus DOES need from the diagnostics area is adjacent: draw.io listens to webContents 'render-process-gone' twice (reads only details.reason into a string) and installs process.on('uncaughtException') → app.exit(1) in export mode; Zettlr handles BrowserWindow 'unresponsive' → destroy() and logs process 'unhandledRejection'; both call app.disableHardwareAcceleration() before ready. So the sequencing answer is: (1) land the host-emitted engine process-gone and Bun-generation-gone events first (they ride on live keld-runtime CrashLedger/KEL-75 generations and on engine hooks keld-wv has not yet wired: WKWebView webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate, WebView2 ProcessFailed, WebKitGTK web-process-terminated); (2) ship process.getHeapStatistics/getCPUUsage/getProcessMemoryInfo as a pure Bun-side facade (Bun 1.4.2 exposes process.memoryUsage, process.cpuUsage, process.resourceUsage, node:v8.getHeapStatistics, bun:jsc heapStats — probed live) with KB conversion and documented ▲ for fields Bun cannot derive (private/shared); (3) ship crashReporter as a local-state facade (start/addExtraParameter/removeExtraParameter/getParameters/get/setUploadToServer BEHAVIOR_MATCH-capable because they are pure data; getLastCrashReport/getUploadedReports honestly return null/[] because Keld has no uploader, and Electron itself only returns UPLOADED reports) with upload gated behind an explicit `net.connect` grant + opt-in — Electron's default uploadToServer:true cannot survive default-deny and is a documented ▲; (4) app.getAppMetrics must consume architecture 01 §5.1's ruled census (keld-owned processes: host, macOS guardian, Bun primary, named roles; engine helpers are separate diagnostics) and its counters (resident set + private companion, KiB) rather than inventing a second census; WebView2 GetProcessInfos gives pid+kind only (caller reads memory itself), WKWebView exposes no public web-process pid; (5) contentTracing is a documented-never in production (Chromium tracing service; WebKit has none; briefing never-list #10) delivered as an arch 07 §2 structured error; (6) GPUFeatureStatus/getGPUInfo are research: only Linux has a Keld-owned signal today (KEL-132 GpuSafeMode three-state), the enum has no 'unknown' value, so an honest mapping needs a ruling. Live Keld today: keld_runtime::CrashLedger {count, last (KELD-RUNTIME-012 + bounded stderr tail 64 KiB head / 192 KiB tail), stdout_len_at_last_crash, self_termination_count, last_self_termination}, Supervisor::crash_ledger()/current_pid(), KELD-RUNTIME-002 breaker (3 crashes/30 s sliding), KELD-CORE-033 surfacing in the no-flag host; @keld/electron exports only `app`; no crash dumps, no uploader, no process census code, no engine process-failure hooks, no GPU status API. Key new observable with no Electron analog: in Keld the developer "main" (Bun) can crash and be replaced while the host-owned window survives; the restarted generation could be told about its predecessor's death — that needs a Keld-named contract (KEL-143 territory), not an Electron API name.

decisions.question: What does the Tier-2 'crashReporter map' honestly mean in Keld, given Keld has no crash-dump capture or uploader and default-deny forbids Electron's uploadToServer:true default?
decisions.proposed_answer: crashReporter becomes a local-state facade in @keld/electron: start(options) validates and stores {submitURL, productName (default app name), uploadToServer, rateLimit, compress, extra, globalExtra} and enforces the documented byte limits; addExtraParameter/removeExtraParameter/getParameters/getUploadToServer/setUploadToServer are pure data and can reach BEHAVIOR_MATCH; getLastCrashReport returns null and getUploadedReports returns [] (this is Electron-faithful whenever nothing was uploaded, because Electron only returns UPLOADED reports). No minidump, no network: uploading anything requires a future approved spec that (a) names the record source (CrashLedger crash-class facts: pid, exit status, bounded stderr tail, generation) — not a minidump — (b) requires a `net.connect` grant whose URL scope covers submitURL, and (c) treats uploadToServer as an opt-in that the manifest, not the app, decides. The effective default (no upload) is a documented ▲ on the scoreboard with a quirks flag, never a silent downgrade (KEL-127). crashReporter in the renderer is ✘ (Keld renderers have no process object; Electron requires preload+contextBridge anyway).
evidence: [fact] Electron: 'This method must be called before using any other crashReporter APIs'; uploadToServer default true; submitURL required unless uploadToServer false; getLastCrashReport: 'Only crash reports that have been uploaded will be returned' (crash-reporter.md v44.4.5, retrieved 2026-10-06)
[fact] Keld has no dump/upload code: grep of crates/ for minidump/crashpad/upload returns nothing; keld-native exposes FsBroker fs.read/fs.write only (briefing current code facts)
[fact] CrashLedger exists and carries pid, exit status, bounded stderr tail, stdout ordering point (crates/keld-runtime/src/lib.rs CrashLedger, SelfTerminationRecord)
[fact] Corpus: zero crashReporter call sites in draw.io, Zettlr, quick-start (grep 2026-10-06)
[fact] Briefing invariant 2: missing Electron permission handler must NOT become allow; arch 03 default-deny
decisions.confidence: medium (shape high; whether Keld ever uploads crash records at all is a user-owned product decision)
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Host-side crashpad/minidump writer + uploader — a new privileged network authority with no spec owner, violates reuse-before-rewrite and YAGNI (zero corpus demand); (b) throw on crashReporter.start() — breaks apps that call it unconditionally at boot (common in the wider ecosystem even if absent from this corpus) and gives no scoreboard cell; (c) returning CrashLedger's last crash from getLastCrashReport — diverges from Electron's uploaded-only semantics and leaks local facts under an API apps treat as 'already sent'.
decisions.unknowns: Electron's behavior when an extra key exceeds 39 bytes / value exceeds 127 (start) or 20320 (addExtraParameter) bytes — throw vs truncate — is not stated in the pinned doc. Whether a future Keld crash record should include Bun-side extras (Electron does NOT propagate main-process extras to renderer crashes). Bun's own panic reporter behavior (prints a bun.report URL; whether any automatic upload exists) unverified.
blocked_by: user decision: does Keld ever transmit crash data off-device (yes → spec with net.connect + opt-in; no → crashReporter stays local-only forever and uploadToServer is a documented ▲)

decisions.question: Which process-gone events can Keld deliver honestly, over which primitive, and with what reason fidelity — given Keld's process family (host, guardian, Bun primary, named roles, engine helpers) differs from Chromium's?
decisions.proposed_answer: Three distinct event sources, one host-emitted event family over the app link, consumed by two Electron facades: (1) webContents/app 'render-process-gone' ← engine web-content-process termination, wired in keld-wv per backend (WKWebView WKNavigationDelegate webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate; WebView2 ICoreWebView2 ProcessFailed with ICoreWebView2ProcessFailedEventArgs2 Reason/ExitCode; WebKitGTK WebKitWebView::web-process-terminated with WebKitWebProcessTerminationReason). Reason fidelity is platform-bound: WebKitGTK → {crashed, oom, killed}; WebView2 → full reason + exitCode (259 STILL_ACTIVE when unresponsive); WKWebView → no reason at all. Proposed ▲: on macOS emit reason 'crashed' with exitCode undefined under a quirks flag `renderProcessGoneReasonCoarse`, because the corpus only stringifies details.reason (draw.io) — never fabricate an exitCode. (2) app 'child-process-gone' (type 'Utility') ← KEL-75 named-role generation exit observed by the supervisor (clean-exit/abnormal-exit/killed by exit status/signal; 'oom' only where the OS says so). (3) The Bun PRIMARY dying has NO Electron analog (Electron's main cannot observe its own death); do not map it to any Electron event. It is a Keld-native contract (KEL-143): the successor generation may read the predecessor's CrashLedger facts through @keld/api, and the renderer sees nothing unless the app chooses to tell it. Events are emitted once per termination, after the engine/supervisor observed it and before any reload Keld performs; window identity survives (host owns it).
evidence: [fact] Electron render-process-gone reasons: clean-exit, abnormal-exit, killed, crashed, oom, launch-failed, integrity-failure, memory-eviction; exitCode is platform launch error when launch-failed (structures/render-process-gone-details.md v44.4.5, retrieved 2026-10-06)
[fact] Electron child-process-gone: type Utility/Zygote/Sandbox helper/GPU/Pepper Plugin..., reason same enum, exitCode, serviceName, name (app.md v44.4.5)

[fact] Apple: webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate(_:) 'WebKit calls this method when the process for the specified web view terminates for any reason' — no reason parameter; macOS 10.11+ (developer.apple.com JSON, retrieved 2026-10-06)

[fact] Microsoft: ICoreWebView2ProcessFailedEventArgs2 get_Reason, get_ExitCode ('always STILL_ACTIVE (259) when ... RENDER_PROCESS_UNRESPONSIVE'), get_ProcessDescription, get_FrameInfosForFailedProcess; introduced 1.0.818.41 (learn.microsoft.com, retrieved 2026-10-06)

[fact] WebKitGTK: WebKitWebView::web-process-terminated 'emitted when the web process terminates abnormally due to reason', since 2.20; reasons WEBKIT_WEB_PROCESS_CRASHED, WEBKIT_WEB_PROCESS_EXCEEDED_MEMORY_LIMIT, WEBKIT_WEB_PROCESS_TERMINATED_BY_API (webkitgtk.org, retrieved 2026-10-06)
[fact] keld-wv has none of these hooks wired (grep 2026-10-06; WebView2 backend registers only NavigationCompleted at crates/keld-wv/src/webview2/mod.rs:1972)
[fact] Corpus: draw.io uses details.reason only as a string in an error message (src/main/electron.js ~1455 and ~3115); Zettlr handles 'unresponsive' → destroy()
[fact] Research 87: 'developer main crashes independently while host-owned windows survive' is a boundary Electron does not provide (inference recorded there, no crash oracle run)
decisions.confidence: medium-high for sources and mapping; low for the macOS reason policy (needs a ruling)
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Mapping Bun-primary death to 'render-process-gone' or 'child-process-gone' — semantically false (the listener IS the process that died) and would hide the Keld-native recovery contract; (b) synthesizing exitCode on macOS — fabricated data; (c) polling engine pids from the host to detect death — no public pid on WKWebView, and the engines already deliver callbacks.
decisions.unknowns: Whether Electron fires 'render-process-gone' when the app itself destroys the window (draw.io comment says 'Not emitted when finalize destroys the window' — corpus lead, not a doc receipt). decisions.question: What census and counters does app.getAppMetrics() report in Keld, and how does it avoid becoming a second, conflicting process census beside architecture 01 §5.1?
decisions.proposed_answer: getAppMetrics is a cold host CALL that returns one ProcessMetric row per keld-owned process exactly as §5.1 defines the census: host (type 'Browser'), macOS guardian re-exec (type 'Unknown', serviceName 'keld.guardian' — no Electron analog), Bun primary (type 'Utility', serviceName 'keld.primary' — the Electron 'Browser' row is the host because the host owns windows; documented ▲ since Electron apps read the Browser row as 'my main process'), named roles (type 'Utility', serviceName = role name). Engine helper rows are appended only where a public API enumerates them: WebView2 ICoreWebView2Environment8::GetProcessInfos (pid + COREWEBVIEW2_PROCESS_KIND → 'Tab'/'GPU'/'Utility'/'Sandbox helper', memory read by the host via OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION) + GetProcessMemoryInfo); absent on macOS (no public WKWebView web-process pid; WebKit XPCs are not the app's children) and on WebKitGTK unless a public pid API is found — documented ▲ 'engine rows omitted'. MemoryInfo uses the same counters §5.1 already names: workingSetSize = resident set (ps RSS / working set), privateBytes = private footprint (Windows per Electron; Keld MAY also fill it elsewhere as a ▲), peakWorkingSetSize where the OS reports it; unit KiB (Electron 'Kilobytes'; divisor to be confirmed, see unknowns). CPUUsage per Electron: first call 0, each call resets the interval for every row at once, interval tracked per API (getAppMetrics vs process.getCPUUsage separately). No row of this API is ever a budget score; §5.1 keeps MEM-IDLE on the harness.
evidence: [fact] Electron: getAppMetrics returns ProcessMetric[] for 'all processes associated with the app'; 'each call starts a new measurement interval for every process at once' (app.md v44.4.5, retrieved 2026-10-06); ProcessMetric fields pid, type (Browser|Tab|Utility|Zygote|Sandbox helper|GPU|Pepper Plugin|Pepper Plugin Broker|Unknown), serviceName, name, cpu, creationTime, memory, sandboxed[mac,win], integrityLevel[win] (structures/process-metric.md)

[fact] Arch 01 §5.1 (KEL-129 ruling): census = keld-owned processes only (host, macOS guardian re-exec, Bun primary, named roles); engine helpers (WebKit, WebView2, WebKitGTK) and CLI dev-loop helpers excluded and 'reported as separate diagnostics'; resident set is the named counter, private footprint is a mandatory companion; 90 MiB = 92,160 KiB

[fact] WebView2 GetProcessInfos 'Provide a list of all process using same user data folder except for crashpad process'; sample code reads memory itself with GetProcessMemoryInfo PrivateUsage/1024 (learn.microsoft.com ICoreWebView2Environment8, retrieved 2026-10-06)
[fact] No census code exists in Keld crates today (grep working_set|rss|task_info|GetProcessMemoryInfo hits only tests/profile/tools)
[fact] learnings 2026-08-24 [bench/windows]: a process-tree RSS sample can be byte-stable while the tree is still incomplete (no msedgewebview2 child yet) — engine rows are timing-dependent
[fact] Corpus: zero getAppMetrics call sites
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) A second 'all children by ppid' census inside the facade — duplicates §5.1's one-owner rule and lies on macOS where WebKit XPCs are launchd children; (b) reporting Bun primary as type 'Browser' — makes the host invisible and mislabels the window owner; (c) private WKWebView `_webProcessIdentifier` — never list.

decisions.question: Can process.getHeapStatistics / getProcessMemoryInfo / getCPUUsage / crash() / hang() be served from Bun alone, and what diverges?
decisions.proposed_answer: Yes for the Bun main role, as a pure facade with no host call: getHeapStatistics ← node:v8.getHeapStatistics() renamed to camelCase and divided to KB (fields totalHeapSize, totalHeapSizeExecutable, totalPhysicalSize, totalAvailableSize, usedHeapSize, heapSizeLimit, mallocedMemory, peakMallocedMemory, doesZapGarbage — all present in Bun 1.4.2's v8 shim); getCPUUsage ← process.cpuUsage() deltas with facade-tracked interval (first call 0, cumulativeCPUUsage seconds since start, idleWakeupsPerSecond = 0 as a ▲ — Electron itself returns 0 on Windows); getProcessMemoryInfo ← Promise of {private, shared, residentSet} where only residentSet (process.memoryUsage().rss/1024) is derivable in Bun; `private`/`shared` need the host (task_info / PROCESS_MEMORY_COUNTERS_EX / smaps_rollup) → ▲ until a host diagnostics call exists; on macOS Electron omits residentSet entirely, so Keld must choose follow-Electron (omit) or extend (quirks flag). process.crash() ← process.abort() (SIGABRT → CrashLedger crash-class record, KELD-RUNTIME-012, restart/backoff — Electron's main-process crash kills the whole app instead: ▲). process.hang() ← busy loop; Keld has no Bun hang watchdog, so nothing observes it (▲/unknown). Renderer-side process.* is ✘ (no Node in Keld renderers; Electron's sandboxed renderer does expose these). getBlinkMemoryInfo/getSystemMemoryInfo: ✘ Blink; system memory via host only.
evidence: [fact] Live probe on Bun 1.4.2 (scratchpad f08-bun-probe.ts, 2026-10-06): process.memoryUsage() {rss, heapTotal, heapUsed, external, arrayBuffers}; process.cpuUsage() {user, system}; process.resourceUsage() incl. maxRSS; node:v8.getHeapStatistics() returns all 14 V8 snake_case fields; bun:jsc heapStats() {heapSize, heapCapacity, extraMemorySize, objectCount,...} and memoryUsage() {current, peak, currentCommit, peakCommit, pageFaults}; process.abort is a function; process.type undefined natively

[fact] Electron process.getHeapStatistics fields and 'all statistics are reported in Kilobytes'; getProcessMemoryInfo 'Chromium does not provide residentSet value for macOS'; getCPUUsage averages since previous call; sandboxed renderers expose crash/hang/getHeapStatistics/getProcessMemoryInfo/getCPUUsage etc. (process.md v44.4.5, retrieved 2026-10-06)
[fact] @keld/electron already patches process.versions.electron and process.type at import (packages/@keld/electron/src/index.ts)
[fact] Corpus: zero call sites for any of these
decisions.confidence: high for Bun-side shapes; medium for divergence policy
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Routing heap/CPU through the host — adds a kipc round trip for data the process already owns and duplicates OS code; (b) implementing a Bun hang watchdog just for process.hang() — YAGNI without a consumer (Electron's own 'unresponsive' is renderer-only).
decisions.unknowns: Electron KB divisor; whether to report residentSet on macOS; Bun's heap_size_limit semantics vs V8's (Bun returns a JSC-derived shim; values are not V8-equivalent — a ▲ note, not a bug).

decisions.question: Is contentTracing dev-only or never?
decisions.proposed_answer: Never in production and not shimmed in dev either: every method throws the arch 07 §2 structured compat error (code, tier status, tracking issue, workaround) — `contentTracing` has no Keld analog because it drives Chromium's tracing service across all Chromium child processes, WebKit (WKWebView/WebKitGTK) has no such service, and WebView2's public COM surface exposes no tracing control [inference]. The useful intent — 'find performance bottlenecks' — is served by the keld-benches registry beacons (PAINT-OPPORTUNITY, kipc client-timed RTT) under `keld dev`, and a future Keld-owned trace export (Chrome trace-event JSON so Perfetto opens it) would be a Keld API, not an Electron alias; it is YAGNI until a consumer appears. Scoreboard mark ✘ with 'documented-never' and the briefing's never-list #10 (full CDP / Chromium flags in production webviews) as rationale.
evidence: [fact] Electron: 'Collect tracing data from Chromium'; 'You should not use this module until the ready event'; startRecording resolves immediately if already recording ('only one trace operation can occur at a time'); stopRecording writes a temp file when resultFilePath omitted; enableHeapProfiling experimental, must precede startRecording (content-tracing.md v44.4.5, retrieved 2026-10-06)
[fact] Briefing never-list #10: arbitrary Chromium/V8 flags, full CDP in production webviews
[fact] Arch 07 §2: compat shim unsupported APIs throw structured errors naming tier status, tracking issue, workaround — never a bare 'not implemented'
[fact] Research 214: api-content-tracing-spec.ts has 18 Electron tests — not runnable under Bun as-is (REFUSE ruling)
[fact] Corpus: zero call sites
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Shimming to Instruments/ETW/perf or to WebView2 DevTools Protocol tracing in production — a fifth unique and a CDP exposure; a no-op that resolves successfully — a silent downgrade forbidden by KEL-127.
decisions.unknowns: Whether WebView2's CallDevToolsProtocolMethod could drive Tracing.* in a dev-only build — not verified and would be dev-only CDP, which the never-list already constrains.

decisions.question: What can app.getGPUFeatureStatus()/getGPUInfo() and app.disableHardwareAcceleration() honestly report or do on each engine, given GPUFeatureStatus has no 'unknown' value?
decisions.proposed_answer: Research atom, not a build decision yet. Facts available today: Linux WebKitGTK has a Keld-owned three-state GpuSafeMode (Normal / preparation required / DMA-BUF) from KEL-132's probe, which can honestly drive gpu_compositing and rasterization as 'enabled' vs 'disabled_software'/'disabled_off_ok'; macOS WKWebView exposes no public GPU-feature or disable-acceleration API [inference]; WebView2 (Chromium-derived) can be launched with host-owned additional browser arguments, so a host-controlled mapping of disableHardwareAcceleration → the engine's software-rendering switch is a single named policy, not 'arbitrary flags' — but it needs a Microsoft receipt and a KEL-132-owned spec amendment. Proposed interim: disableHardwareAcceleration() before ready records intent and is honored only where KEL-132 has a prepared path (▲ elsewhere, logged with a KELD-COMPAT code); after ready it is rejected like Electron's 'must be called before app is ready'. getGPUFeatureStatus returns only fields Keld can prove and omits the rest (▲ 'partial structure' quirks flag) — never fills 'enabled' by default. 'gpu-info-update' fires once after engine construction. Corpus demand is real for disableHardwareAcceleration (draw.io and Zettlr both call it at boot) and zero for the getters.

The code says otherwise: GpuSafeMode is an NVIDIA+Wayland DMA-BUF mitigation state, not a GPU-feature probe. `Normal` is documented as 'No known-risky driver/session combination detected' (crates/keld-wv/src/webkitgtk/mod.rs:62-72) and detect_gpu_safe_mode_with returns Normal for every non-NVIDIA or non-Wayland session regardless of whether WebKitGTK is hardware-accelerated. Emitting 'enabled' from Normal would be the fabrication the atom itself forbids, and even NvidiaWaylandDmabufDisabled only proves the DMA-BUF renderer is off, not that compositing or rasterization is software. The Linux-has-a-signal premise is therefore overstated; today no Keld owner can prove any GPUFeatureStatus field on any OS.
verdicts.evidence: crates/keld-wv/src/webkitgtk/mod.rs:55-135 (enum docs, is_degraded, reason strings, detect_gpu_safe_mode_with); docs/specs/kel132-webview-gpu-media.md:49-53,112,261-262; docs/architecture/05-webview-and-native.md:93-103; f08-refute/app.cc:1155-1160 (DisableHardwareAcceleration after ready → ThrowError 'can only be called before app is ready'), 1514-1535 (GetGPUFeatureStatus is a synchronous content::GetFeatureStatus(); GetGPUInfo rejects 'Invalid info type' / 'GPU access not allowed'); f08-refute/api_structures_gpu-feature-status.md (no 'unknown' value); corpus: drawio-desktop/src/main/electron.js:166 and zettlr/source/main.ts:79 call disableHardwareAcceleration().
verdicts.correction: (1) Replace the Linux mapping claim with: GpuSafeMode supports at most one derived fact — when is_degraded() is true, the DMA-BUF renderer is disabled — which maps to no GPUFeatureStatus field without a KEL-132-owned ruling; getGPUFeatureStatus returns an empty partial structure under the ▲ flag until a real engine signal exists. (2) Two unknowns are settled from Electron source: disableHardwareAcceleration() after ready throws with the exact message above (the Keld facade must throw identically), and getGPUFeatureStatus has no readiness throw in source (the doc's 'only usable after gpu-info-update' is advisory). (3) The cheapest experiments that would move this from research to a decision: read ICoreWebView2EnvironmentOptions.AdditionalBrowserArguments for a Microsoft receipt on --disable-gpu under a shared user-data folder (WebView2), and confirm WebKitGTK's webkit_settings_set_hardware_acceleration_policy as the single named Linux policy for disableHardwareAcceleration — both are host-owned single policies, not 'arbitrary flags', but need KEL-132 spec amendment and remain unverified here.

extra_findings.finding: Supervisor records no terminating signal. RuntimeError::ChildCrashed carries { pid, exit_code: Option<i32>, stderr_tail } and SelfTerminationRecord carries exit_code: Option<i32> only; every signal death collapses to None. Any Electron reason finer than abnormal-exit (killed / crashed / oom) for a Bun generation or named role is unprovable until KEL-116's fixed-size record gains an allocation-free signal field. This blocks D2's reason fidelity and weakens the D4 crash() oracle.
extra_findings.evidence: crates/keld-runtime/src/lib.rs:161-195, 527-540; crates/keld-runtime/src/role.rs:248-264, 317-324

extra_findings.finding: Electron emits app 'child-process-gone' only from the crashed/killed observer callbacks; a normal child exit only disconnects the metrics row. The research object's child-process-gone trap oracle (exit-0 role → clean-exit event) is contradicted by source and must be re-run against a real Electron oracle; clean exits belong to the utilityProcess 'exit' event (receipt not yet collected: utility-process.md v44.4.5).

The 'structured compat error + registry test' proof cited by D5 and by every documented-never cell has no owner yet — it is a program-wide prerequisite, not an F08 detail.

extra_findings.finding: Electron normalizes percentCPUUsage by NumberOfProcessors (bindings.cc:290). A Bun-side getCPUUsage facade that computes cpuUsage deltas over wall time without dividing by core count over-reports by up to N×; the object's CPUUsage trap omits this.

KEL-74 denominator honesty requires one declared oracle per cell; any F08 cell landing in the same panel needs a ruling on per-cell versus per-panel oracle version before it can be scored.

D2's 'keld-wv wires no engine process-failure hook (no owner today)' understates the live code; the correct plan is to extend this owner (same module, same handler pattern) with add_ProcessFailed and to reuse the known browser pid for D3's Windows engine rows.

The object should cite these rather than schedule oracle runs for them.

The KEL-143 'successor reads predecessor' contract therefore applies to crash-class exits only; D2 should say so explicitly so process.exit(0) in main is not mistaken for a recoverable event.

verdicts.lens: Electron semantics accuracy and corpus demand (pinned v44.4.5 docs + v44.4.5 source where docs are silent; corpus clones re-grepped; Keld origin/main d150a14 re-grepped; vendor receipts re-fetched 2026-10-06)

verdicts.reason: The local-state facade shape is Electron-faithful: lib/browser/api/crash-reporter.ts shows getLastCrashReport() is literally the newest entry of getUploadedReports() or null, getUploadToServer/setUploadToServer throw outside the browser process, and start() defaults uploadToServer=true and throws 'submitURL must be specified when uploadToServer is true'. Corpus demand is zero (grep of drawio-desktop, zettlr, electron-quick-start finds no crashReporter). Keld has no dump/upload code (grep confirms). But two stated facts in the object are wrong and one surface is missing.
verdicts.evidence: crash-reporter.md v44.4.5: 'Keys with names longer than the maximum will be silently ignored. Key values longer than the maximum length will be truncated' (both NOTEs). shell/common/crash_keys.cc v44.4.5: kMaxCrashKeyNameLength=40 with `if (key.size() >= 40) { EmitWarning(...ignoring it); return; }`; CrashKeyString<20320> truncates. shell/browser/api/electron_api_crash_reporter.cc Start(): `for (extra) crash_keys::SetCrashKey(...)` — same 20320 path. crash-reporter.md addExtraParameter bullet says 'no longer than 127 bytes' while its NOTE says 20320. lib/browser/api/crash-reporter.ts lines 1-75. Doc 'In Node child processes' section: process.crashReporter.{start,getParameters,addExtraParameter,removeExtraParameter}.
verdicts.correction: (1) Delete the 'throw vs truncate' unknown: it is documented and confirmed in source — keys ≥40 bytes are ignored with a warning, values are truncated. (2) Do not enforce the doc's 127-byte value limit for start().extra: the v44.4.5 code truncates both start().extra and addExtraParameter at 20320 bytes; the doc contradicts itself (127 vs 20320) and the facade must follow the oracle binary, with the doc defect recorded in the conformance cell. (3) start() must throw the exact Electron message when uploadToServer is true/omitted and submitURL is missing; setUploadToServer is a no-op before start(). (4) Add the missing `ignoreSystemCrashHandler` option and the `process.crashReporter.*` surface that Electron exposes in utilityProcess children — the KEL-75 named-role facade needs it. (5) Renderer ✘ is right but its blocker is 'no preload injection' (Electron requires preload+contextBridge), a cross-unit dependency, not the absence of a process object.

verdicts.reason: The three-source mapping and the refusal to map Bun-primary death onto any Electron event hold, and every vendor receipt re-fetched matches: Apple webViewWebContentProcessDidTerminate has no reason parameter (macOS 10.11+); Microsoft get_ExitCode is 'always STILL_ACTIVE (259)' for RENDER_PROCESS_UNRESPONSIVE; WebKitGTK web-process-terminated carries CRASHED/EXCEEDED_MEMORY_LIMIT/TERMINATED_BY_API. draw.io's two render-process-gone handlers only stringify details.reason (src/main/electron.js:1455, 3115). However two evidence lines about Keld are false, one 'unknown' is settled by the receipts the author already had, and the sequencing claim '(1) land this first' is blocked by a dependency the object omits.
verdicts.evidence: crates/keld-wv/src/webview2/mod.rs:1225-1263 registers `environment5.add_BrowserProcessExited` reading BrowserProcessId + BrowserProcessExitKind (NORMAL vs failed) — a live engine process-exit hook; the same file also registers add_PermissionRequested (1927) and add_NewWindowRequested (1946), so 'registers only NavigationCompleted' is false. grep of crates/keld-wv/src/wkwebview for WKNavigationDelegate/didFinish/navigationDelegate returns nothing (only define_class for the bridge handler in macos_bridge.rs:444), so 'WKWebView navigation delegate … lives in the same per-backend module' is false. grep of crates/keld-wv/src/webkitgtk/mod.rs for connect/signal returns nothing. learn.microsoft.com ICoreWebView2ProcessFailedEventArgs: ProcessFailedKind 'is a combination of process kind … and failure (exit, unresponsiveness)'. webkitgtk.org property.WebView.is-web-process-responsive (since 2.34) + method.WebView.get_is_web_process_responsive; method.WebView.terminate_web_process (2.34) emits web-process-terminated with TERMINATED_BY_API. web-contents.md: forcefullyCrashRenderer emits render-process-gone 'with the reason=killed || reason=crashed'. packages/@keld/electron/src/index.ts exports only `app`; briefing: no BrowserWindow/webContents facade.
verdicts.correction: (1) Fix the Keld facts: WebView2 BrowserProcessExited is already wired (reuse it as the browser-process-gone observation; ProcessFailed per-webview is what is missing); WKWebView and WebKitGTK backends have no delegate/signal plumbing at all, so the first macOS slice introduces a WKNavigationDelegate class rather than extending one. (2) Settle the 'unknown': WebView2 RENDER_PROCESS_UNRESPONSIVE is a hang kind and maps to webContents/BrowserWindow 'unresponsive', never render-process-gone; WebKitGTK notify::is-web-process-responsive gives both 'unresponsive' and 'responsive'; WKWebView has no public hang signal (▲). Add 'unresponsive' to the event family — it is Zettlr's only process-health demand (onboarding-window.ts:114). (3) Map webkit_web_view_terminate_web_process / WebView2 TerminateProcess-of-renderer as the forcefullyCrashRenderer analog (reason 'killed'). (4) Add blocked_by: 'BrowserWindow/webContents facade (other unit)' — render-process-gone is a webContents event and @keld/electron has no webContents object, so this cannot be this unit's first Electron-facing tracer bullet; the keld-wv engine-gone observable can land independently as a Keld-native contract.

verdicts.reason: Consuming the arch 01 §5.1 census instead of inventing a second one is confirmed by the spec text (keld-owned processes only; engine helpers 'reported as separate diagnostics'; resident set + private footprint companion; 90 MiB = 92,160 KiB) and arch 04 §3.1 ('A returned PID is diagnostic only'). WebView2 GetProcessInfos (1.0.1108.44, pid+kind only) confirmed. Two unknowns are settled by Electron source and one Electron platform fact the doc omits must be added.
verdicts.evidence: shell/browser/api/electron_api_app.cc v44.4.5 GetAppMetrics: `memory_info.working_set_size >> 10`, `peak_working_set_size >> 10`, `private_bytes >> 10` (Windows) — divisor is 1024, i.e. KiB; the whole memory block is inside `#if !BUILDFLAG(IS_LINUX)`, so ProcessMetric.memory is ABSENT on Linux while structures/process-metric.md carries no platform tag. shell/browser/api/process_metric.cc: macOS working set = task_info resident_size, peak = resident_size_max via TaskForPid; Windows = PROCESS_MEMORY_COUNTERS_EX. electron_api_app.cc:1454 `percentCPUUsage = usagePercent / processor_count`. webkitgtk.org class.WebView index lists only get_page_id, is-web-process-responsive, terminate_web_process, web-process-terminated — no web-process pid accessor (get_web_process_identifier URL is 404). docs/architecture/01-overview.md:216,222; docs/architecture/04-electron-compat.md:124-125.
verdicts.correction: (1) Delete the divisor unknown: Electron 'Kilobytes' is `>> 10` = KiB, identical to §5.1's binary units. (2) Add an Electron platform fact the doc hides: on Linux v44.4.5 omits `memory` from every ProcessMetric row; Keld must pick follow-Electron (omit) or extend under a quirks flag, and the conformance differential must assert field SETS per platform. (3) Close 'unless a public pid API is found' for WebKitGTK: none exists in the stable reference today — engine rows omitted on Linux is the ruling, not a pending search. (4) percentCPUUsage must be divided by the logical processor count for parity. (5) macOS host read of the Bun child's resident size: Electron uses task_for_pid; whether Keld's hardened host may obtain the child's task port is [unknown] — prefer a proc_pid_rusage-class read and record the receipt before the F08-P3 prototype.

verdicts.reason: Re-running the probe under Bun 1.4.2 reproduces every claimed shape (process.memoryUsage rss, process.cpuUsage, process.resourceUsage, node:v8.getHeapStatistics with all 14 snake_case fields, bun:jsc heapStats/memoryUsage, process.abort function, process.type undefined). The divergence policy is right but three parity details come from source, not docs, and the 'dialog' lead is now a fact.
verdicts.evidence: /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/f08-bun-probe.ts run 2026-10-06 under bun 1.4.2: v8.getHeapStatistics total_heap_size=139553, used_heap_size=139553, malloced_memory=139553, peak_malloced_memory=14303232=total_physical_size, total_available_size=17179729631, heap_size_limit=143032320 — degenerate shim values. shell/common/api/electron_bindings.cc v44.4.5: GetHeapStatistics uses `>> 10` on every field; GetCPUUsage sets percentCPUUsage = GetPlatformIndependentCPUUsage / NumberOfProcessors, idleWakeupsPerSecond=0 on Windows, cumulativeCPUUsage = InSecondsF(); GetProcessMemoryInfo rejects with 'Failed to find current process memory details in memory dump' when unresolved and sets residentSet only under IS_LINUX||IS_WIN. lib/browser/init.ts:18-33: default uncaughtException handler calls dialog.showErrorBox('A JavaScript error occurred in the main process', …) only when listenerCount <= 1. grep heartbeat|watchdog|liveness over crates/keld-runtime, keld-core, keld-ipc src: no Bun hang watchdog.
verdicts.correction: (1) Divisor settled: KiB via `>> 10`. (2) percentCPUUsage must be normalized by os.cpus().length and the facade must keep a per-process last-sample for the interval; cumulativeCPUUsage = (user+system µs)/1e6 from process.cpuUsage(). (3) Promote the draw.io 'modal dialog' lead to fact (init.ts) and record the Keld ▲ explicitly: an uncaught exception in Bun main is a CrashLedger crash-class exit + restart (KELD-RUNTIME-012/-002), where Electron keeps main alive behind a dialog unless the app registered its own handler; whether @keld/electron installs a default handler that logs a KELD-COMPAT diagnostic instead of letting Bun die is a user-owned ruling (KEL-143 territory), not a facade default. (4) The getHeapStatistics ▲ must say the Bun shim reports degenerate values (total==used==malloced; ~16 GiB available) so no consumer treats them as V8-equivalent.

verdicts.reason: Every Electron claim matches content-tracing.md v44.4.5 ('Collect tracing data from Chromium'; do not use before 'ready'; startRecording resolves immediately if a recording is running; stopRecording writes a temporary file when the path is omitted; getTraceBufferUsage {value, percentage}; enableHeapProfiling experimental, must precede startRecording). Arch 07 §2 structured-error rule and the error_registry.rs CI check exist; research 214 exists; corpus demand is zero; the never-list rationale is coherent (Chromium tracing service, no WebKit analog).
verdicts.evidence: f08-refute/api_content-tracing.md; docs/architecture/07-agent-experience.md:54-60; crates/keld-cli/tests/error_registry.rs; docs/engineering/keld-error-codes.md has KELD-COMPAT-001..007 headings (new codes continue the sequence); docs/research/library/compatibility-competitors/214-electron-spec-corpus-oracle.md; corpus grep: no contentTracing call sites.
verdicts.correction: None required. Minor: the throw must be a Promise rejection for the four Promise-returning methods (and for enableHeapProfiling), not a synchronous throw, so `await contentTracing.startRecording()` fails the way an Electron rejection would.

verdicts.reason: Treating the GPU getters as research is right (no Keld-owned signal outside Linux; GPUFeatureStatus has no 'unknown' value; KEL-132 GpuSafeMode is live in crates/keld-wv/src/webkitgtk/mod.rs:62). But the one buildable member, disableHardwareAcceleration, has its post-ready behavior settled by source, its corpus demand is overstated, and a WebView2 constraint the author did not cite changes the design.
verdicts.evidence: shell/browser/api/electron_api_app.cc v44.4.5:1155-1178: DisableHardwareAcceleration throws 'app.disableHardwareAcceleration() can only be called before app is ready' when Browser::is_ready(), otherwise appends --disable-gpu; IsHardwareAccelerationEnabled returns !disable_hw_acceleration_ before GpuDataManager init. app.md:1336-1347 also documents `app.isHardwareAccelerationEnabled()` (missing from the object's entity list). Corpus: drawio-desktop/src/main/electron.js:163-167 calls it only when process.argv contains '--disable-acceleration'; zettlr/source/main.ts:77-80 only when the DISABLE_HARDWARE_ACCELERATION CLI flag is set (issue #2127, VMs). learn.microsoft.com ICoreWebView2EnvironmentOptions get_AdditionalBrowserArguments: switches 'important to WebView functionality' are ignored; webview2-idl CreateCoreWebView2EnvironmentWithOptions: creation fails with HRESULT_FROM_WIN32(ERROR_INVALID_STATE) 'if the specified options does not match the options of the WebViews that are currently running in the shared browser process'. app.md:400-402: 'gpu-info-update' is 'Emitted whenever there is a GPU info update'.
verdicts.correction: (1) Delete the after-ready unknown: Electron throws with that exact message; the Keld facade must throw identically after ready. (2) Correct the demand statement: both corpus apps call it only behind an opt-in CLI flag, so it is real but user-triggered demand — rank it below 'unresponsive'/'render-process-gone'. (3) Split disableHardwareAcceleration out of the research atom into a finishable tracer bullet: before-ready records intent + after-ready throws + isHardwareAccelerationEnabled answers consistently; honoring it stays ▲ until KEL-132 rules per engine. (4) WebView2 ruling input: the switch must be fixed at environment creation and a mismatched option set against an already-running shared browser process fails with ERROR_INVALID_STATE, so the mapping is host-owned, per-user-data-folder, and cannot be toggled late; whether --disable-gpu itself is honored remains [unknown]. (5) 'gpu-info-update fires once' is a Keld narrowing of an Electron 'whenever' event — flag it.

extra_findings.finding: Sequencing: the proposed first slice (host-emitted engine process-gone → Electron 'render-process-gone') cannot be this unit's first tracer bullet because @keld/electron has no BrowserWindow/webContents object to hang the event on; the fresh-agent-finishable first slice is the zero-host-change trio — D4 Bun-side process.getHeapStatistics/getCPUUsage/getProcessMemoryInfo, D1 local crashReporter facade, D5 structured-error contentTracing — each with a conformance cell against the pinned oracle; the keld-wv engine-gone/unresponsive observables proceed in parallel as Keld-native contracts.
extra_findings.evidence: packages/@keld/electron/src/index.ts exports only `app`; briefing current code facts: 'no BrowserWindow, no ipcMain, no preload injection'; draw.io attaches both handlers to `contents` (webContents) at src/main/electron.js:1455 and 3115.

extra_findings.finding: Pinned doc self-contradiction on crash-key value limits (addExtraParameter bullet 127 bytes vs NOTE 20320 bytes), and the v44.4.5 code applies the 20320-byte truncation to start().extra as well; a facade that 'enforces the documented byte limits' with 127 would fail the oracle differential it claims to pass.
extra_findings.evidence: f08-refute/api_crash-reporter.md addExtraParameter section; shell/common/crash_keys.cc kMaxCrashKeyValueSize=20320, kMaxCrashKeyNameLength=40; electron_api_crash_reporter.cc Start() loops extra through SetCrashKey.

extra_findings.finding: Electron v44.4.5 getAppMetrics omits the `memory` field entirely on Linux, undocumented in process-metric.md; any Keld conformance cell that populates MemoryInfo on Linux diverges from the oracle and must be a flagged extension.
extra_findings.evidence: shell/browser/api/electron_api_app.cc GetAppMetrics: memory block wrapped in `#if !BUILDFLAG(IS_LINUX)`; structures/process-metric.md has no platform tag on `memory`.

extra_findings.finding: The 'unresponsive'/'responsive' pair is the corpus's actual process-health demand (Zettlr destroys the onboarding window on 'unresponsive') and has engine sources on two of three platforms, yet it is absent from the unit's sequencing and only appears as an 'unknown' inside D2.
extra_findings.evidence: zettlr/source/app/service-providers/config/onboarding-window.ts:114-117; WebView2 ProcessFailedKind RENDER_PROCESS_UNRESPONSIVE (ExitCode 259); WebKitGTK property is-web-process-responsive since 2.34; WKWebView has no public equivalent [inference from Apple WKNavigationDelegate/WKUIDelegate surfaces].

extra_findings.finding: keld-wv already observes WebView2 browser-process exit (BrowserProcessExited with exit kind) for profile lifecycle; the object says no engine process-exit hook exists. Reuse-before-rewrite applies: the browser-process-gone observable should be lifted from this handler, not re-registered.
extra_findings.evidence: crates/keld-wv/src/webview2/mod.rs:1225-1263 observe_profile_browser_exit; ICoreWebView2Environment5::add_BrowserProcessExited.

extra_findings.finding: Electron's main-process default uncaughtException handler (modal error box, suppressed when the app has its own listener) is a fact, not a lead; Keld's equivalent path is process death → CrashLedger → restart → possible KELD-RUNTIME-002, which is a lifecycle divergence apps like draw.io's non-export mode will hit; it needs a user-owned ruling on whether @keld/electron installs a default handler, and a documented ▲ either way.
extra_findings.evidence: lib/browser/api/../init.ts v44.4.5 lines 17-33; drawio-desktop/src/main/electron.js:1075-1083 (handler registered only in export mode); crates/keld-runtime/src/lib.rs RestartPolicy max_crashes 3 / 30 s.

extra_findings.finding: WebView2 refuses environment creation with ERROR_INVALID_STATE when options differ from WebViews already running in the shared browser process, so any disableHardwareAcceleration→browser-argument mapping is a per-user-data-folder, creation-time decision that cannot be toggled after the first WebView; D6's interim 'records intent, honored where prepared' must say the Windows decision point is environment creation.
extra_findings.evidence: learn.microsoft.com webview2-idl CreateCoreWebView2EnvironmentWithOptions NOTE and error table (HRESULT_FROM_WIN32(ERROR_INVALID_STATE)).

extra_findings.finding: percentCPUUsage in both Electron APIs is normalized by the logical processor count; a facade reporting raw process.cpuUsage() deltas over wall time would over-report by a factor of N cores and fail the interval oracle.
extra_findings.evidence: shell/common/api/electron_bindings.cc GetCPUUsage `usagePercent / processor_count`; electron_api_app.cc:1454 same.

extra_findings.finding: `app.isHardwareAccelerationEnabled()` and `process.crashReporter.*` (utilityProcess children) are Electron surfaces in this family's dependency set that the object omits; both are cheap to specify alongside D6/D1 and matter for KEL-75 roles.
extra_findings.evidence: app.md:1342-1347; crash-reporter.md 'In Node child processes' section.

extra_findings.finding: On macOS Electron reads child memory via task_for_pid/task_info; whether Keld's hardened host can obtain the Bun child's task port is unverified — the §5.1-shared per-pid reader should name its macOS primitive (proc_pid_rusage class) with a receipt before F08-P3.
extra_findings.evidence: shell/browser/api/process_metric.cc GetTaskInfo(TaskForPid(pid)); no Keld census code exists (grep working_set|task_info|GetProcessMemoryInfo|smaps over crates returns nothing). [inference] on entitlement constraints.

extra_findings.finding: Bun's node:v8.getHeapStatistics shim returns degenerate values (total_heap_size == used_heap_size == malloced_memory; total_available_size ≈ 16 GiB sentinel), so a getHeapStatistics cell can be SCAFFOLDED/▲ at best, never BEHAVIOR_MATCH on values.
extra_findings.evidence: Live probe output 2026-10-06 under bun 1.4.2: total_heap_size=139553, used_heap_size=139553, malloced_memory=139553, total_available_size=17179729631.

epic.title: compat(diagnostics): process-gone events, crashReporter local-state facade, app metrics census and Bun-side process stats (contentTracing never)
epic.body:
## Scope
12 entities / 63 members: crashReporter (8), contentTracing (5), app metrics/GPU structures, process memory/CPU methods. Corpus demand for the module surfaces is zero; adjacent demand is real: draw.io listens to `render-process-gone` and installs `uncaughtException → app.exit(1)` in export mode; Zettlr handles `unresponsive` → destroy and logs `unhandledRejection`; both call `disableHardwareAcceleration()` before ready.

## Maturity ladder
- L0: every member exists; contentTracing rejects with the arch 07 structured compat error; never rows published.
- L1: `render-process-gone` from engine web-content-process termination (WKWebView webContentProcessDidTerminate; WebView2 ProcessFailed beside the existing BrowserProcessExited observation; WebKitGTK web-process-terminated); Bun-side `process.getHeapStatistics/getCPUUsage/getProcessMemoryInfo` with documented ▲ fields.
- L2: `getAppMetrics` as the arch 01 §5.1 census (host = Browser row; guardian; Bun primary = Utility `keld.primary`; named roles) with KiB units; crashReporter local-state facade at BEHAVIOR_MATCH.

## Linear owners consumed
KEL-105/KEL-116 (crash ledger), KEL-90/KEL-129 (census rules), KEL-75 (generations), KEL-143, KEL-78, KEL-132 (GpuSafeMode).

## Design facts fixed by research (two refuters)
- Bun-primary death is never mapped to any Electron event; a host-emitted process-gone family over the app link feeds `render-process-gone` and `child-process-gone` facades with reason fidelity recorded per engine.
- crashReporter is a local-state facade (start/add/remove/get/setUploadToServer; getLastCrashReport null; getUploadedReports []); keys ≥ 40 bytes ignored with a warning, values truncated (documented); no uploader, no minidumps.
- `getAppMetrics` consumes the §5.1 census (KiB, `>> 10`); percentCPUUsage normalised by CPU count with a per-process last sample.
- contentTracing: never, with Promise rejections for the Promise-returning methods; GPU getters are a research atom (Linux GpuSafeMode yields at most one derived fact).

research.unit: F09 update-packaging (autoUpdater → keld-update adapter; electron-updater/electron-builder/forge → keld.build.ts; bridge release; fuses/ASAR/notarize)
research.summary: Electron's autoUpdater is a 10-member module (setFeedURL/getFeedURL/checkForUpdates/quitAndInstall + 6 events), macOS+Windows only, that delegates verification and installation to Squirrel.Mac / Squirrel.Windows / MSIX and takes an app-selected feed URL [fact: v44.4.5 auto-updater.md]. Neither corpus app uses it directly: draw.io uses electron-updater v6 (setFeedURL({provider:'github',...}), autoDownload=false, autoInstallOnAppQuit, downloadUpdate, download-progress, info.version, logger) and Zettlr ships its own got-based downloader (shell.openPath of the downloaded installer + app.quit) [fact: corpus grep]. Keld today: keld-update implements signed v0 manifest/full verification, Windows x64 extraction/staging, PerUserDirect journaled activation, read-only active selection and startup repair; keld-pack streams Windows v0 packages only; keld-cli `build`/`migrate` are reserved (KELD-CLI-045); @keld/electron exports only `app`; no update event channel to Bun, no keld.build.ts schema, no autoUpdater facade, no bridge recipe [fact: product-status.tsv rows 9/10/13, crates, packages]. Feed orchestration, candidate launch, 30-second health, host consumer, macOS/Linux package cells (blocked on KEL-137 + KEL-103) are TARGET. Design answer: implement ONE host-owned updater (KEL-53) and expose two thin Bun facades over kipc — Electron-core `autoUpdater` and an electron-updater-shaped shim for migrated apps — with the feed URL compiled into the signed host (never app-selected), staged≠activated semantics documented as ▲, errors mapped from KELD-UPDATE-*; `keld migrate` translates electron-builder/forge config into keld.build.ts with a per-field disposition report (fuses/ASAR/custom hooks → explained drops); the arch 04 §7 bridge release is constrained by electron-updater's publisherName Authenticode check + NSIS spawn args on Windows and by Squirrel.Mac's designated-requirement check on macOS, and is only reachable for Windows x64 until KEL-137/KEL-103 land. Six decision atoms below; three prototypes; evidence receipts attached.

decisions.question: Which updater contract does the compat layer clone: Electron-core `autoUpdater` (the F09 census) or the electron-updater v6 surface the corpus actually calls?
decisions.proposed_answer: Both, as two thin Bun facades over ONE host-owned KEL-53 state machine: (a) `@keld/electron`.autoUpdater implements the 10-member Electron-core surface for the per-API scoreboard; (b) `keld migrate` rewrites `electron-updater` imports to a Keld-owned shim exporting the AppUpdater subset draw.io exercises (autoDownload, autoInstallOnAppQuit, downloadUpdate, download-progress, update-available(info.version), update-downloaded, error(err), logger, checkForUpdates():Promise<result|null>, quitAndInstall(isSilent?, isForceRunAfter?)). Provider options ({provider:'github', owner, repo, channel}) are parsed only to cross-check against keld.build.ts and never contacted. Zettlr needs neither (custom got downloader) and scores N/A in this family. Declared as an L3 ecosystem row in the KEL-74 denominator, not as Electron API.
evidence: [fact] draw.io imports {autoUpdater} from 'electron-updater' (src/main/electron.js:17-18), sets autoDownload=false, autoInstallOnAppQuit=silentUpdate (:85-86), calls setFeedURL({provider:'github', repo:'drawio-desktop', owner:'jgraph', channel?}) (:2078), checkForUpdates (:2099), downloadUpdate (:2360, :2389), quitAndInstall (:2350); listens error/update-not-available/download-progress/update-downloaded/update-available (:2228-2355); reads info.version (:2383)
[fact] Zettlr: no autoUpdater/electron-updater; source/app/service-providers/updates/index.ts uses got + semver + sha256 verification, shell.openPath(installer), app.quit()
[fact] electron-quick-start: no updater usage (corpus usage json)
[fact] arch 04 §4 Tier 2 and research 13 line 35: 'autoUpdater → keld-update adapter'

[fact] electron-updater v26.0.12 AppUpdater.ts: autoDownload=true default; autoInstallOnAppQuit=true default (not deprecated at that tag); quitAndInstall(isSilent?, isForceRunAfter?); AppUpdaterEvents list
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Only Electron-core autoUpdater: draw.io (migration candidate #1) would score ✘ on its updater and the arch 04 §7 bridge would have no client contract to meet. Re-implementing electron-updater's providers (GitHub Releases scraping, latest.yml parsing, sha512) inside Keld: duplicates feed parsing/trust (one owner rule), and would copy an app-selected feed into the privileged updater (never list). Forking electron-updater to run on Bun: it spawns installers and reads app-update.yml — contradicts KEL-53 'no arbitrary relaunch helper, no role-writable update state'.
decisions.unknowns: Exact electron-updater version pin draw.io resolves in 2026 (^6.8.9; master already deprecates autoInstallOnAppQuit) — the shim must pin one AppUpdater surface and record it in the denominator. Whether a product decision admits an L3 'ecosystem shim' row at all (KEL-127 says no silent downgrade; a shim is a visible row, but the owner must confirm).

decisions.question: What does `autoUpdater.setFeedURL(...)` do under Keld, given the host's feed, key, app id, channel and target are compiled into the signed host (ExpectedAppIdentity)?
decisions.proposed_answer: setFeedURL is accepted syntactically (no throw, so migrated apps keep running), its argument is compared with keld.build.ts `update.feed`/`channel`, and a mismatch emits a KELD-COMPAT dev diagnostic; the host NEVER reads it. getFeedURL returns the host's compiled-in feed base (read-only). `headers`, `serverType`, `allowAnyVersion`, electron-updater `requestHeaders`, `login` event, `allowDowngrade`, `channel` setter are documented-never (▲ accepted-and-ignored for the first three/last two, ✘ for login). checkForUpdates without a prior setFeedURL succeeds under Keld (▲ more permissive than Electron's 'You must call setFeedURL before using this API').
evidence: [fact] briefing never-list item 10: 'app-selected updater feed URLs into a privileged updater'
[fact] research 186 row 10: macOS passes developer URL to SQRLUpdater; classic Windows spawns Update.exe --update <url> unchanged; 'Never copy an app-selected feed URL into a privileged updater'
[fact] arch 06 §4a step 1: key compiled into the host, 'never fetched from the feed itself'; step 2: app.id/channel/target must match host identity → KELD-UPDATE-006 ManifestIdentityMismatch

decisions.question: How do KEL-53 states map onto the Electron/electron-updater event sequence, and what does `update-downloaded` + `quitAndInstall` mean when Keld's activation can roll back after a failed 30-second health check?
decisions.proposed_answer: Mapping: checking-for-update = feed fetch begins; update-available(info{version, releaseDate=publishedAt, releaseName=version, releaseNotes undefined}) = SelectedFull minted after signature+shape+floor filter; update-not-available = typed empty filtered set; download-progress(percent, transferred, total=full.size, bytesPerSecond) = streamed verify_full bytes (electron-updater shim only); update-downloaded = CompletedWindowsStage exists (staged, verified, NOT published/selected); error(Error{message: KELD-UPDATE-* Display, code}) = any typed refusal, delivered exactly once; quitAndInstall = emit before-quit-for-update → close all windows → before-quit → will-quit → quit → host runs the journaled activation. Documented divergence ▲: 'downloaded' ≠ 'will run next launch'; if the candidate fails health the host rolls back to last-known-good and the next launch runs the OLD version (observable via app.getVersion()). autoInstallOnAppQuit=true (electron-updater default; draw.io's silent path) maps to the same deferred activation at quit. Electron-core autoUpdater's implicit auto-download after update-available is honored; the shim honors autoDownload=false by not fetching the full artifact.
evidence: [fact] auto-updater.md: 'Under the hood calling autoUpdater.quitAndInstall() will close all application windows first, and automatically call app.quit() after all windows have been closed'; before-quit-for-update 'emitted after a user calls quitAndInstall()'; app.md before-quit note: when initiated by quitAndInstall, before-quit fires after closing all windows
[fact] auto-updater.md checkForUpdates: 'If an update is available it will be downloaded automatically'; update-available: 'The update is downloaded automatically'
[fact] F09 family JSON update-downloaded desc: 'It is not strictly necessary to handle this event. A successfully downloaded update will …' (truncated; Electron applies on next start regardless)

[fact] arch 06 §4: candidate must boot the exact version, reach application Ready within 30 s over a private health channel, else rollback to retained last-known-good; floor advances only after the published candidate is re-verified (KEL-270 F1)
[fact] keld-update windows_extraction: completed stage 'is neither published nor selected and active records/journal stay unchanged' (product-status row 9)
[fact] electron-updater v26.0.12 AppUpdater: checkForUpdates emits checking-for-update then update-available|update-not-available; downloadUpdate manual when autoDownload=false
[fact] draw.io dedupes error dialogs within 5 s because one failure 'can fan out into both a sync throw and an error event' (electron.js:92-96, 122-123)
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Emitting update-downloaded only after activation commit: impossible without quitting (activation requires candidate launch), so draw.io's 'Install / Later' dialog would never appear. Emitting error on rollback into the OLD app instance: the old instance was not the caller; instead surface a typed startup diagnostic (KELD-UPDATE-016) and an `error` on the next checkForUpdates. Synchronous throws from facade methods: rejected — electron-updater's throw+event fan-out is the bug draw.io works around; Keld delivers one `error` emission and a rejected promise, never a sync throw.
decisions.unknowns: Whether KEL-53 admits a 'quit without relaunch' activation (electron-updater isForceRunAfter=false / autoInstallOnAppQuit silent install): the transaction needs the candidate to boot and report Ready, so a user-visible relaunch or a headless health boot must be chosen by the KEL-53 owner. Whether electron-updater's checkForUpdates both rejects and emits `error` for the same failure (needs source receipt at the pinned tag) to decide the shim's exactly-once contract.

decisions.question: Where does the facade's authority live and what kipc/guard shape carries it, given Bun roles have zero ambient OS authority and KEL-53 forbids role-writable update state?
decisions.proposed_answer: All network, verification, staging, activation and relaunch stay in the Rust host (keld-update + host lifecycle owner). The main Bun role gets three guarded calls — `update.check` (rate-limited; returns typed result), `update.download` (shim only; honors autoDownload=false), `update.quitAndInstall({silent, forceRunAfter})` — plus a host→Bun event stream (checking/available/not-available/progress/downloaded/error) carrying versions, dates and sizes but never filesystem paths (electron-updater's `downloadedFile`/`updateFile` are undefined ▲). Grants are declared in keld.permissions.jsonc and generated through the existing KEL-98 echo-codegen contract source (no new IDL). Quit sequencing reuses @keld/api app.quit and the F01 before-quit ordering; error text reuses KELD-UPDATE-* Display verbatim.
evidence: [fact] KEL-53 §1 non-goals: 'no arbitrary relaunch helper, shell command, self-update plugin, or role-writable update state'; arch 06: 'strict Keld role restrictions deny Bun/webview writes to the install and updater state'
[fact] arch 03 §5 line 215 example mapping: 'autoUpdater → net to feed URL' as a host-owned grant; arch 01 line 63: network allowed in cold tooling (CLI, packager, updater fetches)
[fact] briefing invariant 7: hot kipc paths are callbacks/state machines; invariant 4: no parallel process model; KEL-127: one contract source + echo-codegen owner (KEL-98), no new IDL
[fact] packages/@keld/electron/src/app.ts: facade pattern (listeners Map, per-listener try/catch, apiApp.quit Promise)
[fact] electron-updater downloadUpdate resolves file paths (v26.0.12: Promise<Array<string>>) and NsisUpdater spawns the downloaded installer itself — exposing paths would recreate that
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Running electron-updater (or a port) inside the Bun main role with a net grant: duplicates feed trust and lets a role spawn installers (never list: raw child_process from strict roles). A single `update.*` wildcard grant: too wide; check vs install are different authorities (install closes windows and terminates the app).
decisions.unknowns: Whether the current kipc/app-link transport already supports unsolicited host→Bun events with backpressure for progress (KEL-80 virtual channels) — if not, progress must be coalesced to the latest-value-wins shape. The exact rate limit for update.check (Electron has none; draw.io checks at boot once per 24 h by default).

decisions.question: What must the arch 04 §7 bridge release (final Electron release whose electron-updater feed points at a Keld installer) satisfy on each platform, and in what order can it ship?
decisions.proposed_answer: The bridge is constrained by the CLIENT already in users' hands (electron-updater v6 via GitHub Releases): (Windows NSIS) latest.yml/latest-arm64.yml files[] must list a Keld installer with sha512+size; NsisUpdater verifies the downloaded .exe's Authenticode publisherName against the configured list ('JGraph Ltd'/'draw.io Ltd') — so the Keld installer must be signed by the same publisher; it is then spawned with `--updated`, `/S` (silent), optionally `--force-run`, `/D=<dir>`, via elevate.exe when perMachine — Keld's NSIS installer must tolerate those args. draw.io's Electron install is perMachine; Keld's default is PerUserDirect → the bridge must either ship MachineUacDirect (T4d, not implemented) or uninstall the old machine install, else two installs coexist. (macOS) latest-mac.yml must list a zip; MacUpdater proxies it to Squirrel.Mac, which validates the new bundle against the running app's designated requirement (SecCodeCopyDesignatedRequirement → SecStaticCodeCheckValidityWithErrors) → the Keld .app must satisfy the Electron app's DR (same team + bundle id [inference]) and be notarized; blocked on KEL-137 + KEL-103. (MSI/APPX/snap) no electron-updater path → repo-level announcement only. Order: Windows x64 NSIS first (matches KEL-53's first admitted cell), macOS/Linux after KEL-137/KEL-103.
