decisions.proposed_answer: Generate keld.build.ts (schema owned by KEL-15/KEL-19 — currently absent) with a per-field disposition report: appId/appBundleId → identity.appId (must equal ExpectedAppIdentity app id); productName/copyright/fileAssociations/extendInfo/UTIs → bundle metadata; files/asar/asar.unpack/extraResource(s) → bundle include/exclude (Keld ships a canonical plain tree; `asar` is dropped with explanation, `original-fs`/app.asar.unpacked paths flagged ✘); win.target nsis/msi → targets; appx/snap/flatpak → ManagedOwner targets with 'no direct updater' note; nsis.perMachine → installMode MachineUacDirect (not yet live) vs default PerUserDirect; publish{provider,channel} → update.feed base + channel∈{stable,beta,canary} (draw.io's `latest-arm64` per-arch channel dissolves into Keld's per-target feed path); mac.hardenedRuntime/entitlements/osxSign/osxNotarize/azureSignOptions/signtoolOptions.publisherName → signing.{mac,win} driven natively by keld build (rcodesign/signtool); custom JS hooks (afterPack fuses.mjs, afterSign notarize.mjs with Quick Look appex embedding, sign-trusted.mjs, forge generateAssets/postMake, Pandoc download) → ✘ 'manual: keld build does not execute arbitrary build hooks'; @electron/fuses → a fuse-disposition table mapping each FuseV1Option to the Keld invariant that subsumes it (RunAsNode/NodeOptions/NodeCliInspect → no inherited env/argv for Bun roles (KEL-75); OnlyLoadAppFromAsar + EmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation → signed full-package contentBlake3 + bound launch path (KEL-53/KEL-254); CookieEncryption → engine profile policy (KEL-135, unknown parity); GrantFileProtocolExtraPrivileges → webview origin policy (KEL-79)). platform_notes.note: [fact] Electron updates require a signed app (Squirrel.Mac); electron-updater needs a zip asset and Squirrel.Mac validates the new bundle against the running app's designated requirement. [fact] Keld macOS package cells are blocked on KEL-137 (executable modes/links in the canonical archive) and signing on KEL-103 (draft) / distribution KEL-141 (Backlog); notarization target is rcodesign without Xcode. [inference] The bridge .app must keep the same team ID and bundle identifier to satisfy the Electron app's DR — needs an Apple receipt. [fact] draw.io's notarize hook embeds and re-signs a Quick Look .appex and hardened-runtime entitlements; keld build has no stated support for PlugIns embedding [unknown]. Universal builds (draw.io dmg universal) have no Keld target name in the §4a list [unknown]. WKWebView is irrelevant to this family except that the relaunched candidate must reach Ready (first window) within 30 s.

[fact] First admitted Keld cell is windows-x64 PerUserDirect (LocalAppData, no UAC); MachineUacDirect (T4d) and MachineSeamlessDirect (T4e) are targets; ManagedOwner (MSIX/App Installer/Store/enterprise) refuses direct activation. [fact] draw.io ships NSIS perMachine:true + MSI + APPX + a separate arm64 channel; Zettlr NSIS perMachine:false. [fact] electron-updater NSIS verifies publisherName Authenticode and spawns the installer with --updated /S [--force-run] [/D=], elevate.exe for admin installs → the Keld bridge installer must be signed by the same publisher and tolerate those args. [fact] Electron's own MSIX updater exists; Keld refuses to mutate MSIX installs → ✘/▲ cell. [unknown] Keld windows-arm64 cell admission; whether electron-builder emits app-update.yml for MSI. WebView2 (Chromium-derived) is irrelevant to update semantics except candidate Ready timing.

[fact] Electron has no built-in Linux updater; electron-updater self-replaces AppImage only; snap/deb/rpm/flatpak updates are owned by the package manager (ManagedOwner → KELD-UPDATE-002). [fact] Keld targets .deb/.rpm/AppImage/flatpak but every Linux package cell is blocked on KEL-137. [fact] draw.io ships AppImage/deb/rpm/snap (snap publish never); Zettlr deb/rpm/zip via forge and AppImage via electron-builder; Zettlr's own updater opens the Downloads folder for AppImage. WebKitGTK irrelevant to this family beyond candidate Ready.

prototype_candidates.question: Will a shipped electron-updater v6 client accept and launch a non-electron-builder (Keld/NSIS) installer from a bridge latest.yml, and which spawn args/signature checks bind?
prototype_candidates.shape: Scratchpad-only: electron-quick-start + electron-updater pinned to draw.io's resolved version, generic provider pointing at a local static feed; latest.yml lists a minimal NSIS installer stub signed with a test cert whose subject matches publisherName; observe verifySignature outcome, spawn argv (--updated /S /D=), elevate.exe path for perMachine, and behavior with an unsigned/mismatched-publisher stub (negative control).
prototype_candidates.shows: Whether the Windows bridge is feasible with Keld's own NSIS output, the exact flag set Keld's installer must tolerate, and whether a PerUserDirect Keld install can replace a perMachine Electron install in one hop (A5).

prototype_candidates.question: Does Squirrel.Mac's designated-requirement check pass for a Keld-built .app signed with the same team and bundle identifier as the Electron app?
prototype_candidates.shape: Sign a trivial Electron app and a trivial non-Electron .app with the same Developer ID + CFBundleIdentifier; run `codesign -d -r-` to dump the Electron app's DR and `codesign --verify -R` / SecStaticCodeCheckValidityWithErrors against the other bundle; negative control with a different bundle id.
prototype_candidates.shows: Converts the A5 macOS [inference] into a receipt and tells KEL-103 which identity fields the bridge must preserve.

prototype_candidates.question: Can one host-driven state machine emit both the Electron-core autoUpdater sequence and the electron-updater sequence with exactly-once errors and correct quitAndInstall ordering?
prototype_candidates.shape: In-process Bun harness with a scripted fake host update driver (states: fetch, selected, streaming(n), staged, refused(KELD-UPDATE-00N), busy) driving both facades; assert ordered event logs, autoDownload=false → zero download calls, error delivered once as Error{message,code} plus rejected promise, quitAndInstall → before-quit-for-update before any window close.
prototype_candidates.shows: The conformance entries for F09 before any host work lands (crates/keld-compat rule), and the ▲ list the scoreboard must carry (A3/A4).

prototype_candidates.question: What fraction of draw.io's five electron-builder configs and Zettlr's forge.config.js + electron-builder.yml translates mechanically into a keld.build.ts draft, and what lands in the manual/✘ disposition list?

never_list.surface: autoUpdater.setFeedURL / electron-updater provider options / requestHeaders / headers / serverType / login as feed authority
never_list.rationale: App-selected feed URLs into a privileged updater are on the program never-list; Keld's key/app id/channel/target are compiled into the signed host (arch 06 §4a step 1; research 186 row 10).

never_list.surface: allowDowngrade / channel-switch downgrade / allowAnyVersion
never_list.rationale: KEL-53's monotonic protected floor is the replay/downgrade defense; honoring downgrade flags would reopen it.

never_list.surface: App-executed installers or exposure of staged artifact paths (electron-updater downloadedFile/updateFile, NsisUpdater spawn, Zettlr shell.openPath of an installer)
never_list.rationale: KEL-53 forbids arbitrary relaunch helpers and role-writable update state; raw spawn from strict roles is never-listed.

never_list.surface: app.relaunch({execPath}) to an updater/Squirrel layout
never_list.rationale: Candidate launch is host-owned under the exact initiating token; app-chosen exec paths are a privilege path.

never_list.surface: Electron's MSIX self-update path and any direct mutation of store/package-manager installs
never_list.rationale: ManagedOwner mode refuses direct activation and registers no competing writer (arch 06, KEL-53 non-goals).

never_list.surface: @electron/fuses as a runtime or permission API
never_list.rationale: Fuses are Electron-binary hardening bits; Keld's equivalents are host invariants, not app-toggled flags (research 186 row 8).

never_list.surface: ASAR virtual filesystem / original-fs / app.asar.unpacked path contracts
never_list.rationale: Keld ships a signed canonical plain tree; an fs shim per role would duplicate FsBroker policy.

never_list.surface: Executing electron-builder/forge JS hooks (afterPack/afterSign/custom sign scripts) inside keld build
never_list.rationale: Arbitrary project code inside the trusted packaging/signing step and a plugin surface Keld does not offer; declarative signing config only.

never_list.surface: Running Electron's api-autoupdater-*-spec.ts under Bun as the oracle
never_list.rationale: Research 214 refuses running Electron's spec tree; cite test identities via an approved per-surface spec and land Keld-owned tests.

verdicts.reason: The policy (host-owned feed, app-selected URL never honored, allowDowngrade/allowAnyVersion impossible under the monotonic floor) survives and is well sourced. The stated mechanism does not: the object says the feed URL is 'compiled into the signed host (ExpectedAppIdentity)' and that getFeedURL 'returns the host's compiled-in feed base from ExpectedAppIdentity'. ExpectedAppIdentityPayload carries only app_id, channel, target and update_public_key; arch 06 §4a step 1 says the host carries 'the key, app id, channel and target'; KEL-254 provenance v2 lists app id, channel, target, mode, owner, roots, baseline, key identity, channel owner — no feed base. No Keld source names an owner for `<feed-base>`.

verdicts.correction: Name the feed-base owner before any facade contract: the cheapest consistent choice is a KEL-53/KEL-19 amendment adding the feed base (or a feed-origin identity) to the signed host identity or to installer provenance v2 — one owner, byte-validated like the other fields — with keld.build.ts `update.feed` as its build-time input. Until that lands, getFeedURL has no source of truth and the conformance entry must be 'unknown', not ▲. Keep setFeedURL as accepted-and-ignored with a dev diagnostic only after a code is allocated (KELD-COMPAT-001..009 are keld-compat evidence-parser codes, and the registry rejects un-emitted codes).

verdicts.reason: State mapping matches landed code and spec: completed stage 'is neither published nor selected' (product-status row 9; arch 06 §4), activation runs journaled publish → candidate launch → 30 s Ready health → commit/rollback with floor unchanged on rollback (KEL-53 criteria 8-9), errors are typed KELD-UPDATE-001..018 and 'CLI/compat render them without remapping' (KEL-53 line 1830), Channel enum is Stable/Beta/Canary, manifest has publishedAt and no release notes. verdicts.correction: (1) Unknown 'quit without relaunch' is answered by KEL-53: there is no headless health boot — the candidate 'starts the app' and must reach Ready; so electron-updater's silent install-at-quit without relaunch (autoInstallOnAppQuit / isForceRunAfter=false) cannot be honored. Record a ▲: Keld either relaunches the app as the candidate at quit, or defers activation to the next user launch (which then pays publish+candidate boot+30 s health). This must be a recorded divergence, not an owner choice. (2) Unknown 'does electron-updater reject and emit' is settled at v26.0.12: checkForUpdates emits 'error' and rethrows; the shim's exactly-once emission + rejected promise is therefore itself a ▲ versus electron-updater (draw.io's 5 s dedupe tolerates it) and must be entered as such.

verdicts.reason: Authority placement (all network/verify/stage/activate in the host; roles get no paths; no installer spawn) is correct and matches KEL-53 non-goals and arch 03 broker pattern. Three mechanism claims fail: (a) 'generated through the existing KEL-98 echo-codegen contract source' — KEL-98 is explicitly 'a bootstrap for the existing echo vertical slice, not Keld's general contract', non-goal 'no general ... IDL, or arbitrary schema generator', and product-status says general schema codegen is absent; today @keld/api channels.ts hard-codes a single echoChannel and rejects any other descriptor. (b) 'Grants are declared in keld.permissions.jsonc' — KEL-53 §'Capabilities, wire and errors' states 'Application permissions cannot grant update authority. No KIPC, renderer bridge or permission-manifest change is introduced', and keld-guard today evaluates only dotted fs.* capabilities with path scopes; an update.* grant is a guard/KEL-102 schema change needing its own spec. (c) The object names the install grant `update.quitAndInstall` in A4 and `update.install` in security_mapping — two names for one rule.

verdicts.reason: The proposed single quitAndInstall ordering ('emit before-quit-for-update → close all windows → before-quit → will-quit → quit') is Electron's NATIVE (macOS) and MSIX behavior only. On Windows Squirrel — the first admitted Keld cell — Electron's quitAndInstall never emits before-quit-for-update and does not close windows first; it calls squirrelUpdate.processStart() then app.quit() (ordinary quit order). electron-updater (what draw.io runs on Windows/Linux) likewise spawns the installer, then setImmediate(emit 'before-quit-for-update'; app.quit()) — ordinary before-quit-first order. Only MacUpdater delegates to the native path. A single ordering oracle therefore contradicts the Electron observable on Windows and the semantic_traps[0] test oracle is wrong for the first cell. The rest of the mapping (events, staged≠activated ▲, exactly-once error) survives.
verdicts.evidence: electron v44.4.5 lib/browser/api/auto-updater/auto-updater-win.ts:11-17 (quitAndInstall = processStart + app.quit; no before-quit-for-update emission anywhere in the file); shell/browser/api/electron_api_auto_updater.cc:116-128 (Emit('before-quit-for-update'); WindowList::CloseAllWindows()) is the native path; auto-updater-msix.ts:460 emits it. electron-updater 6.8.9 out/BaseUpdater.js:13-26 (install() then setImmediate → emit before-quit-for-update → app.quit()); out/MacUpdater.js:233 nativeUpdater.quitAndInstall(). Exactly-once: out/AppUpdater.js:271-272 checkForUpdates emits 'error' AND rethrows (promise rejection), no sync throw — settles the author's second unknown in favor of the proposed contract. Doc staleness: auto-updater.md says 'With Squirrel.Windows only releaseName is available' but auto-updater-win.ts:60-65 emits releaseNotes, version, a faked new Date(), updateURL.
verdicts.correction: Split the quitAndInstall ordering atom by facade × platform: core facade on Windows/Linux-analogue = no before-quit-for-update, before-quit → window close → will-quit → quit; core facade on macOS and MSIX = before-quit-for-update → window close×N → before-quit → will-quit → quit; electron-updater shim on Windows/Linux = before-quit-for-update then ordinary quit order; shim on macOS = native order. Write one conformance entry per cell citing the source lines above (docs alone are wrong for Windows). Payload-shape oracle for update-downloaded must cite auto-updater-win.ts, not the stale doc sentence. Add a cell for electron-updater autoInstallOnAppQuit=false + 'Later': BaseUpdater.js:79-80 logs 'Update will not be installed on quit' and nothing installs at next launch — unlike Electron-core where the update applies on next start regardless; Keld must honor the flag per facade rather than 'same deferred activation'.

verdicts.reason: Host-owned authority with three narrow guarded calls and an info-only event stream is the only shape consistent with KEL-53 non-goals (spec line 207), arch 06 line 499 ('strict Keld role restrictions deny Bun/webview writes to the install and updater state'), and the briefing never-list (raw spawn from strict roles). electron-updater's downloadUpdate resolving installer paths and NsisUpdater spawning them (with elevate.exe) is exactly what must not be reproduced. epic.title: compat(update): autoUpdater and electron-updater facades over the host-owned KEL-53 updater, keld.build.ts translation, bridge release recipe
epic.body:
## Scope
`autoUpdater` (10 members, macOS+Windows) plus the ecosystem reality: draw.io uses electron-updater v6 (setFeedURL provider github, autoDownload=false, downloadUpdate, download-progress, quitAndInstall) with five electron-builder configs and @electron/fuses; Zettlr ships its own downloader. Live today: keld-update verifies signed v0 manifests/full packages, Windows extraction/staging/journaled activation and startup repair; keld-pack streams Windows v0 packages; `keld build`/`migrate` reserved; no update channel to Bun; no keld.build.ts schema.

## Maturity ladder
- L0: both facades exist; feed-URL writes are recorded no-ops ▲; `checkForUpdates` emits a typed error only when invoked without a host updater.
- L1: KEL-53 state machine events reach Bun (checking/available/not-available/progress/downloaded/error) with versions/dates/sizes, never paths.
- L2: `quitAndInstall` ordering split by facade × platform passes pinned entries; bridge release recipe validated on Windows NSIS (publisher match) and macOS.

## Linear owners consumed
KEL-53 (host-owned updater: full-package activation first), KEL-254/KEL-270 (Windows install modes/journal), KEL-19/KEL-15 (keld.build.ts schema — RFC text missing), KEL-103/KEL-141/KEL-137 (macOS package cells), KEL-98 (contract source for update.* calls).

## Design facts fixed by research (two refuters + panel)
- Two thin Bun facades over one host state machine; electron-updater rewritten by migrate to a Keld shim exporting the AppUpdater subset draw.io exercises; pin 6.8.9.
- `setFeedURL` is accepted and recorded (never thrown — draw.io routes throws to a user-facing Update Error dialog); mismatch vs `keld.build.ts` feed → dev diagnostic; the host never reads it; `DRAWIO_DISABLE_UPDATE=true` written into the host-declared role environment by migrate; never a fabricated `update-not-available`.
- `update-downloaded` = staged-and-verified (not published); `quitAndInstall` → host activation with health check and rollback; ordering atoms split per facade × platform (macOS native inverts before-quit).
- Authority: all network/verify/stage/activate/relaunch in the host; Bun gets `update.check/download/quitAndInstall` guarded calls (new guard operations need KEL-102 admission; contract source is open).
- Bridge release: Windows NSIS requires the Keld installer be signed by the same publisher (publisherName verification is skipped when absent from app-update.yml); macOS zip/latest-mac.yml path; Linux AppImage/deb per electron-updater ≥ 6.x sentinel.

tickets.agent_brief:
**Category:** feature

**Current behavior:** No update channel to Bun; no facade.

**Desired behavior:** Expose `update.check/download/quitAndInstall` guarded calls and an info-only host→Bun event stream; implement the 10-member `autoUpdater` and the electron-updater AppUpdater subset draw.io uses; setFeedURL recorded (▲) and compared with `keld.build.ts`; typed error on explicit check without a host updater; `update-downloaded` only after stage+verify; `quitAndInstall` ordering split per facade × platform with conformance entries.

**Key interfaces:** keld-update state machine; guarded update.* calls; facades.

**Acceptance criteria:** the checklist above, each as a test with its negative control.

**Out of scope:** Delta transport; bridge recipe (F09-T2).

research.unit: X01 conformance-oracle-harness (cross-cutting): differential Electron-44.4.5 vs @keld/electron transcript harness
research.summary: Design: a two-arm differential harness shaped like KEL-77 (Rust test owns and reaps each arm; hard failure when a binary is missing; exact arm revision in every record). Arm A (recorder) runs Keld-owned fixture apps under the pinned npm electron@44.4.5 binary (dist shasum 0be094f8e783febba75d591106f5c61c1e511b70; tag v44.4.5 -> commit 694f45852a0f1726cd23bfd379854de489cccb65) and emits a line-oriented transcript (seq, process, event, canonical args, monotonic delta). Arm B (replayer) runs the SAME unmodified fixture files with `electron` resolved to @keld/electron (today: tsconfig paths + `bun` child spawned by crates/keld-compat/tests/electron_lifecycle.rs against keld_core::LifecycleSession; TARGET: `keld dev --headless --smoke`, which is reserved/not live). A Rust comparator in keld-compat normalizes declared nondeterministic fields, diffs ordered sequences, and emits one keld.compat.evidence/v1 record per cell. The golden transcript is evidence-of-record, not the oracle: per AGENTS.md and KEL-77 §4.1 the oracle is the pinned Electron doc sentence (blob at commit 694f4585); a cell with no doc sentence can reach BEHAVIOR_MATCH only. Ladder: BEHAVIOR_MATCH (Keld transcript == golden under normalizers, >=1 OS, legacy_sandbox_off) -> CONFORMANCE_PASS (cited doc sentence + Keld-owned test independent of the diff + named negative control + pass on all 3 OS lanes, or explicit intentional_divergence ▲) -> CORPUS_VERIFIED (same observable matched in a real corpus app run through migrate+dev smoke on both arms, panel:product once a product corpus id is committed, authority profile strict_bun or visibly labeled legacy). Reuse: KEL-237's exact-bytes rule (denominator.corpus_sha256 == sha256 of committed manifest bytes, with mutation negative control) closes research 214's "canonical bytes UNPROVEN"; KEL-77 §4.3 digest for the fixture-set artifact.sha256; KEL-74 score() for all percentages. Placement: fixtures in packages/@keld/electron/fixtures/<family>/ (plain ESM JS runnable in both arms), goldens/manifest/denominator/evidence/receipts in crates/keld-compat/fixtures/<corpus-id>/ mirroring lifecycle-corpus, comparator tests in crates/keld-compat/tests/, corpus apps (draw.io, Zettlr) in the separate corpus repo (arch 04 §6). CI: PR lane = replay only on the existing 3-OS matrix (deterministic, no Electron download); weekly lane = recorder drift re-run at the same pin (Linux via xvfb-run as Electron's own CI does) + corpus-app smoke; regression P1 = `CI required` fails when any committed cell flips pass->fail/unknown or expected-fail->pass, with no retries, skips, or isCI gating (research 214 Table 4). Electron docs are silent on several order/error details (ready-to-show vs did-finish-load, duplicate ipcMain.handle, invoke no-handler text); those are recorded as observed-only cells, not conformance claims.

LIVE: KEL-237 (In Progress, Linear read 2026-10-06) bounded lifecycle corpus `electron-lifecycle-v0` (panel showcase, 3 cells, Electron 44.3.0 @07e46071, per-OS receipts macos-aarch64/linux-x86_64/windows-x86_64, authority_profile legacy_sandbox_off, engine `headless-lifecycle-conformance@<commit>`), with lifecycle_corpus.rs asserting denominator.corpus_sha256 == sha256(exact committed corpus.json bytes) and a mutation negative control, and executing mapped Rust + Bun oracles (source mentions rejected). decisions.question: What is the oracle: the recorded Electron 44.4.5 golden transcript, or the pinned Electron documentation sentence?
decisions.proposed_answer: The pinned doc sentence (blob at commit 694f45852a0f1726cd23bfd379854de489cccb65) is the oracle for any CONFORMANCE_PASS cell; the golden transcript is immutable evidence-of-record that makes BEHAVIOR_MATCH falsifiable and exposes undocumented order/timing. A cell whose behavior the docs do not state (e.g. ready-to-show vs did-finish-load order) is tagged `observed-only` and can never exceed BEHAVIOR_MATCH; it is reported as a lead, not a compatibility claim. Owner: keld-compat comparator; boundary: manifest cell {operation_id, oracle_id, doc_blob_oid, doc_sentence_sha256, golden_sha256, normalizers[], negative_control}; failure mode: a transcript diff passing while the documented contract is violated (mirror oracle); observable contract: deleting the doc-cited Keld test or inverting the asserted sentence fails the cell independently of the transcript diff; first falsifier: a cell with a golden but no doc_blob_oid that is scored CONFORMANCE_PASS.
evidence: AGENTS.md crates/keld-compat: 'Electron documented behavior = oracle. Conformance entry (citing doc/fixture) before implementation' [fact]

docs/specs/kel77-bun-child-process-differential.md §4.1: 'Rejected: using the Node arm's live output as the oracle — a mirror, not an oracle: it cannot distinguish Bun is wrong from Node changed' [fact]
.agents/testing.md: every test MUST use an independent oracle; reimplementing the algorithm is not independent [fact]
research 214 Table 3: selection must be fixed before results ('Tests that pass cannot define N after results exist') [fact]
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Golden transcript as sole oracle — mirror oracle; cannot tell Electron drift/flake from Keld defect; rejected by KEL-77 §4.1 precedent. (b) Electron spec/ tree as oracle — REFUSED by research 214. (c) Doc sentences only, no recorder — cannot falsify ordering/timing/destroyed-object details that docs omit, and gives no denominator-backed evidence of what 44.4.5 actually does.
decisions.unknowns: How many Tier-1 observables have no doc sentence (observed-only share) is unmeasured until the recorder runs once; the docs are silent on duplicate ipcMain.handle error text, invoke no-handler text, ERR_ABORTED on superseded load, and ready-to-show/did-finish-load order.

decisions.question: Which fixture language/packaging lets one unmodified fixture run under real Electron and under @keld/electron, and where does the Electron binary live?
decisions.proposed_answer: Fixtures are plain ESM JavaScript (`"type":"module"`, main.js + preload.js + renderer html) under packages/@keld/electron/fixtures/<family>/; they emit markers with writeSync(1) (current KEL-72 pattern) so neither arm block-buffers. The Electron arm never runs in the PR lane and the Electron binary is never committed: the recorder runs in the weekly lane / corpus repo with network, pins electron@44.4.5 by npm dist shasum 0be094f8e783febba75d591106f5c61c1e511b70 (sha512 integrity recorded) and tag commit 694f4585…, and goldens are copied into crates/keld-compat/fixtures/<corpus-id>/golden/ as reviewed immutable bytes with receipts. Owner: @keld/electron fixtures (apps) + keld-compat (goldens/receipts); failure mode: a .ts fixture Electron cannot execute, or a fixture that silently diverges between arms (two copies); observable contract: `sha256(fixture dir)` per KEL-77 §4.3 is identical in both arms' records (`artifact.sha256`); first falsifier: Electron 44.4.5 refuses the ESM main entry or Bun fails to resolve `import 'electron'` for a .js file via tsconfig paths.
evidence: crates/keld-compat/tests/electron_lifecycle.rs spawn_fixture: `bun ./<script>` with tsconfig.json paths alias asserted present [fact]
packages/@keld/electron/fixtures/*.ts are TypeScript today; Electron's main runs 'in a Node.js environment' (process-model.md) — TS is not a documented Electron entry format [fact]
docs/architecture/04-electron-compat.md §6: corpus/ is a separate repo with gitignored fixtures [fact]
research 214 Table 4 'Pin before run … Never fetch main' and 'No CI hiding' [fact]
KEL-77 §4.3 fixture digest algorithm (path||0x00||u64_le(len)||bytes) [fact]
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) TS fixtures + a transpile step for the Electron arm — two artifacts, digest no longer shared, violates one-source rule. (b) Playwright `_electron.launch` driver — adds a CDP dependency and a third process owner; the tutorial's stdio-ipc custom driver or plain stdout markers suffice. (c) Download Electron in the PR lane — network-dependent, slow, and makes PR evidence depend on a 100MB+ artifact; the replay-only PR lane keeps the Keld arm deterministic.
decisions.unknowns: [lead] Electron ESM main-entry support in 44.4.5 (docs/tutorial/esm.md not fetched here); [unknown] whether Bun applies tsconfig `paths` to plain .js imports at runtime (learnings 2026-08-18 verified .ts only); [unknown] whether a reproducible run of electron@44.4.5 is possible without npm `postinstall` network access on all three runners.

decisions.question: What are the canonical-bytes and digest rules for the manifest, the fixture set and the goldens, and who owns them?
decisions.proposed_answer: Reuse, do not invent: (1) manifest canonical bytes = the exact committed manifest file bytes; denominator.corpus_sha256 == sha256(those bytes), asserted by a test with a one-byte mutation negative control — this is already live in lifecycle_corpus.rs and closes research 214 Table 3's 'UNPROVEN canonical bytes' item; (2) fixture-set artifact.sha256 = KEL-77 §4.3 algorithm over the fixture directory (shared by both arms); (3) each golden transcript file is its own immutable blob, referenced from the manifest by sha256 and from each record as evidence_uri `sha256:<hex>` of the raw run report (KEL-77 §4.5 pattern); (4) oracle revision = Electron commit 694f4585… (not the version string; 214: 'a version string alone is not a pin'). Owner: keld-compat (evidence.rs validates URI/digest format; tests compute digests with the workspace sha2 dev-dependency). Failure mode: two digest algorithms for the same artifact; observable contract: flipping any byte of manifest, fixture or golden fails before any assertion executes; first falsifier: a record whose artifact.sha256 differs between the Electron arm and the Keld arm for the same fixture dir.
evidence: crates/keld-compat/tests/lifecycle_corpus.rs:100-148 asserts corpus_sha256 == sha256(CORPUS_JSON) and that a mutated manifest no longer matches [fact]
research 214 Table 3: KEL-74 'does not prescribe canonical manifest bytes, so that algorithm is UNPROVEN and a future spec must fix it' [fact]
docs/specs/kel77-bun-child-process-differential.md §4.3 digest; learnings 2026-08-19: dropping path-NUL-length framing collides on ('ab','c') vs ('a','bc') [fact]
crates/keld-compat/Cargo.toml: sha2 is a dev-dependency only (test-only digest) [fact]
decisions.alternatives_rejected: JSON-canonicalization (RFC 8785) of the manifest — a second algorithm with its own implementation risk when exact committed bytes already work and are tested; hand-rolled hashing — forbidden duplicate of a primitive (KEL-77 §4.1).
decisions.unknowns: Whether the corpus repo (arch 04 §6) and the keld repo must share one manifest format or the corpus repo only ships goldens+receipts consumed by keld-compat — propose the latter; needs the KEL-19/KEL-17 CLI owner's agreement.

decisions.question: Where does each lane run, and how does 'regression = P1' become a CI contract rather than a slogan?
decisions.proposed_answer: PR lane (existing ubuntu/macos/windows matrix): Keld-arm replay against committed goldens inside `cargo test -p keld-compat`; deterministic, offline, each OS scored separately (as KEL-237 receipts already do). Weekly lane: (a) Electron recorder re-run at the SAME pin on all three OS (Linux under `xvfb-run`, DISPLAY :99.0, as Electron's own test workflow does) to detect oracle nondeterminism — any diff marks the cell `unknown` and proposes a normalizer, never silently re-records; (b) corpus-app smoke (draw.io, Zettlr) once migrate/dev --headless exist. Regression contract: the committed manifest carries `expected_verdict` per cell (live in corpus.json); `CI required` fails when a pass cell yields fail/unknown OR an expected-fail cell passes (forces manifest update); no `todoIf(isCI)`, bare skip, retry, or rerun (Electron's own `--enableRerun=3` is explicitly NOT copied). Re-recording goldens or bumping the Electron pin is a reviewed PR that touches manifest+goldens+receipts together. Owner: .agents/ci.md routing + keld-compat tests; failure mode: a skipped-green lane; observable contract: removing the Bun/Electron invocation fails the lane's own contract (214 Table 4 'CI home'); first falsifier: a job-level `if` that lets the compat lane report skipped while a Rust change touched keld-compat.
evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:99-109 clippy+test matrix os [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest] [fact]
.agents/ci.md: required workflows route at job boundaries; CI required rejects missing/cancelled/skipped evidence [fact]
.agents/testing.md CI tiers: PR = changed packages; nightly = fuzz; weekly = broader OS matrix + real webview/transport smoke [fact]

Electron v44.4.5 .github/workflows/pipeline-segment-electron-test.yml: `xvfb-run script/actions/run-tests.sh …`, DISPLAY ':99.0', and `--enableRerun=3` on the Wayland lane (retrieved 2026-10-06) [fact]
research 214 Table 4: stage-only-passers, test.failing for known gaps, no CI hiding [fact]
docs/architecture/04-electron-compat.md §6: 'A compat regression is a P1' [fact]
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Electron recorder in the PR lane — network + runner cost, and makes PR verdicts depend on Electron availability rather than on Keld. (b) Flake retries — forbidden by .agents/testing.md and research 214. (c) Revision-keyed baseline tables — KEL-77 deliberately did not build one; the pin is exact.

decisions.question: How are transcripts normalized and compared so that ordering is strict, timing does not create flakes, and 'no sleeps' holds?
decisions.proposed_answer: Transcript row = {seq, proc: main|preload|renderer, kind: event|call|error|exit, name, args: canonical JSON after per-cell normalizers, t_ns: monotonic delta}. Comparison is strict on the ordered (proc, kind, name, normalized args) sequence per cell; t_ns is never compared in conformance cells — it feeds separate budget cells (KEL-90/KEL-129) so clock and statistic stay separate atoms. Normalizers are declared in the manifest per cell (e.g. redact pid, window id, file paths, Error.stack; keep Error.message and code), never inferred. Both arms wait only on observable markers (LineLog pattern) with a timeout that is a kill switch; each arm is a child process whose exit code/signal is part of the transcript (subprocess rule for lifetime). Owner: keld-compat comparator; failure mode: a normalizer so broad it hides a divergence (e.g. redacting the whole args object); observable contract: a negative-control mutation in the Keld arm (swap two event emissions, change an error message) flips the cell to fail; first falsifier: a cell whose normalizers reduce args to `{}` while still scoring pass.
evidence: .agents/testing.md: no sleeps; timeout only a kill switch; crash/lifetime in a child process with stdout/stderr/exit/signal assertions [fact]
AGENTS.md: performance decompositions MUST separate census, work, queue/copy, clock, statistic and artifact [fact]
crates/keld-compat/tests/electron_lifecycle.rs LineLog.wait_contains + learnings 2026-08-18 (drain rx before asserting absence) [fact]
Electron docs: 'Errors thrown through handle … only the message property … is provided to the renderer' (ipc-main.md) — message is the comparable field, stack is not [fact]
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Comparing wall-clock timings in conformance cells — Electron and Keld have different cold-start profiles; would make every cell a benchmark. (b) Free-form snapshot testing of console output — no declared normalizers, no negative control, violates independent-oracle rule. (c) Comparing only final state — loses event ORDERING, which AGENTS.md requires to be tested.
decisions.unknowns: Whether Electron 44.4.5 preload/renderer markers can be emitted to the main-process stdout without an IPC hop that itself perturbs ordering (the recorder must route renderer rows through ipcRenderer.send to main for stdout; that hop is part of the system under observation). Prototype decides whether renderer rows carry a separate seq space.

decisions.question: What authority profile and panel can each ladder rung claim, so that a harness result never becomes a 'median-app compatibility' or 'strict profile' claim it did not measure?
decisions.proposed_answer: BEHAVIOR_MATCH and CONFORMANCE_PASS records carry authority_profile `legacy_sandbox_off` (the comparator is an ordinary test process, exactly as KEL-237 and KEL-77 record) and panel `showcase` with corpus ids like `electron-44.4.5-<family>-v1`. CORPUS_VERIFIED requires a corpus-app run under `keld dev` with authority_profile `strict_bun` (KEL-78) or an explicitly labeled legacy profile (KEL-127 'visibly labeled legacy profile'), on panel `product` only after a product corpus id is documented as committed (KEL-74: today none, so `unweighted_percent` is omitted and `complete` is false). Claims use only `{passed}/{N} of {panel} corpus {id}@{digest} ({kind})`. Owner: evidence.rs score() + manifest panel field; failure mode: a legacy_sandbox_off showcase number quoted as product compatibility; observable contract: score() on a product denominator with uncommitted id yields no percent; first falsifier: any published percent whose contributing records disagree on authority_profile or engine.
evidence: docs/specs/kel77 §4.5: 'authority_profile is deliberately not strict_bun … labelling it strict_bun would claim the measurement was taken under Keld's zero-ambient-authority profile, which is false' [fact]

crates/keld-compat/fixtures/lifecycle-corpus/report.md: authority profile legacy_sandbox_off; engine `headless-lifecycle-conformance@…`; 'not a product/median-app Electron compatibility percentage' [fact]

decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Labeling the Rust-test harness strict_bun because it uses kipc — false per KEL-77 §4.5. (b) Promoting a showcase corpus to product when it passes — forbidden by KEL-74 (showcase cannot redefine product tiers). (c) Publishing a 'Tier-1 %' from fixture cells — fixture cells are not median-app workflows; only CORPUS_VERIFIED rows feed a product denominator.

verdicts.reason: The oracle principle is confirmed by three independent owners: crates/keld-compat/AGENTS.md ('Electron documented behavior = oracle. Conformance entry (citing doc/fixture) *before* implementation'), docs/specs/kel77-bun-child-process-differential.md §4.1 ('Rejected: using the Node arm's live output as the oracle — a mirror, not an oracle'), and .agents/testing.md ('Every test MUST use an independent oracle ... upstream behavior'). A pinned recorded transcript is admissible as 'upstream behavior' evidence but cannot be the record's oracle. Two things in the proposed answer are not reuse-clean and must be corrected before it is implemented.

(2) Do not introduce a new cell shape; extend the live KEL-237 manifest cell with optional {doc_blob_oid, doc_sentence_sha256, golden_sha256, normalizers} after extracting that struct to a shared owner (see extra findings), keeping expected_verdict/test_path/test_name so lifecycle_corpus.rs's execution-admission checks still apply.

verdicts.reason: Both named falsifiers were settled by primary evidence: Electron v44.4.5 docs/tutorial/esm.md states ESM main-process entry is supported since electron@28.0.0 when 'The nearest parent package.json has "type": "module"' or the file ends in .mjs; and a local probe shows Bun 1.4.2 applies tsconfig `paths` to a plain .js `import { app } from "electron"` (resolved to packages/@keld/electron/src/index.ts, process.type=browser, versions.electron=0.0.1, exit 0). Never committing the Electron binary matches docs/architecture/04-electron-compat.md §6 ('separate repo, gitignored fixtures') and the dependency-review gate in ci.yml. The CI router already treats packages/@keld/electron/fixtures as part of the parent package and re-routes keld-compat Rust tests on fixture changes (tools/ci_changes.sh lines 276-300, 645-650), so the proposed fixture placement does not create a skipped-green path.

verdicts.reason: The three reuse claims check out: lifecycle_corpus.rs asserts denominator.corpus_sha256 == sha256(exact include_bytes! manifest) and flips one byte as a negative control; KEL-77 §4.3 defines the path||0x00||u64_le(len)||bytes digest with the learnings-recorded ('ab','c')/('a','bc') collision control; evidence.rs validates `sha256:<64 hex>` digests and evidence_uri pins, and keld-compat's Cargo.toml carries sha2 as a dev-dependency only. Using the Electron commit (not version string) as oracle revision matches the live record format `electron-v44.3.0@07e46071...`. The rejected alternatives (RFC 8785, hand-rolled hashing) are correctly rejected under AGENTS.md §2/§3.

Today both primitives are test-local: the Manifest struct and exact-bytes check live only in crates/keld-compat/tests/lifecycle_corpus.rs, and the §4.3 directory digest is a private `fn corpus_digest(dir: &Path)` at crates/keld-runtime/tests/child_process_differential.rs:288. A second corpus that copies either is the duplicate-policy defect AGENTS.md §3 forbids. The X01 spec MUST name one owner (e.g. a keld-compat test-support module or a cold `keld_compat::corpus` module behind the existing sha2 dev-dependency) and migrate KEL-237/KEL-77 callers to it in the same PR series. Also note the live KEL-237 convention sets artifact.sha256 = the manifest digest, while X01 proposes artifact.sha256 = the fixture-set digest; both are valid per corpus but the manifest must declare which, since score() refuses percent when contributing records disagree on artifact digest.

verdicts.reason: The main-process half survives and two unknowns are now facts: docs/tutorial/esm.md (v44.4.5) states ESM main is supported since electron@28 when 'the nearest parent package.json has "type": "module"', and a Bun 1.4.2 probe shows tsconfig `paths` does remap `import 'electron'` from a plain .js ESM file (output `X01_JS_ALIAS object function 0.0.1 browser`, exit 0; .mjs identical; node control fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND). But the packaging as written (preload.js inside a type:module package) is wrong per the same doc: 'Preload scripts will ignore "type": "module" fields, so you must use the .mjs file extension in your ESM preload scripts' and 'Sandboxed preload scripts are run as plain JavaScript without an ESM context ... Loading the electron API is still done via require("electron")'. A preload.js with `import` would fail under Electron's default sandbox, and a preload.js with `require` is a plain script in Electron but ESM in Bun/Node, so the 'same unmodified file' has arm-dependent module semantics. The binary-pin description is also incomplete: electron@44.4.5's npm package.json has NO scripts (no postinstall); index.js downloads lazily on first require/cli run via install.js, which verifies against the bundled checksums.json. The npm shasum therefore pins the binary only transitively, and a recorder that just runs `npx electron .` performs a network download at record time.

epic.title: program(conformance): differential oracle harness — pinned Electron recorder, Keld replayer, comparator, canonical bytes, CI lanes, maturity ladder
epic.body:
## Scope
The measurement machine behind every compat claim: Arm A records Keld-owned fixture apps under the pinned Electron 44.4.5 binary (npm dist shasum recorded; tag → commit 694f45852a0f1726cd23bfd379854de489cccb65) into line-oriented transcripts; Arm B replays the same unmodified fixtures under `@keld/electron`; a Rust comparator in keld-compat normalises declared nondeterministic fields, diffs ordered sequences, and emits one KEL-74 evidence record per cell. The pinned doc sentence is the oracle; the golden transcript is evidence-of-record (observed-only cells cap at BEHAVIOR_MATCH, recorded `unknown` with the oracle id naming the unspecified path).

## Maturity ladder (this is the ladder every family uses)
BEHAVIOR_MATCH (Keld transcript == golden under normalisers, ≥1 OS, legacy_sandbox_off) → CONFORMANCE_PASS (cited doc sentence + Keld-owned test independent of the diff + named negative control + all three OS lanes or explicit ▲) → CORPUS_VERIFIED (same observable matched in a real corpus app through migrate + dev smoke, panel product once a product corpus id is committed, authority profile printed).

## Linear owners consumed
KEL-74 (schema/scorer; shared Manifest/exact-bytes helpers must be promoted out of test-local code), KEL-237 (lifecycle corpus; canonical-bytes rule already live there), KEL-77 (two-arm harness shape; fixture-set digest algorithm §4.3), KEL-81 (CI routing), KEL-78 (authority profile truth), product-corpus owner (none today — DOCUMENTED_COMMITTED_PRODUCT list is empty).

## Design facts fixed by research (two refuters)
- Fixture family: `main.js` (ESM, type:module) + `preload.cjs` (CJS) + `index.html`, markers via synchronous stdout writes; the Electron binary is never committed and never runs in the PR lane.
- Canonical bytes: manifest exact committed bytes (sha256 asserted with a one-byte mutation control — live in the lifecycle corpus test); fixture-set digest per KEL-77 §4.3; each golden is its own immutable blob; the spec must state which digest `artifact.sha256` carries.
- Lanes: PR lane replays committed goldens inside the keld-compat test target on the existing three-OS matrix (offline, deterministic); a weekly recorder lane (TARGET: no scheduled workflow exists) re-records at the same pin to detect oracle nondeterminism and needs its own failure sink or "regression = P1" is unenforced.
- Comparison is strict within one process's sequence space plus explicit causal edges; timing never compared in conformance cells.

research.unit: X02 migrate-tooling (`keld migrate` analyzer/generator/report, migration corpus harness, `keld doctor --web-compat`)
research.summary: [fact] Nothing of this unit is live: `keld migrate` is a reserved verb (`KELD-CLI-045`, exit 2, tracking KEL-17 in `crates/keld-cli/src/verb.rs`), `keld doctor --web-compat` is rejected as `KELD-CLI-044` (`flags.rs`), MCP exposes only keld_doctor/keld_docs_search/keld_permissions_explain (no keld_migrate_analyze), `keld.compat.ts` has no schema anywhere in the repo, the hello `keld.config.ts` is `{name, entry, renderer}` (not arch 04's `defineConfig` shape), no recorder/dev-permissive profile exists (arch 03 §3), and the compat scoreboard is a placeholder with no committed product denominator. What IS live and must be consumed: `keld_guard::parse_manifest` (JSONC, 64 KiB cap, unique keys, `app` principal fs scopes with `$APPDATA`-style roots and deny fix-text that already prints the exact manifest patch), `keld_compat::evidence` (KEL-74 record/denominator/scorer with the only legal claim shape), KEL-237's lifecycle corpus manifest + denominator + runner (`deny_unknown_fields`, upstream Electron commit pin, per-cell negative_control), `DoctorFinding`/`KeldErrorObject` JSON (`{code,message,cause,fix,docs}`), KEL-215's two version-qualified better-sqlite3 rows (arch 04 §5), and the three-app demand scan in this scratchpad. [fact] The demand scan says the first two corpus apps are NOT Tier-1-only: draw.io needs `session.defaultSession.webRequest` filters, `executeJavaScript`, `printToPDF`/`print`, 11 `file://` loads, `electron-updater` (a third-party package, not Electron `autoUpdater`), `electron-store`/`electron-log`/`electron-context-menu` (all `require('electron')` internally), `@electron/fuses` via electron-builder `afterPack`, and five electron-builder JSON configs; the briefing's "<webview> tag usage (7 hits)" is a false positive — every hit is `webviewTag: false` or the `will-attach-webview` preventDefault that disables webviews. Zettlr needs `protocol.handle('safe-file')` without `registerSchemesAsPrivileged`, `sandbox:false` on 2 windows, 6 `sendSync` sites (config-provider/citeproc, including inside the preload), `requestSingleInstanceLock()` + `app.exit(0)` before `whenReady`, macOS `open-file`, a direct `.node` import (`nodehun/build/Release/Nodehun.node`), chokidar+fsevents, `child_process.spawn(..., {shell:true})` for pandoc/gsettings/`--version`, and a webpack+electron-forge pipeline (`forge.config.js` executes `spawn` while packaging) plus electron-builder YAML for installers. Two scratchpad prototypes ran on Bun 1.4.2 (macOS): tsconfig `paths` remapped `require("electron")` from inside a `node_modules` dependency to the shim (so ecosystem packages can be aliased without a bundler on Bun), and main-thread `Atomics.wait` on a SharedArrayBuffer returned `ok` after a worker notify (a blocking-CALL-with-deadline primitive exists in Bun for pre-ready synchronous Electron APIs). Six decision atoms follow: module-alias mechanism (prototype `npm:` alias), read-only analyzer shape (lexical scan + never execute app configs + KEL-127 four-way blocker report), report wording (arch 04 §1's "compat score: 91%" contradicts §4/KEL-74 and must change), permission seeding policy (literal-only static grants, dialog paths as runtime permits, everything else an explicit deny with fix text), synchronous boot facts for pre-ready APIs, and corpus harness ownership (extend KEL-237's manifest; analyzer output is a lead, not a scored cell; `keld dev --headless --smoke` is not live).

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: Must be called before the `ready` event and can be called only once; privileges (standard, secure, bypassCSP, allowServiceWorkers, supportFetchAPI, corsEnabled, stream, codeCache) mint web-platform capabilities for the scheme. Custom protocols are session-bound (`ses.protocol.handle` for non-default sessions).
semantic_traps.receipt: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electron/electron/v44.4.5/docs/api/protocol.md retrieved 2026-10-06: 'must be called before the ready event … can be called only once'; privileges list; session-specific note
semantic_traps.keld_risk: Analyzer must detect call order (pre-ready) and absence: Zettlr calls `protocol.handle('safe-file')` with NO registerSchemesAsPrivileged (non-standard, non-secure scheme) — a shim that registers 'safe-file' as standard+secure would silently widen privileges (research 186 gap 1). Also WKWebView lacks Service Worker on custom schemes (briefing: WebKit 206741) so `allowServiceWorkers` cannot be honored on macOS system engine.
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Conformance fixture pair: (a) scheme registered pre-ready vs after ready vs twice, recorded against pinned Electron 44.4.5 outcomes; (b) for a scheme registered without privileges, assert `fetch()`/`` behavior and `location.origin` match Electron's non-standard-scheme behavior; negative control: Keld facade must NOT grant `standard`/`secure` when the app did not declare them.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: If the handler throws, the invoke promise rejects, but errors are serialized and only the `message` property of the original error reaches the renderer.
semantic_traps.receipt: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electron/electron/v44.4.5/docs/api/ipc-main.md and ipc-renderer.md retrieved 2026-10-06: 'Errors thrown through handle in the main process are not transparent as they are serialized and only the message property from the original error is provided to the renderer process'; 'If the handler in the main process throws an error, the promise returned by invoke will reject'
semantic_traps.keld_risk: Keld's typed `KeldCallError`/KELD-IPC-* and guard denies carry code/cause/fix. Leaking them to the renderer verbatim changes the observable contract and may disclose host paths; dropping them entirely hides guard denials. Zettlr has 187 invoke sites and 26 handle sites, so this is the highest-volume contract in the corpus.
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Fixture handler throws `Object.assign(new Error('m'), {code:'X', stack:...})`; renderer must observe rejection whose `.message` ends with 'm' and no `code` property (Electron oracle); negative control: a guard-denied invoke must still reject (not hang) and the host-side audit log, not the renderer, carries the KELD code.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: Sends a message and expects a result synchronously; blocks the whole renderer until the reply; main sets `event.returnValue`.
semantic_traps.receipt: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/electron/electron/v44.4.5/docs/api/ipc-renderer.md retrieved 2026-10-06: 'Sending a synchronous message will block the whole renderer process until the reply is received'; ipc-main.md: 'you need to set event.returnValue'
semantic_traps.keld_risk: KEL-127 decision 5: an async replacement changes the caller contract; must remain a blocking CALL with deadline, rate-limited, dev-warned. decisions.question: How does a migrated app's `electron` import (app code, renderer bundles, and node_modules packages like electron-store/electron-log/electron-updater that `require('electron')` internally) resolve to `@keld/electron` using only the five files?
decisions.proposed_answer: [inference] Prefer a package-manager alias in package.json (`"electron": "npm:@keld/electron@<pin>"`) so every resolver — Bun runtime, tsc, webpack (Zettlr forge plugin-webpack), vite — sees `node_modules/electron` as the shim with zero bundler config; keep tsconfig `paths` as the proven dev fallback (arch 04 §3 v0 note; scratchpad alias-probe on Bun 1.4.2 showed tsconfig paths remaps `require('electron')` inside a node_modules dependency too) and keep writing bunfig.toml for spec parity. Also requires `@keld/electron` to publish `electron/main|renderer|common` subpath exports (research 214: only bare `.` exists; subpaths error).
evidence: [fact] packages/@keld/electron/src/index.ts header: Bun 1.3.14 honors tsconfig paths; bunfig [alias] does not remap runtime import
[fact] scratchpad prototypes/alias-probe run 2026-10-06, Bun 1.4.2: `app-code electron -> keld-shim`, `node_modules dep electron -> keld-shim`
[fact] research 214: `electron/main|renderer|common` -> Cannot find package 'electron' with today's alias
[fact] Zettlr webpack.main.config.js uses `externals` and forge plugin-webpack; draw.io deps electron-store/electron-log/electron-context-menu/electron-updater all live in node_modules
[fact] arch 04 §2: only package.json and bunfig.toml/bundler alias are migrate-edited; 'Nothing else'
decisions.alternatives_rejected: tsconfig paths alone (does not affect webpack/vite renderer bundles or `node` scripts; proven only on Bun); bunfig.toml alias alone (does not remap runtime on Bun 1.3.x per arch 04 §3); editing webpack/vite configs (outside the five files; forge.config.js is executable JS).
decisions.unknowns: Whether `bun install` honors `npm:` aliases for a workspace/`file:` package pointing at @keld/electron; whether tsconfig paths applies to packages with `exports` maps and ESM `import 'electron'` from node_modules (probe used a bare CJS main); Node-run build scripts (`sync.cjs`, forge hooks) that import electron.

decisions.question: What is the analyzer (`keld migrate` default / `keld_migrate_analyze`): language, parsing depth, what it may execute, and what it reports?
decisions.proposed_answer: [inference] A read-only Rust verb in keld-cli (replacing ReservedVerb::Migrate) that performs a lexical, import-binding-aware scan of JS/TS/Vue sources plus static parsing of package.json, tsconfig, bunfig, electron-builder JSON/YAML; it NEVER evaluates app code or JS configs (forge.config.js spawns processes at load). It reports KEL-127's four blocker classes separately — compatibility (matrix status per call site), security (webPreferences, openExternal dynamics, spawn, custom scheme privileges), engine (file://, SW on custom schemes, print), native-dependency (KEL-215 rows or UNKNOWN) — as `DoctorFinding`-shaped JSON with `KeldErrorObject.fix`, and emits no files unless `--write` is given (atom A4/A5 govern what is written). Classification source is one committed compat matrix owned by keld-compat.
evidence: [fact] KEL-127 body: 'A future migration analyzer starts read-only, reports compatibility/security/engine/native-dependency blockers separately and emits reviewable reversible changes only after authorization'
[fact] arch 07 §4: keld_migrate_analyze is read-only; §2 error objects {code,message,cause,fix,docs} exist in crates/keld-cli/src/error_object.rs

[fact] scratchpad scan_electron_usage.py produced usable module/signal counts for 3 apps but member counting is receiver-blind: `WebContents.replace:22` (draw.io) / `:110` (Zettlr) are String.prototype.replace; `webview_tag:7` for draw.io are disabling lines
[fact] Zettlr forge.config.js line 1-60 requires child_process and spawns get-pandoc.sh inside the config module
[fact] arch 03 §3: migrate seeds the manifest from static analysis
decisions.alternatives_rejected: A Bun/TS analyzer in a hypothetical @keld/cli (no such package; keld-cli is Rust and already owns doctor/MCP JSON shapes); executing the app under an instrumented shim to discover usage (violates read-only + would run forge/webpack code with ambient authority); full AST parser dependency (oxc/swc) before the lexical false-positive rate is measured on the corpus (dependency gate; YAGNI).
decisions.unknowns: False-positive/negative rate of binding-aware lexical scanning on Zettlr (569 files, Vue SFCs, re-exported preload API); whether a Rust JS parser crate is needed for Tier-2 exit (80% median call-site coverage over 20 apps) — no 20-app corpus list exists in the repo.

decisions.question: How does the migrate report express 'compat score' without violating KEL-74/arch 04 §4 (percentages only against a committed denominator)?
decisions.proposed_answer: [fact-backed] The sample report in arch 04 §1 ('compat score: 91% — expected to run') contradicts §4 and KEL-74 ('Public percentages require a committed denominator'; only claim shape `{passed}/{N} of {panel} corpus {id}@{digest} ({kind})`). Fix the spec: migrate prints static coverage COUNTS by status (`✔ n / ▲ n / ✘ n call sites mapped; m unclassified`) labeled 'static estimate, not a compatibility score', and prints a KEL-74 claim line only when the app is a committed corpus member with scored cells. Percentages never appear in migrate output.
evidence: [fact] docs/architecture/04-electron-compat.md §1 sample: 'compat score: 91% — expected to run'
[fact] §4: 'Public percentages require a committed denominator … MUST NOT treat a partial measurement as 100% compatibility'
[fact] docs/engineering/compat-scoreboard.md rule 4: only allowed claim shape; rule 1: no percentage without denominator document
[fact] crates/keld-compat/src/evidence.rs: only `score` constructs Scoreboard; `unweighted_percent` omitted for uncommitted product corpora
[fact] AGENTS.md: code/spec mismatch is a bug in one; fix both in same PR
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Keeping '91%' as a 'soft estimate' (violates invariant 9 and KEL-74 wording rules); computing a per-app denominator on the fly from the scanned call sites (denominator is not committed/digested; `score` requires parsed denominator with committed corpus_sha256).
decisions.unknowns: Whether the maintainers want the per-app static counts to also be excluded from public pages (report is local by default; CI scoreboard is the public surface).

decisions.question: What may `keld migrate --write` put into `keld.permissions.jsonc` when no recorder/dev-permissive profile exists (arch 03 §3 v0)?
decisions.proposed_answer: [inference] Literal-only static seeding through the live guard vocabulary: `app.getPath('userData'|'logs')` + electron-store/electron-log -> `app.fs.read/write $APPDATA/**` class roots; literal `shell.openExternal('https://…')` -> `app.shell.open` origin scopes; literal updater feed (electron-builder publish) -> `app.net.connect` ONLY in keld.build.ts/keld-update config, not an app grant; literal channel names -> `windows.<w>.channels`; `clipboard`/`Notification`/`Tray` usage -> `app.system` tokens. Everything non-literal (dialog paths, dynamic URLs, spawn with variable program, `getPath` with variable) is emitted as a `// TODO KELD-…` comment with the DenyReason fix wording and NO grant. Output must round-trip `keld_guard::parse_manifest` (64 KiB, unique keys). Dialog-chosen paths are runtime permits (KEL-140/KEL-102), never static globs. Recorder-sourced grants arrive only when the recorder exists.
evidence: [fact] arch 03 §3: v0 has no dev-permissive profile or denial recorder; `keld doctor --permissions` planned; 'keld migrate seeds the manifest from static analysis of Electron API usage (dialog → fs read of chosen paths, autoUpdater → net to feed URL, etc.)'
[fact] arch 03 §2 manifest sketch grant shapes (fs/net/shell.open/shell.spawn/system/secrets/windows.channels/csp) and the 'A grant must name a destination' rules
[fact] crates/keld-guard/src/lib.rs:338-353 DenyReason fix text; parse_manifest caps and unique-key rule
[fact] corpus: draw.io getPath literals userData/documents; Zettlr 40 getPath sites, 7 openExternal, spawn with shell:true (run-command.ts:42)
[fact] briefing invariant 2: a missing Electron permission handler must NOT become allow
decisions.alternatives_rejected: Seeding wildcards (`$DOCUMENTS/**`, `https://**`) to make the app 'just run' (default-deny violation; arch 03 §2 explicitly makes host-less globs match nothing); deferring all seeding to a recorder that does not exist (leaves the five-file promise empty); a second manifest writer with its own JSONC emitter (one owner rule).
decisions.unknowns: Exact runtime-permit contract for dialog-returned paths (guard `ScopePermit`/`PathScope` exist by name; minting from a dialog result is unspecified); whether `app.net.connect` is needed for electron-updater's GitHub provider when the adapter runs in the host.

decisions.question: How do pre-ready SYNCHRONOUS Electron APIs (requestSingleInstanceLock, app.isPackaged, app.getPath, setAsDefaultProtocolClient, protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged, process.resourcesPath) get their values when the facade's only channel is asynchronous kipc?
decisions.proposed_answer: [inference] Two-part: (1) host-published boot facts delivered to the Bun role at spawn (today only `KELD_APP_LINK=<endpoint>#<token>` is the env contract; a boot-facts blob — isPackaged, resourcesPath, path catalog, single-instance verdict — would be a KEL-75/KEL-96 host-owned addition, not a facade invention); (2) for anything that must be decided by the host at call time, a blocking CALL with deadline using Bun `Atomics.wait` on a worker-fed SharedArrayBuffer (scratchpad sync-probe: Bun 1.4.2 main thread `Atomics.wait` returned `ok` after a worker notify in 58 ms), rate-limited and dev-warned per KEL-127 decision 5. Single-instance lock itself must be host-owned (OS mutex/socket) so the facade only reads a verdict.
evidence: [fact] Zettlr source/main.ts:35 `if (!app.requestSingleInstanceLock()) { … app.exit(0) }` before whenReady; draw.io electron.js:1718 same pattern
[fact] Electron app.md v44.4.5: requestSingleInstanceLock 'Returns boolean'
[fact] scratchpad prototypes/sync-probe run 2026-10-06: {bun:1.4.2, wait:ok, value:42, ms:58.28}

verdicts.reason: The direction (a package.json dependency alias so node_modules/electron IS the shim) is confirmed for the Bun resolver, but the specific `npm:` form has an unmet precondition and the non-Bun resolvers were never exercised. Confirmed: bunfig `[alias]` is still inert on Bun 1.4.2 (bunfig-probe loads npm electron@44.5.1 from the install cache and fails on `app`), so arch 04 §3's note holds. Confirmed by a new probe (scratchpad prototypes/file-alias-probe): with `"electron": "file:../shim"` bun install links node_modules/electron -> shim, and app ESM `import 'electron'`, the `electron/main` subpath via an `exports` map, a CJS `require('electron')` from a node_modules dependency, and an ESM dep all resolve to the shim. Refuting facts for the `npm:` form: @keld/electron is not published anywhere (arch 06 §2: 'no npm wrapper is currently shipped'; product-status.tsv row package.keld-electron = partial), and the real package is not installable standalone — `packages/@keld/electron/src/app.ts:8` imports `../../api/src/app.ts` outside the package, so `file:` to the real package fails at runtime ('Cannot find module ../../api/src/link.ts'). tsc and webpack resolution were not tested by the author or by me.

verdicts.reason: The sync-probe proves only that `Atomics.wait` returns on Bun's main thread after a worker notify; it does not prove a host round-trip can complete while parked. A refined probe (scratchpad prototypes/starve2, Bun 1.4.2) shows the park starves the same-thread event loop: a socket write issued before the park was delivered at 281.5 ms (park ended 280.2 ms) and a 10 ms timer fired at 281.8 ms. The only kipc transport is `@keld/kipc` transport.ts (`DirectedReader.receive` is async, runs on the thread that imported it, i.e. the Bun main thread), so a main-thread blocking CALL can never receive its reply over the existing link. The 'worker-fed SharedArrayBuffer' therefore requires a worker that owns its own kipc connection — a second authenticated session per role, which the host does not admit today (arch 06 §2: 'the v0 echo listener admits exactly one authenticated session') and which is a principal-minting/link-ownership change (KEL-75/KEL-97/KEL-136), i.e. architecture per root AGENTS.md, not a facade detail. park-probe additionally shows the host side stalls after 8192 B while the client is parked (bytesSeenDuringPark 0), so lifecycle Events queue behind any sync call.

Part 2 (blocking CALL) is an architecture decision, not a prototype result: either a worker-owned second kipc link (needs host multi-session admission + identity rules from KEL-75/KEL-97) or moving the whole transport into a worker with SAB handoff (KEL-136 owner change); both must bound park time and specify Event queuing/backpressure. Keep the analyzer output as a lead attached to the row — confirmed correct, OperationKind has no 'analysis' value (evidence.rs:270-290).

extra_findings.finding: Bun auto-install silently substitutes the REAL Electron package when the alias is not installed. With no node_modules present, `require("electron")` under Bun 1.4.2 auto-installed electron@44.5.1 from the registry into ~/.bun/install/cache and returned the binary path string (`/Users/.../cache/electron@44.5.1@@@1/dist/Electron.app/Contents/MacOS/Electron`). A migrated app run before `bun install` (fresh clone, CI) gets Electron's stub, not @keld/electron, with no error. `keld migrate --write` should pin the alias AND `keld dev`/`keld doctor` should verify node_modules/electron resolves to @keld/electron (or write `bunfig.toml` `[install] auto = "disable"`).
extra_findings.evidence: scratchpad/x02-autoinstall run 2026-10-06: `string <home>`; arch 04 §3 lines 108-110 already notes the install-cache behavior for bunfig alias.

extra_findings.finding: @keld/electron is not CJS-requirable in a stable way. It is `"type":"module"` with a single `.ts` export; a CJS node_modules dependency doing `require('electron')` through tsconfig paths failed with `require() async module … is unsupported. use "await import()"` in one of two runs today (the author's alias-probe main.ts), while a CJS shim passed every time. draw.io's electron-log@5 (CJS src/index.js) and electron-updater@6 (CJS out/main.js) take exactly that path; electron-store@11 and electron-context-menu@5 are ESM (`npm view … type` = module). Any alias decision (A1) is moot until the shim publishes a synchronous CJS entry.
extra_findings.evidence: prototypes/alias-probe re-run 2026-10-06 (main.ts ERR, main2.ts ok, main-cjs.cjs ok, shimcjs variant ok); packages/@keld/electron/package.json exports; `npm view electron-log@5.4.4 exports`, `npm view electron-updater@6.8.10 main`.

extra_findings.finding: Several '[fact]' corpus numbers in the object are inflated by the receiver-blind scan and do not match the source: draw.io electron.js has 7 `file://` lines (object: 11), 9 `dialog.show*` sites (object: 15), 4 `isDestroyed()` (object: 6), 9 `.destroy()` (object: 10), and its `requestSingleInstanceLock` is post-ready (inside `app.whenReady().then`, line 987→1718), not pre-ready. Zettlr sendSync is 5 call sites plus the preload wrapper definition. Relabel scan-derived counts as [lead] until the binding-aware scanner exists, or the migrate report will inherit the same error bars.
extra_findings.evidence: grep -c on corpus/drawio-desktop/src/main/electron.js; awk brace depth 987→1718 = 2; corpus/zettlr grep sendSync.

extra_findings.finding: Aliasing `electron` → shim breaks the app's existing toolchain in the same step: electron-builder and electron-forge read node_modules/electron/package.json to select the Electron binary, so `start: electron .`, `release-*` (draw.io) and forge `start/package/make` (Zettlr) fail immediately after the package.json edit. migrate must rewrite/remove those scripts in the same edit and the report must say so; otherwise the 'five files, nothing else' promise is observably false on the first `npm run`.
extra_findings.evidence: corpus/drawio-desktop/package.json scripts; corpus/zettlr/forge.config.js plugin-webpack config; forge-WebpackConfig.ts externals.

extra_findings.finding: Host-owned single-instance admission (A5 part 1) changes observable pre-lock behavior: Electron executes app code in the second instance up to `requestSingleInstanceLock()`; Zettlr runs `handleExitArguments()` first and draw.io handles `--version`/`--help`/CLI export before its (post-ready) lock. If the Keld host refuses to spawn Bun for a second instance, those CLI paths never run. Must be recorded as ▲ with a conformance ordering fixture, not treated as equivalent.
extra_findings.evidence: corpus/zettlr/source/main.ts:28-35; corpus/drawio-desktop/src/main/electron.js:1700-1720; x02docs/app.md:1079-1090.

extra_findings.finding: The analyzer must follow preload re-exports to count renderer IPC demand: Zettlr renderers are bundled with webpack target `web` and call `window.ipc.sendSync` / `window.ipc.invoke` (preload exposes them via contextBridge), so a scanner keyed on `ipcRenderer.` in renderer files under-counts sendSync/invoke sites and mis-attributes them to the preload only.
extra_findings.evidence: corpus/zettlr/source/pinia/config.ts:20,28,49; preload/index.ts:37; forge-WebpackConfig.ts:264-267.

extra_findings.finding: Adjacent spec/code mismatch the migrate PR will touch: arch 07 §4 says `keld_permissions_explain` 'reads recorder output (dev)' while the live tool wraps `keld_guard::evaluate` and refuses `channel` (KELD-MCP014); and arch 03 §3's 'dialog → fs read of chosen paths' is phrased as a static seed although A4 (correctly) makes dialog paths runtime permits. Both sentences need the same-PR rewording as the 91% line.
extra_findings.evidence: docs/architecture/07-agent-experience.md:92; crates/keld-cli/src/mcp/server.rs:83-87; docs/architecture/03-security.md:214-215.

extra_findings.finding: Electron doc receipts in the object check out against v44.4.5 raw docs: webPreferences `nodeIntegration` default false, `contextIsolation` defaults true, `sandbox` default true since Electron 20 and auto-disabled by `nodeIntegration: true`, `webviewTag` defaults false, `webSecurity` default true, preload 'will always have access to node APIs'; `app.exit` omits before-quit/will-quit; `registerSchemesAsPrivileged` pre-ready/once with session-bound protocol note; `ipcMain.handle` errors serialize only `message`; `sendSync` blocks the renderer; `app.getPath` accepts exactly home, appData, assets, userData, sessionData, temp, exe, module, desktop, documents, downloads, music, pictures, videos, recent, logs, crashDumps; autoUpdater has no Linux support and requires signing on macOS; `shell.openExternal` returns Promise<void> with `activate` macOS-only. No semantic claim in the semantic_traps section was found wrong.

epic.title: program(migrate): read-only analyzer, module alias, five-file generation, honest report without percentages, corpus harness manifest
epic.body:
## Scope
`keld migrate` (reserved today), the module alias, the five generated files, the report format and the corpus manifest for real apps. Live: keld-guard manifest parser (64 KiB, unique keys, deny fix-text that prints the exact patch), KEL-74 scorer, KEL-237 lifecycle corpus runner pattern, KEL-215 addon evidence rows, the scratchpad demand scan (prototype of the analyzer).

## Design facts fixed by research (two refuters + panel)
- Analyzer is a read-only Rust verb: lexical, import-binding-aware scan of JS/TS/Vue plus static parsing of package.json/tsconfig/bunfig/electron-builder/forge configs; never evaluates app code; reports KEL-127's four blocker classes separately; emits reversible changes only after authorization (`--write`).
- The report prints static coverage COUNTS by status (✔/▲/✘/unclassified) labelled "static estimate, not a compatibility score"; a KEL-74 claim line appears only for committed corpus members. Arch 04 §1's sample `compat score: 91%` contradicts §4/KEL-74 and must be fixed in the same PR (also arch 07 §4's `keld_migrate_analyze` row).
- Module alias: a package.json dependency whose key is `electron` (npm: alias once published; file:/link: in dev) so every resolver sees `node_modules/electron` as the shim; tsconfig paths is editor/type mapping only (the refuter re-ran the probe: paths does NOT reach a node_modules dependency's require); the `bunfig.toml [alias]` wording in arch 04 §2 is a spec defect. Open: X03 proposes a Bun preload plugin for the five subpath specifiers — decide one owner (X02-A1).
- `--write` seeds `keld.permissions.jsonc` with literal-only grants through the live vocabulary; `windows.<w>.channels` has no live evaluator (blocker shared with F04-A1); no recorder exists.
- Boot facts are host-published at spawn (panel consensus); blocking pre-ready CALLs wait on PANEL-P1.
- Corpus harness: a new manifest (`electron-apps-v0`, panel product) reusing KEL-237's schema and runner pattern, pinned by upstream commit + canonical bytes; analyzer counts are leads attached to rows, never cells.

decision_tickets.title: One module-alias owner: package.json `electron` dependency alias (X02) vs a Bun preload plugin for the five Electron specifiers (X03)
decision_tickets.question: The refuter proved tsconfig paths does not reach a node_modules dependency's `require("electron")`; a package.json dependency alias does on Bun 1.4.2. X03 proposes a Bun plugin to also cover `electron/main|renderer|common|utility`. Recommendation: package.json alias as the single runtime resolver (bundler-neutral) with package `exports` for the subpaths; a plugin only if exports cannot express them. Decide and fix the arch 04 §2 bunfig wording.

not_yet_specified: Recorder/dev-permissive profile (arch 03 §3 destination) as the source of dynamic grants
`keld doctor --web-compat` scope
never_list: claiming native-addon support without KEL-215-shaped evidence

research.summary: Cross-cutting runtime layer for migrated Electron main processes on Bun. Findings: (1) Electron resolves the five module specifiers (electron, electron/main, electron/renderer, electron/common, electron/utility) with one Module._resolveFilename patch to a single builtin and ships no package.json exports; Keld must do the same with ONE resolver owner — a Bun preload plugin (onResolve covers bare specifiers for both import and require) — because bunfig.toml has no [alias] key at all (architecture 04 §2 names a non-existent key; the KEL-72 fixture still writes it) and tsconfig paths is only verified for ESM import of bare `electron` on Bun 1.3.14 while CI now pins 1.4.2. (2) Process-level Electron facts (process.type/versions/defaultApp/resourcesPath/mas/windowsStore, app.getPath/getVersion/getName/isPackaged/getAppPath) are consumed synchronously at module-evaluation time by real apps (draw.io constructs electron-store at top level), so they must be host-minted and delivered at role spawn, not fetched over kipc after ready. (3) Native addon policy follows the KEL-78 four-outcome tree with no in-process load under strict: better-sqlite3 (N-API, KEL-215 qualified only for 13.0.3/Bun 1.4.2/win-x64), nodehun (N-API, node-gyp source build, imported as a raw .node file by Zettlr), node-pty (N-API 7, KEL-76 host pty row), keytar (N-API 3, archived → safeStorage over keld-native `secrets`), sharp and @parcel/watcher (N-API prebuilds → addon worker). chokidar 5 is pure JS over fs.watch — a Bun fs.watch differential (KEL-77 family extension), not addon policy; fsevents is only a transitive chokidar@3 optional in Zettlr's lock. (4) Both corpus apps spawn external executables; raw child_process stays never-listed under strict, so a scoped `process` broker (KEL-76) with KEL-77's five lifecycle oracles as conformance is on the critical path for Zettlr, while draw.io's spawns are Windows-only. (5) Profile labeling: Electron-compat apps start `unverified`, never silently `legacy`; migrate must write the explicit Keld profile key only on user acceptance and print the forfeit. (6) electron-store/electron-log/electron-context-menu are the cheapest aggregate oracle of the median main-process surface and should become an unmodified package panel in the corpus. Evidence is insufficient to state Bun 1.4.2 Node-API coverage or whether nodehun/node-pty load on it; prototypes are proposed.

keld_state.current: LIVE: packages/@keld/electron installs process.type="browser" and process.versions.electron="0.0.1" at import (src/index.ts); exports only `.`→src/index.ts and only `app`; fixtures/tsconfig.json maps bare `electron` via compilerOptions.paths; fixtures/bunfig.toml writes an `[alias]` table that Bun does not document and that did not remap on Bun 1.3.14 (learnings.md 2026-08-18); CI pins Bun 1.4.2 (ci.yml) and local bun is 1.4.2 — the alias finding has not been re-run on 1.4.2. keld-guard::admit::ProfileState {Unverified, Legacy, Strict} + admit() live (KELD-GUARD008–015); Principal enum has AppProcess/Webview/Plugin only — no AddonWorker. keld-runtime: RoleRegistry (primary + app_bound roles), VirtualPortRegistry, linux_strict, macos_guardian, windows_lpac/job live; KEL-77 child_process_differential.rs covers 6 operations / 5 Node oracles (close-after-exit-order, error-before-close-on-spawn-failure, exit-event-code, exit-event-signal, subprocess-kill-return), macOS arm64 only, authority_profile legacy_sandbox_off; N-API and libuv families are explicit non-goals. keld-native: FsBroker fs.read/fs.write only, unreachable from shipping host until KEL-102/T3; MODULES lists secrets/shell/etc. but no process/pty/auth rows (arch 05 says KEL-76 must approve real behavior). keld-cli: migrate/build reserved (KELD-CLI-045); doctor has no native-module DB scan (arch 04 §5, arch 06). TARGET: electron/* subpath aliases, process.defaultApp/resourcesPath/mas/windowsStore/isMainFrame shims, sync app getters, addon worker (KEL-78 T7 unchecked), profile key in keld.config.ts/keld.permissions.jsonc (KEL-78 §4: key does not exist today), process broker, fs.watch broker, safeStorage facade, keld.compat.ts quirks flags. Ledger drift noted: product-status.tsv row package.keld-api says 'no package is tracked' while packages/@keld/api/src exists (KEL-142 Done).
