epic.title: program(runtime): Node/Bun compatibility layer for migrated mains — process facts, module specifiers, native addon policy, child_process broker, ecosystem packages
epic.body:
## Scope
Process-level Electron facts consumed at module evaluation (type, versions, defaultApp, resourcesPath, mas, windowsStore, sandboxed, contextIsolated), the five module specifiers (`electron`, `electron/main|renderer|common|utility`), native addon classes (better-sqlite3, nodehun, node-pty, keytar, sharp, @parcel/watcher; chokidar 5 is pure JS over fs.watch; fsevents transitive), strict vs legacy labelling, child_process replacement, and the ecosystem packages that wrap Electron (electron-store, electron-log, electron-context-menu).

## Design facts from research (NOT yet independently refuted — batch 2; decisions below stay open except where the panel settled them)
- Boot facts are host-minted at spawn and read synchronously at import (settled by the panel).
- Migrated apps start `unverified` (KEL-78 default) and the report prints it; `legacy` is written only when the user accepts the forfeit; every surface prints "legacy — zero-authority claim forfeited" (settled by the panel).
- Native addon policy follows KEL-78's four-outcome tree with a KEL-215-shaped evidence row per (version, OS/arch, Bun revision, artifact digest, operation); no in-process load under strict.
- child_process under strict is a host `process` broker row (KEL-76 owner) with a child_process-shaped facade conforming to KEL-77's five Node oracles; under legacy Bun's node:child_process with documented gaps.
- electron-store/electron-log/electron-context-menu are an aggregate oracle for the median main-process surface (candidate `package` panel).

**Category:** feature

**Current behavior:** Only process.type/versions.electron at import; bare `electron` via tsconfig paths in fixtures.

**Desired behavior:** Deliver the bootstrap payload beside `KELD_APP_LINK` (role spawn contract) carrying process facts and the path catalogue; `@keld/electron` reads it synchronously at import; resolve `electron`, `electron/main|renderer|common|utility` through the single alias owner decided in X02-A1 (package exports for subpaths); `process.versions.electron` reports the Keld shim version, never a fake Electron release.

**Key interfaces:** Role bootstrap payload; package exports; facade import-time initialisation.

**Acceptance criteria:** the checklist above, each as a test with its negative control.

research.unit: X04 security-mapping (cross-cutting): Electron security-relevant surfaces -> Keld generated host-enforced default-deny
research.summary: Every Electron security surface in scope collapses onto four existing Keld owners, none of which needs a new schema: (1) keld-guard `evaluate(manifest, Principal, capability, resource)` with the arch 03 §2 grant shapes (`app.{fs,net,shell,system,secrets,auth}` and `windows.<w>.{channels, web.*}`), (2) the KEL-142 isolated-world bridge (`window.keld.invoke`) in place of preload/contextBridge/ipcRenderer, (3) KEL-75/78 principalized strict roles in place of utilityProcess/fuses, and (4) the arch 06 §4a host-owned signed feed in place of autoUpdater/ASAR. The decisive inversion is Electron's two independent allow-by-default permission paths (request + check) becoming one guard decision where a missing Electron handler is a `KELD-GUARD001` deny and a registered handler can only narrow, never widen. Live today: `/app` grants for `AppProcess` only; a minted `Principal::Webview` is `KELD-GUARD006` until window-level grants ship (KEL-102/T4), and the media callbacks evaluate resource `*` because wry exposes no origin. Three design atoms are genuinely open and need grilling, not more research: the `shell.open` scheme-class grant spelling (draw.io/Zettlr open arbitrary https/mailto URLs and `https://**` is inert by the KEL-208 authority rule), the CSP profile that must admit draw.io's `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`, and the host-minted one-shot `fs.read` grant for OS-delivered file paths (second-instance/open-file). Device permissions (HID/USB/serial/Bluetooth) have no broker, no principal and no spec: documented-unsupported, not legacy. Nothing in this unit auto-selects `legacy`; KEL-78 fixes that Electron `sandbox:false` is not the legacy key and renderer sandbox is a different column, so Zettlr's two `sandbox:false` windows are a scoreboard ✘/▲ requiring a verified preload audit, not a profile downgrade.

Any principal other than `AppProcess` is `KELD-GUARD006` before grant lookup (lib.rs:705); media callbacks that present a `Principal::Webview` therefore deny today. Codes live: GUARD001 NotGranted, 002 OutOfScope, 003 ChannelForbidden (text exists; channel grants not evaluated), 006 NotAppProcess, 007 MediaPrincipalRequired, 004/005/016/017 manifest errors. URL authority rule (KEL-208) is live in the matcher but no URL-valued capability is wired. `dispatch_privileged` (KEL-69) is the sole guard-before-handler entry; only `fs.read`/`fs.write` via FsBroker (KEL-130) use it and the no-flag host does not register FS_CHANNEL (KEL-102/T3 target). keld-wv: camera/microphone default-denied on macOS 12+/Linux via wry `with_permission_handler` and on Windows via WebView2 `add_PermissionRequested`; resource is the `*` sentinel (`WEB_MEDIA_ORIGIN`), origin-scoped grants unenforceable (media.rs:29-36,57-59); DevTools compiled in only under `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` (media.rs:334-335); `WebEngine::devtools(id, action)` exists on all three backends. keld-runtime roles: exact env list + `KELD_APP_LINK` injected per spawn; strict roles refuse `current_dir` ("fixed /app working directory", role.rs:689-693). @keld/electron: `app` only (whenReady/isReady/quit/on/off/removeListener) over LIFECYCLE_CHANNEL; no BrowserWindow/ipcMain/session/protocol/shell/preload. @keld/api: app lifecycle, `channels.handle` for the one generated echo channel, link.ts. KEL-142 (Done, macOS): `window.keld.invoke` page-world facade + WKContentWorld-isolated script; iframes get no `window.keld`. No `web.csp`, `web.devtools`, `channels`, `el:*`, `shell.open`, `net.connect`, `profile` key, dev-permissive recorder, or deny recorder is live. decisions.question: How do Electron's session.setPermissionRequestHandler / setPermissionCheckHandler (and <webview> permission-request) map onto Keld without reintroducing allow-by-default?
decisions.proposed_answer: One guard decision, two Electron views of it. The host evaluates `windows.<w>.web.<permission>` (same array-of-scopes shape already used by live `app.web.camera`/`app.web.microphone`, moved under `windows` as arch 03 §2/§4 already names) as `Principal::Webview{id, generation}` from the host registry. The facade's request handler and check handler are both invoked AFTER the guard allows and may only narrow (callback(false)/return false => deny); a handler return of true when the guard denied is ignored and emits a dev-warned `KELD-GUARD001` deny with the exact manifest fix. No handler registered => guard decision stands (deny on empty manifest). Check and request return the same value for the same (principal, permission, origin) tuple. Permission-name vocabulary = Electron's documented list mapped 1:1 onto `web.<name>` literals; unknown names deny. Origin scopes use the live KEL-208 authority matcher; until a platform callback supplies the requesting origin (WebView2 `Uri` does; wry does not) the resource stays the `*` sentinel and an origin-shaped grant must not match (already tested in keld-wv `origin_looking_grant_does_not_match_sentinel`).
evidence: [fact] security.md: 'By default, Electron will automatically approve all permission requests unless the developer has manually configured a custom handler.'
[fact] research 186 row 4: request and check are independently allow-by-default paths with different exceptions (geolocation switch, deprecated sync clipboard read).

[fact] keld-guard lib.rs:705 denies any non-AppProcess principal (GUARD006); lib.rs:1899-1936 tests default-deny `web.camera`/`web.microphone` on an empty manifest and deny `https://evil.example` under a `*` grant.
[fact] keld-wv media.rs:29-36,57-59: platform callbacks pass no origin; resource is `*`; origin grants unenforceable.
[fact] arch 03 §4(3): 'Missing identity and AppProcess fail closed (KELD-GUARD007)… A minted webview principal is still KELD-GUARD006 until window-level grants exist.'
[fact] KEL-132 §3: REVOKE requires navigation generation rotation; SAVED-GRANT (KEL-135 §7.1): a persisted engine Allow cannot bypass the next session's denying policy.

[fact] corpus: neither draw.io nor Zettlr registers setPermissionRequestHandler/CheckHandler (grep over src/main/electron.js and source/app/**) — so under Electron they run with auto-approve; under Keld they get deny with fix-it text.
decisions.confidence: high on the inversion and shape; medium on vocabulary breadth (which of Electron's ~46 permission names Keld will ever expose; most have no host broker)
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Honor Electron default (allow when no handler) — violates briefing invariant 2. (b) Let a facade handler returning true grant beyond the manifest — moves authority into Bun, breaks one-owner rule. (c) New per-permission schema block — arch 03 §2 already has `windows.<w>.web.*`; a new block would be a duplicate policy surface. (d) Evaluate as AppProcess with `/app/web/*` — the `/app` grants must never apply to a webview (GUARD007 rule).
decisions.unknowns: Exact Keld behavior of saved engine permission preferences on Windows/macOS (KEL-135 SAVED-GRANT awaiting); whether wry will ever surface origin; which subset of permission names gets a host broker in Tier 1/2 (only media exists).
blocked_by: KEL-102/T4 window-level grants + registry-derived webview principal

decisions.question: What does `keld migrate` + the BrowserWindow facade do with webPreferences that weaken isolation (nodeIntegration, contextIsolation:false, sandbox:false, webSecurity:false, allowRunningInsecureContent, experimentalFeatures/enableBlinkFeatures, webviewTag, enableRemoteModule, devTools)?
decisions.proposed_answer: Compile-time classification in migrate + runtime refusal in the facade, never silent honoring. nodeIntegration:true, contextIsolation:false, webSecurity:false, allowRunningInsecureContent:true, experimentalFeatures, enableBlinkFeatures/disableBlinkFeatures, enableRemoteModule => migrate ✘ with per-call-site diagnostic; at runtime the facade throws a typed `KELD-COMPAT-*` error at BrowserWindow construction (window not created) unless `keld.compat.ts` sets the per-window quirks flag `ignoreWeakWebPreferences` which creates the window with Keld's forced values and logs ▲. sandbox:false => ▲ only: Keld always runs the preload as a host-injected isolated-world user script without Node; if the preload needs `require` of anything outside Electron's own sandboxed-preload module map, that is a code change, not a profile (KEL-78: Electron `sandbox`/`appSandbox` MUST NOT be read as `legacy`; renderer sandbox is a different column). devTools:false => honored (narrowing); devTools absent/true => `windows.<w>.web.devtools: true` is required in release, else `openDevTools()` is a `KELD-*` error (arch 03 §4 'devtools off in release unless web.devtools: true'). webviewTag:true => Tier 3 ✘ now. `process.sandboxed === true` and `process.contextIsolated === true` always in the renderer shim.
evidence: [fact] web-preferences.md v44.4.5: nodeIntegration default false; contextIsolation default true; sandbox 'Default is true since Electron 20'; webSecurity true; allowRunningInsecureContent false; devTools true; webviewTag false; enableRemoteModule absent.

[fact] sandbox.md: 'Setting nodeIntegration: true automatically disables sandboxing for that renderer process'; sandboxed preload `require` is a polyfill limited to electron (contextBridge, crashReporter, ipcRenderer, nativeImage, webFrame, webUtils) + events, timers, url.
[fact] KEL-78 spec: 'Electron `sandbox` / `appSandbox` is not this key and MUST NOT be read as `legacy` or `strict`'; 'Renderer sandbox is a different column.'

[fact] corpus: draw.io sets contextIsolation:true, nodeIntegration:false, webviewTag:false, webSecurity:true on every window (electron.js:721-729,1086-1091,1403-1408,3082-3088) and restates them in setWindowOpenHandler overrides (2207-2212); `app.enableSandbox()` commented out (690-691); filters `--no-sandbox` from argv (1231-1234). Zettlr: sandbox:true + preload on 13 windows; sandbox:false on splash-screen.ts:65 and onboarding-window.ts:72. quick-start: preload only, defaults.
[fact] research 13 never-list: `nodeIntegration: true` in renderer 'Incompatible with default-deny model'.
[fact] keld-wv media.rs:334-335 compiles `with_devtools(true)` only under `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`.
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Silently coerce all weak preferences to Keld values — violates 'divergence must be explicit'. (b) Treat sandbox:false as a legacy-profile trigger — forbidden by KEL-78 and would downgrade the Bun role for a renderer concern. (c) Emulate nodeIntegration via a Node-shaped bridge — a fifth unique / parallel authority path.
decisions.unknowns: [inference] Zettlr's two sandbox:false preloads appear to need Node (comment 'Preload scripts have access to…'); not verified by reading the preload bundles — a 10-minute grep decides ▲ vs ✘ for Zettlr install cell. Whether `ignoreWeakWebPreferences` should exist at all or only ✘ (recommend: exists, dev-only, refused in release).
blocked_by: BrowserWindow facade (F02) and preload injection (F04/F07) design

decisions.question: How do `protocol.registerSchemesAsPrivileged` + `protocol.handle` (Zettlr `safe-file://`) and `webRequest.onHeadersReceived` CSP (draw.io) map onto KEL-79 resource transport and `windows.<w>.web.csp` without letting a renderer turn a locator into filesystem authority?
decisions.proposed_answer: Privilege bits are host declarations, not runtime calls: scheme names and {standard, secure, supportFetchAPI, corsEnabled, stream, codeCache} are declared in `keld.config.ts web.schemes` and registered by the host before first navigation; `registerSchemesAsPrivileged` in app code becomes a no-op-with-check (must equal the declaration, else `KELD-COMPAT` error before `ready`). `bypassCSP` is never. `allowServiceWorkers` is ▲ platform-scored (WKWebView lacks SW on custom schemes). `protocol.handle(scheme, fn)` runs the app's handler in the Bun role but its bytes come only through brokers: a `Response` built from app memory is forwarded; any file read inside the handler is an ordinary `fs.read` guarded by `app.fs.read` scopes, which for Zettlr's workspace roots are dialog-derived scopes (arch 05 dialog row 'scoped-path grants flow into fs scopes'), not `$HOME/**`. The handler receives `request.initiatorOrigin` from the host registry, never from the page. CSP: Keld injects `windows.<w>.web.csp` (`default` | `static-only` | named opt-out); migrate translates draw.io's header-injected CSP into a reviewed named profile; whether `default` must admit `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` and `img-src * data:` is the open sub-question (prototype P2).
evidence: [fact] protocol.md v44.4.5: registerSchemesAsPrivileged 'can only be used before the ready event… and can be called only once'; privileges standard/secure/bypassCSP/allowServiceWorkers/supportFetchAPI/corsEnabled/stream/codeCache; `request.initiatorOrigin` 'is not controlled by the requesting page'; register*/intercept*Protocol deprecated in favor of protocol.handle.
[fact] research 186 row 1 + NEW gap 1: custom schemes mint privileges; registry does not canonicalize a resource path; need traversal/encoding matrix.

[fact] corpus Zettlr custom-protocols.ts:55-100: `protocol.handle('safe-file', …)` decodes pathname, strips Windows drive slash, maps `//share` to `/Volumes/…` on macOS, `fs.access` + `fs.readFile` any absolute path; NO registerSchemesAsPrivileged call anywhere in source (grep empty) — so the scheme is non-standard/insecure under Electron too.

[fact] corpus draw.io electron.js:994-1008: header CSP `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; … img-src * data:; media-src *; font-src * data:; … object-src 'none'`; 1010-1022 `onBeforeRequest({urls:['file://*']})` blocks file loads outside app dir.
[fact] arch 03 §2: 'CSP injection by default on every webview (default = self + keld:// + declared net hosts; static-only = no script eval, no net). Opt-out is a named, linted grant.'
[fact] arch 05: adapter MUST bind an unguessable capability to one active WebView/navigation generation; guard before bytes; 'A Service Worker is optional machinery, not the authorization boundary.'
[fact] briefing: WKWebView lacks Service Worker on custom schemes (WebKit 206741); WebView2 virtual-host SW limits.
decisions.confidence: medium-high on ownership (host declares, broker loads); medium on whether a third CSP level is needed
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Let Bun's handler read files directly (Node fs) — strict profile has no fs authority; would need legacy. (b) Translate `safe-file://` to `file://` — file:// is itself on the migrate-discouraged list (security.md #18) and keld:// isolation already exists. (c) Allow `bypassCSP` under a quirks flag — a quirks flag may not widen authority.
decisions.unknowns: Whether `web.csp` accepts a reviewed custom string (arch 03 says 'named' only); WebKitGTK custom-scheme + SW behavior; exact Keld behavior when registerSchemesAsPrivileged is called after ready (Electron's own failure mode is not quoted in the docs — [unknown]).
blocked_by: KEL-135 profile identity for per-scheme storage partitioning

decisions.question: What grant does `shell.openExternal` (and openPath/showItemInFolder/trashItem) need when real apps open arbitrary https/mailto/tel URLs and the renderer can trigger it?
decisions.proposed_answer: Reuse `app.shell.open: [...]` (arch 03 §2 shape) with two additions that are vocabulary, not schema: (1) a scheme-class literal spelled so it cannot be confused with the inert `https://**` form — proposal `"https:"`, `"mailto:"`, `"tel:"` (bare scheme + colon, which the authority rule already treats as 'names no destination' and so is currently inert; promoting it to 'any destination of this scheme' is an explicit permission-model review gate), alongside exact-origin entries; (2) a caller-identity rule: an `openExternal` whose causal chain starts in a webview (ipc from `el:*`, will-navigate, window-open handler) requires a user gesture recorded by the host for that webview principal within a bounded window, else `KELD-GUARD001`; main-process-originated calls need only the scope. `file:`, `smb:`, `javascript:`, custom app schemes and anything not in the list deny. `openPath`/`showItemInFolder`/`trashItem` require an `app.fs.read` (reveal/open) or `app.fs.write` (trash) scope covering the path; `writeShortcutLink` is `fs.write`. Migrate seeds `shell.open` from static regex/allowlists (draw.io's `allowedUrls` literally yields `https:`,`http:`,`mailto:`,`tel:`,`callto:`) and from literal URLs in menus.
evidence: [fact] shell.md v44.4.5: openExternal 'Returns Promise<void>'; options activate (macOS), workingDirectory/logUsage (Windows); URL limited to 2081 chars on Windows; shell 'will not function in a sandboxed renderer'.
[fact] security.md #15: 'When openExternal is used with untrusted content, it can be leveraged to execute arbitrary commands.'
[fact] session.md permission list includes `openExternal` as a requestable permission name (so Electron already models it as a webview-origin permission).
[fact] research 186 row 3 + NEW gap 3: no allowlist/origin/prompt check in Electron's binding; Keld needs origin, scheme, host, user gesture, confirmation and denied-handler matrix.
[fact] arch 03 §2: `"https://**"` 'matches nothing' (authority rule); 'No glob grants any host for a multi-character scheme — name the origins.'

[fact] corpus draw.io electron.js:4348-4360: `allowedUrls = /^(?:https?|mailto|tel|callto):/i` then `shell.openExternal(url)`; invoked from setWindowOpenHandler (2216) and renderer ipc `case 'openExternal'` (4515-4516). Zettlr attach-app-navigation-handlers.ts:25-44: any non-`safe-file://` will-navigate URL → `shell.openExternal(url)`; `safe-file://` → `shell.openPath(realPath)` for any decoded path; menus open fixed https URLs.
decisions.confidence: medium — the scheme-class spelling is a user-owned permission-model choice
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Require explicit origins only — breaks the config-only promise for both first corpus apps (they open user-authored links). (b) Grant via `system: ["shell.open-any"]` — duplicates the shell block and hides the scheme policy. (c) Host confirmation dialog on every call — Electron parity loss, and dialogs are not authorization. (d) Keep `https://**` inert and add nothing — forces every app into ✘.
decisions.unknowns: Whether the authority-rule owner (KEL-208) accepts a bare-scheme literal as 'scheme-class allow' or wants a different spelling; how the host attributes user gesture across the kipc hop (WKWebView/WebView2 user-activation APIs vs. host-side timing); Linux portal (xdg-open) behavior for mailto/tel.

decisions.question: How are `requestSingleInstanceLock` / `second-instance(argv, cwd, additionalData)` / `open-file` / `open-url` delivered without handing OS-derived argv to a privileged handler, given draw.io reads the file named by argv?
decisions.proposed_answer: Host-owned `deeplink` module (arch 05 table) is the single admission point: the host (not Bun) holds the OS single-instance primitive, parses the second launch's argv/cwd/additionalData as untrusted data, enforces exactly-once delivery and the 32 MB bound, and emits a typed event; the facade surfaces Electron's `(event, argv, workingDirectory, additionalData)` with argv as opaque strings. `workingDirectory` is the second instance's cwd as data; it never changes the strict role's fixed `/app` cwd. Because the strict role has no ambient fs authority, draw.io's `statSafe(commandLine.pop())`/read pattern requires the host to mint a one-shot `fs.read` scope for the exact file the OS named (same mechanism as dialog-derived scopes: user intent via OS open-with/file association is the gesture), recorded in the deny/allow audit; a path that was not OS-delivered gets `KELD-GUARD002`. `setAsDefaultProtocolClient` becomes a `keld.config.ts` declaration packaged by keld-pack (macOS Info.plist at build time), with runtime calls check-only.
evidence: [fact] app.md v44.4.5 second-instance: 'argv will not be exactly the same list of arguments as those passed to the second instance. The order might change and additional arguments might be appended.'; 'If the second instance is started by a different user than the first, the argv array will not include the arguments.'; 'Extra command line arguments might be added by Chromium, such as --original-process-start-time.'; requestSingleInstanceLock: on macOS/Linux a single message 'limited to 32 MB. Larger messages are dropped.'
[fact] research 186 row 2 + NEW gap 2: every handoff field is external input; need cold/warm activation tests proving exactly-once delivery/typed rejection.
[fact] keld-runtime role.rs:689-693: strict roles refuse `current_dir` ('fixed /app working directory'); env is the exact configured list + KELD_APP_LINK.

[fact] corpus draw.io electron.js:1718-1760: lock → on second-instance createWindow, then `commandLine.pop()` → `statSafe` → `blessPath` → `webContents.send('args-obj')`; `open-file` at 2144. Zettlr main.ts:35-45,139-160: lock else `app.exit(0)`; second-instance → `extractFilesFromArgv(argv)` → `roots-add`; open-file handler 162.
[fact] arch 05 broker table: `deeplink` = 'protocol registration + single-instance handoff' → `app.setAsDefaultProtocolClient`; `dialog`: 'scoped-path grants flow into fs scopes'.
decisions.confidence: high on host ownership; medium on the one-shot grant mechanism (not yet specified anywhere)
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Let the Bun role own the single-instance lock (socket/lockfile) — a second authority root and racy with host lifecycle. (b) Grant `$HOME/**` read to make argv files readable — wildcard authority the operator never named. (c) Drop argv entirely and expose only additionalData — breaks both corpus apps' file-association flows.
decisions.unknowns: Whether OS-delivered open-file intent is accepted as a gesture equivalent to a dialog selection (permission-model gate); Windows single-instance primitive choice (named mutex vs. pipe) and its interaction with KEL-101 DACLs; how `additionalData` is bounded/validated (postcard size cap).
blocked_by: KEL-130 FsBroker dynamic scope insertion (today scopes are manifest-only, snapshot-verified)

decisions.question: What do `autoUpdater.setFeedURL`, electron-updater provider configs, Electron fuses and ASAR integrity become under Keld's host-owned trust chain?
decisions.proposed_answer: Feed trust is host-only: `keld.build.ts` declares the feed base; the facade's `setFeedURL(opts)` is check-only — a URL/provider that does not resolve to the declared feed base is a `KELD-UPDATE-*` error with no network, and `checkForUpdates`/`quitAndInstall`/events map onto keld-update's manifest fetch, floor filtering and KEL-53 activation (▲ for `releaseNotes`/`releaseName` fields the manifest may not carry). Migrate translates electron-updater `provider: 'github'` (draw.io) and Forge publishers into the §4a feed layout + the arch 04 §7 bridge release. Fuses have no runtime equivalent and migrate reports each: `runAsNode`/`nodeOptions`/`nodeCliInspect` → covered by exact role env + no CLI flags (strict admission KEL-78); `cookieEncryption` → KEL-135 per-app profile store (encryption-at-rest status [unknown] per engine); `embeddedAsarIntegrityValidation` + `onlyLoadAppFromAsar` → signed package + ExpectedAppIdentity (KEL-19/KEL-254) verified before launch, no loose-directory fallback; `grantFileProtocolExtraPrivileges` → not applicable (keld:// isolation, file:// discouraged); `loadBrowserProcessSpecificV8Snapshot`/`wasmTrapHandlers` → N/A (no V8 in host). A fuse setting is never an input to Keld authority.
evidence: [fact] auto-updater.md v44.4.5: 'Your application must be signed for automatic updates on macOS'; Linux 'no built-in support'; setFeedURL {url, headers (macOS), serverType json|default (macOS), allowAnyVersion (MSIX)}; events error/checking-for-update/update-available/update-not-available/update-downloaded(releaseNotes, releaseName, releaseDate, updateURL)/before-quit-for-update.

[fact] fuses.md: defaults runAsNode on, cookieEncryption off, nodeOptions on, nodeCliInspect on, embeddedAsarIntegrityValidation off, onlyLoadAppFromAsar off, loadBrowserProcessSpecificV8Snapshot off, grantFileProtocolExtraPrivileges on, wasmTrapHandlers on; flipped at package time before signing.

[fact] asar-integrity.md: macOS (16+) and Windows (30+) only; 'If no hash is present or if there is a mismatch in the hashes, the app will forcefully terminate'; needs both EnableEmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation and OnlyLoadAppFromAsar.
[fact] research 186 rows 8-10 + NEW gap 7: ASAR-only lookup and integrity are separate controls; Squirrel/MSIX delegation is not a Keld manifest/signature/rollback contract.

[fact] arch 06 §4a: detached ed25519 `.sig` over `updates.json`, key 'compiled into the host binary at build time (never fetched from the feed)', `app.id`/`channel`/`target` must match compiled-in identity, monotonic floor, deterministic release selection; KEL-53 §3: 'Command line, environment, cwd, caller paths and feed bytes convey no authority.'

[fact] corpus draw.io electron.js:2078-2083 `autoUpdater.setFeedURL({provider:'github', repo:'drawio-desktop', owner:'jgraph', channel})` (electron-updater), autoDownload false, autoInstallOnAppQuit; Zettlr forge.config.js:295-301 flips RunAsNode false, EnableCookieEncryption true, NodeOptions false, NodeCliInspect false, GrantFileProtocolExtraPrivileges true; draw.io package.json lists @electron/fuses (briefing) but no fuse config in electron-builder-*.json (grep empty — [unknown] where it is applied).
decisions.alternatives_rejected: (a) Accept app-supplied feed URL with HTTPS-only check — briefing never-list item; the key must not be feed-adjacent. (b) Emulate fuses as `keld.compat.ts` switches — a fuse that 'turns on' would be a permission without an owner. (c) Ship an ASAR reader for compatibility — a second package format with no integrity story on Linux.
decisions.unknowns: Whether electron-updater's GitHub-releases JSON can be bridged by a static generator into §4a layout (arch 04 §7 says a recipe exists, not implemented); engine-level cookie encryption at rest per platform (WebView2 UDF vs WKWebsiteDataStore vs WebKitGTK); `releaseNotes` carriage in the manifest.

platform_notes.note: [fact] wry `with_permission_handler` passes no origin; guarded media denial works on macOS 12+ only (pinned wry does not consume the callback below 12 on debug hosts) — KEL-132 open item. WKContentWorld isolation (KEL-142) needs macOS 11+. [fact] WKWebView lacks Service Worker on custom schemes (WebKit 206741) → `allowServiceWorkers` scheme privilege is ▲ on macOS. [fact] Electron parity items that are macOS-only: `open-url`/`open-file` events, Info.plist protocol declaration at build, `openExternal({activate})`, autoUpdater signing requirement and `serverType: json`. Keld analogue: keld-pack writes CFBundleURLTypes from `keld.config.ts`; keld-update is the updater regardless of Squirrel.Mac. [fact] Safari Web Inspector is the DevTools; must be disabled in release builds (today only `debug_assertions` compiles it in).

[fact] WebView2 is Chromium-derived — say so: it exposes CDP (`--remote-debugging-port`, DevTools) and `PermissionRequested` with `Uri`; Keld's v0 adapter reads only `PermissionKind` and evaluates `*`. Window-level origin grants are therefore implementable first on Windows. [fact] Zero-capability LPAC is the strict authority boundary (KEL-210); Job object is cleanup not authority. [fact] Electron Windows-only surfaces: `openExternal` 2081-char limit, `workingDirectory`/`logUsage`, shortcut-link APIs (→ `fs.write` scope), MSIX vs Squirrel.Windows detection, ASAR integrity via `Integrity` resource (Electron 30+). Keld analogue: KEL-53 journaled activation + KEL-254 installed-root boot; Machine-UAC helper (KEL-270) has no feed parser. [fact] Bluetooth pairing requiring validation auto-cancels without a handler.

[fact] Strict profile = Bubblewrap namespaces + empty-root exact mounts + seccomp (x86_64 only; other arches fail closed) + Landlock; `NotImplemented` Landlock never selects legacy (arch 06 §1). [fact] WebKitGTK `UserMediaPermissionRequest` deny path landed (KEL-132 #162); portal-first for file dialogs/openExternal (xdg-open) — gesture attribution via portal is [unknown]. [fact] Electron has no ASAR integrity and no built-in autoUpdater on Linux, so Keld's signed package + keld-update is strictly more than parity here (claim only with measurement). [fact] Research 214 refuses the D-Bus notification fixture; Bluetooth pairing auto-cancels without handler. [unknown] WebKitGTK custom-scheme Service Worker support.

verdicts.lens: Keld invariants, ownership and reuse: four uniques only; default-deny never bypassed or defaulted to allow; no Electron-isms in keld-core/keld-ipc; no parallel process model/transport/schema/parser/policy owner; reuse of existing owners (KEL-75/76/77/78/79/80/53/74/102/135/139-144); performance claims must be measured; spec+Linear gate; prior decisions #312/#313/#319/#322/#323/#325 and KEL-127 delegated direction. Verified by reading crates/keld-guard/src/lib.rs, crates/keld-wv/src/media.rs, crates/keld-runtime/src/role.rs, docs/architecture/02,03,04,05,06, docs/specs/kel78/kel102/kel130/kel132/kel135/kel142/kel75, research 186/13, and the scratchpad corpus (draw.io electron.js, build/fuses.mjs, electron-builder-*.json; Zettlr custom-protocols.ts, attach-app-navigation-handlers.ts, splash-screen.ts, onboarding-window.ts, main.ts, forge.config.js, source/common/modules/preload/index.ts). Not verified by me: Electron v44.4.5 doc receipts (no network fetch in this headless session) and Linear live state.

verdicts.reason: The inversion (one guard decision; Electron request+check handlers only narrow; missing handler = deny) is consistent with every live source: keld-guard evaluate() denies any non-AppProcess principal before grant lookup (lib.rs:704-706), empty manifest default-denies web.camera/web.microphone (lib.rs:1896-1936), media.rs routes a minted Principal::Webview into evaluate with the `*` sentinel (media.rs:124-133, 59), arch 03 §4(3) states the GUARD006/GUARD007 rules verbatim, research 186 row 4 records the two independent allow-by-default paths, and neither corpus app registers setPermissionRequestHandler/CheckHandler (grep over drawio electron.js and Zettlr source/ + forge.config.js is empty). Alternatives (a)-(d) are correctly rejected by briefing invariant 2 and the GUARD007 rule. Two secondary claims are wrong and must be corrected before this becomes a ticket.
verdicts.evidence: crates/keld-guard/src/lib.rs:704-706 (`if principal != Principal::AppProcess { return Deny(NotAppProcess) }`); lib.rs:1896-1936 tests; crates/keld-wv/src/media.rs:29-36,59,124-133; docs/architecture/03-security.md:239-263; docs/research/library/compatibility-competitors/186-electron-micro-surfaces.md row 4; corpus grep for setPermission*Handler: no matches in either app.
verdicts.correction: (1) blocked_by names 'KEL-102/T4 window-level grants' but KEL-102/T4 explicitly 'Preserve[s] default denial until a separately approved window-grant slice exists' (kel102-host-guard-enforcement.md:698-700) and KEL-102-D9 says the spec 'authorizes no ... manifest-schema change' (line 92). The `windows.<w>.web.*` evaluator has NO owner; the decision must name it as unowned new spec work (permission-model + manifest-schema gate), not as a KEL-102/T4 deliverable. The summary's 'none of which needs a new schema' is therefore overstated: keld-guard today parses and ignores `windows` (lib.rs:563-569) and must grow a `windows` reader. (2) 'Permission-name vocabulary = Electron's documented list 1:1 ... unknown names deny' has no owner either: keld-guard has no capability registry — evaluate() allows any `app.<g>.<a>` string array that matches (lib.rs:707-725), so 'unknown names deny' would be implemented in the facade, making it a second policy owner. Put the closed capability vocabulary in the generated schema/keld-guard, and schema-reject any `web.<name>` that has no host broker (today only camera/microphone).

verdicts.reason: The proposed spelling rests on a wrong reading of the live matcher. The author states a bare `"https:"` grant 'the authority rule already treats as names no destination and so is currently inert'. In keld-guard, `names_no_destination` is only consulted after `pattern.strip_suffix("/**")` succeeds (lib.rs:1191-1200); a pattern without `/**` takes the exact-match branch `path == pattern`. So `"https:"` is inert only because no URL literally equals `https:`; the authority rule never sees it. Promoting that literal to 'any destination of this scheme' is not 'vocabulary, not schema': it is a new wildcard semantics in the ONE shared path/URL matcher, which arch 03 §2 forbids as written: '`**` is the only wildcard a path or URL scope has; a lone `*` matches literally' and 'No glob grants any host for a multi-character scheme — name the origins' (03-security.md:120-123). Because `evaluate` uses the same `path_in_scope` for fs.read, net.connect and shell.open, a scheme-class special case in the matcher would silently also make `net.connect: ["https:"]` grant any host — a hidden coupling between atoms. The corpus demand is confirmed (draw.io allowedUrls regex at 4348 and renderer ipc 'openExternal' at 4515-4516; Zettlr will-navigate → openExternal/openPath at attach-app-navigation-handlers.ts:25-43), so the need is real, but the proposed mechanism and its 'currently inert via authority rule' justification are incorrect.
verdicts.evidence: crates/keld-guard/src/lib.rs:1136-1210 (`names_no_destination`, `path_in_scope`: exact-match branch when no `/**`); docs/architecture/03-security.md:104-123 (`**` only wildcard; lone `*` literal; name the origins); docs/architecture/05-webview-and-native.md:250 (shell broker row, not live); corpus drawio electron.js:4348-4360, 4515-4516; zettlr attach-app-navigation-handlers.ts:25-43.
verdicts.correction: Do not touch the shared matcher. Define `shell.open` as a capability whose broker canonicalizes the URL into two resources and evaluates both as exact literals with today's matcher: first the scheme token (`https:`, `mailto:`, `tel:`) against the grant list (exact match already works: `path_in_scope("https:", "https:")` is true), then, if a scheme is not class-granted, the origin against `https://host/**` entries. This keeps `**`-only wildcard semantics intact, confines the scheme-class policy to the shell broker, and still requires an arch 03 §2 amendment recording that a bare `scheme:` literal under `app.shell.open` (and only there) means 'any destination of that scheme' — a permission-model review gate plus a `keld doctor` loud-wildcard warning. `openPath`/`showItemInFolder`→fs.read, `trashItem`→fs.write, and the user-gesture rule remain open as stated (no Keld gesture mechanism exists; name it as unowned).

extra_findings.finding: keld-guard has no closed capability vocabulary: `evaluate` allows any `app.<group>.<action>` string array whose scope matches. epic.title: program(security): every Electron security surface mapped onto keld-guard, the KEL-142 bridge, principalized roles and the host-owned signed feed — with negative tests
epic.body:
## Scope
Permission request/check handlers, weak-isolation webPreferences, protocol privileges + CSP, shell.openExternal grants, single-instance/open-file intents, autoUpdater/fuses/ASAR trust, device permissions, media, devtools-in-release. Live today: `/app` grants for AppProcess only; a minted webview principal is `KELD-GUARD006` until window-level grants ship (KEL-102/T4); media callbacks evaluate resource `*` (wry exposes no origin); `windows`, `audit`, `roles` manifest sections parse-and-ignore.

## Design facts fixed by research (two refuters + panel)
- One guard decision, two Electron views: `windows.<w>.web.<permission>` evaluated as the webview principal; a missing handler is a deny; handlers only narrow; permission vocabulary is engine-hook-dependent (three columns).
- Weak-isolation webPreferences: privilege-escalating fields fail loudly; `disableBlinkFeatures` and engine flags are ignored with a diagnostic (draw.io sets it on every window); `sandbox:false` ▲ ignored, never a profile key.
- Scheme privileges are host declarations; `bypassCSP` never; `allowServiceWorkers` ▲ per engine; the CSP profile must admit draw.io's `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` and its style/img/connect sources (prototype P2 scope).
- OS-delivered intents (second-instance, open-file) are untrusted data admitted by the host; the file path becomes a host-scoped one-shot intent, not an ambient grant (corrected by the semantics refuter).
- Feed trust is host-only; fuses: draw.io flips RunAsNode=false, EnableCookieEncryption=true, NodeOptions=false, OnlyLoadAppFromAsar=true, EmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation=false (resolved from its build script); nine fuses incl. wasmTrapHandlers dispositioned.
- Device permissions (HID/USB/serial/Bluetooth): documented-unsupported, not legacy.

research.summary: Answer to "backward compatibility AND better performance, faster": compatibility is bought by cloning Electron's observable contract in a TS facade over kipc, and performance is bought by what the facade does NOT ship (bundled Chromium, Electron main-process stack). The two meet at one cost model: every Electron main-process call that is synchronous in Electron and needs host state becomes either (i) a blocking CALL (one kipc round trip, Windows Bun<->Rust diagnostic p50 ~47 us / p99 ~101 us vs 100 us budget, not publication-eligible; macOS/Linux Bun arm unmeasured; Rust<->Rust macOS library arm p99 9.25-9.6 us), (ii) a facade-side state mirror answered synchronously and kept coherent by host events carrying a generation/sequence stamp (write-through on setters), or (iii) an async-only divergence (▲) that changes the caller contract. Evidence says: [fact] the corpus does use sync getters in time-critical paths (draw.io persists getSize/getPosition/isMaximized/isFullScreen inside a close handler; 6 isDestroyed guards), [fact] Zettlr has 6 sendSync sites and 186 ipcRenderer.invoke sites, [fact] KEL-142's live minimum renderer bridge admits exactly one pending invoke per WebView, so the ipcRenderer facade cannot reach L1 for Zettlr until bounded multi-pending correlation (KEL-80 owner) exists. What gets cheaper is measured only narrowly: [fact] 78% lower main-process RSS in one Windows direct-COM session (total RSS NOT lower there), [fact] Bun bootstrap 53.3% sooner / 42.8% lower RSS in a narrow VS Code extension-host PoC, while [fact] Electron led first paint 275 ms vs Keld 469 ms (Chromium controller-creation floor, KEL-62). No compat-overhead lane exists in gyldlab/keld-benches (README fetched 2026-10-06), so facade cost today is a model, not a measurement; the plan is a same-app Electron-vs-Keld lane under KEL-90/KEL-129 census rules with p50/p95/p99 block-bootstrap and three never-blended claim classes (measured / target / projection). "Faster" delivery comes from parallelizing families that own disjoint crates/packages (native-desktop brokers, windowing registry+mirror, updater adapter, session/protocol transport) after one small serial step: a single-owner kipc channel-id and guard capability-name allocation rule, because keld-ipc frame constants, @keld/kipc transport.ts mirror constants, keld-guard manifest schema, Cargo.toml and root AGENTS.md are single-writer files that every family would otherwise collide on. Conformance entries and fixtures for every Tier 1 family can start now with zero code collision. "Faster" MUST NOT mean skipping conformance entries, widening permissions, retries, sleeps, a Rust rewrite as proof, blending claim classes, or publishing a percentage without a committed denominator.

Benchmarks: keld-benches has PAINT-OPPORTUNITY, MEM-IDLE, DISK, IPC-RTT (+ registry ids NATIVE-WINDOW, CRASH-RECOVERY); NO same-app compat-overhead lane. Measured facts: Windows kipc Bun<->Rust p50 47.6/p99 101.6 us fresh, p99 100.5 us warm (KEL-99, 25-byte payload, 1 session, diagnostic only); macOS Rust<->Rust library arm p99 9.25-9.625 us small / 10.08-10.46 us representative (note 243, 2026-09-10); macOS Bun arm UNMEASURED; Windows first paint host-only --hello 469 ms vs Electron 275 ms vs Tauri 479 ms; main-process RSS 19,552 KB vs Electron 89,140 KB (total RSS NOT lower). decisions.question: How do Electron-synchronous main-process window getters (getBounds/getSize/getPosition/isMaximized/isFullScreen/isDestroyed/getFocusedWindow/getAllWindows) get implemented without either lying (stale) or blocking the Bun event loop on every read?
decisions.proposed_answer: Facade-side window-state mirror, host-authoritative: the host (keld-core window registry, TARGET) emits window-state events (bounds, maximize/unmaximize, fullscreen, focus, destroyed) over the app link, each stamped with a monotonic per-window state generation. Getters read the mirror synchronously (zero kipc traffic, zero allocation per read). Setters (setBounds/maximize/...) are write-through: the facade applies the requested value to the mirror and issues the CALL; the host's confirming event (with the new generation) reconciles or corrects it, and a correction emits the Electron-visible event ('resize'/'move'). isDestroyed() and the 'Object has been destroyed' throw are answered purely from the mirror's destroyed flag, set by the host's destroyed event and by local destroy(). Divergence to record as ▲: between an OS-initiated change and arrival of the host event the getter can be one generation stale; Electron reads Chromium's in-process view so it is never stale. [inference] Reads dominate writes in the corpus (draw.io: 6 isDestroyed, 3 isFullScreen, 2 isMaximized, getSize/getPosition in a 'close' handler; Zettlr: 3 isMaximized, 3 getSize, 2 getBounds, 7 'resize' listeners), so the mirror removes nearly all round trips from these paths.

decisions.question: Can ipcRenderer.sendSync keep Electron's blocking-renderer contract on system webviews, as KEL-127 directs (blocking CALL with deadline, rate-limited, dev-warned), or is async-only the only honest option?
decisions.proposed_answer: Treat it per engine and record each as its own scoreboard cell. [fact] Electron: 'Sending a synchronous message will block the whole renderer process until the reply is received, so use this method only as a last resort'; main sees it as the distinct 'ipc-message-sync' event. [fact] WebView2 (Chromium-derived) exposes chrome.webview.hostObjects.sync.* synchronous proxies (Microsoft how-to page shows `chrome.webview.hostObjects.sync.sample.dateProperty` usage), so a blocking renderer->host hop is available there. [fact] WKWebView's documented JS->native paths (WKScriptMessageHandler, WKScriptMessageHandlerWithReply via window.webkit.messageHandlers.<name>.postMessage) are asynchronous; Apple's page describes no synchronous call path. [lead] The only known blocking emulation on WKWebView is a synchronous XMLHttpRequest to a WKURLSchemeHandler-served custom scheme (renderer web-content process blocks while the host completes the task asynchronously); this is unverified in Keld and must be prototyped, including its deadline behavior and whether sync XHR is still permitted on the main thread in the pinned WebKit. [unknown] WebKitGTK path. Proposed contract regardless of engine: the sendSync facade is a CALL on the same guarded channel as invoke, carries an absolute deadline (kel133 model: host-minted Instant, no renewal), is rate-limited in keld.compat.ts, dev-warns once per channel, and on deadline returns a thrown KELD error rather than hanging; where the engine cannot block, the cell is ▲ 'async-only' with a migrate diagnostic naming the site, never a silent Promise. Corpus demand is small but real: Zettlr 6 sites (config-provider get-config/set, citeproc-provider; preload/index.ts:37,57,63,74; pinia/config.ts:28,49), draw.io 0.

decisions.question: Does the live renderer bridge (KEL-142: exactly one pending invoke per WebView, second invoke fails immediately) allow an ipcRenderer.invoke facade that real apps can use?
decisions.proposed_answer: No. [fact] Zettlr has 186 ipcRenderer.invoke call sites across 65 files and 25 ipcMain.handle sites; Vue components issue overlapping invokes during mount. Under KEL-142's rule the second concurrent invoke fails immediately rather than queueing, so Zettlr would fail at L1 (basic behavior), not at some semantic edge. The ipcRenderer/ipcMain family therefore has a hard sequencing dependency: bounded multi-pending correlation per WebView (host-minted correlation ids, bounded window, slow-consumer rejection with a typed error, no hidden unbounded queue, stale-reply discard on navigation) must be specified under the KEL-80 owner (virtual channels/backpressure/replay) and KEL-142's §6 rules before any ipcRenderer facade claims BEHAVIOR_MATCH. Electron itself has no documented concurrency limit on invoke; the Keld bound must be published as ▲ with its number. This is also the performance lever: pipelined invokes overlap kipc round trips instead of serializing 186 calls at ~50-100 us each.

decisions.question: What is the hot-path cost model for the chatty one-way patterns (webContents.send main->renderer; ipcRenderer.send renderer->main; window event fan-out), and which rules keep facade hot paths allocation-free and semantically honest?
decisions.proposed_answer: Model (per call): Electron webContents.send = structured clone + one Mojo hop, in-process on the main side, synchronous throw at the call site for Function/Promise/Symbol/WeakMap/WeakSet arguments. Keld webContents.send = facade serialization in Bun -> one kipc frame Bun->host (today: TS FrameReader/WriteQueue allocate per frame; Rust read_frame allocates one Vec per payload) -> host routes to the window-bound virtual channel -> engine postMessage/evaluateJavaScript into the isolated world -> page listener. So Keld adds one extra process hop versus Electron's main process but removes Electron's main-process Chromium stack; whether net latency is better is UNMEASURED. Rules: (1) serialization semantics are the contract: throw synchronously at the facade for the same type set Electron rejects; do not silently drop or JSON-null them; (2) one serialization, one frame, no second buffering layer in the facade (the kipc WriteQueue is the only queue; arch 02 §6 'per-link single-producer queues'); (3) event fan-out from host to many windows is host-side routing, never N facade CALLs; (4) the zero-steady-state-allocation rule is arch 02 §6's destination and is NOT met by the live code (research 101/163) - the facade MUST NOT be claimed allocation-free until the attributed allocation lane in keld-benches shows zero per CALL in both Bun and Rust arms; until then the honest status is 'bounded, per-frame allocating'; (5) payload bound: MAX_FRAME_LEN 16 MiB for frames, MAX_PORT_MESSAGE_LEN 4096 for virtual ports - a webContents.send of a large object over a 4096-byte port path must fail with a typed error, not fragment silently.

decisions.question: What is the minimum sequencing and the maximum safe parallelism for the compat families, given single-writer files and the product spine?
decisions.proposed_answer: Serial step 0 (small, one owner, before fan-out): a channel-id and capability-name allocation rule. Today channel ids are hand-mirrored constants in two files (crates/keld-ipc/src/frame.rs|lib.rs and packages/@keld/kipc/src/transport.ts: ECHO_CHANNEL=1, LIFECYCLE_CHANNEL=3) and guard capability names live in the keld-guard manifest schema; every family that adds a channel or grant touches the same lines. The rule (keld-ipc owner, KEL-98 codegen as the generator) should reserve id ranges per family and generate the TS mirror, so families stop colliding. Then parallel tracks with disjoint write sets: T-A native-desktop (F06: dialog/shell/clipboard/Notification/screen/nativeImage) -> keld-native brokers + guard grants + @keld/electron modules; T-B windowing (F01/F02) -> keld-core window registry + keld-wv + @keld/electron BrowserWindow + the A1 state mirror; T-C ipc-bridge (F04) -> KEL-80 multi-pending + preload injection + ipcMain/ipcRenderer/contextBridge (depends on KEL-142 Done, blocks on A3); T-D session/protocol (F05) -> KEL-79 webview origin/resource transport (custom schemes, SW limits); T-E updater/packaging (F09) -> KEL-53 full-package activation adapter + bridge release recipe; T-F diagnostics (F08) -> crashReporter map over supervisor crash accounting. Spine coupling: KEL-140 (guarded fs) and KEL-143 (Bun generation recovery) are on the spine; T-A/T-B/T-E do not need them to start, but T-C's recovery semantics (stale reply discard, no replay) must consume KEL-143's ordering, and anything claiming CORPUS_VERIFIED on macOS needs KEL-141 prebuilt CLI. Zero-collision work that can start immediately for every family: conformance entries + Electron-oracle fixtures (tests before implementation per crates/keld-compat/AGENTS.md), the X05-A5 bench lane (separate repo), and scratchpad prototypes (A1 mirror, A2 WKWebView sync XHR). Single-writer files that serialize merges regardless of track: Cargo.toml (new crate or dependency = review gate), crates/keld-ipc frame/receive constants, @keld/kipc transport.ts, keld-guard manifest schema, root AGENTS.md and nested AGENTS allowlist (`just agents-md`), docs/engineering/product-status.tsv, compat-scoreboard.md, llms.txt (`just llms-check`).

epic.title: program(perf): facade cost model, sync-getter mirrors, compat-overhead benchmark lane, channel-id allocation rule and parallelism plan
epic.body:
## Scope
How compatibility and performance meet: every Electron main-process call that is synchronous in Electron and needs host state becomes a facade mirror read (zero traffic), a write-through Call, or a documented ▲; renderer→main hops double versus Electron; the kipc client cannot block today (panel); measurement rules from arch 01 §5/§5.1.

## Measured today (never blended with targets)
Windows host-process RSS 19,552 KB vs Electron 89,140 KB (Electron won total process tree); host-only first paint Keld 469 / Tauri 479 / Electron 275 ms (Electron leads); Windows kipc Bun↔Rust diagnostic p99 ≈ 101 µs (1 session, not publication-eligible); macOS Rust↔Rust library arm p99 ≈ 9.3–9.6 µs; Bun extension-host bootstrap PoC 53% sooner (narrow). Forbidden claims are listed on the map.

## Design facts from research (NOT yet independently refuted — batch 2; X05-A1/A3 settled by the panel)
- Window-state mirror: host events stamped with a monotonic per-window state generation; getters read the mirror synchronously, setters are write-through; zero steady-state allocation per read.
- The KEL-142 one-pending floor blocks Zettlr at L1 (186 invoke sites): floor v2 (F04-T2) is a hard prerequisite for ipcRenderer.invoke.
- Hot-path cost model: Keld webContents.send = facade serialisation → kipc frame → host routing → engine script evaluation into the isolated world (≥ 3 serialise stages vs Electron's 2); per-frame allocation exists today in the TS reader/writer and the Rust frame read.
- Benchmark lane: same-app compat-overhead arms in gyldlab/keld-benches (electron-quick-start first, then draw.io), registered metric ids FACADE-RTT (renderer invoke → ipcMain.handle → reply), FACADE-DELTA (`@keld/electron` minus raw `@keld/api`), SEND-FANOUT, SYNC-BLOCK, plus the §5.1 product census (idle RSS, first paint) with interleaved rounds, ≥20 sessions × 100k calls for IPC.
- Serial step 0: a channel-id and capability-name allocation rule (reserved id ranges per family, generated constants) because every family touches the same hand-mirrored constants in keld-ipc and the TS transport.

research.summary: Program structure for the Electron-compat wayfinder map. [fact] The product spine has moved since #322: KEL-139 (spec) and KEL-142 (macOS renderer bridge + @keld/api lifecycle/channel) are Done (Linear, 2026-10-01); KEL-140/141/143/144 are Backlog with native blockedBy edges; KEL-102/T3 (checkbox unchecked in docs/specs/kel102-host-guard-enforcement.md at d150a14), KEL-103 and KEL-118 are In Progress; KEL-75 T4 (window-bound role lifecycle) and T5 (utilityProcess facade) are unchecked; KEL-79/KEL-80/KEL-97 are Backlog. [fact] KEL-127 non-goals forbid "broad Electron API expansion ... before G2" and order G2 spine -> G3 clean-Mac -> G4 "distribution and wider compatibility"; Prompt Tracker docs/06 says later compat prompts are generated only when a phase-gate artifact proves prerequisites. [fact] Live Keld surface relevant to compat: single host-owned window with a LifecycleSession window counter (keld-core lifecycle.rs), Ready/LastWindowClosed/Quit over LIFECYCLE_CHANNEL, window.keld.invoke(numeric channel, Uint8Array, bounded) in a WKContentWorld isolated world on macOS 11+ only, one guarded fs broker (fs.read/fs.write, FS_CHANNEL 2) not yet reachable through the product adapter (KEL-140), KEL-74 evidence/denominator scorer plus a 3-cell showcase lifecycle corpus pinned to Electron 44.3.0, and @keld/electron exporting only `app`. No window registry, no host->renderer push (`window.keld.on/send` are destination-only in arch 05 §2), no app-preload injection, no string-channel IPC, no migrate (KELD-CLI-045 reserved). Proposed structure: (1) entry condition = conformance entries, oracle-pin/manifest spec, read-only migrate analyzer and decision tickets start now; BrowserWindow/ipcMain/contextBridge implementation slices are hard-blocked on landed task artifacts KEL-140 (first guarded product route), KEL-143 (same-window/document recovery), a new approved keld-core window-registry spec, a host->renderer push slice recorded on KEL-80, and an app-preload-in-isolated-world slice recorded on KEL-79; KEL-144 gates only the clean-machine corpus claim; KEL-97 is not a Tier-1 facade predecessor (KEL-102 approved kel97_predecessor_task_id=none; KEL-142 landed without it). (2) Epic order by corpus demand and dependency: F01 app (extend KEL-72) -> F02 BrowserWindow core -> F04 ipc/contextBridge -> F06 native Tier-1 brokers (dialog, shell, Menu, clipboard, screen/nativeTheme, Notification, Tray, nativeImage) -> Tier 2 F03 webContents, F05 session/protocol, F04 utilityProcess (KEL-75/T5), F09 autoUpdater->keld-update (KEL-53), F08 crashReporter map -> Tier 3 F07 webview tag (corpus demand zero; draw.io disables it). (3) Decision tickets: 3 grilling (G2/G4 entry reading of KEL-127; window-registry + two-phase Quit wire scope; tier placement of nativeTheme/systemPreferences/app.getPath), 2 research (corpus-manifest canonical bytes + Electron oracle repin to v44.4.5; isolated-world preload matrix across WKWebView/WebView2/WebKitGTK), 3 prototype (string-channel structured-clone envelope under the 4096-byte inline bound; sendSync blocking CALL with deadline per engine; exposeInMainWorld emulation parity), 4 task (HITL tracker-config adoption through .agents/instructions.md budget rules; Linear bridge when cap allows; rescan corpus without ambiguous-name noise; refresh Prompt Tracker doc 06 after the G2 artifact). (4) Fog and out-of-scope lists enumerated in open_unknowns/never_list. (5) GitHub: one wayfinder:map with sub-issues; decision tickets wayfinder:<type>; epics `epic`+`electron-compat`+`compat:tier-N`+`crate:*`+`needs-spec`, blocked-by the entry ticket via native blocking links; conformance-entry sub-issues `type:test`+`ready-for-agent` startable now; two dated-free milestones mirroring arch 04 §4 tier exits; no milestones exist today. semantic_traps.electron_behavior: quit: 'Try to close all windows. The before-quit event will be emitted first.' If all windows close, will-quit then quit; exit: 'Exits immediately with exitCode ... before-quit and will-quit events will not be emitted.'
semantic_traps.keld_risk: Keld Quit is a single correlated kipc Call that the host executes with ordering accept->reply->quiesce->revoke->terminate (KEL-96). A cancelable before-quit requires a host->Bun pre-close phase (two-phase Quit) — a wire change owned by keld-core; app.exit must map to a non-cancelable path without emitting the two events. Zettlr listens to before-quit and will-quit; draw.io to before-quit.
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Sequence test: register before-quit (preventDefault once) -> app.quit() -> assert no window closed and no will-quit; second quit -> before-quit, window close, will-quit, quit in that order; app.exit(3) -> process exit code 3 with neither event; ordering captured as a transcript, not booleans.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: 'If you do not subscribe to this event and all windows are closed, the default behavior is to quit the app; however, if you subscribe, you control whether the app quits or not.'
semantic_traps.keld_risk: Already matched for one window (KEL-72 ✔). With a window registry the counter must be shared with BrowserWindow.destroy/close paths; quick-start keeps the app alive on darwin with zero windows, so the host must not exit the process when count hits zero and a listener exists.
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Existing cell app.window-all-closed.policy extended: two windows, close both -> exactly one LastWindowClosed; listener present on darwin -> process alive; `activate` then recreates (count 1).

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: 'Emitted when the web page has been rendered (while not being shown) and window can be displayed without a visual flash.' Pattern: show:false then win.once('ready-to-show', () => win.show()).
semantic_traps.keld_risk: Keld host windows are created visible by the hello/app path; without a host first-paint/hidden-window signal the facade either fires ready-to-show before paint (flash) or never (Zettlr 14 sites would never show). First-paint attribution exists only as a bench oracle (KEL-64).
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Create window show:false; assert not OS-visible (AppKit/Win32/GTK visibility oracle) until ready-to-show fires; after show() visible; negative: firing ready-to-show before the engine's document-rendered callback fails the test.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: close: 'emitted before the beforeunload and unload event of the DOM. Calling event.preventDefault() will cancel the close.' destroy(): 'unload and beforeunload event won't be emitted ... close event will also not be emitted ... guarantees the closed event will be emitted.' closed: 'you should remove the reference to the window'. The Keld facade must map a dead WebviewId to a thrown Error with exactly that message, must not emit `close` on destroy, and must guarantee `closed` even when the host revoked the window during Bun recovery (KEL-143).

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: 'If the handler in the main process throws an error, the promise returned by invoke will reject. However, the Error object in the renderer process will not be the same as the one thrown in the main process.' ipc-main.md: 'Errors thrown through handle in the main process are not transparent as they are serialized and only the message property from the original error is provided to the renderer process.'
semantic_traps.keld_risk: Keld's canonical CallError{code,message} (keld_ipc::write_call_error) would leak a KELD-* code or alter message text if passed through verbatim; research 186 says stringified errors cannot be the canonical kipc contract — the compat envelope must carry message-only to the page while the host keeps the typed code for the scoreboard/diagnostics.
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Handler throws `Object.assign(new Error('boom'), {code:'X'})` -> renderer rejection: err.message === 'boom', err.code === undefined, err instanceof Error; negative: deny path yields a KELD-GUARD code in host logs but the page sees only a message.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: 'Arguments will be serialized with the Structured Clone Algorithm, just like window.postMessage, so prototype chains will not be included. Sending Functions, Promises, Symbols, WeakMaps, or WeakSets will throw an exception.'
semantic_traps.keld_risk: window.keld.invoke takes a Uint8Array with a 4096-byte inline bound (host test negative at 4097 bytes; MAX_PORT_MESSAGE_LEN 4096) and numeric channels. A JSON envelope would silently stringify Dates/Maps and drop functions instead of throwing; oversized Zettlr payloads would hit the bound. Prototype P1 decides chunking vs larger frames.
semantic_traps.test_oracle: send(() => {}) throws synchronously; send(new Map([[1,2]])) round-trips as Map; send(Object.create({x:1})) arrives without prototype property; payload of 64 KiB either succeeds or fails with one typed error — never truncation.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: 'Sending a synchronous message will block the whole renderer process until the reply is received, so use this method only as a last resort.' Tutorial: 'sends a message to the main process and waits synchronously for a response.'
semantic_traps.keld_risk: KEL-127 binds: replacement must stay a blocking CALL with deadline, rate-limited, dev-warned; a Promise return changes the caller contract. Zettlr's pinia config store calls sendSync('config-provider', {command:'get-config'}) at init and exposes sendSync through contextBridge, so an async shim breaks state initialization. WKScriptMessageHandlerWithReply is asynchronous; a synchronous renderer block needs an engine-specific primitive (prototype P2).
semantic_traps.test_oracle: In page: `const v = window.api.sendSync('x'); typeof v !== 'object' || !('then' in v)` and value available before any microtask; deadline expiry yields a thrown typed error, not a hang; rate-limit beyond N/s produces a dev warning line in the host capture.

semantic_traps.electron_behavior: 'Create a safe, bi-directional, synchronous bridge across isolated contexts.' Table: Error 'Custom properties on the Error object will be lost'; Function 'Prototype modifications are dropped'; Symbol 'cannot be copied across contexts'; exposing the whole ipcRenderer module 'will result in an empty object'.
semantic_traps.keld_risk: Only WKWebView has a live isolated world in Keld; page-world objects cannot be shared across WKContentWorlds, so exposeInMainWorld must be emulated via a page-world proxy whose calls stay synchronous for sync functions — a message-passing emulation would turn `window.api.fn()` into a Promise (parity break; Zettlr/draw.io expose sync wrappers).
semantic_traps.test_oracle: Preload exposes {fn: () => 42, err: () => Object.assign(new Error('e'),{k:1})}; page asserts window.api.fn() === 42 without await; window.api.err().k === undefined; Object.getPrototypeOf(window.api.fn) === Function.prototype; exposing ipcRenderer yields {}.

ipcMain.handle: handler called on ipcRenderer.invoke; Promise result returned as reply; errors are serialized and only `message` reaches the renderer; handleOnce/removeHandler semantics

sendSync blocks the whole renderer process; invoke rejects with a different Error object; Structured Clone serialization and throw cases; postMessage transfers MessagePorts; contextBridge needed under contextIsolation; sendToHost targets <webview>
